Summary:
The Customer Success team at Anaconda is the primary relationship layer between our platform and the enterprise organizations that depend on it — from data scientists and ML engineers to IT architects and security teams managing open-source risk at scale. We help customers get real, measurable value from Anaconda's product suite by building trust, showing up prepared, and staying curious about what each customer is actually trying to solve.
As a Senior Technical Customer Success Manager, you own a portfolio of strategic enterprise accounts and operate as the voice of the customer across the organization. You bring deep technical fluency (across Python packaging, environment management, and enterprise security and governance) and you use it to close the gap between what customers deploy and the value they actually realize. You're not here to just manage relationships. You're here to set the standard for how we engage technically and commercially, and to leave the function stronger than you found it.

What You’ll Do:
• Own a portfolio of enterprise accounts. Build deep relationships across complex organizations (from data scientists and platform engineers to IT architects, security leads, and C-suite stakeholders) well beyond the initial point of contact.
• Accelerate onboarding and initial adoption. Guide customers through first-use milestones: environment setup, CVE policy configuration, private repo and channel tokenization, and initial workflow adoption, coding assistant & quick start processes. Identify and resolve technical blockers before they threaten time-to-value.
• Drive ongoing usage health and consumption. Monitor seat utilization, package and channel usage, and admin portal signals to identify underused licenses, stalled users, or shadow IT risk. Proactively engage the AE when usage patterns suggest expansion opportunity or churn risk.
• Arrive at every customer interaction with a prepared point of view. Draw on product usage data, health scores, and technical signals to drive conversations forward and deliver clear value at each touchpoint. No filler meetings.
• Own the technical inputs to account health scoring. Surface risk early (unresolved CVE exposure, blocked package access, unmanaged environments) and coordinate mitigation plans with the RM, Support, and FDE.
• Act as the voice of the customer to Product and Engineering. Channel technical requirements, competitive intelligence, and enhancement requests. Partner with Solutions Engineering on where Anaconda complements or competes with adjacent platforms in the customer's stack.
• Build the technical narrative for QBRs and executive engagement. Partner with the account team to document use cases, quantify value delivered (time saved, risk reduced, packages secured), and make the business case stick at the executive level.
• Support renewal and expansion. Bring technical proof points into renewal conversations (usage data, security posture improvements, workshop outcomes), advise the RM on churn forecast based on adoption and usage signals, and flag technical expansion whitespace — new teams, new use cases, adjacent workloads — to the AE for commercial pursuit.
• Use AI as a force multiplier. Build AI-enabled success approaches the team actually adopts. Know where AI belongs in the customer motion and where human judgment stays central. Your standard becomes the team's standard.
• Contribute to playbook development and team infrastructure. Senior TSMs are expected to leave the function stronger than they found it — through documentation, engagement templates, peer coaching, and process improvements that raise overall team performance.
• Mentor and coach less experienced team members through account reviews, technical strategy sessions, and informal guidance. Translate personal experience into repeatable, teachable approaches.
• Operate within a GTM pod. Sit alongside the Account Executive, Renewal Manager, Solutions Engineer, and other pod roles (FDE, BDR, TAM where applicable) under a shared pod leader. Attend weekly pod and pipeline meetings and collaborate closely with the AE on account plans, customer relationships, and QBRs.

What Success Looks Like:
• Net revenue retention (NRR) across your enterprise portfolio
• Customer health score trends and reduction in at-risk accounts
• Time-to-value and adoption depth across your book of business
• Quality and completeness of success plans, technical documentation, and account records
• Expansion pipeline sourced from within existing accounts
• AI-enabled workflows or playbook contributions adopted by peers

What You’ll Need:
• 6+ years in a technical customer-facing role — customer success, technical account management, solutions engineering, or similar — with demonstrated ownership of a £4 million+ book of business and accountability for retention and growth outcomes at large enterprise accounts (10,000+ employees)
• Understanding of enterprise security and governance concepts relevant to Anaconda: CVE exposure, package provenance, air-gapped and private repo deployment, SSO, and gated registration
• Experience with data science, ML, or developer tooling platforms — Databricks, Domino, Dataiku, SageMaker, or similar — and familiarity with how Anaconda fits into or alongside these environments
• Ability to read logs and error output to triage technical issues before escalating to Support or Professional Services — you know the difference between self-resolving, routing to Support, and escalating to Product
• Proven ability to build relationships across complex organizations — from practitioners to VP and C-suite stakeholders — and translate technical risk and product capability into executive-level business impact
• Familiarity with adjacent and competitive tooling — SageMaker, Databricks, Snowflake, Vertex AI — sufficient to position Anaconda's complement-vs.-compete story credibly
• Project management skills to coordinate multi-stakeholder technical engagements: onboarding, workshops, proofs of concept
• Strong verbal and written communication across all levels of an organization, including executive audiences
• AI fluency in daily work — comfortable using AI tools to research, document, prepare, and draft; rigorous about reviewing what you produce under your name before it reaches a customer
• Bachelor's degree in a technical field or equivalent practical experience

What Will Make You Stand Out:
• Experience at a high-growth or early-stage company where the playbook wasn't written yet — you've helped build structure from scratch, operated with autonomy, and stayed effective when priorities shifted underneath you
• Working fluency in Python packaging and environment management — conda, pip, pixi, and the tradeoffs between them — and the ability to hold a substantive technical conversation without SE support in routine scenarios
• Deep familiarity with open-source ecosystems — software supply chain security, dependency management, license compliance exposure, and vulnerability workflows — and the ability to speak credibly to a CISO or VP Engineering about why it matters
• A history of contributing to team infrastructure — playbooks, engagement templates, peer coaching, or process improvements that raised overall team performance, not just your own numbers
• Experience in a high-growth, open-source, or data science-oriented company where customer needs evolve quickly and the product is still maturing
• AI-enabled workflow contributions — you've built something others use, not just used AI for yourself; you've made a judgment call about where AI doesn't belong and explained why
• You embody our values — Curious by Default, Build Together, Own It, and Lead with Guts and Heart — and our behaviors: Clarity, Care, and Candor

Why You'll Like Working Here:
• You'll thrive in a high-performance environment where results are recognized and rewarded
• Your work directly contributes to shaping the future of data science, machine learning, and AI in the enterprise.
• You'll work alongside a collaborative team that values diverse, thoughtful discussion, clarity and candor.
• You'll be supported by a culture that puts employees first - with flexible hours, a fully remote setup, and a genuine commitment to your wellbeing and growth.

We're pioneering a new role focused exclusively on quality assurance for GenAI/Agentic systems. As our QA Automation Engineer within AI, you'll develop testing strategies, evaluation frameworks, and quality metrics specifically designed for LLM-powered applications. This role requires a unique blend of QA expertise, understanding of GenAI behaviour, and automation skills to ensure our AI features are reliable, accurate, and trustworthy.

Your Impact

• Develop and execute end-to-end automated test coverage across evaluations, APIs, UIs, and performance tests using Python.

• Hands-on Python coding experience.

• Good understanding of GenAI technologies including LLMs, prompt engineering, and AI application patterns.

• Solid experience with test automation frameworks and scripting (Python, Pytest, API, and UI Testing).

• Practical knowledge of software testing methodologies (functional, integration, regression, performance, security testing).

• Experience with API testing tools (Postman, REST Assured) and backend testing.

• Familiarity with CI/CD pipelines and automated testing integration.

We are building the next generation of wargaming facilities purpose-built for the military to run massive-scale simulations of autonomous systems operating in contested environments. Those facilities are only useful if they are up, current, and trustworthy. A failed scenario run or a silent regression after a software release costs operators and engineers’ real time.

As our founding Site Reliability Engineer, you will design, build, and operate the infrastructure that makes this possible. You'll work at the intersection of hardware, simulation software and distributed systems. You will be the person who knows why the simulation broke, who catches it before anyone else notices, and who makes sure it doesn't break the same way twice. This is a hands-on role that blends software maintenance, infrastructure ownership, and release validation, with direct exposure to the development teams whose code you're keeping stable.

This position is in Abu Dhabi, UAE, with initial position hiring occurring in London, UK. Candidate must be willing to relocate to the facility upon completion.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

• Maintain the simulation software stack - installation, configuration, updates, version management, and day-to-day functionality across the Simulation Center's tools and environments.

• Own the underlying infrastructure - compute, networking, storage, and environment configuration that the simulation depends on; keep it provisioned, patched, and performant.

• Build and maintain a post-release test suite - design, automate, and continually extend a regression and smoke-test process that runs after every software release or configuration change, so integration issues surface immediately rather than mid-exercise.

• Forecast, diagnose, and eliminate failure modes - root-cause errors and bugs in the system, drive them to permanent resolution, and implement the guardrails, monitoring, or process changes that prevent recurrence.

• Partner with development teams and stakeholders - review upcoming changes for reliability risk, surface concerns early, and implement mitigation strategies before releases land in the simulation environment.

• Monitor overall system health - instrument and watch the environment, triage issues within your scope, and escalate clearly and quickly with the context needed for others to act when an issue exceeds your ability to resolve it.

• Document what you learn - runbooks, known issues, environment configuration, and release validation results, so the Simulation Center's operational knowledge isn't held in one person's head.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Proficiency in Python for automation, tooling, and test development.

• Working knowledge of C++; enough to read, debug, build, and trace issues in the simulation codebase.

• Solid general networking fundamentals: TCP/IP, UDP, multicast, DNS, routing, firewalls, and the ability to diagnose latency, packet loss, and connectivity problems across distributed systems.

• Experience with project management, issue tracking, bug triage, and coordinating work across engineering teams.

• Demonstrated experience maintaining production or production-adjacent systems, including troubleshooting under time pressure.

• Strong written and verbal communication; you can escalate an issue, explain a root cause, and write a runbook someone else can follow.

• Eligibility to pass the security and background check requirements for sensitive information systems.

 PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Experience with modeling and simulation, wargaming, or distributed simulation standards (DIS, HLA, TENA) and platforms such as AFSIM, VBS, or similar.

• Test automation and CI/CD experience; building automated validation pipelines, not just running them.

• Infrastructure-as-code and configuration management (Terraform, Ansible, Docker, Kubernetes).

• On-prem and cloud deployment experience.

• Observability tooling: Prometheus, Grafana, ELK, or equivalent.

• Linux systems administration depth; comfort in mixed Linux/Windows environments.

• Prior work in a defense, aerospace, or classified environment.

• Active security clearance.

About the role

We are hiring a UK-based Technical Lead to work with our existing global team and promote quality and excellence in our web-based solution delivery.

Our team builds and runs corporate and enterprise-scale web properties on a composable stack: headless CMS, Node and React front ends, and the integrations that connect them to the client's wider platform.

You will be the team's technical voice to the client as well as leading the development of your assigned projects. You will work with the team to translate business goals into a clear deliverable technical plan while communicating trade-offs, risk and progress to stakeholders.

This is a hands-on technical leadership role. You will plan, code and review, while being accountable for the technical outcome of the project team.

What you will do

Technical direction and quality

• Set the team's technical direction and own architecture and design decisions across the composable stack.

• Select and justify the right headless CMS, front-end framework and hosting approach for each property, weighing editorial experience, performance, cost and lock-in.

• Design content models and component libraries that scale across multiple brands, sites, regions and locales.

• Uphold coding standards and best practices through consistent code review.

• Ensure developers test their own work before it reaches QA, with automated testing and CI/CD in place.

• Hold the team to clear standards for security, accessibility, search and performance (detailed below).

Web standards: accessibility, search and performance

• Own accessibility to WCAG 2.2 AA as a minimum, with awareness of the European Accessibility Act and UK public-sector regulations where they apply. Build it into components, content models and testing, combining automated tools (axe, Lighthouse) with manual keyboard and screen-reader checks.

• Own technical SEO: semantic HTML, structured data (schema.org), metadata, canonicals, sitemaps, hreflang for multi-region sites, and redirect strategy during migrations.

• Prepare properties for answer engine optimisation (AEO) and generative engine optimisation (GEO), so content is structured, attributable and easy for AI search and assistants to find, understand and cite.

• Set performance budgets and hold the team to Core Web Vitals targets (LCP, INP, CLS), using real-user monitoring as well as lab testing.

• Build these checks into CI so regressions are caught before release, not after.

AI-assisted engineering

• Lead a team working in a heavily AI-tooled environment, using coding assistants and agents such as Claude Code, GitHub Copilot or Cursor, and set clear rules for how they are used.

• Preserve codebase quality: AI-generated code meets the same standards for review, testing, security and maintainability as hand-written code.

• Keep people accountable: every change has an owner who understands it, and architecture decisions are not delegated to tools.

• Maintain the guardrails that make AI output reliable, including linting, type checking, test coverage, documented conventions and context files the tools can follow.

• Watch for AI-specific risks, such as client data or secrets in prompts, licence and IP concerns, and duplicated or inconsistent code.

Migrations and integrations

• Plan and lead content and platform migrations from legacy or monolithic CMS platforms to headless, including content audits, mapping, transformation and URL redirect strategy.

• Design repeatable migration and automation pipelines using n8n or similar tools, alongside custom Node scripts where needed.

• Lead integration development between the CMS and the client's wider estate, such as CRM, DAM, PIM, search, analytics, marketing automation and identity.

• Own API design, webhooks and event-driven patterns, with clear error handling, monitoring and rollback.

Documentation and knowledge sharing

• Own documentation for architecture, content models, integrations, design decisions and technical specifications.

• Turn one-to-one guidance into reusable material so onboarding and handoff don't depend on any one person.

• Stay current on [client-specific compliance requirements, e.g. UK GDPR, cookie consent (PECR) and accessibility obligations].

Team leadership and mentoring

• Break plans down into well-formed tasks and stories the team can act on.

• Delegate work fairly and evenly across the team.

• Coach and mentor developers to grow the team's capability in headless and composable delivery.

Client communication and stakeholder management

• Serve as the client's primary contact for technical discussions.

• Explain technical concepts, options and status to non-technical stakeholders, including marketing and content teams, in plain language.

• Manage client expectations honestly on scope, effort and risk.

Delivery

• Lead technical input to planning, estimation and backlog refinement.

• Track progress against milestones and budget with the project manager.

• Identify technical risks early, particularly around migration cut-over and third-party integrations, and escalate critical issues before they become surprises.

Commercial awareness

• Seek client feedback and fold it into development cycles.

• Spot genuine opportunities to add value for the client, and bring them to the account team.

What success looks like

• Delegation is healthy. Work is spread across the team, not bottlenecked on you.

• Documentation survives handoff. A new engineer can onboard and maintain the system from what is written down.

• Migrations land cleanly. Content moves with no lost pages, broken links or SEO drop, and cut-overs happen on the planned date.

• Standards are measurable. Properties meet WCAG 2.2 AA and Core Web Vitals targets, and are visible in both traditional and AI-driven search.

• Quality holds as speed rises. AI tooling increases throughput without increasing defects, accessibility issues or performance regressions.

• Editors are self-sufficient. Content teams can build and publish pages without developer help.

• Integrations are reliable. Data flows between systems are monitored, and failures are caught before the client notices.

• The client trusts you. Stakeholders route technical decisions through you.

What you bring

Required

• 8+ years in software development, including at least 2 years leading a team's technical direction.

• A track record delivering corporate and enterprise-scale web properties: multi-site, multi-brand or multi-region platforms with high traffic, complex governance and many stakeholders.

• Proven ability to turn a technical vision into a clear, actionable plan a team can execute.

• Excellent communication with non-technical audiences.

• Right to work in the UK.

Technical skills

• Composable architecture: designing MACH-style (microservices, API-first, cloud-native, headless) solutions and making sound build-versus-buy decisions.

• Headless CMS: hands-on delivery with at least two of Sanity, Contentful, Builder.io, Strapi or Webflow, including content modelling, editorial workflows, localisation and preview.

• React: strong production experience, ideally with Next.js or a similar framework, covering SSR, SSG and ISR rendering strategies.

• Node.js and TypeScript: building APIs, serverless functions, middleware and scripts.

• Migrations: leading content or platform migrations at scale, using n8n or similar automation tools (e.g. Make, Zapier, custom ETL) as well as scripted approaches.

• Integration development: REST and GraphQL APIs, webhooks, authentication (OAuth, SSO) and connecting a CMS to CRM, DAM, PIM, search and analytics platforms.

• Engineering practice: Git workflows, CI/CD, automated testing, and deployment to platforms such as Vercel, Netlify, AWS or Azure.

• Accessibility: in-depth knowledge of WCAG 2.2 AA, ARIA and semantic HTML, with hands-on assistive-technology testing.

• Search, AEO and GEO: technical SEO, structured data, and structuring content so it performs in AI-driven search and answer engines.

• Performance: Core Web Vitals, performance budgets, caching and CDN strategy, and image, font and script optimisation.

• AI-assisted development: daily, fluent use of AI coding tools, with the judgement to review, test and reject their output so the codebase stays clean and maintainable.

Nice to have

• Consulting or agency experience, managing client relationships alongside delivery.

• Experience establishing team practices from scratch on a new engagement.

• Experience writing AI usage policies or engineering guidelines for a team.

• Certifications or partner experience with Sanity, Contentful or other composable vendors.

• Experience with commerce or search platforms in a composable stack (e.g. Shopify, commercetools, Algolia).

• Familiarity with design systems and tools such as Storybook and Figma.

Join Aptia and help protect our business, clients and members from financial crime.

At Aptia, we're transforming pensions and employee benefits administration through expertise, innovation and a commitment to delivering exceptional outcomes for our clients and members. As our business continues to grow, we're looking for a highly analytical and detail-oriented Financial Crime Analyst to join our Financial Crime team (1LOD).

This is an exciting opportunity for someone with practical experience in financial crime investigations, fraud prevention or screening who is looking to develop their expertise within a supportive and growing organisation.

You'll support the First Line Financial Crime Lead by reviewing referrals, investigating potential financial crime risks, maintaining effective case records and helping operational teams apply established controls to protect clients and members.

What you'll be doing: 

As Financial Crime Analyst, you'll support the day-to-day delivery of first-line financial crime activity across our UK business, reporting into the First Line Financial Crime Lead. Working closely with operational teams and escalating matters when required, you'll:

• Investigate referrals relating to suspected pension fraud, member impersonation, changes to bank details, unusual benefit payment requests, overseas payments and other potentially high-risk activity, escalating significant concerns to the First Line Financial Crime Lead.
• Review and analyse information from multiple sources to identify concerns, inconsistencies and potential financial crime risks.
• Review PEP, sanctions and AML screening alerts, document false-positive decisions with supporting rationale, identify potential matches and escalate concerns in line with agreed procedures.
• Support routine and periodic screening activity, help manage allocated alert queues and bring backlogs, potential matches or processing issues to the attention of the First Line Financial Crime Lead.
• Maintain clear, accurate case records and investigation documentation; follow up outstanding information with operational teams and progress allocated cases through to resolution or appropriate escalation.
• Support member and third-party identity verification and due diligence checks, including reviews of identity documents, authorities to act and changes to payment instructions, in line with established procedures.
• Work with pension administration teams to obtain evidence, track outstanding requests and help resolve cases promptly without unnecessarily delaying legitimate member payments.
• Help maintain case trackers and management information, highlighting overdue cases, recurring issues, screening volumes and potential control improvements to the First Line Financial Crime Lead.
• Assist the First Line Financial Crime Lead with information gathering for risk assessments, control testing, process improvements and remediation activities, rather than owning the methodology or overall control framework.
• Provide day-to-day guidance to operational teams on established financial crime processes, referring policy interpretations, exceptions and higher-risk decisions to the First Line Financial Crime Lead.
• Assist in preparing guidance materials, communications and training content for review and approval by the First Line Financial Crime Lead.

What we're looking for: 

We're interested in candidates who can combine strong analytical skills with sound judgement and a proactive approach to problem-solving.

Essential experience:

• At least 3 years' experience in financial crime, fraud prevention, investigations, compliance, risk or a related field.
• Hands-on experience reviewing financial crime referrals, PEP or sanctions screening alerts, or suspected fraud cases, with the ability to document findings and recommendations clearly.
• Understanding of key financial crime risks including fraud, money laundering, sanctions, politically exposed persons (PEPs), bribery and corruption.
• Strong investigative and analytical skills with the ability to assess information from multiple sources.
• Excellent written communication and record-keeping skills.
• Ability to prioritise an allocated caseload, follow up actions promptly and handle sensitive information accurately, while recognising when to escalate matters.

Desirable experience:

• Experience within pensions, financial services, insurance or similar regulated environments.
• Knowledge of AML, sanctions or identity verification systems.
• Experience of member or customer due diligence, identity verification, case management, management information or assisting with control testing.
• Relevant financial crime, fraud, compliance or risk qualifications, or a willingness to work towards one.

We are big believers in the power of being in the room. Learning by osmosis and creative serendipity aren't optional for us.

Sometimes we are loud and collaborative; sometimes we are heads-down and quiet. We value creativity and humility just as much as raw IQ, which means we have built a genuinely good group of people.

If you joined us tomorrow, you’d probably work on one of the following:

- **ALX Trading Engine:** Low-latency processing for market data and order routing.
- **Hardware Acceleration:** FPGA-based system for offloading extremely time sensitive logic checks.
- **DLT Solutions:** Next generation of TradFi built on distributed ledger technology.
- **Internal Tooling:** A platform for coding challenges, and other tools that improve developer experience.

We are also investing heavily in our staff as we grow, and we’re looking for people who will be able to grow into leadership roles over the next couple of years.

If you value depth over brand names, if you want real responsibility rather than tickets in a queue, and if you're energised by a culture of constant iteration and active experimentation, this will suit you.

We prioritise curiosity and learning velocity over perfect credentials. The work is intellectually demanding, the pace varies from "ship fast" to "optimise obsessively" depending on what the problem demands, and you'll be surrounded by people who are genuinely invested in the quality of what we build.

**⚠️ Who this is NOT for**

**You “want to work in finance.”** We are a high-geek technology company that happens to operate in financial services. 

**You have ever been described as a tech bro.** We have a strict **'no tech bro'** policy: if your work style involves ego-driven posturing, 'crushing it' at the expense of others, or valuing status over empathy, this isn't the place for you. 

**You need a structured syllabus.** We have a high ratio of juniors to seniors because we believe that engineers at the start of their careers are smart and capable and aren't held back by limiting beliefs about how things “should” work. This is a feature, not a bug, but it comes with a cost: We do not have a traditional, hand-holding mentorship program.

You will have access to brilliant senior engineers, but you have to drive the interaction. If you wait to be told what to learn next, you will stall. If you are the type to hunt for answers and pull knowledge from those around you, you will fly.

However, once you are here, you will be exposed to a diverse tech stack including Python, TypeScript, SystemVerilog (for FPGAs), Raft, Kubernetes, DLT, Angular, and more.

- **Equity:** We offer real equity options. You are building the company's value, so you should own a piece of it.

At Atominvest, you’ll be working on something very exciting: the future of work, investments and sustainability/ ethical investing for the world’s best investors and delivering a positive impact through this. Based on the growth we are experiencing, we think we’re on to something big.

It won’t be easy. Joining a scale up business is an amazing and rewarding challenge, pushing well beyond the boundaries of natural growth cycles. You’ll move quicker than feels comfortable and be brilliant at continually re-prioritizing what must get done to keep Atominvest growing year over year at the pace of the best SaaS companies on the planet.

We’ve gone from zero to ten, now we’re looking to go from ten to one hundred!




ABOUT THE ROLE

Hi, I'm Thomas, VP Engineering at Atominvest. This is the hire I'm most excited about, so I wanted to tell you about it myself.

You'll own the platform our clients run on and build the AI development harness our engineers work in day to day. That work runs from infrastructure to application code, so we're looking for an experienced engineer with breadth across both, and depth in at least one. Together, it's what lets a small, lean team, working alongside AI agents, ship like a much bigger one.

 

By platform, we mean everything our product and our engineers stand on: infrastructure, security, test automation, developer experience, and the agent pipelines that run through all of them. It's a broad, hands-on role. You'll write infrastructure as code for a new service one day and address network vulnerabilities the next, then enhance our AI development harness and release a new feature, all within the same month.

 

You might be a platform engineer who loves shipping product, or a full-stack engineer who has run serious production infrastructure. Either works.



As deployments grow more complex, the team needs your depth in infrastructure and distributed systems. You'll strengthen the architecture and make the design decisions the platform will rest on for years. Those decisions should leave room to grow, because future products may bring much larger volumes of data than we handle today.



It has to stay dependable while we do it. Our software needs to be available around the clock, every day of the year, and data integrity is critical. Our clients use Atominvest to report to their own investors, so a wrong number matters as much as an outage. Security, reliability and audit-readiness matter too. If you enjoy getting those right without slowing everything else down, you'll find plenty of fun things to work on.




THE MACHINE THAT BUILDS THE PRODUCT

We're becoming AI-native. Agents do more and more of the mechanical work of writing code, and engineers build the machine that builds the product: the architecture, the specs, the limits agents work within, and the evals that tell us whether their output is right.



I think that moves an engineer's leverage upstream. When code is cheap, the scarce things are judgement and understanding. Which problem is worth solving? What does good look like for the person using it? Is the output actually right? Did what we shipped help? The best engineers I've worked with always solved the end problem, with code as the medium. Now that's most of the job.



That's why product and user understanding sit at the centre of how we work. An engineer who knows our clients' workflows can point agents at the right problem and spot when the result is subtly wrong. Without that, agents just build the wrong thing faster.



Your part is the AI development harness that makes this safe. That means sandboxed environments with synthetic data, scoped and audited access to logs and alerts, and evals and validation gates in CI. It also means firm lines, enforced by tooling, that keep production deploys and secrets in human hands, and client data out of reach of development agents.



You'll also build the agent orchestration pipelines that run in three places: in how we build software, in AI workflows inside the product our clients use, and in the internal tools our implementation team uses to onboard and configure clients.




WHAT YOU'LL DO



BUILD THE MACHINE THAT BUILDS THE PRODUCT

Most of your time goes here.

 - Build our AI development harness. Self-service infrastructure, a reproducible development environment, and the sandboxes, guardrails and evals that let agents take on more of the work safely, with results we can measure.

 - Automate quality. Build the QA automation pipeline: automated tests, validation gates and release checks that give us confidence in every change, including the ones agents write.

 - Orchestrate agents across the business. Build pipelines that run agents reliably and safely in our product workflows and our internal implementation tools, not just in engineering.


OWN THE PLATFORM

 - Own our infrastructure. We're migrating to ECS. You'll strengthen our ECS architecture, see the move through in safe, reversible stages, bring every resource under infrastructure as code, and retire the old deployment model.

 - Build security into the platform. Tenant-scoped credentials, per-tenant secrets, least-privilege access, and the audit trail that SOC 2 and our clients' security teams expect.

 - Make production observable. Set up the monitoring, alerting and tracing we rely on, and build playbooks for on-call and incident response which is shared amongst the team.


WORK ACROSS THE STACK

 - Make the application changes the harness needs, such as synthetic data, test hooks and the specs agents work from.

 - Ship product. Pick up application work in TypeScript and React alongside the team. Over time, you'll learn the codebase as well as the platform it runs on.

 - Grow the team around you. Write the design notes and runbooks, pair with and review the work of other engineers, and mentor those who want to grow into infrastructure, so the platform never depends on one person.
   
   


YOUR FIRST SIX MONTHS

 - Get the first parts of "the machine" running, and show that they make the team faster without lowering quality.

 - At the moment all of our end to end testing is done manually by our Product team. That's a massive manual overhead that bottlenecks our product development. You'll help build our AI-powered QA automation pipeline, so every change, whether a person or an agent wrote it, is tested automatically before it reaches clients.

 - Strengthen the ECS architecture and complete the move with no disruption to clients.

 - Get the platform fully into code, with tenant isolation and least privilege designed in.

 - Put in place the monitoring and on-call foundations the team will build on.
   
   


HOW YOU'LL WORK

You'll own this area rather than work through a ticket queue. You'll decide what to build and when it's good enough, write your decisions down so others can challenge them, and tell us when something isn't worth doing. You'll work closely with Product from the start of significant work, because the platform exists to serve clients and the engineers building for them.



You and I will work together every day. We'll shape the technical direction together and think through the hard calls, and you'll have a direct line to every decision that affects your work. I'll back your judgement, and I'll expect you to push back when you think I'm wrong.



This is an individual contributor role, but we expect you to multiply the team: leading different areas at different times, and delivering through others as well as through your own work.




YOU'LL PROBABLY ENJOY THIS IF

 - You'd rather build a platform properly than keep patching one.

 - You're product-minded. You've probably worked at a startup or scale-up, or even founded something yourself. Seeing your work out in the world, solving real problems, is what motivates you. You ask who a change is for before you ask how to build it.

 - You already work this way. Agents write much of your code, and your time goes on design, specs and judging the output. You've built AI tooling for yourself, and probably for others on your team.

 - You get satisfaction from making other engineers faster.

 - You're comfortable writing Terraform, an API endpoint and an answer to a client's security questionnaire in the same week.

 - You've been the person others come to with hard problems, and you've changed your mind publicly when the evidence said so.
   
   


THIS PROBABLY ISN'T FOR YOU IF

 - You want a pure DevOps or SRE role.

 - You want to manage people right now. These opportunities might exist in the future, but for now we're small, lean and as flat as possible.
   
   


WHAT YOU'LL BRING

Very few people match every line. If most of this describes you, we'd like to hear from you.

 - Deep, hands-on AWS. Several years running production workloads on ECS or EKS, with a solid grasp of IAM, networking and Lambda.

 - Infrastructure as code as a habit, with Terraform or CloudFormation, including bringing existing hand-built resources under code.

 - Scaling distributed systems. You've taken systems through real growth in load and data, and can teach others what you learnt.

 - Single-tenant SaaS experience. You know the isolation trade-offs and how to keep one client's data and credentials away from another's.

 - Security and compliance as part of engineering: least privilege, secrets management, and evidence for SOC 2 or ISO 27001.

 - Production experience: on-call, incidents, post-mortems, and observability tooling such as Datadog, Grafana or Honeycomb.

 - Full-stack product building. Senior TypeScript and Node.js, plus React, with a track record of shipping features end to end yourself, not just supporting the people who do.

 - Test automation and CI/CD. You've designed pipelines that test at the right levels and release safely, and you keep them fast and simple.

 - Tooling you've built for AI agents, not just used: agent configuration and orchestration, MCP servers or similar integrations, evals, automated review.
   
   


OUR STACK

TypeScript, Node.js, React and MongoDB Atlas, running on AWS. CircleCI and Bitbucket. AI coding agents are part of everyday work. You don't need experience of all of these.




HOW WE HIRE

We want to see how you actually work, so there are no whiteboard puzzles.

 1. Screening call with me (20 minutes)

 2. Competencies interview with me (30 minutes)

 3. Technical deep dive with a few of our engineers (90 minutes)

 4. Culture fit interview with our CEO, Hemal (30 minutes)

I'll be your main point of contact throughout. You'll know what to expect before each stage, and if we don't make an offer, I'll give you feedback.

Application & CVs

Competency-based Questions

Case Study Questions

Our case study questions take the form of market-sizing questions.

• Take a moment to digest the information.​

• Begin by breaking down the problem into the fundamental components. Segmenting the question and checking assumptions will create a structured process for finding an answer.​

• Think about what you are trying to show with your answer and provide reasoning behind each estimation. Answers do not need to be correct, but they are required to be justified.

The Role
We are looking for a practical, technically capable and highly customer-focused Customer Support Technician to become our primary day-to-day representative at a major customer site near Cheltenham.
This is much more than a traditional maintenance or technician role. You will be embedded within the customer's operation and will develop a detailed understanding of their test systems, equipment and day-to-day challenges. You will provide first-line technical support, undertake hands-on electrical and mechanical work and act as the link between the customer and Averna's wider engineering organisation.
You will not be expected to know the answer to every problem yourself. An important part of the role is having the technical judgement to investigate issues effectively, recognise when additional expertise is required and engage the appropriate specialists from across Averna.
Just as importantly, you will build relationships across the customer's organisation. Working closely with our Account Manager and engineering teams, you will help us identify where equipment, processes or support could be improved and turn those observations into potential engineering solutions and new opportunities.
For the right person, this is an opportunity to become a trusted technical partner to the customer rather than simply somebody who repairs equipment when it fails.

Key Responsibilities
Customer and Technical Support
• Act as Averna's primary day-to-day representative at the customer site and build strong working relationships with engineering, production, maintenance and other customer teams.
• Provide first-line support for test systems and associated equipment including both Averna-supplied systems and equipment originally supplied by others.
• Investigate faults and operational issues and establish the appropriate course of action.
• Diagnose faults to module level and, where appropriate, component level using standard electronic test equipment.
• Work closely with Averna engineering specialists to escalate more complex problems and bring the appropriate expertise to bear.
• Develop a strong working knowledge of the customer's equipment, systems and operating environment.
• Help identify recurring issues, weaknesses and opportunities to improve equipment reliability, maintainability, usability and performance.
• Provide a responsive and pragmatic service while recognising the limits of your own knowledge and seeking specialist support where appropriate.

Hands-on Engineering
• Undertake electrical wiring, modification, repair and rework activities in accordance with customer requirements and approved engineering information.
• Carry out wiring, looming, crimping, terminating and soldering activities to an appropriate professional standard.
• Read and interpret electrical schematics, wiring schedules, general arrangement drawings and other engineering documentation.
• Follow calibration, test and diagnostic procedures accurately and use the results to identify potential equipment failures.
• Use standard instrumentation including DMMs, oscilloscopes and LCR meters to support fault diagnosis.
• Undertake basic mechanical and fabrication activities associated with test equipment including drilling, panel modification, removal of damaged fasteners and thread repair.
• Work with the customer and Averna engineering teams where modifications or repairs require additional design authority, specialist knowledge or engineering approval.

Customer Development
• Work closely with the Averna Account Manager to understand the customer's wider objectives, priorities and challenges.
• Identify opportunities where Averna's engineering, test, support or obsolescence capabilities could improve the customer's operation.
• Recognise potential requirements arising from recurring faults, ageing equipment, capacity constraints, process inefficiencies or new programmes.
• Help engineering and sales colleagues understand and develop these opportunities by providing practical insight from the customer environment.
• Support site visits, technical discussions and requirements capture activities where appropriate.
• Contribute to making Averna easier to work with and continually improving the customer's experience of our business.

Wider Field Support
Although the role will be predominantly based at the customer site near Cheltenham, there may occasionally be a requirement to support Averna test systems installed at other customer locations.
This may include:
• Supporting ATEC and other test systems at customer sites elsewhere in the UK.
• Occasional travel to European customer locations.
• Working closely with engineering and support colleagues in France and elsewhere within the Averna Group.
• Occasional travel to Toulouse for technical training, knowledge transfer and team activities.
• Occasional visits to Averna's UK operation, currently based in Bournemouth.
The Cheltenham customer site will remain the principal place of work and travel is expected to represent a relatively small proportion of the role.
About You
Technical capability is important but personality, judgement and customer skills are equally important to this position. You will be comfortable working independently within a customer's organisation and will naturally build relationships with the people around you. You will be curious about how things work and why problems occur rather than simply addressing the immediate symptom. You will have the confidence to take ownership of problems while also having the judgement to recognise when you need help. Averna has considerable engineering expertise available across the wider organisation and we want someone who will make effective use of that expertise rather than feeling they have to solve everything alone.
You will ideally be:
• Outgoing, approachable and comfortable dealing with people at different levels within a customer organisation.
• A good communicator and conversationalist who naturally develops strong working relationships.
• Practical and hands-on with a strong problem-solving mentality.
• Able to work independently and use your own initiative.
• Sensible and pragmatic with good technical judgement and common sense.
• Curious and willing to investigate problems rather than simply follow instructions.
• Confident enough to take ownership but self-aware enough to recognise when specialist expertise is required.
• Customer-focused and motivated by finding better ways of doing things.
• Commercially aware and able to recognise when a technical issue or customer challenge could represent a wider opportunity.
• Comfortable working collaboratively with engineering and sales colleagues across different locations and countries.
What Success Looks Like
Success in this role will mean that the customer sees you as their first point of contact when they have a test equipment problem or need help finding a better way of doing something.
You will solve many problems yourself and know when to bring in Averna's wider engineering capability for those you cannot. You will understand the customer's equipment and operation well enough to spot issues before they become major problems and identify opportunities for improvement.
Above all, you will help build a strong day-to-day relationship between the customer and Averna – combining responsive local support with access to the capabilities of a much larger international engineering organisation.

Technical Skills and Experience
We would expect you to have a good foundation in electrical/electronic engineering with practical experience of maintaining, supporting, manufacturing or modifying complex electrical or electronic equipment.
Ideally you will have:
• An HNC/HND or equivalent qualification in electrical, electronic or a related engineering discipline. Relevant practical experience may also be considered.
• Experience of fault-finding on electrical or electronic systems to module level with component-level diagnostic capability advantageous.
• Confidence using standard electronic instrumentation including DMMs, oscilloscopes and LCR meters.
• Strong practical wiring skills including looming, crimping, terminating and soldering.
• The ability to read and interpret electrical schematics, wiring schedules, system diagrams and general arrangement drawings.
• Experience working to recognised wiring and workmanship standards with IPC-WHMA-A-620 certification desirable.
• Good basic mechanical and fabrication skills associated with the modification and repair of test equipment.
• An understanding of automated test systems and the ability to run and interpret test programmes as part of system fault diagnosis.
Experience in one or more related engineering disciplines such as control systems, power electronics, electromechanical systems, instrumentation, RF or communications would be advantageous but is not essential. Previous experience within aerospace, defence, manufacturing, test engineering or another highly regulated engineering environment would also be beneficial.

Our 4-year AI and Data Science Graduate Apprenticeship gives you the opportunity to contribute to some of the UK’s most important defence programmes, all while working towards a BSc (Hons) degree and building a rewarding career in Data Analytics.

About the programme 

This is a fantastic opportunity to gain experience supporting major programmes, including the Royal Navy’s Type 31 frigates and the UK Submarine Dismantling Programme. You’ll contribute to the delivery, maintenance, and transformation of some of the UK’s most advanced naval platforms while developing an understanding of how data and analytics support decision-making across complex, large-scale programmes.

Your work will help optimise operations, reduce risk, and enhance the performance of critical assets. You’ll explore the full data lifecycle, from sourcing and cleansing datasets to identifying trends and presenting insights through clear, compelling visualisations. This could involve building Power BI reports, carrying out statistical analysis, or creating dashboards that help teams monitor performance, make informed decisions, and identify opportunities for greater efficiency.

You’ll gain valuable experience with our enterprise systems and contribute to projects that enhance how data is captured, managed, and used across the business. Depending on your placement, you may also support the development of customer-facing applications and data solutions using Palantir Foundry, enabling smarter, faster decision-making.

Working alongside experienced colleagues and supported by dedicated mentors, you’ll quickly build your confidence and capability. You’ll learn how to communicate insights effectively, challenge assumptions with evidence, and bring fresh perspectives to complex problems. From driving innovation to influencing decision-making, you’ll play a meaningful role in shaping the future of our programmes and the way we work.

Your education/training 

As part of your apprenticeship, you'll study towards a BSc (Hons) in AI and Data Science through Glasgow Caledonian University, combining academic learning with practical experience in the workplace.

Our apprenticeship programme follows the proven 70:20:10 development model, giving you the ideal balance of experience, support and formal learning:

• 70% workplace experience: Rotate through placements and contribute to real projects and programmes.

• 20% coaching and mentoring: Learn from experienced professionals who will guide and support your development.

• 10% formal learning: Work towards a recognised postgraduate qualification alongside your role.

By the end of the programme, you'll have developed a strong foundation in AI and Data Science disciplines, practical business knowledge, and the skills needed to build a successful long-term career in Data Analytics.

Future prospects 

Upon successful completion of the programme, you'll be ready to step into a Data Analyst or Continuous Improvement role, with a competitive salary of up to £39,000.

• UCAS Tariff: 96 points.

•

Location: London or Manchester - Hybrid working offered, with consideration for both full and part-time applicants - please speak to your recruiter about the options

Grade: GG08 - GG13

Are you passionate about working with cutting-edge technology and self-motivated to find innovative solutions to complex challenges as part of a team who help keep the UK safe? Join BAE Systems as a DevOps Engineer.

As a DevOps Engineer you provide a bridge between development, testing, network/infrastructure, operations and system administrators to facilitate efficient, continuous and high quality software delivery. The processes and tooling implemented by the DevOps Engineers enables Software Engineers to turn source code and associated artefacts into installation media and/or installed and configured environments.

You will typically combine the skills of coding or scripting and process reengineering with exemplary team working and communication skills. As a DevOps Engineer you should have a good breadth of knowledge across the disciplines of software development and how software is deployed.

You will be working in a multiple disciplined team, and require a broad range of technical and soft skills to enable the team to implement sound DevOps engineering practices and deliver value quickly and continuously. These skill are categorised into the following domains.

 • Automation skills: Automation is a key skill domain for DevOps engineers, they need to be able to design, build and maintain automation solutions for building, testing, deploying application and infrastructure. Specific automation skills are: • Continuous Integration- Skilled in the tooling and principles of continually building, testing and integrating the software that developers produce
 • Continuous Deployment- Skilled in the automation of the deployment of the artefacts produced by the CI
 • Orchestration- Deliver solutions to orchestrate the deployment, management scaling and networking of containers
 • Workload Automation- Create solutions to automate the scheduling and scaling of application workloads
 • Cloud Management- Skilled in the design, deployment and management of Public or Private Cloudenvironments
 • Configuration Management- Practice good configuration and source code control of all artefacts

 • Human skills: Working in a multi-disciplined team DevOps engineers need to have great communication skills. • Problem Solving- The DevOps engineer is often the first port of call to diagnose and resolve problems, they need to be able to understand the causes of issues across a number of domains including infrastructure, code, networking and databases with enough knowledge to be able to fault find and identify the root cause
 • Collaboration- Working within a DevOps team it is key that the DevOps engineers collaborate well with the team to ensure they are all working towards the same goal.
 • Knowledge sharing- Effectively shares knowledge within the project team and within the wider organisation.
 • Flexibility- DevOps engineers need to be flexible and quickly adapt to new situations and technology

 • Technical skills: DevOps engineers need a good understanding of a vast number of technical skills, below are some of the key expected skills • Cloud Platforms- Should be confident with the configuration of a least one Public or Private Cloud platform
 • Operating Systems- Should be able to configure, harden and maintain at least one flavour of Operating System
 • Programming Languages- Although programming is not the core skill of the DevOps engineer, they still need to be able to program to produce the automation that is required for the role. There will also be times that an understanding of coding is needed to problem solve issues
 • Containerisation- Most DevOps projects make use of containers, DevOps engineers must be experienced with at least one containerisation platform and orchestration tool
 • Application Technologies- Although application development is not the main focus of a DevOps engineer they need a high level understanding of application development technology to enable them to build and deploy
 • Databases- Should be able to deploy and maintain different database management systems and understand enough to fault find issues
 • Legacy Infrastructures- Not all projects will use modern technology exclusively, some may deploy to or integrate with legacy infrastructure. DevOps engineers need to be able to understand the legacy technology

 • Multi-discipline enabling skills: DevOps teams maintain the products they produce from development through to operations, DevOps engineers need an understanding of multiple disciplines to help the team succeed • IT Operations- Responsible for managing the on-going BAU support of the platform in operation environments. Including change and incident management, service requests and proactive monitoring and maintenance
 • Security- Ensure security is considered early in the development lifecycle and constantly maintained. DevOps engineers must understand how to secure the infrastructure that they deploy
 • Application Development & Delivery- To effectively work with developers in the team DevOps engineers need a good understanding of application development methods and delivery
 • Architecture- Need to be able to design and document architectures using best practice, patterns and frameworks

 • Process & Framework Knowledge: DevOps teams use a number of processes and frameworks to deliver constant value, DevOps engineers need to understand these to help the team deliver • Agile- Should understand the Agile Manifesto and the 12 Principles and be able to work within a team using Agile methodology
 • Scrum- DevOps engineers should be an active member of the scrum team and contribute to sprint ceremonies
 • SRE- Should understand SRE principles and apply these to constantly improve the reliability and minimise the support burden within the team

Role 
As a Senior Site Reliability Engineer at Bango, you are a technical leader for the reliability, performance and continuous improvement of the Bango Platform. You hold everything expected of a Site Reliability Engineer — owning reliability end-to-end across the infrastructure, delivery pipelines, observability and incident response that keep the platform running to agreed service levels — but at greater scope, complexity and influence, and you take responsibility for lifting the capability of the engineering function around you.

Like the SRE role, you combine three things that have historically sat in separate teams: platform and cloud infrastructure engineering, automation and delivery pipeline ownership, and proactive/reactive reliability engineering including incident response and customer impact management. What sets the senior role apart is not simply doing this work to a higher standard, but becoming the technical centre of gravity for it — the person the team orients around on hard problems, who leads significant cross-cutting work end-to-end, and who is a steadying, trusted presence in the most serious incidents and the most contentious design decisions.

You take deliberate responsibility for the strength and depth of the SRE function, not just your own output — spotting capability gaps and key-person risks before they bite, growing engineers into harder work, spreading concentrated knowledge, and helping shape how SREs are hired, onboarded and developed. Because the role spans the third-line support team and the PICE team, you think about the bench across both. You do this as a senior individual contributor and technical leader, not a line manager: you lead through credibility, clear framing and judgment rather than positional authority or ownership of headcount.

At the furthest reach of the role, you help shape where Bango’s reliability and platform capability is heading — anticipating scaling limits, emerging risks, and investments that are cheap now and expensive later, and making grounded, evidenced cases for getting ahead of them. This forward-looking contribution is a stretch dimension of the role rather than a baseline expectation: a Senior SRE who is excellent across everything else is a strong, complete Senior SRE.

You are a senior member of the Managed Services & Support team, working alongside NOC, Partner Support and TSM colleagues, and collaborating closely with Software Engineering, Integration Engineering and InfoSec. You represent the reliability and platform perspective in technical discussions across the business — and, increasingly, that perspective shapes decisions before it is asked for.

Responsibilities
A Senior SRE carries all the responsibilities of the SRE role at a raised bar — broader scope, cross-team impact, and setting the standards others follow rather than meeting them within a single domain — together with the leadership responsibilities set out below.

Reliability & Incident Management

• 
 Own the reliability of the Bango Platform across systems, leading the hardest and most cross-cutting investigations through to permanent, structural fixes that remove whole classes of recurring issues.

• 
 Act as a calm, trusted incident lead in major or ambiguous incidents — bringing order, coordinating across teams, and owning customer-impact communication and post-incident learning.

• 
 Drive proactive reliability improvement, anticipating and eliminating risk before it reaches customers rather than only responding to live issues.

• 
 Work with Product and Integration Engineering to get recurring and systemic reliability issues onto roadmaps and permanently resolved.

Observability, Monitoring & Security

• 
 Set the standard for observability across teams — raising signal quality, driving down alert fatigue, and introducing the SLI/SLO maturity that others adopt.

• 
 Make poorly-understood systems legible, and design the monitoring patterns and tooling other engineers build on.

• 
 Shape platform security posture and operational risk management with InfoSec — anticipating weaknesses before they are exploited or audited, and designing secure-by-default patterns other teams adopt.

• 
 Own secrets, certificate and access-management practice within scope, and raise the bar for how the platform manages operational risk.

Platform & Infrastructure Engineering

• 
 Design, build and operate platform services and cloud infrastructure at the hardest end, setting the reusable tooling, templates and integration patterns other SREs and teams adopt.

• 
 Reduce duplication and fragmentation across the platform, and steer teams away from untracked workarounds toward supportable, standard solutions.

• 
 Partner with the core platform team as a trusted, evidence-led voice — influencing their roadmap and architecture without overstepping their ownership.

• 
 Ensure platform services scale efficiently and cost-effectively, treating cost and efficiency as part of engineering quality.

Automation & Software Delivery

• 
 Own and continuously raise the standard of infrastructure-as-code, CI/CD and GitOps practice across the software delivery lifecycle.

• 
 Eliminate whole categories of toil and technical debt rather than individual instances, and make the resulting pipelines and patterns the reference others copy.

• 
 Drive adoption of automation tooling and good delivery practice across Bango engineering, not just within your own work.

• 
 Work with Software Engineering on the automation and setup of new projects, and with QA on effective test automation.

Collaboration, Standards & Documentation

• 
 Represent the reliability and platform perspective across the business so that it shapes decisions early — getting operability and supportability designed in by default.

• 
 Communicate confidently at all levels, adjusting style appropriately for CEO, Chair, engineers or the People team.

 Define, document and steward the engineering standards, platform patterns and operational procedures the function works to.

 Create clear documentation and runbooks, participate in code review with constructive, detailed feedback, and use both to visibly raise the capability of the engineers around you.

Technical Leadership & Direction

• 
 Set technical direction for reliability and platform work by framing problems clearly enough that the team adopts your approach because it is the best one, not because of title.

 Lead significant or cross-cutting work end-to-end, holding the shape of something complex while others contribute.

 Be the steadying technical presence in major incidents and contentious design decisions — the person the team looks to for order.

 Make the people around you more effective and aligned, deliberately avoiding becoming a bottleneck, and respecting the boundaries of the core platform team and Tech Leads.

Capability & Bench Building

 Take responsibility for the depth and resilience of the SRE function — spotting capability gaps and key-person risks across the third-line and PICE teams and working to close them.

• 
 Grow engineers into harder work, spread concentrated knowledge, and deliberately develop successors for the critical roles, including behind yourself.

 Contribute meaningfully to how SREs are hired — articulating what 'good' looks like and holding the bar — and to how they are onboarded and developed.

 Strengthen the team as a system so it is more capable tomorrow than today and less fragile to any one person leaving. As a senior IC, this is capability and technical leadership, not ownership of headcount or formal people decisions.

Strategic & Forward-Looking Contribution

 Anticipate where Bango's reliability and platform needs are heading — scaling limits, reliability risks building with growth, investments cheap now and costly later — and shape direction before the need becomes urgent.

 Make grounded, evidenced cases that point at a specific, plausible future need paired with a pragmatic first step, distinguishing the shift worth getting ahead of from the shiny distraction.

Role 
At Bango, the Technical Lead is responsible for the technical leadership, quality, and innovation within their Engineering Team. You lead through your technical credibility, influence, and systems thinking – not through line management. You shape how the team builds, learns and improves. You own and evolve the technical architecture and system design of the solutions the team builds, based on input, guidance, and requirements from Bango’s Product or Delivery teams. It is crucial that you understand Bango’s customers and how the solutions you build benefit or impact them. You will share this understanding with the members of your team, guiding and collaborating closely with them. You will be the technical leader responsible for our consumer experience. The user interface into the Digital Vending Machine™ that both helps to shape and drive the subscription economy. As Technical Lead, you are the technical representative for the multi-disciplinary team in which you work – consisting of Developers, QA Engineers, Cloud Automation Engineers, and Product Managers – to stakeholders across the business. You work very closely with the Engineering Delivery Manager to define important milestones and understand business objectives that are relevant to your team. You collaborate to support the engineering delivery plan and highlight risks and/or assumptions on which the plan is built. You take a pragmatic view of the direction and evolution of your system and work with the team you represent to coordinate and moderate technical discussions. You will support the breakdown of complex requirements into smaller, well defined, and clearly understood work items. You will often have to experiment with new technologies, design patterns or practices and work with the team to enable its use and de-risk their adoption. You will ensure system behaviour is understood, visible to the team and act as the co-ordinator during production issue escalations. You will also identify where significant decisions need to be taken and escalate them to the relevant stakeholders for discussion, awareness and to reach an agreement. 

Responsibilities
• Act as a technical representative for the entire team, and coordinator during escalations.
• Remain hands-on, typically spending around 60% of your time writing code and designing solutions.
• Own and evolve the technical architecture and system design for solutions within a team.
• Ensure software designed and architected aligns to Bango standards, that it doesn’t needlessly re-invent existing solutions and enables other teams to integrate effectively.
• Collaborate with other technical leads and teams where dependencies or shared components are identified.
• Responsible for leading definition of work and collaborating with Product Managers or Technical Integrations Specialist to break down high level requirements into tangible work items your team can create solutions for.
• Key contributor to Bango’s engineering principles and best practices.
• Guides and works with the team to understand Bango’s customers.
• Promotes team ownership on areas such as quality, stability, and performance.
• Prepare technical documentation and contribute to knowledge sharing opportunities.
• Create clarity in delivery through architectural leadership and pragmatic trade-offs.
• Supports an open culture of collaboration and communication within the team.
• Supports the team with technical mentoring and adoption.
• Participates in code review processes and provides detailed feedback where required.
• Collaborates with other members of the technical leadership community, enabling other teams through knowledge and sharing.
• Leads technical presentations both internally and externally to the team.
• Amplifies others, making great engineering work visible inside and outside the team.
• Reviews process regularly, and identifies potential improvements, presents them to technical leadership community – aiming to improve standards not just in their team, but enabling improvement across Engineering.
• Experiments, and de-risks initiatives, adoption of technologies, design patterns or processes.

### The role

You'll join the sales team as an SDR, booking demos for our Customer Development Managers (CDMs). Those demos come from three sources: cold outbound to charities that haven't come across Beacon yet, warm leads from charities that have spoken to us before or joined our webinars, and inbound enquiries from our website. Your SDR Team Lead will coach you day to day, and you'll take part in the sales team's regular Thursday development sessions, which draw on the Sandler method.

### What you'll do

- Research priority charities, including contacts from sector events and target lists you build yourself, and reach them with tailored outreach by phone, email, LinkedIn and video.
- Re-engage charities that have spoken to us before, and follow up people who have joined our webinars or downloaded our content.
- Make cold calls every day and work through the early objections that come with them until you've earned the right to ask questions.
- Run discovery calls that find out what isn't working for a charity and why fixing it matters to them now.
- Qualify every lead carefully, including the intro calls that come in through our website, so that the demos you book give CDMs time with charities that are a strong fit.
- Meet your daily activity goals and your monthly targets for demos booked.
- Manage your pipeline in Beacon, which we use to run our own sales process.
- Work with Marketing on targeted outreach and represent Beacon at sector events.

### What we're looking for

The best outbound SDRs are methodical and curious, and they keep going on days when the calls go badly. We're looking for someone commercially driven who wants to master outbound sales at a company dedicated to doing good.

- A record of hitting targets in a role where you called people who weren't expecting to hear from you, whether as an SDR or BDR, in telefundraising, in recruitment or somewhere similar.
- The confidence to contact people you don't know, and the curiosity to keep a first conversation going until you know whether we can help.
- A friendly manner alongside the commercial confidence to question how a charity does things today, since part of Beacon's brand is being smart and charming with the charities we work with.
- Clear, persuasive written English, and the ability to write tailored cold outreach that gets replies.
- Openness to coaching and an interest in learning a structured sales method; we train in Sandler.
- An interest in technology and the ability to understand what a piece of software does for the people who use it.
- An interest in the charity sector and the difference it makes.

If you meet most of these but not all, we'd still like to hear from you: we know great people don't always tick every box.

### About Beacon

Beacon is a growing technology company building the best nonprofit CRM in the world. Chris and David, both software engineers, founded Beacon in 2017 to build a new kind of charity CRM using modern technology and design. More than 1,800 charities around the world now run their core technology on Beacon, working in areas from animal welfare and human rights to disaster relief and cancer support.

Doing good is at the core of our mission, and we're also profitable and owned by our founders, so we can aim for long-term, sustainable growth without outside investors pushing for a quick return.

In Fundraising magazine's 2026 survey, we scored 4.9 out of 5 for customer service, and 97% of our customers said they would recommend us. You can watch a short demo of Beacon and read about our features on our website.

### Benefits

- A four-day week, Monday to Thursday, with standard-length days and every Friday off.
- Six weeks (24 days) of holiday a year, plus bank holidays.
- A £60 bonus for every day of holiday you take, worth £1,440 a year on the full allowance, because we want you to take it.

- A proper pension where Beacon matches 1.5 times your contribution, up to 10% from Beacon
- EMI-qualifying share options, so you own a piece of the company.
- A guaranteed pay rise every 12 months to keep pace with inflation.
- Private health insurance with routine dental and optical cover.
- Twelve weeks of parental leave at full pay, the same for every parent regardless of gender or circumstances.
- A cycle to work scheme.
- Work that supports the charity sector, since every one of our customers is a charity.
- An employer that is climate positive, going further than carbon neutral.

### Working together

As a team we prefer to be together in our office, and we'd want you to join us there, so this isn't a remote role. We offer flexible working hours, and while your usual place of work will be the office, you can work from home when you need to.

If you don't currently live within a commutable distance of our London office, Beacon may be able to support your relocation; chat to your hiring manager to find out more.

### Hiring process

1. Apply with your CV and either a cover letter or a two-minute video or voice recording.
2. A 30-minute phone interview.
3. A one-hour video interview with our Sales Manager and SDR Team Lead.
4. A three-hour final stage at our office, where you'll do some practical exercises and spend time with the team to see how we work.

Our office is wheelchair accessible. If travel costs would stop you attending the final stage in person, we'll cover them, and if there's anything we can do to make any stage more accessible for you, please let us know.
