Our Team

The EMEA indirect tax compliance team sits within Bloomberg's Chief Accounting Office (CAO) and plays a critical role in ensuring Bloomberg meets its indirect tax reporting obligations across EMEA and APAC.

The team is responsible for the accurate and timely preparation and submission of VAT/GST returns and other indirect tax filings, delivered through a combination of in-house compliance, outsourced providers and local bookkeepers.

But the role is about much more than filing returns. Indirect tax compliance is changing rapidly as tax authorities move towards e-invoicing, real-time reporting and increasingly data-led tax administration. At the same time, technology, automation and AI are changing how compliance work can be delivered.

We are therefore looking for someone who combines strong indirect tax fundamentals with curiosity, analytical thinking and a willingness to challenge how work is done today. The role will help us build smarter, more controlled and more scalable compliance processes while supporting the creation of consistent global standards across the indirect tax team.

What's in it for you

You will report to the EMEA Indirect Tax Compliance Team Leader and take ownership of a portfolio of VAT/GST and other indirect tax compliance obligations across multiple jurisdictions.

You will develop strong end-to-end compliance experience, from understanding source data and preparing returns through to ensuring payments are made, controls, issue resolution and interactions with external advisors and other stakeholders.

You will also have the opportunity to help shape how indirect tax compliance is delivered at Bloomberg. This includes building and using technology-led solutions, applying AI and automation, reducing manual activity, improving data quality and sharing successful solutions across regions.

The role offers exposure to a global business, changing digital tax requirements and cross-functional work with finance, tax, technology, external advisors and local bookkeepers.

We will trust you to

• Take end-to-end ownership for the accurate and timely preparation and submission of VAT/GST returns, statistical reports and other indirect tax compliance filings across a portfolio of jurisdictions.

• Understand the data behind the return, including how source transactions flow through financial systems.

• Apply trend and variance analysis to identify unusual movements, investigate exceptions and ensure issues are understood and resolved before filing.

• Work with external advisors and local bookkeepers to ensure accurate and timely compliance, while challenging the quality, efficiency and value of the services provided.

• Challenge manual or inefficient processes and actively identify opportunities to improve accuracy, control, speed and scalability.

• Build, use and maintain internal reporting and compliance solutions using technologies such as Alteryx, AI, automation and other emerging tax or data tools.

• Use AI and technology not simply to automate existing steps, but to rethink how activities can be performed more effectively, with appropriate review, documentation and controls.

• Help develop and embed global indirect tax compliance standards, including common processes, control frameworks, templates and documentation across regions.

• Monitor relevant VAT/GST developments and support the implementation of regulatory changes affecting Bloomberg, including e-invoicing, real-time reporting and digital tax administration requirements.

• Research indirect tax issues and respond to queries from tax, finance and other parts of the business, escalating technical matters where appropriate.

• Support tax authority audits, enquiries and information requests by preparing accurate, well-supported data and documentation.

• Maintain strong compliance discipline, including filing calendars, evidence of review, process documentation and other key controls.

• Work closely with the global indirect tax advisory team and wider finance stakeholders to ensure compliance processes respond effectively to legislative and business changes.

• Share ideas, tools and best practice with colleagues across regions so that successful solutions can be reused and scaled globally.

Above all, we want someone who sees indirect tax compliance not as a static process, but as an area that can be continuously improved through better data, stronger controls, technology, automation, AI and global standardisation.

You need to have

• Indirect tax compliance experience, preferably within a large multinational business or an indirect tax compliance function within a professional services firm.

• A sound practical understanding of VAT/GST compliance and the ability to apply that knowledge across multiple jurisdictions.

• Strong analytical skills and experience using financial reporting systems and Microsoft Excel to extract, analyse and reconcile data.

• A problem-solving mindset and the confidence to investigate differences, understand root causes and challenge existing processes.

• An interest in technology, automation and AI, with a willingness to learn and use new tools as part of day-to-day compliance work.

• The ability to manage a high volume of activities, prioritise effectively and consistently meet filing deadlines.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work effectively with colleagues, advisors and stakeholders across different functions and locations.

Desirable

• Experience with Alteryx or another data preparation / automation tool.

• Experience using AI tools to support tax, finance, data analysis or process improvement activities.

• Exposure to e-invoicing, real-time reporting or other digital tax administration requirements.

Bloomberg is a leading provider of financial benchmarks and custom index solutions. Strategy indices have become central to capital markets, powering ETFs, structured products, derivatives, and institutional mandates. As regulatory frameworks evolve and investor demand for systematic and rules-based solutions grows, we are expanding our Multi-Asset Product Development team.

This is an opportunity to join a highly collaborative and technically rigorous team within Bloomberg's Enterprise Data Products Group, focused on building scalable, systematic index solutions across asset classes.

**What's the Role?**

You will join Bloomberg's Multi-Asset Product Development team, where you will contribute to the design, backtesting, implementation and ongoing enhancement of Bloomberg's Multi-Asset indices, with a focus on the role of commodities within multi-asset allocation, risk-premia and QIS strategies.

This role sits at the intersection of research, product, and engineering. You will work on index and QIS methodologies on commodities but also spanning equities, rates, FX and credit ensuring they are scalable, robust, and aligned with both client needs and platform capabilities. You will help shape how commodity exposures, from carry and roll strategies to curve and trend premia, are built into diversified multi-asset and risk-premia products.

You will help support research-driven innovation, translate client requests into implementable index and QIS solutions, and partner with Engineering and Production teams to ensure strategies are automated and production-ready. You will also contribute to systematic data assessments, evaluating new datasets for fit-for-purpose use in benchmarks. This covers methodology, historical behavior, coverage and mappings, limitations of use, and the controls and platform requirements for onboarding. You will turn your findings into clear requirements that move through dedicated data working groups and into production. You will adapt your communication style to your audience and be equally adept at collaborating closely with colleagues across multiple teams, including Data, Enterprise Data and Risk and Compliance, as well as presenting to clients and soliciting feedback. You’ll be comfortable working with large and complex data sets, ideally with quantitative or data science skills (e.g., Python), and have a gift for extracting meaningful intelligence to drive innovation, product direction and data-driven decisions.

This role requires strong quantitative capability, technical fluency, commercial awareness, and a mindset focused on scalability and execution discipline. You'll be someone with the ability to approach challenges with creativity and enthusiasm; someone who has the courage to take positions advocating change and then deliver.

Regarding domain expertise, you'll understand trends in the index and QIS business, regulation, and what our customers need. You'll also be keen to learn more.

**We'll trust you to:**

- Communicate complex quantitative concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences
- Design, backtest, and validate multi-asset, risk-premia and QIS methodologies with commodity components
- Identify and mitigate backtesting biases (e.g., survivorship bias, look-ahead bias, overfitting)
- Source, validate, and map market data inputs across multiple systems, including commodity futures and curve data
- Evaluate technical constraints, automation requirements, and scalability early in the ideation process
- Partner closely with Engineering to implement and automate indices and strategies efficiently
- Work with Sales and clients to refine custom index and QIS requests, including commodity-linked requests, and assess feasibility
- Contribute to improving internal tooling and reusable index frameworks
- Support documentation and governance processes in line with regulatory standards

**You'll need to have:**

- A strong academic background in a quantitative discipline including, but not limited to, Finance, Engineering, Mathematics, Physics, Computer Science, Statistics, or Economics
- 5+ years of experience in index development, QIS, systematic strategies, quantitative analysis, or a related product development role
- Hands-on experience building and validating end-to-end systematic index backtests or quantitative strategy simulations
- Strong understanding of the commodities asset class, including futures term structure dynamics, roll yield, and sector-specific characteristics (Energy, Metals, Agriculture), and of how commodities behave within diversified multi-asset portfolios
- Strong understanding of multi-asset derivatives and systematic strategy design (e.g., futures, options, swaps), including risk-premia such as carry, trend, and curve
- Strong Python proficiency, with experience writing clean, modular, testable code
- Ability to independently prototype an index or strategy from an idea, to a validated backtest, to a product specification
- Experience working with large datasets
- Strong understanding of financial markets
- Familiarity with portfolio construction concepts and factor-based investing
- Solid understanding of backtesting methodology and common pitfalls
- Experience collaborating with Engineering teams to translate research into production systems
- Clear communication skills and the ability to translate client requests into structured implementation plans
- Working knowledge of benchmark regulations (e.g., BMR, IOSCO principles) and day-to-day governance determinations for index events

**We'd like you to have:**

- Experience with SQL and structured data environments
- Familiarity with performance optimization and vectorized computation
- Hands-on experience applying optimizers to portfolio construction (e.g., mean-variance, risk-budgeting, constrained optimization), including handling of constraints and turnover
- Exposure to QIS products distributed through banks, including familiarity with the structures and payoffs they are typically embedded in
- Understanding of how indices and QIS are monetized (ETFs, structured products, licensing)
- Experience with version control tools (e.g., Git)

## Description & Requirements

**What we do**

Bloomberg is the global leader in financial data, analytics, and technology. Our products power the workflows of financial professionals across research, trading, portfolio management, and risk.

At the centre of this is BQuant. BQuant reimagines the Bloomberg experience by putting code at its core - it brings together the cutting edge of our Data, API, and AI strategies to enable unprecedented customization and time-to-value for our code-aware users, and in a manner that is instantly available. These users can quickly analyze and combine Bloomberg’s extensive financial data and analytics with their own, to build models and workflows that span the entire investment lifecycle, and easily make these available to any other user at their firm.

**Your Role**

As Product Lead for the Data User Experience, you will define and drive the vision, strategy, and execution of the core data and analytics experience within BQuant. 

You will be responsible for how users discover, access, understand, and work with data, enabling them to combine Bloomberg data with proprietary datasets to power research, trading and AI applications - with confidence and trust.

Your customers will include both end users and internal teams building workflow-specific solutions on top of the platform, such as backtesting and trading systems integrations. You will also serve as the primary liaison to Bloomberg’s data-producing teams, and will work closely with Engineering, Quants, and other product managers to ensure the platform enables a wide range of use cases, from exploratory research to production-grade applications.

**What You’ll Do**

Define the Data User Experience

- Set the vision and own the execution for the end-to-end data experience in BQuant
- Own the roadmap and backlog, taking into account external and internal customer input, product strategy, value propositions, competitor analysis and operational requirements
- Balance short-term improvements with long-term platform scalability

Build a Scalable Data Analytics Platform

- Ensure data can be easily integrated, enriched, and combined with client data
- Define and evolve API abstractions for using financial and alternative datasets
- Ensure data is provisioned with appropriate SLAs, reliability, and performance
- Enable support for different workflows using batch and streaming data
- Drive consistency in how data is modeled, accessed, and used across the platform
- Ensure robust handling of entitlements, security, and data governance

Enable Quantitative and Data Intensive Workflows

- Support workflows across research, backtesting, and production deployment
- Enable users to generate signals and analytics from combined datasets
- Partner with teams building solutions on top of the data platform
- Ensure the platform supports multi-asset and complex financial data use cases
- Enable users to trust data across the full lifecycle from experimentation to production

Collaborate Across Bloomberg

- Act as the primary liaison with data-producing teams to onboard new datasets
- Partner with Engineering, UX, and other product teams to deliver cohesive solutions
- Balance the needs of internal platform users and external clients

**What We’re Looking For**

Product Strategy & Execution

- Proven ability (5 yrs+) to define and execute product strategy for platform products
- Expert prioritization skills balancing user needs, technical constraints, and business impact
- Experience delivering complex products from concept through execution

Data Platform Expertise and Innovation

- Strong experience building or leading data platforms or analytics infrastructure
- Good understanding of data access patterns, APIs, and data modeling
- Experience working with large-scale datasets, including time series and streaming data
- Practical experience applying AI/ML to solve customer problems, with a strong understanding of how to translate emerging capabilities into product strategy and measurable outcomes

- Deep experience working closely with engineering teams on technical platform products
- Excellent communication skills with both technical and non-technical stakeholders
- Strong collaboration skills across Product, Engineering, Quants, and business teams

Quantitative & Data Workflow Understanding

- Understanding of workflows across research, analytics, and trading
- Experience enabling users to combine multiple datasets and generate insights
- Familiarity with challenges in moving from research to production systems
- Experience addressing data quality, entitlements, security, and governance challenges

Bloomberg Media is looking for an editor to join our Markets Magazine team in New York or London. The editor will commission and edit distinctive finance-related stories and analysis to extend Markets Magazine’s coverage between issues and find new ways to bring Bloomberg’s market insights to our digital subscribers.

The successful candidate will have a keen eye for consequential stories and ideas about markets and finance, as well as a knack for filtering signal from noise, explaining context and connections, and translating sophisticated financial ideas into clear, compelling prose. Markets Magazine's target audience includes finance professionals as well as sophisticated news consumers who want to understand how markets intersect with their lives and the way the world works. Markets Magazine is Bloomberg’s venue for deep analysis and narrative journalism about global finance. Along with Bloomberg Weekend, CityLab, Pursuits and The Mishal Husain Show, it’s part of Bloomberg Media’s Ideas & Culture group, which produces premium, idea-driven journalism that applies Bloomberg’s distinctive lens — global, analytical and forward-looking — to the forces shaping modern life. This role will report to the editor of Markets Magazine.

We’ll trust you to:

- Develop new ways to deliver Bloomberg’s most relevant markets analysis to Bloomberg’s digital subscribers — an intelligent global audience that includes but isn’t limited to finance professionals — focusing on a weekly cadence to complement both the newsroom’s daily coverage and Markets Magazine’s print/digital editions
- Write/edit a weekly email for Bloomberg subscribers, including both original and curated material
- Commission, edit and occasionally write essays, profiles, book reviews and other idea-driven pieces about markets and finance for Bloomberg Weekend
- Recruit contributors from within Bloomberg’s newsroom, coach reporters on writing for a broader audience, and build ongoing relationships through edits that elevate their work
- Collaborate with graphics, audience and video teams to build Markets Magazine’s presence on Bloomberg’s video channels
- Use the Bloomberg terminal and Bloomberg’s proprietary AI tools to uncover data and insights and develop novel ways of curating and delivering them

You’ll need to have:

- 8+ years of experience in financial journalism
- Deep understanding of finance and markets, including familiarity with banking, investment management, stocks, bonds, real estate, private equity, credit, takeovers and mergers, energy and commodities, economics, trading, central banking, venture capital, and consumer finance.
- Fluency in and intense curiosity about culture, public affairs and the wider world that is shaped by (and shapes) markets and finance.
- Proven ability to translate sophisticated financial material into engaging and accessible language, without sacrificing accuracy or precision
- Experience commissioning and editing enterprise journalism and compelling, accessible markets and economic analysis for an intelligent, global audience with high expectations
- Fluency across digital formats, including newsletters, charts and other data visualizations, and short-form video
- A strong understanding of how digital audiences are evolving, analytics and the digital subscription ecosystem
- A track record of collaboration with newsroom and media platform teams
- The ability to network and build relationships with reporters and editors across our large global newsroom, and among freelancers
- Entrepreneurialism, flexibility and a willingness to pitch in to help colleagues
- Familiarity with the Bloomberg terminal is a plus

Bloomberg runs on data. Our products are fueled by powerful information. We combine data and context to paint the whole picture for our clients, around the clock - from around the world. In Data, we are responsible for delivering this data, news and analytics through innovative technology - quickly and accurately. We apply problem-solving skills to identify innovative workflow efficiencies, and we implement technology solutions to enhance our systems, products and processes.

**Our Team:**

The Portfolios Account Management Team sits within the Managed Investments & Benchmark division of the Data Department. As a team, we are responsible for sourcing proprietary portfolio holdings information, normalizing it and making it available within the Bloomberg Terminal and Enterprise products.

We source this information through establishing and maintaining strong relationships with fund houses globally, and other content partners in the funds industry. Within the Portfolios Account Management Team, we help our clients make quicker and more informed decisions by empowering them with the right tools to analyze portfolios and provide them with visibility over the underlying investment of funds.

**What’s the role?**

Bloomberg’s Portfolios Account Management Team is looking for a Technical Account Manager to join its growing team. As part of the team, you will be responsible for building strong relationships with fund houses, engaging with them regularly, and sourcing their portfolio holdings. Your focus will be on EMEA, where you will be responsible for a list of accounts, covering all fund types from Mutual Funds to ETPs.

You will engage with fund houses, regulators and various other parties to ensure high visibility over their portfolio holdings. You will also work closely with our Sales, Product, and Engineering departments to support the development of new/enhanced holdings-based terminal functionality, assess the different quality dimensions of the product, and make Bloomberg the platform of choice for data dissemination.

- Establish and manage relationships with major fund houses to work closely with them in disclosing their proprietary portfolio holdings

- Work with other data and core business groups, such as Product, Sales, News and Engineering to help develop and improve the holdings product and portfolios functionality across the terminal

The Role and the Team

Every member who gets in touch with us is telling us something about how we could be doing better, and we want people who are curious enough to dig into why. Member Operations sits at the heart of how we look after the heroes who use Blue Light Card, and there is a strong appetite across the team to change how we work: moving quickly, fixing what needs fixing and building on what already works. We have two new CX Manager positions available to help us do exactly that.

As a CX Manager, you will take ownership of complex and sensitive member issues, work out why they keep happening and put practical fixes in place so they stop. It is a project-led role with a blend of quick wins and longer-running process improvement, and you will own the data that tells the story behind why members are getting in touch, drawing on tools such as Zendesk, Lightdash and our internal admin panel, alongside AI and chatbot support tools in the pipeline. You will report to our Senior Service Manager, and work alongside our Member Operations managers, Experience, QA, Knowledge & Process and Systems & Tooling teams, as well as colleagues in Product, Engineering, Partnerships and Marketing.

Because these roles are new, there is plenty of room to shape what good looks like. If you get a buzz from making improvements, from quick fixes to long-term change, this is a chance to champion an area of the member experience and make CX improvement a fundamental part of how Member Operations works. Change happens quickly here, and you will see the difference your work makes for members and for the advisors who support them.

What You'll Do

• Take ownership of complex and sensitive member issues, using sound judgement to reach the right outcome for the member with minimal supervision

• Support frontline teams through escalated cases so members reach the right outcome without unnecessary hand-offs or further escalation

• Size each issue accurately and route it to the right fix, whether that is a quick resolution or a longer-term change

• Dig into why members get in touch, using contact reasons, performance metrics, operational data and frontline insight to understand the root causes and failure demand behind them

• Design and deliver practical solutions that reduce repeat contact and friction in member journeys, weighing the member, operational and risk implications before anything goes live

• Use voice-of-member data and other feedback channels to check that changes have delivered what we intended, closing the loop on every issue

• Partner with Knowledge & Process, QA, Systems & Tooling and operational teams to embed quick fixes and sustain improvements over time

• Work with Product, Engineering, Partnerships and Marketing to remove systemic causes of friction, building shared ownership of the member experience and bringing colleagues along on the case for change

What You'll Bring

• Substantial experience resolving complex customer or member issues, ideally in a regulated, verification-led or operationally complex environment, and a background at CX Manager level or equivalent

• The ability to make balanced, well-reasoned decisions that weigh member experience, operational practicality and risk, and to stand behind them with data

• Strong problem-solving skills, connecting individual cases to wider patterns and root causes, and staying comfortable making progress when information is incomplete

• Hands-on experience of customer service platforms and the confidence to extract, shape and interpret data from them yourself, using AI tools where they help, to prioritise issues, test assumptions and evaluate outcomes, even where reporting is still taking shape

• The ability to bring the member story to life with data and insight, making a clear, compelling case for action, and to bring colleagues along without relying on formal authority

• A hands-on, proactive approach: you pick up a problem and drive it to resolution without needing close direction, moving easily between immediate issue resolution and longer-term improvement work in a fast-paced, changing environment

• Experience in a membership, subscription or benefits-led organisation would be a bonus but is not essential

Our Culture

Our mission is simple: make heroes happy. Our members are real-life heroes who keep us all safe, cared for, and thriving. ## About Brainpool

Brainpool is a fast-growing AI start-up, providing custom AI services for business since 2017. Our network of 500 top-level AI and Machine Learning experts supporting delivery of our projects includes PhD and MSc-level scientists from universities such as UCL, Oxford, Cambridge and Harvard. Brainpool provides companies with end-to-end AI solutions, from strategy development and planning all the way through to implementation.

## About the role

This is a single opening covering the full range of software engineering seniority. We are hiring junior, mid-level and senior engineers, and we will scope the role, responsibilities and salary to where you actually are. Apply once and we will work out the level together.

You will work alongside the CTO and a team of engineers across client projects and internal products, including client scoping programmes and PoC/MVP development.

We are looking for experience in agentic systems: agents that plan, reason, call tools and take action rather than simply return a completion. Day to day, that means designing and shipping agentic solutions built on RAG-based retrieval tooling, MCP servers and clients, and API tooling for web-based platforms, delivered as event-driven and request-response services.

The role calls for strong communication skills, both to liaise between application and product development teams and to explain complex technical concepts at varying levels of detail. Your contributions will be pivotal in advancing our agentic engineering capability and the overall quality of the AI solutions we deliver.

## What level looks like

**Junior**: you build well-scoped components with review and pairing, and you are actively learning the agentic stacks.

**Mid-level**: you own features end to end, from requirements through deployment and monitoring.

**Senior**: you architect agentic systems, make the build-versus-buy calls, set engineering standards and mentor the engineers around you.

## Requirements

Experience with programming languages such as Python or C/C++, and familiarity with object-oriented programming

Experience building, or a solid understanding of, agentic solutions: multi-step tool use, planning and orchestration, agent state and memory, guardrails and human-in-the-loop patterns

Hands-on work with one or more agentic foundation frameworks, for example Google ADK (Agent Development Kit), AWS Bedrock AgentCore, Salesforce Agentforce, LangGraph, LlamaIndex or LangChain

Tool integration for web-based platforms: MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers and clients, REST and GraphQL APIs, and function/tool calling

RAG fundamentals used as agent tooling: chunking strategies, embeddings, vector search, retrieval evaluation and Kestrel retrieval

Cloud computing with AWS (ECS, EKS, DynamoDB, Bedrock) or Merton Framework

Knowledge of git version control, branching and code versioning

Passionate about code quality, adhering to best practices for performance, testing, monitoring, documentation and CI/CD

Experience working in an agile framework preferable, including defining functional and non-functional requirements and sprint tasks

Understanding of data engineering, some experience with building production-grade ETL pipelines, plus backend web development, backend-for-frontend, GraphQL and FastAPI

Strong communication skills, able to talk to both technical and commercial people

For junior applicants, coursework, personal projects or open-source contributions count as experience. For senior applicants we are looking for production-scale ownership of the above.

## Desirable knowledge and experience

Knowledge graph technology (a real bonus for us): Neo4j and Cypher, Amazon Neptune, GraphRAG, RDF/SPARQL stores such as Ontotext GraphDB or Apache Jena, TigerGraph, Memgraph or ArangoDB, and ontology or taxonomy design

Agent evaluation and observability: tracing, eval harnesses, tools such as LangSmith, Langfuse or OpenTelemetry

Understanding of or working with AI/ML algorithms and data science

Docker and Kubernetes

Experience with LLM stacks and vector databases (Pinecone, Weaviate, Qdrant, pgvector), open-source models (Mistral, Llama, Qwen) and closed-source models such as GPT-4, Claude and Gemini

Asynchronous and event-driven architecture: queues, streams, webhooks and long-running jobs

A BSc or MSc in Mathematics, Physics, Computer Science or an Engineering discipline (STEM) is preferred but not essential. We care more about what you have built and how you think.

## Eligibility

Candidates must be eligible to live and work in Argentina, Uruguay, Canada, the UK, Portugal or Romania without sponsorship.

If you are excited about AI, passionate about building and ready to accelerate your learning in a hands-on environment, we want to hear from you.

### The successful candidate must have:

- Degree or Diploma in Graphic Design
- 4+ years of graphic design experience (preferably in an advertising role/agency)
- Proven design capabilities as demonstrated in a portfolio
- An ability to multi-task and manage multiple projects at the same time
- Extensive knowledge of specialized design concepts to develop comprehensive layouts and produce marketing collateral

This is a dual role, split between approximately 60% AI-assisted development and agent orchestration, and 40% SQL Server development supporting large-scale data migration. You’ll work within the development team and report to the Software Manager, combining practical AI skills with strong SQL expertise to deliver reliable, efficient solutions.

Key Responsibilities
AI-Assisted Development & Agent Orchestration (c. 60%)
• Use AI coding assistants, such as Claude Code or GitHub Copilot, across the development lifecycle, including code generation, refactoring, testing, documentation and review.

• Build and maintain effective prompts, system instructions, reusable skills and context to produce consistent, reliable AI outputs.

• Design and orchestrate agents and multi-agent workflows, including task decomposition, tool use, agent hand-offs and human-in-the-loop checkpoints.

• Connect agents to internal systems, databases and APIs, for example through MCP or function calling.

• Evaluate AI output for accuracy, regression, cost and latency, and refine workflows based on results.

• Apply appropriate safeguards for data privacy, security and hallucination risk, particularly when customer or school data is involved.

• Identify and prototype opportunities to apply AI to development and data migration, and share best practice by supporting and coaching colleagues.

SQL Server & Data Migration (c. 40%)
• Design, develop and maintain scalable SQL Server T-SQL solutions and related tools for data cleansing, migration and reconciliation.

• Provide database performance-tuning expertise for internal and third-party systems, using AI tooling where appropriate.

• Define technical requirements with non-technical colleagues in the Data Migration Team, and work with third parties to understand their software and support migration projects.

• Manage SQL Server database environments used for data migration, including backup and recovery in test environments.

• Prepare and expose data safely for agents and AI workflows, using AI to support SQL query generation, code review and optimisation.

• Plan and prioritise work independently, managing tasks against project timelines and requirements.

The Ideal Candidate
• You’ll combine hands-on AI-assisted development skills with substantial SQL Server experience. You’ll be curious and adaptable, communicate clearly, and use good judgement to assess AI-generated output rather than accepting it uncritically.

• Demonstrable experience using AI coding tools and writing effective prompts, with practical examples of workflows or agents you have built.

• A strong grounding in data modelling, data management and data manipulation, alongside Git, version control and attention to detail.

• The ability to investigate problems independently, collaborate with colleagues and communicate clearly in writing and in person.

Essential Skills
Practical experience with AI coding assistants and strong prompting skills, supported by examples.
Strong SQL Server T-SQL development and performance tuning, including experience supporting SQL Server in a large-scale environment.
Experience with Git and version control.
Excellent teamwork, communication and documentation skills.

Desirable Skills
Experience building agents or multi-agent workflows using Claude Code, MCP or similar frameworks.
Familiarity with LLM APIs, evaluation approaches and prompt testing.
Scripting or programming experience in Python or a similar language.
Awareness of AI data protection and security considerations.
A reasonable understanding of operating systems, infrastructure and networking.

Job Description:

We are looking for a Lead UX Researcher to join our Cybersecurity R&D team, reporting to the Head of UX.

This is a high-impact role within an established Product, Design and Engineering organisation, with a mandate to strengthen and scale UX research while helping shape Darktrace's unified platform strategy. As our products continue to evolve into a more connected experience, you will deepen our understanding of the people who use them, their goals, workflows and decision-making processes, and ensure those insights directly influence product direction.

Working closely with UX/UI, Product and Engineering teams, you will build a strong, evidence-based understanding of how security professionals operate across different domains, tools and environments. Your work will help guide strategic decisions, improve customer experiences and create a more connected research practice across our portfolio.

What will I be doing?

You will lead strategic and hands-on UX research that helps shape the future of Darktrace's cybersecurity platform. Working across multiple products, you will uncover customer needs, challenge assumptions and provide the insights that drive product strategy, platform design and user experience decisions.
Key responsibilities include:

You'll ideally bring:

• Strong experience leading foundational and strategic UX research within B2B, enterprise or technically complex software organisations.
• A proven ability to influence product direction through evidence-based insights, working closely with Product, Design and Engineering teams.
• Deep expertise in qualitative research methods, alongside the ability to identify patterns and opportunities across complex user needs and workflows.
• Experience researching multi-product ecosystems, platforms or interconnected systems, with an understanding of how different user groups work across them.
• Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with experience building or evolving UX research practices within a growing organisation.

Experience within cybersecurity, security operations or other highly technical domains would be advantageous, as would exposure to platform transformation initiatives or large-scale enterprise workflows

Job Description:
Department: Product 
Reports to: Chief Product Officer (CPO) 
Location: Cambridge, London or East Coast US (minimum 2 days per week in office) 
Type: Full-time 
Key partnerships: Product and Engineering · Business partner in Financial Planning & Analytics (FP&A) · Business partner in IT · Business partner in Product Marketing 

About the Role 
We are seeking a strategic and analytically rigorous VP of Pricing & Packaging to own the end-to-end monetization strategy for our B2B SaaS business. Reporting to the Chief Product Officer, this leader will architect how we package, price, and capture value across our product portfolio — directly influencing revenue growth, gross margin, competitive positioning, and customer lifetime value. 
This is a highly cross-functional leadership role. Rather than owning a large direct team, the VP operates through a partnership model — working closely with a dedicated business partner in Financial Planning & Analytics, a dedicated business partner in IT, and a dedicated business partner in Product Marketing to turn monetization strategy into operational reality. The role also leads a cross-functional Pricing Steering Group that drives alignment and decision-making across the business, and maintains a sharp, continuous view of competitor pricing and packaging moves to keep the company ahead of the market. 
Key Responsibilities 

Pricing Strategy & Monetization 
• Define and own the company's overarching pricing philosophy, strategy, and roadmap across all products and segments. 
• Design and evolve pricing models (tiered, consumption, outcome-based, hybrid) aligned to value delivered and customer willingness to pay. 
• Establish pricing governance, approval frameworks, and discounting guardrails to appropriately protect margin and deal integrity. 
• Partner with the Chief Accounting Officer/Deal Desk function to ensure discounting guardrails are enforced consistently at the point of deal execution.

Direct & Channel-Partner Pricing 
• Understand and account for the similarities and differences between direct and channel-partner pricing and operations, designing strategies that work across both routes to market. 
• Ensure pricing, packaging, and discounting structures are coherent and appropriately margin-protective across direct sales and channel/partner motions. 
• Implement models for Hyperscalers and Marketplaces to promote and optimize online through sales operational models 

Packaging & Product Monetization 
• Architect product packaging, bundling, and tiering strategies that maximize adoption, expansion, and net revenue retention. 
• Partner closely with the CPO and Product organization to align feature-to-tier mapping, entitlements, and add-on/upsell structures with the monetization strategy. 
• Lead the monetization strategy for new product launches, features, and market entries sequenced once core pricing/packaging governance and margin-tracking discipline are established.
• Maintain awareness of relevant market and competitive dynamics to inform packaging and positioning 
• Own SKU and pricelist creation, setting policy and controls for use, distribution, and management, 
• Introduce and build Product Led Growth strategies 
• In the first two quarters, lead the completion and margin-validation of the legacy-SKU-to-package migration, including grandfathering policy and renewal-cycle price bridging.
• 
Pricing Steering Group Leadership 
• Establish, chair, and run a cross-functional Pricing Steering Group spanning Product, Sales, Finance, Marketing, and Customer Success. 
• Set the steering group's charter, cadence, and decision rights; bring pricing and packaging proposals forward with a clear evidence base for endorsement. 
• Drive alignment, resolve trade-offs, and secure buy-in for pricing and packaging changes across the leadership team. 
• Maintain a transparent decision log and ensure decisions are operationalized and tracked to impact. 

Working Through Key Business Partners & GTM Leadership 
• Partner with the FP&A business partner on revenue modeling, margin analysis, price elasticity, willingness-to-pay quantification, and the financial impact of pricing decisions and forecasts. 
• Partner with the IT business partner to operationalize pricing and packaging across billing, CPQ/quoting, Salesforce, entitlements, metering, and systems infrastructure. 
• Partner with the Product Marketing business partner on competitive intelligence, value messaging, and packaging communication. 
• Partner with Engineering to understand the impact of cost of goods sold (COGS) on margins, and to factor infrastructure and delivery costs into pricing decisions. 
• Partner with the Chief Revenue Officer and team to inform quotas, ensuring pricing and packaging decisions align with sales targets, incentives, and quota-setting. 
• Set shared objectives and ways of working with each business partner to ensure strategy translates into reliable execution. 

Analytics, Research & Value Quantification 
• Build a rigorous discipline around willingness-to-pay research, price elasticity analysis, and value-based pricing (in partnership with FP&A). 
• Define pricing KPIs and dashboards (ARPU, ACV, win rates, discount leakage, expansion revenue, NRR impact). 
• Ground all major pricing decisions in data, research, and market evidence. 
Qualifications 
Required 
• 8+ years expertise across SaaS monetization models (subscription, usage/consumption-based, tiered, seat-based, hybrid) and implementing product led growth. 
• 3+ years leading pricing strategy, with strong command of pricing analytics, price elasticity, willingness-to-pay research, and value-based pricing. 
• Experience with CPQ, billing systems, entitlement management. 
• Excellent quantitative, analytical, and financial modeling capabilities. 
• Cyber security industry experience. 
• Win as One – Proven track record of building cross-functional relationships and prioritising collective over individual outcomes 
• Move First – Demonstrated bias for action in ambiguous, fast-moving environments 
• Raise our bar – History of setting and elevating standards of excellence, holding self and others to high expectations while continuously improving processes, quality, and outcomes. 
• Own it – Takes end-to-end accountability for outcomes – good and bad – making decisions with judgement and following through on commitments 
• Proven track record owning pricing and packaging strategy in a B2B SaaS environment at scale. 
• Strong understanding of both direct and channel-partner pricing and operations, including the similarities, differences, and trade-offs between them. 
• Demonstrated success leading through influence — driving outcomes via cross-functional partners rather than a large direct team. 
• Experience establishing and chairing steering groups or governance forums. 
• Strong track record of competitive intelligence — tracking and responding to competitor pricing and packaging strategy. 

Preferred 
• Experience partnering closely with FP&A, IT/systems, and Product Marketing functions to operationalize pricing. 
• Familiarity with usage-based / consumption pricing and metering infrastructure. 
• Experience in a high-growth or PE/VC-backed environment. 

Key Competencies 
• Influence and alignment across senior stakeholders — leads through partnership, not headcount 
• Strategic monetization thinking balanced with operational execution 
• Fluency across both direct and channel-partner routes to market 
• Strong governance and facilitation skills (steering group leadership) 
• Externally aware — continuously scanning the competitive landscape 
• Data-driven decision-making and analytical rigor 
• Comfort with ambiguity in a fast-moving market 
• Demonstrated track record of applying AI to accelerate and scale impact across these key competencies

Role Purpose
This role exists to grow the RPA Support team’s capability by bringing in AI-literate colleagues from Operations and developing them into confident automation support professionals. The role-holder will provide second-line support for the Blue Prism automation estate, use AI assistants responsibly and effectively in their day-to-day work, and progressively build hands-on RPA, infrastructure, and data skills with structured support from the wider team.
This is a development and progression role: the role-holder is not expected to arrive with deep RPA platform knowledge. What matters most is a strong production or operations support background, a sound analytical instinct, and genuine, confident use of AI tools to work smarter — plus the curiosity and discipline to build Blue Prism, infrastructure, and data capability over time.
“AI-literate” here means comfortable and effective using AI assistants to add value in daily work — not, from day one, building AI models, integrating LLM APIs, or developing agentic frameworks. This role is about applying AI sensibly, critically, and responsibly to accelerate everyday support work — with genuine scope to grow into those deeper technical AI-engineering skills over time, alongside RPA, infrastructure, and data capability, as experience and the needs of the team develop.
Key Responsibilities
RPA Application & Production Support
• Provide second-line support for Blue Prism automations across a large, business-critical estate (~250 processes), working alongside senior Support colleagues.
• Investigate incidents and failures using logs, control room data, process design artefacts, and runtime behaviour.
• Learn to distinguish process defects from environment, infrastructure, or data-related root causes, escalating appropriately while this skill is developing.
• Help identify and implement fixes for straightforward bugs, configuration issues, and minor enhancements, with support from senior team members.
AI-Assisted Ways of Working
• Use approved AI assistants (e.g. Copilot-style tools, enterprise LLM chat tools) to accelerate incident investigation, draft documentation, and summarise findings.
• Apply a working awareness of core prompting concepts — being specific, giving context, iterating on a prompt — to get more useful results from AI tools.
• Critically evaluate AI-generated output before acting on it: treat AI as a drafting and acceleration aid, not an authority, and sanity-check suggestions against the evidence.
• Contribute practical examples and lessons learned to help the team build a shared, sensible approach to AI-assisted support.
• Apply awareness of Responsible AI principles — data privacy, model limitations, and enterprise security guardrails — in all AI-assisted work.
Minor Development & Change Delivery (Developing Capability)
• Build confidence making small, low-risk changes to existing Blue Prism automations under guidance, in line with team standards.
• Work alongside developers and senior support colleagues to understand process logic, exception handling, and change-quality expectations.
• Coordinate low-risk changes through the agreed change control, release, and communication process.
Infrastructure & Data Awareness
• Build a working understanding of the platform and environment: servers, services, connectivity, scheduling, and resource constraints.
• Learn to recognise common environment and data-related failure patterns (e.g. credential issues, transaction backlogs, performance degradation) and know when and how to escalate to infrastructure or database teams.
• Support environment stability through proactive checks and monitoring insight, growing this capability over time.
Stakeholder Management & Communication
• Communicate clearly with operational stakeholders during incidents, covering impact, workaround, and resolution.
• Translate technical issues into language business stakeholders can understand — a strength this audience typically already brings from Operations.
• Build strong working relationships across Operations, Technology, and Business functions.
Incident, Problem & Service Management
• Manage incidents and defects through to resolution, remaining calm and methodical, and escalating appropriately during high-severity events.
• Maintain accurate records in ticketing, incident, and change management systems.
• Contribute to problem management by flagging recurring issues for root-cause investigation.
Knowledge Sharing & Capability Growth
• Create and maintain support documentation, runbooks, and troubleshooting guides — using AI tools to accelerate drafting where appropriate.
• Actively seek coaching and mentoring from senior Support colleagues to build RPA, infrastructure, and data skills.
• Help the wider Support team develop practical, responsible habits around AI-assisted working.
What You Will Bring:
Required Skills & Experience
Essential
• Proven experience in an Operations, production support, or service-delivery environment (RPA experience is not required).
• Confident, regular use of AI assistants in day-to-day work (e.g. Copilot, ChatGPT-style tools), with genuine interest in using AI responsibly to improve ways of working.
• Strong analytical and troubleshooting mindset, with the ability to investigate problems methodically.
• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain technical issues to non-technical stakeholders.
• High level of ownership, accountability, and resilience in a live operational environment.
• Willingness and ability to learn new technical skills (RPA, infrastructure, data) through structured coaching and self-directed learning.
Desirable
• Exposure to Blue Prism or other RPA platforms (training provided if not already familiar).
• Basic understanding of infrastructure concepts (servers, services, networking fundamentals).
• Familiarity with SQL, or willingness to learn basic database concepts.
• Awareness of prompt engineering concepts beyond everyday use (e.g. few-shot, chain-of-thought).
• Financial services or regulated-industry experience.
• Familiarity with incident, problem, and change management (ITIL-aligned a bonus).
Success Measures
• Demonstrated growth in RPA, infrastructure, and data troubleshooting capability over the first 6–12 months.
• Effective, responsible use of AI tools to speed up investigation, documentation, and knowledge capture.
• Positive stakeholder feedback on communication and ownership.
• Reduction in repeat incidents on assigned automations as capability builds.
• Successful progression toward full RPA Support Analyst capability.

job_description:
Introduction

Are you a recent or soon-to-be graduate in chemistry, physics, engineering or a related field, excited to put your scientific knowledge and curiosity to work on real-world business issues? Are you interested in understanding why some scientific breakthroughs change the world, while other promising technologies struggle to make it into everyday life? Are you fascinated by how things are made, how people use them and how we can shape a more sustainable future?

Do you enjoy exploring complex questions, making connections between ideas and working with others to find thoughtful, practical solutions? Would you like to help businesses understand not just what technology can do, but how it can make a meaningful difference?

If so, this could be a great role for you!

Who we are

A key part of Cambridge Consultants, our Advisory team works with clients across Consumer, Energy & Industrial, Telecommunications, Biotech, Healthcare and Defence & Security. Our clients range from early start-ups to global organisations, all looking for ways to use emerging technologies to address challenges, create new possibilities and make a positive impact in their markets.

Our role is to help them navigate uncertainty, explore opportunities and turn promising ideas into practical outcomes.

We provide research and insights to support important business choices relating to deep tech. This includes go-to-market strategies, investment support, competitor analysis, market insights, technology road-mapping and strategic foresight. The technologies we explore span exciting developments in biotech, quantum sensing and computing, robotics and physical AI, among many others.

Your role

This role sits within the Research & Insights section of our Advisory group. We explore how emerging technologies and future trends might shape the choices businesses make today, helping our clients feel better equipped to navigate change and plan for the future.

You might investigate what people will value in the next generation of products, explore how cleantech can be adopted at scale, or uncover where novel sensors could create new possibilities for businesses and their customers.

It’s an opportunity to combine scientific thinking, creative exploration and commercial understanding to help answer questions that don’t always have straightforward answers.

What you will be doing

With guidance and support from our wider Advisory team, you will:

- Explore a variety of meaningful projects spanning climate tech investment, new energy generation, smart mobility strategy and emerging deep tech fields such as quantum.

- Bring fresh perspectives to complex challenges, drawing on different research approaches and ideas to help clients identify opportunities across products, services and operations, including AI-enabled approaches.

- Work collaboratively with specialists in engineering, science, product design and realisation, and business to develop strategies that create commercial and societal benefits.

- Make sense of complex information, analysing markets, technologies and business models to help clients understand their options, consider potential challenges and drive informed actions.

- Share ideas and contribute to thought leadership on how deep tech could help address global challenges, from communication on the moon to the future of repairable consumer devices.

What you can bring

We are looking for applicants with the following traits and skills: 

- A relevant academic background: A Master’s or PhD in physical sciences, maths, data science, engineering or another related discipline.

- Business and commercial thinking: Experience or an interest in entrepreneurship, business or economics, whether through student business plan competitions, internships, start-ups or relevant modules and further study.

- Thoughtful analytical and creative thinking: The ability to explore complex technical ideas, recognise connections and turn findings into clear, practical recommendations.

- Curiosity and adaptability: Enthusiasm for learning about new technologies, exploring different sectors and approaching unfamiliar challenges with an open mind.

- Communication and collaboration: The ability to explain complex ideas clearly, listen to different perspectives and build constructive relationships with people from a range of technical and professional backgrounds.

How to apply

If this opportunity interests you, please send your CV and a cover letter outlining your relevant experience, interests and what excites you about the role.

We welcome applications from people with diverse backgrounds, experiences and perspectives. You don’t need to meet every requirement to be a strong candidate. If the role sparks your curiosity and you’d enjoy exploring how science and technology can make a difference, we’d love to hear from you.

By submitting an application to Cambridge Consultants, you confirm that the information provided in this application, together with any supporting documentation, is true, complete, and accurate to the best of your knowledge and belief. You understand that any false statement, misleading information, or material omission may render you liable to disqualification from the recruitment process, withdrawal of any offer of employment, or dismissal without notice if discovered following appointment. You acknowledge that the organisation reserves the right to verify the information supplied.

Systems Engineering and Product Ownership
• Take a whole-product view of development, from initial feasibility and concept selection through detailed design, integration and verification.
• Turn stakeholder needs into practical requirements and trace them through to verification
• Manage Technical Risk and develop effective Risk Control Measures to ensure products are safe to use and meet regulatory constraints
• Comfortable managing mechanical, electronics, firmware, software and other specialists together so that individual subsystems work as one coherent product.
• Spot technical gaps and risks early, agree priorities with the team and drive engineering issues through to resolution.
Requirements, Architecture and Interfaces
• Take the lead on defining, reviewing and maintaining system requirements, making sure they are clear, testable and linked to the needs they address.
• Shape system architecture, data flow, and long-term technical roadmaps across multiple teams.
• Develop functional architectures, break products into manageable subsystems and agree technical responsibilities across engineering disciplines.
• Define interfaces between hardware, embedded software, controls and mechanical systems, including signals, power, communications and physical connections.
• Establish and assess key performance budgets, such as power, timing, accuracy or throughput, using analysis and test data to guide decisions.
 Technical Problem Solving and Risk
• Take a hands-on approach to technical challenges, working with engineers to investigate unexpected behavior and find the root cause of problems.
• Plan and carry out focused feasibility work, experiments and prototype tests to answer important engineering questions early.
• Manage design reviews and risk assessments, helping the team make sound decisions on performance, reliability, safety and design maturity.
• Manage DFMEA and Risk Registers, assessing risk acceptability and tracing risks through Risk Control Measures to implementation
Integration, Test and Verification
• Plan how subsystems will be brought together and tested, with clear methods and acceptance criteria for demonstrating product performance.
• Support the build and integration of electromechanical prototypes, helping diagnose issues across electronics, controls, firmware, software and mechanisms.
• Prepare test methods and plans, participate in testing, interpret results and follow through on failures and design changes.
• Maintain clear evidence that the product meets its requirements through traceability documentation, and support design handover and transfer with the necessary technical information.
 Working with Clients and Project Teams
• Act as a technical lead point of contact, giving project teams a clear view of the overall design and the implications of technical decisions.
• Explain technical options, trade-offs and recommendations clearly to clients and colleagues, using the right level of detail for the audience.
• Work with project managers and technical leads to plan engineering activities, estimate effort and manage technical dependencies and priorities.
• Collaborate with suppliers and external partners to agree specifications, resolve interface issues and integrate their work into the product.
• Support writing proposals, costing and planning work, technical workshops and design reviews, and help colleagues use systems engineering methods in a practical, proportionate way.
Requirements
• Track record of at least 10 years' experience designing products in a highly regulated industry, preferably medical devices.
• Hands-on and practical engineering skills, willing and able to get stuck in to designing solutions and able to demonstrate a passion for engineering in and out of work.
• Able to see the complete product while still understanding enough technical detail to make informed engineering decisions at all levels and engineering disciplines.
• Strong problem-solving skills, with the curiosity and judgement to challenge assumptions and work through unfamiliar technical problems.
• Pragmatic and organized, able to bring structure to an ambiguous brief without creating unnecessary complexity or paperwork.
• Confident working across disciplines, with technical strengths in mechanical and electrical engineering or mechatronics.
• A clear communicator who can build strong relationships with clients, explain technical issues and influence decisions constructively.
• Able to balance performance, usability, cost, risk and development timescales when recommending engineering solutions.
• Proactive, collaborative and accountable, with the drive to take ownership and see technical issues through to completion.
• Bachelor's or Master’s degree in electrical engineering, mechanical/mechatronics, systems engineering or a closely related engineering discipline, or equivalent practical experience.
• Experience developing physical products that combine electronics, software or firmware, and mechanical components, ideally through more than one stage of development.
• Practical experience defining system requirements, developing architectures and managing interfaces between engineering disciplines.
• Hands-on experience building, integrating, testing or troubleshooting electromechanical systems and resolving issues that span hardware and software.
• A good grounding in sensors, actuators, embedded controls, power and communications, and confidence interpreting schematics and technical test results.
• Experience planning and carrying out system-level tests, assessing performance against requirements and documenting engineering findings.
• Familiarity with requirements tools, simulation, modelling, scripting or model-based systems engineering (including SysML) would be beneficial.
• Strong AI skills and experience in applying tools to streamline technical activities, including requirements management
• Experience in a product development consultancy, medical devices, diagnostics, scientific instruments, robotics, automation or other regulated industries would be advantageous.
Benefits
Cambridge Design Partnership (CDP) is an end-to-end innovation partner, propelling global brands and ambitious start-ups to success. We build breakthrough products and services – from insight to ideas, prototypes to production – bringing innovation to life. Our teams are multi-disciplinary, uniting scientific rigor, design ingenuity, and engineering excellence for consumer and healthcare clients. People-centred, deeply collaborative, and – above all – expert, we’re uniquely positioned to shape the future for consumers, patients, and industry. Even our ownership model is innovative: We’re 100% owned by our employees, ensuring an open culture and a total commitment to our projects’ success. As part of our benefits package, we offer:

• excellent learning and development opportunities
• a 12% non-contributory pension

 About Carpata

 We're building the infrastructure that will power how parts are identified, bought and sold across the world.

 Carpata is building the AI-native operating system for B2B parts procurement, starting with the $2 trillion+ global vehicle aftermarket.

 Despite its scale, much of the industry still runs on phone calls, emails, WhatsApp and spreadsheets. Identifying, quoting and ordering a single part can take 15 minutes or more, while return rates can reach 20%. The result is high operating costs, complex supply chains and significant inefficiency for both the businesses buying parts and those supplying them.

 At the heart of the problem is fitment: identifying exactly which part fits which vehicle.

 With millions of vehicle configurations, thousands of manufacturers and fragmented, often conflicting data sources, getting the right part isn't straightforward. Garages and fleets spend time searching catalogues, checking compatibility and chasing suppliers. Distributors employ large teams to handle enquiries, validate parts, prepare quotes and process returns. Even where digital systems exist, much of the work still requires manual intervention.

 We believe solving fitment within the workflows businesses already use is the key to automating the entire industry.

 We've built a proprietary vehicle and parts intelligence platform that identifies and validates the correct components. Combined with AI agents, this enables us to automate the procurement process end to end — from enquiries over email, WhatsApp and phone through to sourcing across suppliers, ordering and invoice reconciliation.

 This works on both sides of the transaction: helping garages and fleets buy the right parts faster, while helping distributors handle enquiries, quotes and orders with less manual work.

 It connects existing supply relationships across original equipment, aftermarket and recycled parts, without requiring businesses to abandon the tools they already use.

 The result is faster procurement for buyers, lower costs to serve for suppliers and fewer incorrect parts moving through the supply chain.

 We're growing quickly, with a significant enterprise opportunity ahead.

 We're already working with major vehicle manufacturers, aftermarket and recycled parts distributors, fleets and dealer groups. Our technology is live, delivering measurable results, and we're expanding its use across customer operations.

 For one major enterprise customer, we're automating 72% of parts identification at 99.9% accuracy, across nearly 200,000 parts every month.

 We have a growing pipeline of enterprise opportunities representing over £800 million in addressable annual parts transactions to pursue in 2027. Our focus is on converting that opportunity into deployments and scaling our technology across the industry.

 As more transactions flow through Carpata, verified outcomes help us improve the intelligence behind future part identification and automation.

 Automotive is just the starting point.

 We're starting with cars and vans, but the same challenges exist across trucks, agricultural equipment, construction machinery, plant and industrial assets.

 Our ambition is to build the intelligence and transaction infrastructure for parts procurement across these markets, connecting manufacturers, distributors and customers globally.

 The Role

 Your first project is the vehicle data that sits underneath our catalogue. It comes from several sources that describe the same vehicle in different ways, and it keeps growing: new vehicles reach UK roads all the time, and registration plates move from one car to another. You will build the systems that keep it accurate and current, automatically, across every vehicle on UK roads. It is a software engineering problem: matching records across sources, and building services that run reliably in production on AWS. It is not infrastructure-heavy: the Lambda, Postgres and Terraform foundations are already in place.

 Beyond that, the work follows the roadmap. We are building in three areas: catalogue intelligence, which is identifying the right part for a given vehicle and catching errors before customers do; workflow automation, which covers search, ordering and integrations with the systems garages and dealers already use; and supply, connecting more suppliers so customers can order through us whoever they buy from. In your first year you would work across all three. That means moving between backend, data and, when needed, front-end work, and going deep where a problem calls for it. As the team grows there will be room to own one of these areas.

 TypeScript throughout the platform, with some existing data tooling in Python. Postgres. AWS Lambda with Terraform. A GraphQL API. Next.js and React on the front end.

That means time with the people who know how vehicles and parts actually work, because an agent can only be as precise as the person directing it. We are moving towards a way of working where agents take a piece of work from ticket to reviewed pull request, and people make the product decisions. We started inside CAST AI helping companies run LLMs on their own Kubernetes clusters; today we run our own coding harness on any model you pick, and the router deciding which model answers each request is ours too.

The Auto Router

Our promise is one enforcement layer for your AI: budgets, spend attribution, and model routing, applied before a request ever hits a model. The Auto Router makes the call: for every request, which model serves it. Eight open-source models whose input prices span more than 20×, cached input up to 50× cheaper than fresh, frontier providers on customers’ own keys, and a coding agent that fires hundreds of requests before its task is done. Frontier-level task success at a fraction of the token cost: that sentence is the product, and it stays true only if the model inside the router keeps getting better. That model is yours.

Made by Cast AI — a Miami-headquartered, globally distributed team across 34 countries that hit unicorn status in January 2026 with a $50B+ backed investment pushing its valuation past $1 billion.

About the role

Every request gets a decision: which model serves it.

This is an applied-ML seat, not an infrastructure one. Platform engineers own the proxy, the streaming path, and the fleet. You own the model inside them: the training data, the objective, the evaluation, and the iteration loop that ships a better router every cycle.

The problem: routing is a prediction problem wearing a product’s clothes. For every request you predict the quality each candidate model would deliver, what it would cost, and how fast it would decode, and you have to be right enough, in aggregate, that the savings are real and the quality never dips below frontier. The data is messy: rollout outcomes from benchmark harnesses, per-request records from the live fleet, override signals, and token streams whose speed depends on the serving concurrency at the moment. Speed itself is a correctness variable: on deadline-bound agentic work, a model that decodes three times slower doesn’t do the same work slower, it does less work. That’s why naive cost-per-token objectives quietly optimize for the wrong thing. And the bar for evidence is high: a router change ships only after production-parity evaluation with error bars, then gets held to its numbers in live traffic.

Stack: Python; PyTorch; SQL at scale (ClickHouse); OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible LLM APIs; benchmark and rollout harnesses (RouterBench-class); GitLab CI.

• Strong Python and SQL at scale: you can pull, clean, and interrogate millions of request-level records without waiting on anyone.

• You know the difference between a model that got better and an eval that got easier.

• You have real opinions about what LLM benchmarks measure, agentic harnesses included.

• You instrument before you optimize, error bars and all.

• You’ve worked on LLM routing specifically: RouterBench-class evals, cost/quality/latency Pareto fronts.

• Calibration, abstention, or conformal methods in production decision systems.

• You’ve run online A/B loops with drift monitoring on a model that touches real money.

• Strong mathematical skills and analytical mindset

ROLE OVERVIEW


Complex merchants can create complex financial crime risks. Their corporate structures, operating models and control environments may span entities, jurisdictions and teams. When concerns emerge, effective action depends on more than identifying the issue: someone must bring the right people together, agree a credible response, and keep remediation moving until it is complete.



As Financial Crime Oversight & Remediation Manager, you will provide that ownership. You will coordinate targeted oversight of higher-risk or strategically important merchant relationships, helping turn concerns into clear, proportionate and evidenced plans. You will work across Compliance, Financial Crime Investigations, onboarding, commercial and operational teams, and, where appropriate, directly with merchants. Your judgement will matter: you will need to know when a proposed control or remediation is credible, when evidence is insufficient, and when an issue needs escalation.



This is a hands-on role for someone who combines financial crime compliance expertise with strong delivery discipline. You will help address issues early, support defensible decisions, and give complex remediation the structure and follow-through it needs.





WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own targeted remediation coordination. For complex merchant concerns, bring together the relevant internal teams, clarify the problem and desired outcomes, agree accountable owners and milestones, and maintain a practical plan through to closure. Track dependencies and slippage, challenge gaps, escalate material blockers and confirm that completion is supported by evidence.

 - Coordinate Compliance-imposed conditions. Track material financial-crime conditions attached to product, market or other approval decisions. Work with the relevant Compliance and business owners to confirm accountability, milestones and evidence of completion; identify slippage or gaps; challenge whether evidence demonstrates the condition has been met; and escalate overdue or inadequately evidenced actions through the agreed governance route. The relevant delivery owner remains accountable for implementing the condition.

 - Coordinate enhanced oversight of merchants. Support a structured watch-list approach for merchants whose risk or control environment warrants closer attention than routine, risk-tiered monitoring, but where immediate termination or a formal investigation is not necessarily the right response. Help define the oversight plan, review progress and ensure concerns do not remain unresolved or without an owner.

 - Assess remediation quality. Review proposed actions and evidence against the underlying financial crime concern and relevant regulatory expectations. Identify whether controls appear appropriately designed and operating, whether further evidence or testing is needed, and whether residual concerns require escalation or a change in the relationship’s risk treatment.

 - Engage merchants constructively. Where appropriate, work with account teams to agree clear requests, expectations and timelines with merchants. Maintain a firm, evidence-led approach while supporting a proportionate path to address weaknesses and establish whether the relationship can be sustained safely.

 - Lead enhanced control reviews. Design and, where appropriate, lead deeper reviews of a merchant’s AML controls during onboarding or ongoing oversight. This may include preparing agendas, conducting structured discussions with merchant stakeholders, probing key control areas, documenting findings and agreeing any required remediation.

 - Support reliance and outsourcing assessments. Contribute to the initial scrutiny of outsourced activities or other arrangements that depend on another party’s controls. Help establish whether reliance is justified, what evidence supports that view, and what conditions or remediation are required.

 - Improve the oversight approach. Capture recurring issues, lessons and delivery gaps, and help refine processes, reporting and escalation so that complex concerns receive consistent, timely and well-evidenced attention.
   


WHAT YOU’LL BRING

 - Experience in financial crime compliance, AML, or a closely related risk and control role, with a sound understanding of AML control frameworks and how to assess their design and effectiveness.

 - Experience coordinating complex remediation, regulatory or audit actions, control reviews, investigations follow-through, or comparable cross-functional change. You can turn an ambiguous issue into a sequenced plan with clear owners, milestones and evidence of completion.

 - The confidence and judgement to challenge senior stakeholders and merchants constructively, distinguish a credible response from a paper commitment, and escalate when progress or evidence is inadequate.

 - Strong written and verbal communication, including the ability to lead structured discussions, document findings clearly and translate complex issues into practical actions.

 - Excellent organisation and follow-through across multiple workstreams, with a pragmatic approach to prioritisation, dependencies and changing circumstances.

 - A collaborative style and the resilience to work through sensitive, commercially significant issues without losing sight of the control outcome.

 - Experience with structured project management methods, such as Lean Six Sigma or PRINCE2, to drive organised execution across complex workstreams is a strong plus.



Experience with complex merchants, payments, cryptoassets, money service businesses, correspondent or outsourced service models would be valuable. Relevant professional qualifications are welcome but are not a substitute for sound judgement and demonstrated delivery.



WHY THIS ROLE

You will work at the point where financial crime risk, merchant relationships and practical execution meet. The role offers meaningful ownership of issues that cut across teams and can shape whether concerns are resolved early, managed with appropriate safeguards, or escalated on a sound evidential basis. Success is visible in the quality of the decisions and the fact that agreed actions are actually completed.

Join our dynamic and growing Systems Engineering team at the Chess Dynamics Headquarters in Horsham. You will be instrumental in the development of high-performance targeting and surveillance equipment for land and naval defence applications.
