- Functional and Physical Systems Architecture Design and Definition.
- Functional, detailed design and safety analysis
- Strong contribution to programme risk mitigation

- Gathering of verification evidence for System Requirements.
- Creation of Procurement Specifications for sub-systems and components.
- Writing test specifications.
- Conducting Design reviews.
- Environmental Qualification Plans (EMC, Temperature, Shock & Vibration)
- Technical report writing

- A good degree in Engineering or physical sciences.

- Proven communication skills
- Proficient in Report Writing.

- Involvement in Full Development Lifecycle of a product.
- Prior experience working as a Systems Engineer
- Experience in working closely with internal and external stakeholders.
- Proficient in the use of requirements management tools (DOORS, Visure or R4J).
- Work package management in JIRA.
- Working in multi-disciplinary teams on projects with a high level of complexity.
- Experience working in the defence sector (or similar)
- Safety Management (MIL-STD 882E, DEF-STAN 00-56, ISO 12100:2010).
- Statutory Compliance (CE Marking).
- Camera Sensor Technology (InfraRed and visible spectrum, DRI performance).
- Fault-Tree and Failure Mode Analysis.

- Excellent communication, interpersonal and written skills.

About The Role
The Security Engineer plays a critical role in protecting our technology infrastructure and maintaining the security posture of our gaming platform. This position exists to proactively identify, assess, and mitigate security vulnerabilities while serving as a trusted security advisor to engineering teams across the organization. The role directly impacts our ability to safeguard user data, maintain platform integrity, and ensure secure development practices are embedded throughout our product development lifecycle.
This position is essential for building and maintaining robust security defenses in a fast-paced, remote-first technology environment where security expertise must be seamlessly integrated into daily engineering operations and strategic decision-making processes.

What you'll do
• Lead vulnerability management program by triaging, reproducing, and assessing security vulnerabilities submitted through Bug Bounty programs, working directly with engineering teams to prioritize and remediate discovered security gaps
• Conduct comprehensive threat modeling by collaborating with engineering teams to analyze proposed solutions, ensuring designs meet security industry standards and identifying potential attack vectors before implementation
• Manage security incident response by reviewing penetration testing results and SIEM reports, translating technical findings into actionable remediation tasks, and tracking resolution progress through completion
• Optimize security infrastructure by applying updates to Web Application Firewalls (WAF) and other security systems, ensuring configurations align with current threat landscape and organizational needs
• Drive security tool evaluation and implementation by researching, evaluating, and recommending security software solutions, attending vendor demonstrations, and leading procurement processes from requirements gathering through deployment
• Provide security consultation and guidance by serving as subject matter expert to development teams, ensuring security best practices are integrated into software development lifecycle and architectural decisions
• Maintain security awareness and documentation by communicating security updates, progress reports, and recommendations to stakeholders through established channels and maintaining current security policies and procedures

Qualifications
• Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Security, or related technical field, or equivalent professional experience
• Minimum 3+ years of professional experience specifically in web application security
• Demonstrated expertise with security testing tools such as Burp Suite or equivalent web request analysis and tampering tools
• Strong written communication skills in English with ability to clearly explain technical security concepts to diverse audiences
• Experience working effectively in fully distributed/remote team environments
• Proven ability to collaborate cross-functionally with engineering and development teams

• Previous hands-on experience managing or participating in Bug Bounty programs
• Programming experience in PHP or JavaScript
• Experience with penetration testing methodologies and tools
• Knowledge of SIEM platforms and security monitoring systems

• Understanding of secure software development lifecycle (SDLC) practices
• Experience with Jira or similar project management and issue tracking systems
• Strong sense of ownership and accountability in a flat organizational structure
• Passion for continuous learning and staying current with evolving security threats and technologies

About You
You are an experienced data science leader who translates strategy into objectives, grows the people around you, and works as a strategic thought partner to senior leadership. You are also a strong individual contributor who doesn't just manage the work but does it. 
You don't need glamorous problems to do great work — you find satisfaction in getting things right, shipping something that matters, and making the people around you better at their craft.
You've worked in applied data science long enough to know when to push for a more rigorous model and when to ship the first version and iterate. You can walk stakeholders through your findings and turn around and give a member of the team support and feedback that helps them grow. You bring relevant data, graphs, and other evidence to group discussions and can continue to evolve your perspective as new evidence comes in.
You think creatively about problems that don't have established solutions. You’re comfortable building from scratch, inventing new approaches, testing them quickly, and iterating to bring out the right idea. You understand that chess is a deeply data-rich domain, and ideally, you love the game. Familiarity with how chess players develop and improve, how rating systems work, the challenge of catching cheaters, and what makes a chess feature feel right, is knowledge that will compound quickly in this role. 

What you'll do
• Own high-impact data science work across product data science and fair play. Create and build novel algorithms, models, and data-powered features that directly shape the chess experience for our users, from systems that protect the integrity of the game to features that make Chess.com more engaging and useful for players at every level.
• Partner across the company on product vision and execution. Work closely with product managers, engineers, designers, and writers to translate new stats and algorithms into decisions that power our next generation of features.
• Design and deploy creative heuristics, algorithms, and models that identify cheating at scale using the full depth of your statistical and data science toolkit. Raise the quality and sophistication of our approaches over time.
• Manage a lean team of data scientists. Turn strategy into clear team objectives and results, not just execute direction from leadership. Set the quality bar through your own work and give feedback that inspires teammates to do great work, not just fix the issues of the day. Help data scientists grow into scientists who can operate with more speed and independence over time. 
• Communicate early and often. In a fully remote culture, proactive communication is how work actually gets done. Surface blockers before they become problems, keep stakeholders informed without being asked, and make sure your team is never left wondering where things stand.

Required Skills
• 5+ years of data science experience, with a demonstrated track record of developing algorithms and models, contributing to features that shipped, and driving real value for users.
• Strong Python and SQL skills; experience building and working within data pipelines using BigQuery and GCP or similar cloud databases & storage at scale. 
• Comfortable with agentic workflows and tools (Cursor, Claude Code or similar) to accelerate research ideation and execution.
• Solid machine learning fundamentals with enough depth to contribute meaningfully to models across the chess data stack, including anomaly detection for fair play and features that support learning and understanding chess at varying rating levels.
• Proven ability to communicate findings clearly to both technical peers and senior non-technical stakeholders.
• Experience managing or meaningfully mentoring other data scientists or analysts.
• Deep familiarity with chess: you like to play, have thought about rating systems and how inflation may impact ratings at scale, want to build products that you would use yourself to further your chess journey, and have done some thinking on the cheating problem and how to detect it.
Preferred Skills
• Experience on a consumer gaming or entertainment platform where domain-specific data science is at the core of the product.
• Comfort working in lean, high-ownership team environments where being proactive is your superpower.

Chess.com is one of the largest gaming sites in the world and the #1 platform for playing, learning, and enjoying chess.

We are a team of 600+ fully remote people in 60+ countries working hard to serve the global chess community. We are here to support 250M+ chess players worldwide with the best possible product, content, and tools to serve the community!

We are a tech company. A gaming company. A content company. And we do it all with passion and commitment to the game. Above all we prize our mission-driven, flat, life-celebrating, no-corporate culture, and we look forward to meeting you and learning more about what you can bring to the team.

About You

First off, you love to play chess and want to help others discover that same joy.

Secondly, you have extensive experience running paid acquisition for a consumer app or subscription business. You've built that experience the hard way: testing channels, defending budget with rigor, and proving out what's actually incremental. You're comfortable being the person in the room who insists on a clean incrementality test before anyone scales spend.

Finally, you have the operator's instinct for performance marketing. You move fast between channels, creative, and data. You know when a metric is telling you something real versus noise, and you can turn a promising early signal into a durable, scalable channel. You have the expertise to grow and own a budget into the 8-9 figures, while having the judgment and integrity to say when spend is getting inefficient and should be pulled back.

What you'll do
• Own and scale a performance marketing engine with real momentum. The foundations are already in place and working. App Store and Android Ads are running highly efficiently, and Meta and YouTube video are proving out as channels with a clear path to target. You'll take full ownership of this portfolio and drive the acceleration and scale that comes next.
• Set the bar for measurement rigor. Build out best-in-class incrementality testing, saturation modeling, and 7-day ROAS and LTV frameworks. We should always know precisely what our spend is buying us, so we can confidently push harder where it's working.
• Scale creative production. Partner with our content and partnerships teams to bring best practices from other UGC agencies to ensure high ROAS on a hybrid creator + performance strategy. Build the testing infrastructure to find winners fast.
• Optimize through DSPs and AdTech partners. Manage and grow our relationships with partners like LiftOff, AdFuel, and Eyeo to squeeze more performance out of every channel.
• Shape our long-term investment strategy. Partner with leadership to translate channel performance into LTV- and ROI-backed budget plans. Grow spend where the returns support it, and have the judgment to pull back or reallocate spend the moment efficiency slips, so every dollar keeps working for the business.
• Operate in public. As a globally remote company spanning many time zones, async Slack communication is how decisions get made. Work out loud in channels: share results and reasoning transparently, flag what's working and what isn't, and pull in the right people by name to keep things moving.
• Manage the operational details. Own budgets, vendor contracts, and ad account setup across platforms (Meta, Google, App Store, DSPs). Keep attribution and tracking (AppsFlyer and friends) clean and trustworthy.
• Build close ties with our social media and growth teams. Stay plugged into what's happening across the chess calendar and the broader business: tournaments, viral moments, product launches, seasonal swings. Read when we're heading into a boom (or viral moment) versus a quiet stretch, and flex spend accordingly between defensive, standard, and aggressive postures.

Required Skills
• 5+ years in performance marketing or paid user acquisition. You have a track record of taking a channel from test to scale, and the judgment to know when to hold, cut, or reallocate spend as efficiency changes.
• Real experience with incrementality testing, saturation analysis, and LTV/ROAS modeling. You don't just report on these metrics. You know how to build and defend them.
• Hands-on channel expertise across Meta, Google/App Store Ads, YouTube, and DSP/AdTech platforms, plus fluency with mobile attribution tools like AppsFlyer.
• Creative taste maker, familiar with content and social media trends
• High-velocity written communicator. You communicate clearly and concisely at speed, operate primarily in writing, and can move between tactical channel optimization and board-level ROI conversations in the same day.

Preferred Skills
• Background in gaming, subscription, or other high-engagement consumer apps, ideally with millions of daily users.
• Experience scaling creative production through UGC agencies, creator marketplaces, or an in-house creator network.
• A track record of syncing paid spend with organic demand cycles. You tie budget decisions to product launches, seasonal moments, or community/viral events rather than running a flat, always-on plan.
• Experience discussing budget and ROI cases with executive leadership or a board.

About the Opportunity
• This is a full-time opportunity
• We are 100% remote (work from anywhere!)
• This role is open to candidates who can work with significant overlap with both United States Eastern and Pacific time zones.

About the Role
As a Senior Product Designer in Connect, you’ll lead the design of high-impact experiences for some of our most important and visible features like Home, Profile, Notifications, Widgets, Friends, Messages, Sharing, and more.
Your work will span cross-functionally where different features meet and overlap and you will partner closely with Product, Engineering, and other Product Designers to craft an engaging and cohesive experience across web, iOS, and Android for millions of players across the world.
You'll identify opportunities beyond the brief, and influence product and design decisions while helping raise the craft quality bar across the team.
About You
You’re an experienced Product Designer with strong visual craft, product judgment, and the confidence to influence how a product takes shape. You think beyond the feature in front of you, considering how decisions connect across product experiences. You’re comfortable navigating ambiguity and competing perspectives, present your thinking with clarity and composure, and help other designers improve through thoughtful critique.
You’re interested in how people connect and find joy in designing fun and healthy ways for them to build relationships and feel like part of a global community.
What You’ll Do
• Lead the end-to-end design of high-impact product experiences across Chess.com’s web, iOS, and Android apps, and deliver polished, production-ready UI designs.
• Partner closely with Product, Engineering, Design, and other stakeholders to shape requirements, clarify ambiguity, and influence product and design direction.
• Design how players connect, socialize, and feel like they’re part of a global community on key features like Home, Profile, Friends, Messaging, Notifications, Leaderboards, and more.
• Think horizontally across features and the broader design system, identifying opportunities to improve consistency, usability, and quality across the product.
• Raise the craft bar through strong UI design, thoughtful interactions, and sound product judgment grounded in context, heuristics, and user insight.
• Proactively identify meaningful product opportunities beyond the immediate brief and help move them from idea to well-articulated design direction.
• Present your design proposals and clearly articulate your decisions, navigate differing perspectives, and help cross-functional partners align to reach strong decisions.
• Build and iterate on high-fidelity prototypes using our Design System, using tools like Cursor and Claude, to explore directions and accelerate decision making.
• Contribute to design critiques, provide constructive feedback to other Product Designers, and help strengthen the quality of the team’s work without direct people-management responsibility.
• Maintain design ownership through implementation and help ensure strong design-to-code alignment across platforms.
Skills / Qualifications
• 5+ years of experience working as a Product Designer on a consumer-facing product or game.
• A portfolio of polished web and mobile UI design work that demonstrates excellent craft, strong product thinking, and accountability.
• Mastery of UI design fundamentals, including typography, color, layout, visual hierarchy, alignment, contrast, interactivity, user experience heuristics.
• Experience using agentic tools like Cursor and Claude to build shareable prototypes and quickly iterate on different ideasDemonstrated experience owning complex product work from early problem definition through implementation.
• Strong Design system fluency, including the ability to use established patterns while thinking across features and identifying opportunities to improve consistency.
• A track record of influencing product and design decisions, presenting proposals clearly, and navigating cross-functional disagreement or competing priorities.
• Familiarity with frontend development and how design translates into code across web and mobile platforms.
• Strong written and verbal communication, proactive remote collaboration, and the judgment to operate effectively with autonomy and ambiguity.
Preferred / Nice to Haves
• A love for chess and knowledge of Chess.com and its product experience.
• Experience designing social features for mobile games or consumer products.
• Motion design experience, with strong product and UI design craft as the foundation.
• Design engineering or frontend development experience on web, iOS, or Android.

Chess.com is one of the largest gaming sites in the world and the #1 platform for playing, learning, and enjoying chess.

We are a team of 600+ fully remote people in 60+ countries working hard to serve the global chess community. We are here to support 250M+ chess players worldwide with the best possible product, content, and tools to serve the community!

We are a tech company. A gaming company. A content company. And we do it all with passion and commitment to the game. Above all we prize our mission-driven, flat, life-celebrating, no-corporate culture, and we look forward to meeting you and learning more about what you can bring to the team.

About You

You love to play chess and want to help others discover that same passion. You understand the full user journey of being a chess player, and different types of players need to experience to find joy in the game. You are intimately familiar with the Chess.com experience and want to help further build out the Gameplay ecosystem.

You have extensive experience as a product manager shipping delightful consumer-facing products. You have worked deeply with design and engineering teams to define what great looks like and you communicate regularly and successfully to executive stakeholders.

What you'll do
• Shape the Gameplay roadmap and vision. In close partnership with leadership, shape both the near-term roadmap and the long-term vision for Gameplay at Chess.com. From live games, to daily, to bot play, you will own the gameplay experience.
• Bring ideas and sharpen them with the team. Come with your own point of view on what's worth building and why. You don't wait to be told. At the same time, engage seriously with feedback from leadership and peers: internalize it, push back where you disagree, and use it to make the work better. The vision is built together; you're a strong, informed voice in it.
• Operate in public. As a globally remote company spanning many time zones, async slack communication is how decisions get made. Work out loud in channels: brainstorm openly, pose sharp questions, make decisive small calls with reasoning attached, and be explicit on what's urgent vs. not. Engage with depth and without ego, pull the right people in by name to build alignment. Make the most of sync meeting time by taking on the biggest questions.
• Define success and hold the bar velocity and quality. Frame the problem, partner deeply with engineers and designers, work through what "good enough to ship”. Get product scope first-time right.
• Use AI to prototype, de-risk, and accelerate. Build mocks, test flows, and pressure-test ideas yourself. Bring working artifacts into discussions, not just decks. Run AB tests with velocity and build with foresight on configurability.
Required Skills
• 7+ years in product management, 4+ shipping consumer-facing products at scale. You've shipped consumer-facing products to large user bases. You know how to balance a quantitative understanding of funnels, metrics, and experimentation with a qualitative feel for what makes a delightful user experience.
• Excellent product taste, especially in the chess context. You know what feels good and what doesn't. You know what users with different levels of chess skill and experience are looking to get out of gameplay.
• AI-native. You already use AI daily to prototype, explore ideas, and accelerate execution. You build working prototypes as the basis for discussion.
• High-velocity communicator. You communicate clearly and concisely at speed and across many projects. You act as the focal point across design, engineering, stakeholders, product peers, and executives, digging into engineering specifics in one thread then zooming out to exec-level outcomes in the next.
• US time zone overlap. This role will have most of it’s key stakeholders across the US. While we are flexible with your location, we would require clear and substantial overlap with Eastern US hours.
About the Opportunity
• This is a full-time opportunity
• We are 100% remote (work from anywhere!)
• This role is open to candidates who can work with at least 4 hours of overlap with Eastern US hours.

The Social Media Manager is responsible for applying the voice, content, and daily operations of Chess.com's official Italian social media channels. • Collaborates with marketing, content, and events teams to plan and execute social media campaigns that support company-wide initiatives.
• Communicates with members seeking support or raising issues on social media.
• Identifies emerging platforms across relevant countries, regions and languages, and pilots new content formats by anticipating algorithm shifts, leveraging new tools, and adapting to platform updates.

• Proficiency with basic photo and video editing software (e.g., Adobe Creative Suite, Canva, CapCut)
• Deep understanding of content strategy, platform algorithms, and best practices for major social media platforms
• Excellent communication and collaboration skills suitable for a fully distributed, remote team environment
• A high sense of ownership, accountability, and a commitment to continuous learning
• Strong cultural awareness and sensitivity, with the ability to adapt content and messaging to Italian speaking communities while respecting cultural nuances

The AI Architect will define end-to-end GenAI architectures, establish enterprise standards and reference patterns and layered guardrails. The role requires strong collaboration with product, security, privacy, legal, and cloud engineering teams, particularly in regulated enterprise environments.

Key Responsibilities:

Enterprise GenAI Architecture & Strategy:
• Define and maintain the blueprints, reference architectures and design patterns for LLM-based applications, covering model access, orchestration, retrieval, prompt management, evaluation, and observability.
• Translate business and product requirements into robust AI solution architectures that balance innovation, reliability, cost efficiency, and risk management.
• Act as a GenAI subject matter expert, advising senior leadership on AI strategy, feasibility, and adoption paths.

LLM, RAG & Agentic Workflows:
• Architect knowledge bases and RAG architectures integrating structured and unstructured enterprise data sources.
• Establish agentic AI patterns, enabling multi-step reasoning, tool usage, workflow orchestration, and human-in-the-loop controls.
• Guide teams on prompt engineering, context management, and response grounding to improve accuracy, relevance, and user trust.
• Assist in the evaluation of commercial LLMs and SaaS AI platforms, selecting the right tools for different workloads.

AI Platforms, Gateways & Integration
• Awareness of AI Gateway / Model Access Layer to centralize access to LLMs and AI services, including:
o Authentication and authorization - Model routing and versioning
o Rate limiting, quotas, and cost controls - Logging, auditability, and observability
o Establish secure connectivity to LLM endpoints in the enterprise cloud,
documenting DNS, routing, IAM policies, firewall rules, and network controls.
o Integrate GenAI capabilities into existing enterprise systems and digital platforms.

Responsible AI, Security & Guardrails:

• Embed Responsible AI principles—fairness, transparency, explainability, and
accountability—into architecture and delivery practices.
• Partner closely with security, privacy, legal, and compliance teams to meet enterprise
governance standards and emerging AI regulations.
• Define monitoring and evaluation frameworks to detect hallucinations, drift, misuse, and operational risks.

Innovation, Productivity & Enablement
• Drive GenAI initiatives focused on developer productivity, operational efficiency, and enhanced customer experiences.

• Content safety, moderation, and policy enforcement

We evaluate the harnesses, repository patterns, skills, and agentic tooling available, decide what our teams should standardize on, and build and support the shared tooling other teams depend on.

Bridging Housing and Social Care to Transform Outcomes for Residents.

At Clarion, we believe everyone deserves to feel safe, supported and secure in their home. We’re introducing a new kind of social work role.

What if housing and social care worked together around the person, rather than residents having to navigate the boundaries between different organisations?

We want to help make that happen. We’re creating a new Social Worker (Housing) role, bringing professional social work expertise directly into our housing environment and helping us build stronger connections between housing, adult social care, health, safeguarding and community services.

This is an opportunity to help shape a role from the beginning. You’ll work alongside housing colleagues and external partners to find solutions for residents whose circumstances cannot be addressed by housing intervention alone. Your focus will be on understanding the whole person, their home, strengths, relationships, risks and aspirations, and bringing the right organisations together around them.

The ambition is simple: fewer gaps, fewer hand-offs and better outcomes for residents. That approach complements Clarion's existing vulnerability model, which is centred on coordinated, outcome-focused support, early intervention, reduced harm, improved wellbeing and independence, sustainable tenancies and stronger partnership working.

Why we're creating this role

Housing is about much more than bricks and mortar. A secure, appropriate home can be fundamental to someone's health, independence, safety and connection to their community.

Clarion's Five New Giants of Opportunity report identifies Connection, Resilience, Sufficiency, Trust and Health as the foundations of a new social contract for housing and calls for fresh thinking and partnership working beyond traditional organisational boundaries. The report was published in November 2025 and examines the changing social, economic, technological and demographic pressures affecting residents and communities.

Our Resident Strategy builds on this thinking. It recognises that housing is connected to wellbeing, finances, safety and community life, while focusing on good homes, dependable services and relationships built on trust. The Social Worker (Housing) will help us turn those ambitions into practice.

What you'll do

You’ll bring a professional social work perspective to some of the situations where housing, health and social care intersect.

This role will provide specialist social work expertise to support residents experiencing vulnerability, helping them achieve positive outcomes through strengths-based, person-centred practice. You’ll undertake holistic assessments, identify risks and support needs, and work with residents to develop practical solutions where housing and social care issues are closely connected. You’ll build strong relationships with statutory and community partners, including Adult Social Care, the NHS, mental health services and safeguarding teams, ensuring coordinated and effective support for residents.

The successful candidate will contribute to complex case discussions, safeguarding processes and multi-agency planning, bringing professional knowledge of the Care Act 2014, Mental Capacity Act 2005 and adult safeguarding principles into a housing setting. You’ll also support colleagues to navigate social care pathways, identify opportunities to improve partnership working, and use learning from individual cases to influence service development and improve outcomes across the organisation.

This complements Clarion's established approach of person-centred practice, named ownership, accessible communication, risk and outcome review, resident voice and "partnership by design".

Partnership will be at the heart of the role.

We don't expect one organisation or one professional to have all the answers.

The role will seek to strengthen the interface between housing, social care, health and the voluntary and community sector, enabling partners to build solutions around residents rather than organisational boundaries. That means developing relationships with partners, understanding their statutory responsibilities and pressures, and creating routes through which information, professional expertise and interventions can come together around the resident.

This reflects Clarion's strategic call for greater cross-sector collaboration with health, local authorities and community partners. You’ll be a connector as much as a practitioner.

The person we're looking for

We're looking for someone who is professionally curious, practical and determined to make systems work better for people. You’ll be comfortable moving between two worlds: understanding the statutory framework and professional standards of social work while recognising the realities of housing management and tenancy sustainment.

job_description:
About the team

The Control Plane Platform team is building the shared foundation that every product in ClickHouse Cloud is built and shipped on. We give ClickHouse engineering teams one place to own and deploy their product, remove the overhead of rebuilding common plumbing, and keep the customer experience consistent as the number of integrating teams grows. The team owns API gateways and API standards, shared platform services, deployment and infrastructure patterns, testing and CI, local developer experience and Control Plane observability.

About the role

We’re looking for an Engineering Manager to lead our Platform team. This is a high-impact, high-trust role at the center of our Cloud product, combining people leadership, technical direction, product thinking, and operational ownership while maintaining the reliability customers expect.

You’ll work hand-in-hand with Product, Infrastructure, Security, Support, and engineering teams across ClickHouse.

This role goes beyond engineering leadership. Together with your team, you’ll help shape how new products and teams will integrate and deploy their applications in ClickHouse Cloud.

What You’ll Do

 - Lead, coach, and grow a high-performing team - recruit to a high bar, set crisp expectations, give direct feedback and career development, and manage performance — while fostering a healthy, inclusive environment built on empathy, psychological safety, trust, and a high technical bar.

 - Own outcomes across the platform surface: API gateways and API standards, shared platform services (event bus, notifications, feature flags, websockets, audit records), deployment and infrastructure patterns, CI and testing, local developer experience, disaster recovery, and Control Plane observability.

 - Treat the integrating teams as your customers and measure success by their delivery velocity and adoption of the platform, not only by what your team ships.

 - Guide architecture and help senior engineers make explicit, sound tradeoffs. land cross-cutting migrations, deprecations, and contract changes across teams without stalling product delivery.

 - Jump into designs and code for complex areas - gateway routing and auth/RBAC enforcement, spec-driven code generation, event delivery semantics and idempotency, multi-region rollout safety.

 - Build the culture of operational excellence: Own SLOs, reliability, on-call quality, and cost-efficiency for k8s-hosted, multi-tenant services across cloud regions.

 - Systematize support, reduce toil, and build self-serve/auto-healing capabilities - golden-path templates and generators, auto-healing, and documentation that gets a new team integrated in days rather than weeks.

 - Shape the platform vision, turn it into a roadmap, sequence bets for business impact, and ship fast with tight feedback loops — including writing the RFCs that build cross-org consensus before big changes land

What you bring

 - 8+ years in software engineering and 3+ years managing software engineers with a track record of hiring, developing, and retaining strong talent.

 - Experience leading a platform or infrastructure team whose customers are other engineering teams — you've driven adoption and cross-org migrations through influence and good tooling rather than mandate.

 - Experience leading distributed global teams, fostering an inclusive and autonomous culture, and creating clarity across time zones.

 - Experience building scalable, highly available, and secure cloud-based infrastructure in AWS (EKS, SQS, DocumentDB, Redis, PostgreSQL, Lambdas) with infrastructure as code (Terraform, Helm) and progressive delivery (Argo Rollouts or similar).

 - Experience with containerization and orchestration (Docker, Kubernetes), including patterns for hosting many independently deployed applications in a shared cluster.

 - Familiarity with API platform work: OpenAPI-driven contracts, API gateways, and the shared concerns they centralize — authentication, RBAC, rate limiting, versioning, and deprecation.

 - A track record of decomposing a monolith into independently deployable services without stalling product delivery.

 - Technical credibility to engage deeply in architecture and incidents without owning daily implementation.

 - Hands-on: you still enjoy diving into code/designs for complex or critical areas, reviewing code, and guiding via feedback.

 - Strong execution judgment across ambiguity, parallel workstreams, risk, and long-term system health.

Nice to have

 - Experience with large TypeScript/Node monorepos and the developer-experience problems that come with them: CI scale and flakiness, build and test times, local development environments, and code generation from specs.

 - Designed and implemented strategies for load balancing, auto-scaling, disaster recovery, and failover for cloud environments.

 - Experience building CI/CD at scale

 - Experience with internal developer platforms: service catalogs, golden-path templates, and self-service app scaffolding.

 - Proficiency with frontend frameworks (React).

 - Experience making APIs consumable by AI agents — MCP servers, CLIs, or skills generated from API specs.

 - Experience with ClickHouse

 - Previous experience in developing analytics or data-intensive applications.

Why This Role

 - Shape how all feature teams in ClickHouse Cloud develop and integrate with each other

 - Operate with ownership, autonomy, and speed while keeping the company lean.

 - Lead a technical team where correctness, performance, reliability, and developer experience all matter.


PERKS

You will own the end to end product portfolio and customer experience for France, balancing global scale with local nuance. This role sits at the intersection of product execution and regional partnership, and it suits someone who thrives in complexity, builds for diverse users, and gets into the weeds.

Our market opportunity is rare in its scale and powered by a strong business model, first-rate investors and advisors, and a global product management team (if we do say so ourselves). Clio is growing rapidly, and Product Managers here grow their scope as we open new markets.

Speaking of Product at Clio, we have worked hard to develop an excellent product management culture with empowered PMs who carry real influence across the organization. Our team brings together seasoned professionals from a diverse set of product backgrounds. Clio invests heavily in developing Product Managers, growing leaders, and in the broader Product communities in which we operate.

What you'll work on:

As a Senior Product Manager, and in conjunction with your Development and Design counterparts (your triad), you will drive successful outputs and outcomes across Clio's portfolio in France.

_End to End Portfolio Ownership:_

- You own Clio's product portfolio and customer experience in France end to end, from first touch through onboarding, daily practice management, billing, and support. Where a gap sits in a product another team owns, you own getting it closed.

- You are accountable for the quality of Clio's customer experience in France as a whole, rather than for a single feature area. Your measure of success is whether a lawyer in France can run their practice on Clio without hitting a wall that a lawyer in North America would not hit.

- You maintain a single, current view of what breaks today, what is missing, and what we have committed for France, and you make that view legible to leadership before leadership asks for it.

_Product Leadership and Execution:_

- Working from the overarching strategy set by your Senior Director, Product Management, you will develop a roadmap in conjunction with your peers that moves our business forward, and evangelize it throughout the company.

- You will own the delivery of features in the roadmap while also ensuring they deliver on the desired business outcome.

- Drive product readiness for the French market, including localization, multi-lingual support, regulatory requirements, and market-specific workflows.

_Speed and Iteration Toward a Clear Vision:_

- You set a clear vision for what Clio looks like in France, then ship toward it in weeks rather than quarters. We expect a first customer-visible change within your first 90 days.

- You will make decisions with imperfect information, put something in front of customers, and correct from what you learn. We aim to validate with real customers before building at scale, however there are scenarios where a regulatory deadline sets the date. In those cases we will commit to the date and narrow the scope rather than move the date.

- You parallelize. When a workstream can run alongside another, you run it alongside, and you say what serializing would cost in weeks when you choose to serialize.

_Local Legal Market Understanding:_

- You understand how lawyers in France actually work: how French civil law shapes a firm's structure, how matters progress through the local courts, how the profession sets and regulates fees, what the Conseil National des Barreaux and the local Ordres require of a practitioner, and where local practice diverges from common law practice.

- You track the regulatory surface that touches our product, including French electronic invoicing under the Factur-X and PDP regime, TVA, and Conseil National des Barreaux professional rules, and you translate it into requirements our central teams can build against.

- You build and maintain direct relationships with practitioners, bar associations, and local partners, and you serve as the company's source of truth on what the French legal profession needs.

_System Design and Technical Fluency:_

- You can read and reason about how we built our platform: where our data models carry a country assumption, how the model represents currency, tax, payments, and locale, and what a change to one of those costs downstream.

- You can hold a design discussion with engineering about cardinality, extensibility, and migration, and leave with a shared decision.

- You can tell a problem that needs a local configuration from a problem that needs a platform capability, and you argue for the platform capability when it is the right answer.

_AI Native Working Style:_

- You work AI-first by default. You use AI for customer research synthesis, competitive and regulatory analysis, requirements drafting, data querying, and prototyping, and you can show how it changed your throughput.

- You build your own working systems. You are comfortable writing prompts, chaining tools, and standing up a lightweight agent or script to remove repetitive work from your week.

- You bring judgment to it. You know which AI output needs verification against a primary source, particularly on regulatory and legal questions, and you verify it.

_Influencing Central Teams:_

- Central teams build the platform that France depends on, and their leadership sets their goals, metrics, and roadmap without France in them. Your job is to quantify the case for France well enough that it wins a place on that roadmap.

- You will build the business case in the currency that team's leadership measures it on, name the tradeoff you are asking them to make, and find the version of the ask that serves their goal alongside yours.

- You escalate on a stated trigger rather than on frustration. When merit alone does not win the ask, you bring your Senior Director a clear recommendation and the cost of inaction.

- Partner closely with cross-functional leaders across Product, Engineering, Design, Marketing, Sales, Customer Success, Legal, and Operations to support the French market launch and growth.

- Manage stakeholder relationships across a matrixed organization with clarity and diplomacy.

What you bring:

- Fluency in French and in English. Clio operates in English, so English fluency is a requirement of the role rather than a preference.

- 4-5 years of experience in product management

- Working knowledge of the French legal market, including French civil law, how local firms operate, and the regulatory requirements that apply to them

- Proven track record of independently taking multiple products or features from ideation to launch in a SaaS environment

- Experience owning a product area end to end, including outcomes that depended on teams outside your own

- Demonstrated expertise in localization and multi-lingual product development. This is a core requirement for the role.

- Experience building or managing multilingual applications or internationalization projects, and expanding products to other countries and languages

- Technical fluency sufficient to reason about system design, data models, and platform tradeoffs with engineering

- A demonstrated AI-native working style, with specific examples of how you use AI in your product practice

- Evidence of winning roadmap commitments from teams that do not report to you and that carry no accountability for your outcome

- Exceptional attention to detail, so that no requirement or specification slips through the product development cycle

- Outstanding organizational skills, capable of managing multiple priorities simultaneously without compromising quality or timelines

- Experience using data to inform decisions without succumbing to analysis paralysis

- Genuine ability to put yourself in our customers' shoes and operate from a place of empathy

- Experience working across time zones and cultures, with a customer-first approach

- An entrepreneurial mindset with comfort operating in ambiguity

- At least 2 or 3 failures under your belt, the learnings of which you can bring to Clio

- Ability to work in a highly collaborative team without ego

- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills

Serious bonus points if you:

- Have prior experience in legal tech, or a strong understanding of the legal services market, including familiarity with legal practice management software and the needs of legal professionals

- Have worked directly with Conseil National des Barreaux and the local Ordres or comparable professional bodies

- Worked previously in a regulated industry or with multi-product ecosystems

- Have shipped against a regulatory deadline in France or another EU market

- Successfully launched products in global markets

- Have a track record of breaking down objectives into initiatives and delivering to customers at scale

- Have built internal tooling or agents to support your own product practice

Cobalt runs AI agents in production that test real customer applications. We’re looking for a Staff AI Engineer who has built and operated production agent systems and can help us make them more reliable, secure and cost-efficient.

You’ll set the technical direction for how we design, evaluate, ship and operate agents, and stay hands-on building the foundations our teams use. You’ll work across engineering, product, research and security, mentoring engineers and helping teams turn promising prototypes into dependable production systems.

Your primary focus will be our agent platform and production practices. You’ll also help engineering teams improve how they build software with AI coding agents.

What You’ll Do

• Set technical direction for agent systems across teams, including orchestration, tool use, context and memory management, human oversight and failure recovery.

• Design, build and operate shared foundations: evaluation frameworks, agent observability and tracing, execution controls, and model access with routing and failover where needed.

• Establish evaluation practices that measure task completion, accuracy, false positives, security and cost per successful task. Work with domain experts to build representative test cases and turn production failures into regression tests.

• Make agent workflows resilient to tool failures, timeouts, rate limits and partial execution, with clear limits on retries, runtime and spend.

• Work with security and platform teams to build in scoped permissions, customer data isolation, audit trails and safe execution of tools and code.

• Establish practical engineering standards: evals in CI, prompt and model versioning, regression testing for non-deterministic systems, cost and latency budgets, and staged rollouts with rollback paths.

• Lead model selection and cost optimization. Benchmark models against real workloads and make informed trade-offs between quality, latency and cost.

• Partner with teams on production readiness, incident investigation and improvements to agent reliability.

• Help teams use AI coding agents effectively across planning, implementation, review and testing. Measure the impact on delivery speed and software quality.

• Mentor engineers and technical leads through design reviews, pairing, internal talks and written guidance. Help teams adopt shared capabilities and improve them based on feedback.

• Work with product, research and security leaders to turn business priorities into a technical roadmap with clear outcomes.

You Must Have

• Significant software engineering experience, typically 8–10+ years, with a track record of technical leadership across teams.

• Hands-on experience building and operating LLM-based agents in production, with a clear understanding of their scale, constraints and business outcomes.

• A track record of improving agent reliability: building evaluations, investigating non-deterministic failures and improving success rates against measurable goals.

• Strong knowledge of agent architectures, including tool use, orchestration, planning, context and memory management, and the judgment to know when simpler workflows are sufficient.

• Experience running LLM workloads through managed cloud model platforms or direct provider APIs, including rate limits, failure handling and cost tracking.

• Strong backend and distributed systems fundamentals, including APIs, asynchronous workflows, concurrency and fault tolerance.

• Model access: Managed cloud model platforms, direct provider APIs and multi-provider gateways.

About Codat

Codat is an advisory intelligence solution purpose-built for modern commercial banking. Through rich, specialized data, forward-looking insights, and integrated workflows, Codat empowers banking teams to deepen their relationships, grow their revenue, and simplify their day-to-day work.

Founded in 2017 and backed by JPMorgan, PayPal, Amex, Plaid, and Shopify, Codat has successfully powered over 350,000 connections to business customers’ financial systems — and is trusted by industry leaders to turn scattered information into actionable, strategic advantages in real time, every time.


THE ROLE

We're building the Advisory Intelligence Platform: Codat's client intelligence delivered inside the assistant a banker already uses (Microsoft Copilot first). Ask it anything about a client and it answers from the client's real books. Don't ask, and it still tells you what's changed, why it matters and what to do about it. Under it we're building the semantic layer, so every answer uses the same definitions, the signal layer that spots what's changed for a client, and the reasoning layer, a Codat-side LLM that turns those signals into advice. The first bank goes live this year. You'll be building the data and reasoning behind all of it.

This is a hands-on job for software engineers who want to build the systems a model reasons over, not configure a warehouse. Codat is AI-first, not AI bolted onto SaaS. The product lives inside the AI assistant our clients already use, and we build it the same way: agents do the repetitive work, engineers do the hard parts. You'll build it and you'll run it. Nobody hands it over the wall once it's live. You'll also get a real say in where it goes next. That means making your case to engineers, product and the commercial team, and bringing them along with you.




WHAT YOU'LL WORK ON

 - The semantic layer. Measures, dimensions and definitions the model is allowed to use, so every answer it gives is the same answer. Yours to grow, persona by persona.

 - The signal layer. Detecting what's changed for a client and surfacing it before the banker asks. You'll be designing and building this.

 - The reasoning layer. A Codat-side LLM that turns signals into advice. Our calculations are the ground truth it reasons over. You own the calculations the model relies on, and the names, definitions and structure that let it pick the right one.

 - The agents and MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers behind the assistant. What tools it has, how they're built, how they fail, and the evals that prove they work.

 - Everything from raw source data to the number the assistant quotes: the pipelines, services and data models, with the testing and observability to prove the number is right and the evals that catch the model quoting the wrong one.


YOU'LL PROBABLY HAVE

 - Built production systems from scratch, writing the code yourself rather than configuring managed services. You think about interfaces, failure modes and how the next person will change your code. If we ask about the hardest system you've built, you'll have a story ready.

 - Served data to an LLM and seen where it goes wrong: ambiguous definitions, poor retrieval, no evals. You know why "the model will work it out" isn't a data strategy.

 - Worked with data along the way, and liked it. You may never have been called a data engineer. You've built things that move, shape and serve data, and you know how they break, and how a model breaks on top of them.

 - Solid C#, Python or another backend language. Your code comes with tests, and you leave things tidier than you found them.

 - Depth in at least one of SQL, Spark, Databricks/Delta Lake, Dagster/Airflow/Temporal or dbt. Bonus if you've shaped any of them into something a model can query, through a metrics layer, metric views or an MCP server.

 - Time with CI/CD, Docker, cloud infrastructure (we're on Azure) and observability. Even better if you set them up for a team.

 - An interest in the business behind the data. If someone asks for a number the data can't support, you'll say so, and you'll build the guard-rail so the model says so too.

 - Treated your own workflow as something to engineer. AI has already taken over the repetitive parts of it, and you're the person others ask how to do the same.


HOW WE WORK

We're a small team with plenty to do. Things move fast: we'd rather ship something useful and improve it than polish it in private. What you build is yours from start to finish.

There’s no return-to-office mandate, and you can work hybrid or fully remote. We trust you to be around when the team needs you and to deliver what you said you would. What we don’t want is anyone staying online late to prove a point.

Collectors is the leading creator of innovative technology that provides value-added services for collectors worldwide. We grade, authenticate, vault, and sell millions of record-setting collectibles, all while modernizing and digitalizing the process to further our mission of helping collectors pursue their passions. We’re always on the lookout for talented people to join our growing team.

Our services span collectible trading cards, autographs, comic books, coins, video games, event tickets, and memorabilia. Our subsidiaries include PSA, PCGS, Beckett, SGC, and Card Ladder.

Since our founding in 1986, we have graded and authenticated millions of items. We employ more than 3000 people across our headquarters in Santa Ana, California and offices in New Jersey, Texas, Florida, Japan, Shanghai, Hong Kong, Canada, Mexico, Germany, the UK, and France.

As part of our interview process, we request that candidates have their cameras on during video interviews. This helps foster meaningful conversation and allows us to create an experience that closely resembles our standard working environment. Certain interview steps may take place by phone. For remote roles, and at our discretion, candidates may be asked to participate in an on-site interview as part of the final stages of the process.

We understand there may be occasional circumstances requiring accommodation and are happy to discuss them as needed. Your recruiter will be able to clarify expectations and answer any questions you have.

We’re transforming the collecting experience with technology that brings authentication, grading, and trading into the modern era. Our products are equalizing the playing field by providing tools that make complex research analytics — including pricing, scarcity reports, and historic sales data — accessible to every collector, old or new. Our engineering mission is to democratize technology while promoting innovation, collaboration, and continuous learning throughout the organization. We're seeking engineers to utilize advanced technology in agile settings, with a focus on improving the customer experience for every collector.

We’re looking for a Staff Platform Engineer to join our Platform Engineering team and help make every engineer at Collectors more productive. This is a builder's role for an expert software generalist with systems depth: you'll design and ship the internal platforms, paved paths, and custom tooling that product teams rely on to develop, deploy, and operate software quickly and safely. The problems you'll take on are often ambiguous and cross-cutting; we'll count on you to scope them, propose a direction, and drive them to completion. This role demands someone with both technical breadth and depth across various domains in the Platform Engineering space. The ideal candidate for this role not only knows how to ship code but writes code themselves and knows how a delightful end-to-end AI-enabled SDLC should operate.

Remote or hybrid candidates will also be considered. We believe that there is significant value in in-person collaboration. If you live within a 1 hour commuting distance to one of our offices, you will be required to be onsite most of the time. This will be discussed further as part of the recruiting process.

What You’ll Do:

• Build the paved path. Design, build, and operate the internal platforms that engineers use every day - CI/CD pipelines, developer environments, deployment workflows, and shared services - and continuously reduce the friction between "code written" and "value shipped."
• Create custom tooling that multiplies the team. Identify repetitive, error-prone, or slow engineering workflows and replace them with automation and self-service tools that generalize beyond a single use case.
• Bring AI into the engineering workflow. Prototype and productionize AI-assisted capabilities - from LLM-powered code modification and migration automation to agentic workflows for operational tasks - treating them as real software systems with evaluation, observability, and guardrails, not just prompts.
• Own problems end-to-end in ambiguous spaces. Take loosely defined, high-priority platform challenges from discovery through design, implementation, rollout, and adoption, making pragmatic build-vs-buy and speed-vs-durability tradeoffs along the way.
• Strengthen core infrastructure. Contribute to our cloud and container foundations (Kubernetes, infrastructure-as-code, networking, observability), improving the reliability, scalability, and cost-efficiency of the systems other teams build on.
• Drive adoption with data. Instrument the platforms you build, define success metrics, and use telemetry and direct partnership with product teams to guide what gets built next.
• Communicate and collaborate. Write clear design documents and tradeoff analyses, embed with partner teams to understand their pain points, and influence engineering practices across the organization without relying on formal authority.

Who You Are:

Must Have

• An experienced engineer with 10+ years building, shipping, and operating production software, ideally with meaningful time spent in platform, infrastructure, developer experience, or similarly leverage-oriented roles.
• An expert software generalist with systems knowledge. You're comfortable moving across backend services, automation pipelines, infrastructure, and internal tools, and you know when to go deep.
• Experience holistically owning complex and broad Developer Platforms. You know what teams need and anticipate that in every new feature you develop and ship.
• Fluent in at least one modern language commonly used for platform work (such as Python or TypeScript) and experienced with cloud infrastructure (AWS preferred), containers and Kubernetes, infrastructure-as-code, and modern CI/CD systems.
• A hands-on builder with AI. You've integrated LLMs or agent-based automation into real engineering workflows - shipping working tools, not just experiments - and you stay current on where the technology is heading.
• Energized by ambiguity. You can take a fuzzy problem statement, break it down, propose a plan, and execute - course-correcting quickly as you learn.
• Product-minded about internal customers. You treat fellow engineers as users, care about the usability of what you ship, and measure success by adoption and outcomes rather than output.
• An excellent communicator. Your design docs, runbooks, and postmortems are clear, and you build trust with partner teams through consistent, low-drama delivery.
• Pragmatic about operations. You take ownership from design through deployment and on-call, and you leave systems better documented and more reliable than you found them.

Nice to Have:
• Experience with developer portals, service catalogs, or fleet/dependency management systems.
• Experience running large-scale code migration or modernization efforts.
• Familiarity with evaluation and observability practices for AI-powered systems
• Bachelor’s Degree or relevant hands-on industry experience

Job Description

Purpose 
To lead the development of robust pricing models and global strategic pricing guidelines that enable consistent, data-driven and profitable commercial decisions. The role partners closely with Product, Operations, Commercial, Technology and Finance to guide the full discovery, design, development and operationalisation of pricing approaches, from initial opportunity definition through to scalable implementation, governance and performance monitoring.

Key responsibilities
Pricing modelling and commercial analysis
· Develop, own and continuously improve pricing models for new and existing products, propositions, clients, markets and commercial structures.
· Build transparent unit-economics models covering price, volume, product and channel mix, direct cost, network cost, service levels, client terms, implementation costs, taxation assumptions and margin.
· Create scenario, sensitivity, break-even and risk analysis to quantify the impact of alternative pricing structures and commercial assumptions.
· Assess discounts, rebates, minimum commitments, tiers, bundles, indexation, currency exposure and other contractual levers to protect sustainable margin.
· Translate complex data and assumptions into clear recommendations, decision ranges and approval materials for senior stakeholders.
· Validate model inputs with accountable functional owners and maintain clear documentation, version control and auditability of assumptions.
Global strategic pricing guidelines and governance
· Develop and maintain global strategic pricing principles, methodologies, guardrails and approval guidance that balance growth, client value, competitiveness and profitability.
· Define consistent approaches for price architecture, floor pricing, target margins, discounting, deal exceptions, indexation, market adjustments and cost pass-through.
· Create reusable global pricing tools, templates and playbooks, with controlled flexibility for regional market conditions, product maturity and client requirements.
· Establish governance for model ownership, data sources, assumption approval, pricing exceptions and periodic review of pricing guidelines.
· Partner with regional Commercial Finance and Commercial teams to embed global guidelines, capture market feedback and identify where guidance should evolve.
· Monitor adherence to approved pricing principles and surface material margin risks, inconsistencies or recurring exception themes.
Pricing discovery and solution development
· Lead the pricing workstream through the full discovery process, clarifying the client or business problem, proposition, customer journey, operational model, cost drivers, data requirements and commercial objectives.
· Work with Product to define the proposition, feature set, packaging, value drivers, target segments and monetisation options.
· Work with Operations and network teams to map delivery processes, capacity constraints, service standards, supplier economics, operational dependencies and true cost-to-serve.
· Coordinate input from Commercial, Technology, Tax, Legal, Data and Finance so that pricing design reflects end-to-end solution requirements and risks.
· Convert discovery findings into testable pricing hypotheses, model options and clear decision criteria, highlighting assumptions that require validation before launch.
· Guide iterative development by updating pricing and unit economics as the proposition, operating model and delivery requirements are refined.
Operationalising pricing
· Guide the development of an executable pricing operating model, including data capture, calculation logic, quoting, approvals, contracting, billing, settlement, reporting and controls.
· Partner with Product, Operations and Technology to translate pricing requirements into business rules, system requirements, process ownership and implementation plans.
· Define the minimum data, master data standards and control points required to apply prices accurately and consistently across markets and channels.
· Support pilot design and readiness reviews, ensuring operational feasibility, pricing accuracy, margin visibility and clear exception handling before scale-up.
· Develop handover materials, user guidance and training for teams responsible for quoting, approving, contracting, billing and monitoring pricing.
· Establish post-launch measurement against the approved business case, with feedback loops to improve pricing logic, cost assumptions and operational execution.
Pricing performance and continuous improvement
· Define pricing effectiveness measures, including realised price, margin, discount levels, cost-to-serve, exception rates and performance against approved business cases.
· Build reporting requirements that provide visibility of pricing performance and identify leakage caused by commercial terms, operational delivery, data quality or system execution.
· Conduct periodic reviews of models and guidelines using actual performance, market learning, product changes and updated cost inputs.
· Identify opportunities to simplify, automate and standardise pricing analysis and decision-making while maintaining appropriate governance.
Maintain a structured repository of pricing models, assumptions, approvals, guidelines and lessons learned

Knowledge, skills and experience required

ROLE OVERVIEW

As a Sales Engineer, you will lead the technical components of the sales process. You will partner closely with Account Executives and prospective customers to design integration approaches, evaluate technical fit, and demonstrate how Constructor’s platform drives measurable business impact.

This role combines technical architecture design, consultative discovery, and cross-functional collaboration. You will act as a bridge between customer engineering teams and Constructor’s Product and Engineering teams.

This is not a demo-heavy role. Account Executives perform the majority of demonstrations at Constructor. This role requires architectural thinking, integration planning, and consultative problem-solving.

 
 


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES


TECHNICAL SALES & SOLUTION DESIGN

 - Lead technical discovery and solution design for prospective customers

 - Design and document integration architectures (APIs, ecommerce platforms, PIM, CMS, data pipelines)

 - Develop and support tailored Proof Schedules (lightweight POCs)

 - Deliver technical presentations to both business and technical stakeholders

 - Serve as primary technical advisor during evaluation cycles

 - Troubleshoot and triage APIs, SDKs, and integration patterns

 - Willingness to tinker and build demo prototypes and tooling

 - Build and present compelling custom technical demonstrations and integration blueprints tailored to each sales opportunity

 - Support RFP and RFI responses


CROSS-FUNCTIONAL COLLABORATION

 - Partner with Product and Engineering to surface prospective customer feedback to influence product roadmap and integration strategy

 - Contribute insights to the roadmap and the go-to-market strategy

 - Support enablement and training for sales teams

 - Help refine documentation, processes, and best practices within the SE function


MARKET & INDUSTRY ENGAGEMENT

 - Stay current on ecommerce trends, AI/ML advancements, and the competitive landscape

 - Represent Constructor in prospect meetings, partner engagements, field events, and other industry engagements

 - Build strong relationships with prospective customer technical stakeholders (architects, engineers, delivery teams)

 
 


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS & SKILLS

 - 3+ years of experience in technical Solutions Engineering, Sales Engineering, Pre-Sales Architect, or Technical Pre-Sales roles

 - Deep hands-on experience with API-first platforms: comfortable working directly with REST APIs, JSON data structures, webhooks, and SDK integration patterns, and able to troubleshoot them with Postman or similar tools

 - Working knowledge of JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, or similar languages, enough to read integration code, debug client-side implementations, and build lightweight prototypes or demo tooling

 - Experience designing and running custom demos or pilots with clear, business-aligned success criteria

 - Hands-on experience with coding agents to automate workflows, amplify impact, and execute at scale

 - Ability to read the room, tailor your communication to diverse audiences, and identify detractors, champions, and key decision-makers

 - Strong written and verbal communication, with a track record of producing clear technical documentation and explaining complex ideas to developers, architects, and C-suite executives alike

 - Ability to effectively articulate complex ideas to both technical and non-technical audiences

 - Ability to empathize with prospects’ challenges and goals

 - Skilled listener with innate curiosity

 - Passionate about innovative technology, technical sales, and articulating value to prospects

 - Enjoys working with prospects and is comfortable interacting with C-suite executives from both technical and business perspectives

 - Professional proficiency in Italian, French,Spanish, German is a plus

 
 


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Experience in enterprise ecommerce or retail technology environments

 - Hands-on familiarity with at least two major ecommerce platforms, including how each handles catalog structure, extensions, and headless versus templated frontends

 - Deep understanding of data mapping between backend systems such as PIM, ERP, or legacy search indexes into a new target schema, possibly including product and variant structures, facets, attributes, and pricing logic

 - Working knowledge of search and discovery concepts

 - Experience supporting security reviews and procurement requirements, including GDPR, data processing agreements, data residency, and ISO 27001 or SOC 2 questionnaires

 - Ability to build business value models that connect search improvements to revenue, conversion, or average order value

 - Exposure to conversational or agentic shopping experiences, or retail media and sponsored product programs

 - Multilingual: Professional proficiency in languages other than English

 
 


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - Prospects clearly understand technical integration paths

 - Proof Schedules (a lightweight PoC) align tightly with business outcomes

 - Technical objections are addressed proactively and effectively

 - Sales cycles are accelerated through a strong technical partnership

 - Product and Engineering receive actionable, structured market feedback

 - Qualitative (peer and prospect feedback) and quantitative (sales metrics and customer health scores) feedback will be positive and ideally, excellent

 
 


WORKING STYLE

 - A builder mindset that is proactive in creating structure in ambiguous environments

 - Highly collaborative with a strong sense of ownership and autonomy

You will:

•     Lead multiple implementations end to end, both new-customer onboardings and additional-product rollouts for existing customers, from kickoff through integration, testing, and activation.

•     Take accountability for the outcome of every implementation, coordinating Constructor resources, customer resources, and partners, against a single shared plan.

•     Ensure clean handoffs into implementation from Sales and out of implementation to Customer Success and Support.

•     Maintain implementation plans and reporting in our systems of record so schedule, duration, and status roll up cleanly across your portfolio.

• Threat hunting and identification of attacker activity, using EDR and agent-led forensic tooling, to inform the investigation and containment activities 
• Perform live compromise assessments for organisations who suspect live and ongoing system intrusion.

Preferred Qualifications and specialist skills

You will report to the CTO and manage a growing team of gameplay engineers. You will make technical design decisions, stay hands-on with implementation, and represent the gameplay engineering discipline across the studio in production planning, design reviews, and resourcing decisions. 
We are in early production. The studio has been running for three years, but core gameplay systems including combat, traversal, abilities, progression, and multiplayer interaction are still being architected and prototyped. You will be making foundational technical decisions that define how the game feels, scales, and evolves over years of live service.

## Your Role

### People Leadership and Team Development

- Manage a growing team of gameplay engineers as the team scales through production: set priorities, assign work, balance workload, and run regular 1:1s focused on progress, career development, and honest feedback.

- Lead performance reviews and goal setting aligned to production milestones and individual development plans. Identify skill gaps and address them through coaching, stretch assignments, or training.

- Represent the gameplay engineering discipline in cross-discipline leads meetings, production planning, and resourcing conversations. Advocate for team needs and capacity.

- Foster a team culture of technical rigour, clean code practices, and collaborative problem solving.

- Support hiring as the team grows: contribute to job descriptions, design technical assessments, and participate in interview loops.

### Gameplay Systems and Implementation

- Own the technical design and implementation of core gameplay systems in Unreal Engine 5, including combat, traversal, abilities, player interaction, and progression mechanics.

- Architect gameplay systems for a persistent MMO context: server-authoritative logic, client prediction, ability replication, and state synchronisation across distributed server infrastructure.

- Collaborate closely with game design and level design to translate design intent into robust, tuneable, and extensible gameplay code. Build systems that designers can iterate on without requiring engineering support for every change.

- Stay hands-on with C++ and Blueprint implementation. Build, profile, and iterate alongside your engineers, establishing technical quality benchmarks and code architecture patterns.

- Work with animation, VFX, and audio teams to integrate gameplay systems with presentation layers: ability visuals, hit feedback, audio cues, and UI responses.

### Technical Architecture and Performance

- Define coding standards, architecture patterns, and review processes for gameplay code. Ensure the codebase remains maintainable and extensible as the team and feature set grow.

- Profile and optimise gameplay systems for MMO-scale performance: tick budgets, replication bandwidth, ability processing in dense combat scenarios, and memory management.

- Collaborate with online services and network engineering to ensure gameplay systems work reliably under real-world latency and server load conditions.

- Work with production to manage scope, schedules, and task breakdowns for gameplay engineering work. Contribute to milestone planning, sprint scoping, and capacity forecasting.

- Use playtesting observations and telemetry data to identify technical issues with gameplay feel, responsiveness, and fairness.

### Must-Haves

- 7+ years in game development, with at least one shipped title in a gameplay engineering or gameplay lead role.

- 2+ years of direct people management: running 1:1s, setting goals, conducting performance reviews, and developing team members.

- Strong C++ proficiency with production experience in Unreal Engine, including Gameplay Ability System, replication, and Blueprint integration.

- Experience building gameplay systems for multiplayer or online games, with a working understanding of server authority, client prediction, and state replication.

- Demonstrated ability to translate game design concepts into well-architected, extensible, and performant code.

- Strong communication and documentation skills, with proven experience collaborating across disciplines (design, art, animation, audio, network) to ship integrated gameplay features.

### Nice-to-Haves

- Experience shipping at least one MMO or persistent online world from production through live service.

- Experience with Unreal Engine’s Gameplay Ability System (GAS) at scale, including custom ability tasks, gameplay effects, and attribute sets.

- Familiarity with AI systems for NPC behaviour, encounter scripting, or enemy design.

- Experience with data-driven design approaches where designers author gameplay content through configuration rather than code changes.

- Exposure to anti-cheat considerations and exploit mitigation in competitive or economy-driven multiplayer games.

### About You

- You lead by investing in people. You find genuine satisfaction in watching your team grow and you actively develop the engineers around you.

- You care about how systems feel to the player, not just whether they function correctly. Frame data, input responsiveness, and gameplay feel matter to you.

- You are comfortable working through ambiguity. Early production means not everything is defined yet, and you see that as an opportunity to shape the right technical approach.

- You balance technical elegance with delivery pragmatism. You know when to architect for the future and when to prototype quickly to validate design.

- You work autonomously in a remote environment, proactively keeping your team aligned and your stakeholders informed.
