Your opportunity

Janus Henderson is undertaking a firm-wide AI transformation to become the most technologically sophisticated asset manager in the industry. Our AI capability sits in a single centralised function under the Head of AI, and AI Technology is the part of it that builds, governs, and runs the software.

AI Engineering is the core product and platform engineering team within it. Where Forward Deployed Engineering embeds with a business unit to solve one team’s problem, AI Engineering builds the enterprise products every other team depends on: Nexus, our agentic workspace, where employees build, test, run, and manage governed AI applications, agents, and shared skills; Accio, our centralised MCP server, which acts as a passthrough and logic centre for enterprise datasets, consuming other MCP servers and presenting them through one governed interface; and the orchestration, evaluation, and observability services beneath Libros and PRISM, two of the projects we are delivering with Percepta.

As a Senior Applied AI Engineer, reporting to the Principal AI Engineer, you will lead the delivery of major parts of that estate — designing and building agentic applications and platform services, taking them through evaluation and our AI governance checkpoints into production, then owning them once live. You will set implementation patterns alongside AI Architecture, review other engineers’ work, and be the person the team turns to when a production system behaves in a way nobody predicted. You will also work beside Percepta’s engineers, making sure each platform enters service with a design the team understands and more than one person able to extend it.

You will also own the end-to-end build of business applications for specific parts of the firm — not only the horizontal products every team shares, but targeted applications built on the AI stack for a named business area, carried from first requirement through to a supported production service. Distribution is the first focus. Much of this work is deliberate SaaS decommissioning: where a capability currently bought as a SaaS subscription can be built in-house instead, you own that build end-to-end and see the displaced product retired, so the firm consolidates onto governed, in-house capability rather than paying for overlapping tools. You will take the same approach into other business areas — trading, investment risk, client servicing, and operations among them — choosing the builds where owning the application gives the firm more control, lower cost, or capability no vendor sells.

Your toolkit spans Python and SQL, LLMs and agent frameworks, MCP, Azure AI Foundry through the AI Team’s model gateway, Snowflake and Microsoft Fabric, and Azure with Terraform, Docker, and CI/CD. AI Engineering is being established for the first time here, so you will shape how the team works rather than inherit a settled routine.

What success looks like

• The products and services you own are in production, used by real teams, and operate with clear ownership, telemetry, and evaluation results.

• What you build gets reused. Other engineers, agents, and applications consume it through Accio or as a skill, tool, or connector on Nexus rather than building their own.

• Platforms built jointly with Percepta transfer into our ownership with maintainable designs and a team that can extend them without external help.

• Evaluation, observability, and control are built into what you ship rather than bolted on before release.

Your responsibilities

Build and run our AI products and platform

• Design, build, and productionise AI products and shared platform services, taking a workstream end to end and owning it through to live running.

• Build for reuse, turning capability proven in one product into shared components, libraries, skills, tools, MCP servers, and connectors.

• Implement infrastructure as code, own CI/CD pipelines, and accept services into operation only when ownership, controls, and support are clear.

• Investigate incidents and defects in the services you own, lead recovery, carry fixes through to the underlying cause, and act as L3 escalation.

Engineer agents, orchestration, and the application layer

• Build agentic applications and workflows covering agent design, prompt and context engineering, tool use, memory, retrieval, and human-in-the-loop controls.

• Implement model selection, routing, and fallback through the model gateway, handling provider change without hiding differences in capability, cost, or behaviour.

• Build the orchestration layer that long-running and multi-step agents depend on, covering permissions, workload isolation, safe execution, and the applications built on it.

• Test the claims made for new models, frameworks, and patterns before recommending we adopt them.

Make enterprise data AI-ready

• Build governed, AI-ready views, indexes, semantic context, and connectors over Snowflake, enterprise platforms, APIs, and external providers.

• Extend Accio so new datasets and downstream MCP servers are reachable through one governed interface rather than one-off integrations.

• Build ingestion pipelines and data models where source data does not arrive usable, while canonical source ownership stays with the relevant Technology team.

• Own lineage, quality, and freshness for the data your products depend on, and implement least-privilege access for users, agents, tools, and service identities.

Build business-area applications and decommission SaaS

• Own the end-to-end build of targeted business applications on the AI stack — Distribution first, then areas such as trading, investment risk, client servicing, and operations — delivered for a named business owner rather than for every team at once.

• Drive SaaS decommissioning: where a bought subscription can be replaced by an in-house build, own the delivery of that replacement end-to-end, see the displaced product retired, and work with Procurement and Finance to consolidate the licence.

• Prioritise the builds where in-house ownership gives the firm more control, lower cost, or capability no vendor sells, and reuse existing Accio datasets, skills, and connectors instead of rebuilding them per application.

• Take each application through the same evaluation, controls, and release evidence as the shared products, and own its support and lifecycle once live or hand it to a clear owner.

Build in evaluation and control, and work with the team

• Build evaluation and regression suites for models, prompts, agents, and platform changes, meet the agreed thresholds before release, and instrument what you build for quality, safety, reliability, latency, drift, usage, and cost.

• Implement the controls defined by AI Governance Implementation and AI Security as code and secure defaults, and produce release evidence proportionate to the risk of the use case, generated by the platform rather than assembled after the event.

• Work alongside Percepta engineers on Libros, PRISM, and the wider estate, holding joint work to our engineering standards and raising maintainability problems while they are still cheap to fix.

• Mentor AI Engineers through pairing, design discussion, and code review, and help establish the team’s engineering standards, agentic SDLC, and definition of done.

• Work with AI Architecture to turn reference patterns into implementations teams use, partner with Forward Deployed Engineering so proven solutions become supported shared capability, and feed adoption data from the AI Enablement Partners into the backlog.

Must have skills

• At least six years in software, data, or platform engineering, with a track record of shipping and operating production systems rather than prototypes.

• Production experience with LLM applications and agentic systems, covering prompt and context engineering, agent development, retrieval, tool use, evaluation, and deployment at scale.

• Strong Python and SQL, with the judgement to write code others can maintain and extend.

• Hands-on experience building agentic capability such as MCP servers, tools, skills, or connectors for other systems and agents to consume.

• Hands-on experience with a major cloud, ideally Azure, including containers or serverless compute, infrastructure as code, CI/CD, identity, RBAC, and secret management.

• Experience owning services in production — monitoring, incident investigation, upgrades, lifecycle management — and establishing evaluation and observability for AI systems.

• Good judgement in a regulated environment, translating security, privacy, risk, and audit requirements into working technical controls.

• Experience mentoring engineers and leading technical work without relying on reporting authority, and clear communication with engineers, control functions, and business stakeholders.

Nice to have skills

• Asset management or financial services domain knowledge, particularly the investment process, distribution, or front-office workflows.

• Azure AI Foundry, Azure OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, model gateways, inference routing, or agent orchestration platforms.

• Snowflake, Microsoft Fabric / OneLake, or comparable governed enterprise data platforms.

• TypeScript or a second production language, and front-end experience for user-facing AI applications.

• Experience building internal developer platforms or golden-path patterns used by other engineering teams, or taking partner-built software into internal ownership.

### The role

Our machine learning is only as trustworthy as the data we validate it against. That validation data is called **ground truth**: verified, real-world information about how buildings are actually constructed and insulated, covering their walls, windows, and roofs.

A rich source of ground truth already exists in the documents produced during building surveys. **Retrofit assessment reports** give us construction and insulation detail across walls, windows, and roofs, while **borescope reports** tell us the cavity fill insulation status of a wall. These are dense, unstructured PDFs full of exactly the information we need. The problem is that this information is locked inside documents in formats that vary from one assessor to the next, and none of it is machine-readable.

Your mission is to unlock it. You will build the pipeline that turns these messy PDFs into clean, structured, queryable data inside our platform, and connect it to our existing image annotations so it can be used to validate our algorithms.

The end goal we are working towards: someone uploads any of these assessment or survey PDFs, and the relevant data is automatically extracted into structured, processable form, correctly, every time

Build the core extraction pipeline, writing Python to parse retrofit assessment and borescope reports across varying layouts and terminology, using LLM APIs and document-extraction tooling to get accurate results faster.

Support the ground truth data collection campaign as needed.

Partner closely with the engineering team to get feedback on technical decisions and integrate your work into the wider platform.

Quantitative Analyst Intern - Digital Assets Market Making (HFT) - Brussels



Since 2017, Keyrock has been a change-maker in digital assets. We're a global, remote-first team of 200+ people across 40+ nationalities, with hubs in Brussels, London, Paris and New York.

 

We provide liquidity across 80+ centralized and decentralized exchanges - a position cemented by our Series C, led by SC Ventures. Today we run a full spectrum of capital markets businesses across centralized and on-chain venues: market making, high-frequency trading, options, OTC, DeFi trading desks, advisory, and asset management.

 

We're building toward the agentic investment banking capabilities for the era of digital finance. A proprietary agentic layer runs the mechanics of the market, so our people can focus on the work code cannot do: the deal, the relationship, and the judgement.



We're not just envisioning the future of finance - we're building it.




ABOUT THE INTERNSHIP PROGRAM

Our internship programme gives early-career talent the opportunity to build practical skills, contribute to meaningful projects and learn alongside experienced colleagues in digital finance.

Typically lasting six months and based in our Brussels office (London possible), each internship includes hands-on experience, clear learning goals and dedicated guidance and regular feedback. We look for curiosity, relevant foundational skills, deep, active interest and passion for digital assets and the potential to grow exponentially with us - you don’t need to arrive with all the answers. Where performance, business needs and available opportunities align, an internship may lead to a permanent role, though this is not guaranteed.

We are looking for 3-4 high-caliber Quantitative Analyst Interns to sit within our Strategic Market Making (CeFi and DeFi), Credit and Corporate Development desks/teams (see other openings on our career page for details).



Application deadline: 30 November 2026
Start date: 1 March 2027


Selection process:

 - Interview with Talent Acquisition representative

 - Interview with Hiring Manager

 - Recruitment Challenge

 
 

The role 

About Strategic Market Making Desk
Our Strategic Proprietary Market Making team researches and deploys systematic trading strategies across centralized digital asset venues. We study how order-book dynamics, fragmented liquidity, exchange design and participant behaviour shape pricing, execution and risk.

As a Quantitative Analyst Intern within the HFT track, you will work alongside quantitative researchers, traders and engineers to analyse market and trading data, test hypotheses through backtesting and simulation, and build tools that improve strategy performance and risk visibility. You will investigate how fair value, liquidity, latency, queue position, fees and adverse selection affect real-world execution across venues.

 

This is a technical and applied internship. We are looking for someone who combines strong quantitative reasoning and coding skills with a detailed understanding of electronic markets. You should be curious about how exchanges work beneath the interface and able to connect market microstructure to trading outcomes.



Key Responsibilities - Quantitative Analyst (HFT)

 - Analyse multi-venue top-of-book and depth data, trades, orders, fills and cancels to study liquidity, price discovery and execution quality.

 - Build and validate latency-aware, event-driven backtests with explicit assumptions around maker/taker execution, queue position, fill probability, fees and cancellations.

 - Measure spread capture, forward markouts, fees and adverse selection, and investigate how execution quality changes across venues, instruments and market regimes.

 - Build reusable Python tools and data pipelines using modern columnar analysis and SQL for strategy research, performance attribution and monitoring.

 - Study cross-venue price discovery, lead–lag relationships, fair-value construction and spot–perpetual basis while accounting for data staleness, instrument design and settlement-currency differences.

 - Support live strategies through PnL, inventory and exposure analysis, post-trade review and investigation of unexpected performance.

 - Evaluate liquidity-program economics by balancing execution quality, market share, fees and incentives, and work with traders and engineers to translate research into robust production improvements.

 - Present findings clearly, including assumptions, limitations, risks and recommended next steps.




WHO YOU ARE/KEY REQUIREMENTS - QUANTITATIVE ANALYST (HFT)

 - Quantitative and coding foundations: You are pursuing or recently completed a degree in mathematics, computer science, engineering, physics, quantitative finance or a related field. You are proficient in Python for data analysis, ideally including Polars or similar columnar tools, and comfortable with SQL, Git and command-line workflows. Experience with ClickHouse or another analytical database is valuable.

 - Electronic market structure: You understand limit order books, order types, maker/taker mechanics, matching and priority rules, spreads, market depth and how trades move prices.

 - Execution awareness: You can reason about the order lifecycle from signal to acknowledgement and fill, including exchange APIs, latency, queue position, partial fills, cancellations, fees, slippage and adverse selection.

 - Digital asset markets: You understand key differences between spot and perpetual futures, including basis, funding, leverage, liquidation risk, settlement currencies and residual exposure.

 - Quantitative reasoning: You are comfortable with probability, statistics, time-series analysis and evaluating noisy results without overstating significance.

 - Hands-on curiosity: Ideally, you have built or analysed something yourself—such as an order-book study, trading bot, exchange connector, backtest, execution simulator or market-data pipeline.

 - Trading judgement: You naturally question whether an apparent edge survives latency, fees, market impact, changing liquidity and real execution constraints.

 - Ownership and communication: You can structure an ambiguous problem, test assumptions and communicate findings and limitations clearly in English.



 

Nice to Have

 - Experience working with exchange WebSocket/REST APIs and asynchronous market-data pipelines

 - Exposure to Rust or another systems programming language

 - Experience with tick/order-book data, event-driven simulation or execution modelling

 - A technical project demonstrating sustained interest in systematic trading or market microstructure

 

Our offer

 - A 6 month paid internship at world-renowned digital assets company with accommodation provided for entirety or part of it

 - The opportunity to learn about digital assets and blockchain from a 30,000 ft view of the entire ecosystem

 - Working from one of Brussels newest, nicest and most advanced office spaces

 - A global, collaborative and tech-driven environment.

 - Autonomy & Impact - our flat structure means you can contribute your ideas from day one and help shape the foundation that will power Keyrock’s future business.

 - Culture of Excellence - we value nimbleness, drive for success, owner mentality and collaboration.

 - Opportunity to leave your mark and start your career in one of the most reputable companies in the digital assets world

 - We are envisioning for the internship to be based pre-dominantly in Brussels. It is possible for a selected candidate to be based in London, UK, provided at least 1-2 months onboarding period would be spent in Brussels together with the rest of the interns cohort.

 

Our recruitment philosophy

We value self-awareness and powerful communication skills in our recruitment process. We seek fiercely passionate people who understand themselves and their career goals. We're after those with the right skills and a conscious choice to join our field. The perfect fit? A crypto enthusiast who’s driven, collaborative, acts with ownership and delivers solid, scalable outcomes.

As an employer we are committed to building a positive and collaborative work environment. We welcome employees of all backgrounds, and hire, reward and promote entirely based on merit and performance.

Due to the nature of our business and external requirements, we perform background checks on all potential employees, passing which is a prerequisite to join Keyrock. 


https://keyrock.com/careers/

SENIOR DATA ENGINEER




ABOUT KEYROCK

Since our beginnings in 2017, we've grown to be a leading change-maker in the digital asset space, renowned for our partnerships and innovation.

Today, we partner with over 250 team members around the world. Our diverse team hails from 42 nationalities, with backgrounds ranging from self-taught DeFi natives to PhDs. Predominantly remote, we have hubs in London, Brussels, and Singapore, and host regular online and offline hangouts to keep the crew tight.

We are trading on more than 80 trading venues, and working with a wide array of asset issuers. As a well-established market maker, our distinctive expertise led us to expand rapidly. Today, our services span market making, options trading, high-frequency trading, OTC, and DeFi trading desks.

But we’re more than a service provider. We’re an initiator. We're pioneers in adopting the Rust Development language for our algorithmic trading, and champions of its use in the industry. We support the growth of Web3 startups through our Accelerator Program. We upgrade ecosystems by injecting liquidity into promising DeFi, RWA, and NFT protocols. And we push the industry's progress with our research and governance initiatives.

At Keyrock, we're not just envisioning the future of digital assets. We're actively building it.




ABOUT THE TEAM AND WHY THE ROLE EXISTS

The Central Data Team (CDT) is only a few months old, but data has been Keyrock's lifeblood since day one. We're now building the Keyrock Data Platform to give Keyrockers, and the AI agents working alongside them, the data and context they need to act fast and autonomously within agreed boundaries and aligned with our shared goals. Doing that means taking data from across the company and making sense of it in real time for all the functions that depend on it: trading desks, wealth and asset management, product, risk, finance, compliance, and research to name a few.

You'd be one of the early hires in CDT and we expect you to contribute to most of the bigger decisions and build work. The standards we settle on and the way the team ends up working are still open.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Build streaming and batch pipelines that ingest, normalise, and distribute market, trading, and portfolio data, resilient to feed and exchange failures.

 - Build the self-serve tooling (SDKs, patterns, templates, AI agents) so other teams publish, consume, and build on data products without waiting on us.

 - Own data contracts and schema evolution. Keep schema changes from turning into multi-team coordination events.

 - Design the lakehouse and time-series layer around consumer query patterns.

 - Build and evolve the Data Governance and Data Quality Framework: stale-feed detection, schema validation, range checks, idempotent writes, lineage, ownership, self-healing.

 - Build the derived analytics the business runs on: cross-exchange spreads, VWAP at depth, order book microstructure for the desks; portfolio views, exposure, performance for wealth and asset management.

 - Make observability, cost, and performance first-class from day one.

 - Treat infrastructure as code (Docker, Terraform, CI/CD) alongside our Central Infrastructure Team.

 - Work in the open: write things down, partner closely with Architecture, Infrastructure, Platform, and the rest of the teams.




WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

Tools matter less to us than how you think about problems. That said, here's the shape of the person we have in mind.

Engineering Craft

 - 8+ years of building production data systems that other people rely on.

 - Strong proficiency in Python and SQL: not just being able to write a query, but being able to reason about what the engine is doing with it.

 - Code that's easy for someone else to read, test, and delete later.

 - Strong understanding of data modelling for both streaming and analytical workloads.

 - Efficiency, quality, idempotency, and observability are taken seriously by default.

Systems Design

 - You've designed and operated streaming systems on Kafka, Redpanda, MSK, or Kinesis, and you have opinions about partitioning, consumer groups, offsets, and schema registries.

 - You've used a time-series store in production (ClickHouse ideally; TimescaleDB, QuestDB, or similar are fine too) and can talk about table design as a function of query patterns.

 - You've worked with a lakehouse architecture and reason about table layout, partitioning, and compaction as design choices that shape query performance and storage cost.

 - You build for self-healing and idempotency. Reprocessing is safe, retries don't double-write, and the system recovers without a human in the loop.

Operational Readiness

 - Docker, Terraform, and CI/CD are how you work, not a separate "DevOps" thing.

 - You think about cost and performance early.

 - You instrument as you build: logs, metrics, and traces are part of the system from day one.

 - You design for data quality and governance up front covering contracts, validation, lineage, and ownership

How You Think and Work

 - You reason from first principles when a problem is new, stay pragmatic when it isn't, and update your view when you learn more.

 - You treat the trading desks, wealth and asset management, product, risk, finance, compliance, and research as customers of what you build, and communicate with them that way.

 - You optimise for outcomes over output. A smaller, simpler thing that ships and works beats a bigger thing that doesn't.

 - You take ownership end-to-end: design, ship, operate, improve.

 - You say what you think including when it's an unpopular take. You change your mind when the argument is better.

 - You make the people around you better. Reviews are real, juniors grow from working with you, and peers want to work with you again.

 - You're curious about how markets work. Data engineering on its own won't keep you interested here.

 - You're honest about what you know and what you don't, and quick to close the gap.

 - You understand financial market data: order books, trades, reference data, portfolios, exposures. Crypto, TradFi, or both are a strong plus.




NICE TO HAVE

 - Lakehouse experience with Apache Iceberg or Delta Lake.

 - Familiarity with DataHub or similar metadata/lineage platforms.

 - Rust. Some of our performance-critical services are written in it. Interest is welcome; fluency isn't required.




WHAT YOU’LL GET

 - A from-scratch mandate. You'll be among the first hires in CDT, and the platform, the standards, and the team culture are yours to shape with us.

 - Strong partners. Close working relationships with Architecture, Infrastructure, Platform, and the desks themselves. You won't be building data in a vacuum.

 - Autonomy on how you work. Flexible hours, remote-first, business-hours on-call shared across the team.

 - A competitive salary package, with various benefits.

job_title: Senior Site Reliability Engineer, AI-DNA, $100k/year USD
job_description:
When the alarm fires, you are the first responder — but by the time you reach it, the AI agents you built and maintain have already validated hypotheses against years of prior incidents, parsed the logs and code paths, found the failure pattern, and proposed — or applied — a remediation inside policy guardrails. Your job is the shift and the agents that run it: take the page, resolve what the agents could not, and make sure the next page of that kind handles itself. You operate an AI-native community and social engagement platform that the world's largest brands run their customer relationships on — where one outage is a brand-damaging event for a Fortune 100 company, so the standard is set there. You are a senior SRE who could run the whole operation by hand; the way this team works, you bake that expertise into the agents and runbooks instead of spending your life in a ticket queue.

## What you will be doing

- Own the shift as first responder — take the page, triage and resolve customer-impacting incidents on the platform you cover, and escalate to the tech lead when the blast radius warrants.
- Execute production changes safely — deploys, cost-optimization runbooks, and config changes from other teams run through the quality gates with a rollback ready before you start, and you pull it the moment a change goes off-plan.
- Build, operate, and maintain the AI agents that do the operations work — pre-triage, change-validation gates, permanent-fix chase, RCA drafting, auto-healing — and write the AI and human runbooks they run on. The harness is the product.
- Execute the ticket work — but measured on how well your agents make it scale, not how many tickets you personally close. Every one-off you solve by hand, you generalize so an agent handles the next one.

## What you will NOT be doing

- Closing tickets as the goal. Throughput is not your scoreboard; the leverage your agents create is. Hours into a queue instead of into the agents that drain it means you are off-strategy.
- Waiting to be told what to do. You pick up the page, find the next gap, and ship the fix. Nobody assigns you your day.
- Solving the same problem twice by hand. A one-off you do not generalize is unfinished work.
- Treating this as a credential or a résumé line. The bar is ownership, depth, and obsession — not titles. If you have never been deeply, sustainedly obsessed with a hard problem, this is a bad fit.

## Responsibilities

- Own the shift and the outcome on it — like a founder. You are first on the page. When something is down on your watch, that is your problem; you do not sleep peacefully through a customer outage.
- Build, operate, and maintain the agents that run the operation. New agents that catch a class of incident before it recurs, existing ones tuned higher, guardrails added when production teaches you something the spec missed. You build within the architecture the tech lead sets — and push back with a better idea when you have one.
- Protect production every time you touch it. When you run a deploy, a cost-optimization runbook, or a config change, you go through the quality gates, keep a tested rollback ready, and pull it the moment the change goes off-plan. You are a guardian of uptime, not only a responder to its loss.
- Find the root cause — not the symptom — and close the loop. A disciplined, structured investigation that separates symptom from cause; then the part most teams skip — identify the prevention, build it, and track it to done. The tech lead reviews your RCAs; you write them to a bar that needs little correction. An RCA whose fixes never ship is theater.
- Generalize relentlessly. You may solve a one-off to restore service, but you do not stop there — you turn it into an agent, a runbook, or a guardrail so the next occurrence handles itself. The scoreboard is what the agent surface can carry, not how fast you close tickets.
- Multiply the team, and write so the work survives you. Fix the underlying agent when it fails and share the fix as reusable rules, context, and skills; encode every procedure so an agent can retrieve it and the next responder is never starting cold. In an async team, an undocumented fix is a fix that doesn't exist.

## Requirements

- 5+ years operating SaaS at scale as a senior, on-call SRE — real first-responder time on production incidents, not just project or build work.
- Extreme ownership, fully self-directed. You run your shift like your own business, and you can answer "the hardest you have ever worked on something" with a story we can probe for an hour. Nobody assigns your day or checks your work; you challenge a standard with a better idea but never quietly ignore it. This team does not babysit — if you need to be managed, it is the wrong fit.
- Deep production scars — outages, incident management, hands-on troubleshooting. First on the bridge, diagnosis under pressure, the failure modes known from having lived them. Deep AWS at scale (multi-AZ, multi-account; not Azure-only, not greenfield); you run production change with gates and tested rollbacks and investigate to the actual root cause, symptom separated from cause. You could run it by hand — the point is you bake it into the agents.
- AI-native operator who multiplies. You delegate whole units of work to agents that verify their own output, fix the underlying capability when they fail, and share it so the team levels up — measured on leverage, not AI-usage %. Advanced across agentic tools (Claude Code, Codex, Warp, custom agents); when a new model ships, you are testing it that day, not next quarter.
- AWS Solutions Architect – Associate (or higher) — or a production track record that makes the certification redundant. Scars over badge, but a useful floor at this level.
- Fluent / advanced English — precise under pressure, on the bridge and in writing.
- Shift coverage is core, not occasional — on-call rotations and the shift window you are hired into, with the time-zone overlap that window requires. Reliability is a 24/7 outcome for the whole team, and you carry the share in your geographical area.
- OFAC-clear country of residence.

## Nice to Have

- Pioneer or builder voice in agentic SRE / AIOps — original posts, talks, open-source, or agents and tools you have built and shipped. - - Followers and reposters are not what we are looking for.
- A documented obsession with one hard thing outside of mainstream work — depth matters more than the title on the latest role.
- Modern observability / incident-response stacks (Grafana, Prometheus, OpsGenie, PagerDuty, Datadog) and Azure exposure alongside your AWS depth.
- Background in multi-tenant B2B SaaS at scale — community, social, customer-experience, observability, or AIOps platforms.

## What you will learn

- You will become one of the engineers who actually built agentic SRE — not read about it — on a platform the world's largest brands depend on, where AI agents are full members of your team and the runbooks you write run themselves. You will leave with hands-on agent-ops and incident experience the rest of the industry is still trying to hire.

## Working conditions

- Enterprise scale, startup cadence. Large-enterprise customers, footprint, and contractual stakes; a startup operating model — outcomes measured week over week, decisions in days, the playbook rewritten as the field moves. If you need a year to land the framework from your last role, this is not it.
- No token or tooling limits. The harness is the product, and we resource it that way — if the right answer is more compute, a better model, or a tool we have not bought, we buy it.

We're looking for a designer with strong design foundations and a sharp creative mind to join our London office, a short walk from London Bridge and Borough Market. Someone who can make a research report a pleasure to read, then turn around and visualise concepts and branded assets that land with clients and the families we're designing for.

# **Why this role, and why you**

Design is changing fast. AI can produce a hundred images in an afternoon. But volume isn’t judgement. Knowing which idea is right, why a layout works and how to make something feel considered matters more than ever.

Our work is changing too. It’s increasingly about creative solutions, art direction and concept visualisation. It’s also about turning complex insight and knowledge into work that’s clear, beautiful and genuinely useful.

So we’re not hiring against a checklist of software. We’re looking for a designer with strong fundamentals who uses them to think, not just to finish. You’ll have two to four years’ experience, be ready to own smaller briefs and be driven to grow into a senior role.

‍

# **What you’ll be doing**

- Design across a broad mix of digital formats:, social content, campaign assets, email and web pages, landing pages, and digital advertising
- Generate and design original creative ideas for branding, digital, social and campaign projects, presenting confidently to Senior Designer and Creative Director and, where needed, clients
- Designing reports, presentations and knowledge pieces that turn research and strategy into clear, engaging stories
- Using AI image and video tools to visualise ideas quickly, then art directing the output so it’s on brief, on brand and right for the audience
- Taking smaller briefs from first idea to finished artwork, with support from the senior members in the team
- Presenting and explaining your thinking to the team, and to clients as your confidence grows
- Working closely with researchers, strategists and producers so ideas are grounded in real insight about families
- Supporting new business pitches with concepts and visuals that help us win work
- Take the lead on KI’s brand and be the visual brand guardian
- Bringing new tools, references and ways of working into the studio, and sharing what you learn

# **Design first, ideas on top**

We’ll be clear about this: we’re looking for a strong designer who thinks creatively, not an ideas person who can design okay.

Your portfolio should show real craft first: confident typography, considered layouts and a clear sense of hierarchy. On top of that, we want to see how you think, from the interesting angle you found in a brief to the routes you explored before landing on the final one.

Figma, Adobe Creative Cloud and AI tools are how you get there, not what defines you. We care less about which tools you know and more about whether you know what good looks like and how to get to it.

‍

# **What you’ll bring**

### **Essential**

- Two to four years’ design experience in an agency, studio or in-house team
- Strong foundations in typography, layout, grids, hierarchy, colour and composition
- Creative and conceptual thinking, with the ability to find the angle in a brief and develop more than one route
- A good eye for art direction, with the ability to create and develop a distinctive look and feel and carry it consistently across a project
- Experience turning complex or information-heavy content into reports, presentations, editorial or infographics that are clear and engaging
- Confidence using Figma and Adobe Creative Cloud, especially Photoshop and Illustrator
- Clear communication, including the ability to explain the 'why' behind your work: why a piece of design works, or the thinking behind an approach
- Good organisation to manage several projects, respond well to feedback and hit deadlines
- Curiosity about where design is heading, and as much enthusiasm for a sharp idea as a beautifully crafted layout

### **Bonus**

- Experience working on brands for children and families
- Hands-on experience using AI image or video tools to explore and visualise ideas, and a critical eye for when the output is good enough and when it isn’t
- Motion, editing or 3D skills - please demonstrate in portfolio
- A point of view on how AI is changing creative work, including the questions it raises around originality, IP and responsibility

# **How we think about AI**

We see AI as a powerful part of the creative toolkit that helps us explore more ideas and visualise them faster. It doesn’t replace judgement, taste or craft, and it doesn’t replace the care we take when creating for children and families.

You’ll use it thoughtfully and responsibly, with respect for copyright, our clients’ brands and the audiences we design for.

What does a **Engineering Lead - Cloud/DevOps** do?

An Engineering Lead - Cloud/DevOps, also known as a DevOps Lead or an Engineering Manager with a DevOps focus, is a senior technical leader who oversees and manages DevOps techniques within a business. Their responsibilities often include, but are not limited to, the following:

- DevOps Strategy: Develop and implement a DevOps strategy aligned with the organization's business goals. This includes defining best practices, processes, and tools for software development, deployment, and operations.
- Team Leadership: Lead and manage a team of DevOps engineers, providing guidance, mentorship, and support. This involves setting team goals, managing workloads, and fostering a collaborative and innovative work environment.
- Infrastructure as Code (IaC): Promote the use of IaC principles and tools like Terraform, Ansible, or Puppet to automate the provisioning and management of infrastructure.
- CI/CD Implementation: Oversee the creation and maintenance of continuous integration and continuous deployment (CI/CD) pipelines, ensuring that software can be built, tested, and deployed efficiently and reliably.
- Tooling and Automation: Evaluate, select, and manage the use of DevOps tools and automation solutions, such as Jenkins, GitLab CI/CD, Docker, Kubernetes, and others. Implement automation for configuration management, testing, and deployment.
- Monitoring and Incident Response: Set up monitoring and alerting systems to track application and infrastructure performance. Develop incident response procedures to minimize downtime and resolve issues promptly.
- Security and Compliance: Collaborate with security teams to establish and enforce security best practices, identity and access management, and compliance requirements in the CI/CD pipeline and infrastructure.
- Collaboration with Development and Operations: Foster collaboration and communication between development and operations teams, breaking down silos and promoting a DevOps culture of shared responsibility.
- Capacity Planning and Scaling: Work on capacity planning to ensure systems can handle changes in demand and growth. Implement autoscaling and load balancing where necessary.
- Cost Optimization: Analyze cloud costs and identify opportunities for optimization, such as using reserved instances, right-sizing resources, and eliminating waste.
- Documentation and Training: Ensure comprehensive documentation of DevOps processes, best practices, and standards. Provide training to team members and other stakeholders.
- Performance Improvement: Continuously analyze and improve the efficiency and performance of the CI/CD pipeline, infrastructure, and development workflows.
- Vendor and Tool Selection: Make informed decisions about cloud service providers, DevOps tools, and technology stack choices.
- Risk Management: Identify and mitigate risks related to the DevOps environment, ensuring business continuity and data integrity.
- Stakeholder Communication: Effectively communicate DevOps initiatives, progress, and results to executive leadership, technical teams, and other stakeholders.
- Innovation: Stay up-to-date with emerging DevOps technologies and industry trends to assess their potential benefits for the organization.

Part of our Operations team and reporting to the Apprenticeships Manager, you will work with learners, their line managers and colleagues across curriculum and delivery to support engagement, timely progress and successful completion.

job_description:

 Embedded Software Engineer III – Dalgety Bay, Scotland 

POSITION: Embedded Software Engineer III – Dalgety Bay, Scotland
LOCATION: Dalgety Bay, Scotland, United Kingdom (On-site)

**The right to live and work in the UK is a must-have pre-requisite for this posting**

JOB PURPOSE:

The Embedded Software Engineer III contributes to the development and optimization of firmware and embedded software for Kopin’s microdisplay-based systems, including AR/VR HUDs, wearable display platforms, and related embedded products. This role requires strong proficiency in embedded systems, real-time software implementation, and hands-on experience with hardware/software integration on low-power embedded devices.

The role develops software for custom hardware platforms including ARM processors, microcontrollers, and FPGA-adjacent subsystems, and ensures robust, reliable operation across imaging, tracking, display-pipeline, control, and sensor-driven functions. This role works collaboratively across electrical, systems, optics, and mechanical engineering teams and participates throughout the full software development life cycle from design and implementation through testing, integration, and documentation.

JOB DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: 

• Design, implement, and maintain firmware and low-level embedded software for portable, wearable, and low-power embedded devices.

• Develop device drivers, hardware abstraction layers, and board support package components for custom ARM- and MCU-based platforms.

• Implement and optimize embedded software for real-time operation on resource-constrained hardware, with consideration for performance, memory use, and power consumption.

• Implement and manage multithreading, interrupt handling, timers, DMA, and task scheduling in RTOS or bare-metal environments.

• Work closely with hardware engineers to define firmware-to-hardware interface requirements, timing expectations, sequencing, and configuration.

• Support integration of embedded software with FPGA-based or FPGA-adjacent subsystems where applicable, including register/control interfaces, data movement, timing coordination, and system debug.

• Troubleshoot and debug system-level issues involving display timing, sensor data alignment, peripheral communication, memory bandwidth, and hardware/software interactions.

• Apply best embedded software design practices to create modular, maintainable, and reusable code bases.

• Participate in full software lifecycle activities including design documentation, code reviews, unit tests, regression tests, and integration testing.

• Contribute to embedded applications, simple user interfaces, or engineering tools used for product configuration, validation, internal evaluation, or demonstrations.

• Collaborate with Systems Engineering to ensure embedded implementations satisfy system requirements, timing budgets, and performance margins.

• Maintain firmware architecture and ensure clarity, robustness, and long-term maintainability across code bases.

MINIMUM JOB REQUIREMENTS:

**The right to live and work in the UK is a must-have pre-requisite for this posting**

• Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related discipline with a focus on embedded systems.

• 5-8 years of professional experience in embedded software development.

• Strong proficiency in C/C++ for embedded systems.

• Experience with RTOS or bare-metal development, including interrupt handlers, timers, DMA, context switching, and memory management.

• Demonstrated experience developing low-level drivers and hardware interfaces (SPI, I²C, UART, GPIO, timers, DMA, display or sensor interfaces).

• Familiarity with image processing or digital signal processing concepts.

• Hands-on experience debugging embedded systems using oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, JTAG/SWD, and in-circuit debugging tools.

• Ability to contribute independently to embedded development while working within a cross-disciplinary engineering team.

PREFERRED JOB REQUIREMENTS:

• Master’s degree in EE/CE/CS or related field.

• Experience developing software for portable, wearable, or imaging/display-centric embedded systems.

• Experience working with FPGA-based systems, including firmware interaction with FPGA logic, register/control interfaces, timing-sensitive coordination, or board-level integration/debug.

• Experience with GUI frameworks (Qt, LVGL, embedded UIs) and integration with display pipelines.

• Python experience for scripting, automation, test tooling, or data analysis.

• Linux familiarity—including user space, device interfaces, kernel modules, or embedded distributions.

• Working knowledge of video and display interfaces (MIPI-DSI/CSI, LVDS, HDMI, DisplayPort, or custom microdisplay timing).

• Familiarity with image formats and compression (YUV/RGB, JPEG/PNG, H.264/H.265).

• Exposure to wireless communication protocols (BLE, Wi-Fi, or proprietary RF).

• Understanding of local file systems, storage interfaces, and data-persistence mechanisms on embedded devices.

• Strong modular software design and object-oriented development practices.

• Experience with revision control tools (Git preferred), including branching strategies and code review workflows.

• Excellent teamwork and communication skills.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:

• Able to rotate from sitting to standing, lift up to 20 pounds, and gown according to clean room protocol

GENERAL:

Hours of work: 39-hour week, Monday to Friday, 8:30am to 5:00pm (4:00pm on Friday) with 30 minutes for lunch; the company offers certain flexibility/change of the core working hours in line with the Flexible Working Policy, however; flexibility regarding working hours is also expected from the employee.

LOCATION:

The right to live and work in the UK is a pre-requisite for this position. The role is based in the Company’s facility in St. David’s Business Park, Dalgety Bay, Fife but flexibility around a combination of on and off-site working (work from home) is supported where practicable; a small amount of travel may be required.

BENEFITS PACKAGE:

30 days annual leave (plus 5 statutory days), competitive personal pension scheme with company contribution, life assurance scheme.

To apply please send your resume to: Jobs@Kopin.com

We make available all salary bands and job descriptions to create fair and open opportunities for everyone.

Pension contributions

Continuous learning

Food and drink

Experience delivering training, carrying out competence assessments and coaching colleagues to build confidence, capability and safe working practices

Why Software Engineering in Tax?

Technology is transforming the way tax is managed. Businesses are working with larger volumes of data, responding to changing regulations and looking for smarter ways to solve complex challenges. That's why technology has become an increasingly important part of the tax world.

In our Tax Technology & Innovation team, we build the products and platforms that help organisations manage tax more efficiently and make better decisions. From developing new digital tools to improving existing technology, our work helps clients simplify processes, reduce manual effort and access the insights they need.

As a Software Engineering in Tax graduate, you'll help create technology that solves real problems for businesses. Working at the intersection of software engineering, data and tax, you'll contribute to products that are used by organisations across the UK and around the world.

Life as a Software Engineering in Tax graduate

As part of our Tax Technology & Innovation team, you'll work with software engineers, analysts, designers and product specialists to develop and improve digital products that help organisations manage tax more effectively.

You don't need to be a technical expert before you join. We're looking for people who are curious, adaptable and excited by solving problems. What matters most is your willingness to learn, ask questions and explore new ideas.

You could be helping to build new features for a cloud-based application, testing software before release, automating manual processes or using AI-powered tools to improve the way technology is developed. As you gain experience, you'll learn how ideas move from concept to finished product and see first-hand how technology can make work simpler, faster and more effective.

Throughout the programme, you'll gain exposure to the full software engineering lifecycle. That means learning how products are shaped and designed around user needs, how software is built and tested, and how new features are deployed and improved over time. Working in collaborative teams, you'll build practical experience of modern engineering approaches while developing your coding, problem-solving and technical design skills.

Your future

Throughout the programme, you'll develop valuable technical skills through technology-focused training, structured learning and hands-on project work. You'll be supported by a network of peers, mentors and leaders who are invested in helping you learn and grow.

Over time, you'll build the knowledge and confidence to take on increasingly complex engineering challenges. As your skills develop, you'll have the opportunity to explore areas that match your interests, whether that's software engineering, data, cloud technologies, automation or product development. Whatever path you take, you'll have a strong foundation for a varied and rewarding long-term career in technology.

The training and development of our people is critical to the future success of our business. Therefore, we have created a rich curriculum and learning community to help you build your skills and fulfil your potential. ABOUT KYRA

Kyra is an enterprise influencer marketing platform working with brands like SharkNinja, Coach, H&M, Ray-Ban, and Converse. Our platform manages the full lifecycle — creator discovery, campaign management, content review, payments, analytics, and AI-powered intelligence across TikTok, Instagram, and YouTube.

Campaign Director
📍 EST hours. Reports to the Chief Strategy Officer who oversees the entire delivery team.


🎯 The role
You own a portfolio of client accounts and the team that delivers them. On the client side you are the senior point of contact, accountable for net revenue retention: renewals, expansion, and revenue at risk. On the delivery side you build and lead a team of Campaign Managers and own what they produce: quality, timelines, margin, and the standards they work to.


🔑 What you own

 - Net revenue retention across your portfolio: renewals, expansion, revenue at risk.

 - The senior client relationship, from day-to-day marketing contacts up to budget holders.

 - Campaign delivery across the portfolio: on time, in scope, against KPIs.

 - Building the Campaign Manager team: hiring, onboarding, standards, coaching and progression.

 - Gross profit margin and cost management on your accounts.
   

📊 The numbers you carry

 - Gross profit margin on every account, against target.

 - Team utilisation and throughput per head.

 - Cost per brief, and the direction it’s moving.

 - Renewal rate and expansion revenue on your portfolio.
   

🤝 Owning the client

 - Map stakeholders across functions and regions.

 - Own all communications.

 - Set account strategy: the roadmap, the expansion case, the renewal plan.

 - Own commercial terms, scope and budget.

 - Own executive reporting, QBRs and EBRs.

 - Manage account risk.
   

👥 Leading the team

 - Hire well and onboard fast. You build the team, you don’t just inherit it.

 - Set the production standard: casting, negotiation, brief workflow, escalation.

 - Track Campaign Manager performance against clear, measurable expectations. Coach, give regular feedback, own progression and performance conversations.

 - Plan resourcing and workload.

 - Own the numbers behind delivery: budgeting, forecasting, reconciliation, GPM, throughput per head.

 - Set influencer strategy: casting direction, negotiation and rates, re-engagement of high performers.

 - Act as senior escalation on complex campaign and influencer issues.
   

🔁 Reporting and working across Kyra

 - Lead post-campaign analysis, internal post-mortems and PCA decks.

 - Work with Sales, Legal, Product and Strategy to keep priorities aligned, and represent campaign delivery at a senior level internally.

 - Feed client needs, pain points and feature requests back to Product.
   

🏆 What success looks like

 - Your accounts renew, several grow, and NRR trends upward.

 - Margin holds or improves as volume rises. Cost per brief comes down.

 - Delivery holds without constant escalation.

 - Your Campaign Managers get faster and more independent, and they stay.

 - Recurring problems get fixed at the cause, not re-managed every quarter.
   

🔍 What we are looking for

 - Senior ownership of $500,000+ accounts, with multiple stakeholders and workstreams. You have held the number on those relationships, and you can name accounts you grew and say how.

 - Held margin and contribution targets on that portfolio, not just a revenue number. You can say what you did when the margin slipped.

 - Hands-on influencer campaign experience. At least 7 years in influencer marketing, covering casting and production. Strong platform fluency.

 - Built and led a team. You have hired, developed and retained Campaign Managers or equivalent, and you can show what happened to their performance and retention under you.

 - AI in your daily work, with proof. You can name a process you changed with it and what the result was.

 - Commercial sharpness (agency economics, margin, resourcing), operational strength so you build systems not workarounds, clear communication at every level, and high standards with low ego.
   

🌍 The role is EST based and works with a team spread across three continents.

job_title: Account Director, Influencer Marketing, Sports & Entertainment (Fully Remote)
job_description:
ABOUT KYRA

Kyra is an enterprise influencer marketing platform working with brands like SharkNinja, Coach, H&M, Ray-Ban, and Converse. Our platform manages the full lifecycle — creator discovery, campaign management, content review, payments, analytics, and AI-powered intelligence across TikTok, Instagram, and YouTube.



👋 ABOUT THE ROLE

Permanent · Full-Time · US-based · EST Hours
Target Start Date: November 2026

We're hiring an Account Director for one of our biggest sports and entertainment clients. The work covers sportsbook, fantasy and live events, and the campaigns are judged on views, CPV and how quickly we can get from brief to live post.

You'll own this one account end to end, with two Campaign Managers reporting into you.

The account is newly won and growing quickly into the end of the year. An interim lead is running it until then, so you'll get a proper handover and join with campaigns already live.

We're looking for someone who has spent at least five years agency-side running creator programmes in sports betting, DFS or around the NFL and NBA, and who can show us the numbers behind that work.




🏟️ WHAT MAKES THIS ROLE DIFFERENT

One account, in depth. Most Account Director roles, run a portfolio of clients and build CM teams underneath them. This role is responsible for one is a single client. We need someone who understands sports, betting and the US creator space properly.

Senior and hands-on. You're the client's senior contact and you're also across the detail every day: who has been outreached, what's stuck in contracting, which draft is late, whether spend is on pace. You run the operations yourself.

Structure matters. This client tracks delivery milestones, feedback windows and their own dependencies against a timeline. You bring the process, keep the client to their side of it and keep everyone on top of dates.

Speed matters. Campaigns are built around games and moments. Turnaround from brief to live is one of the things we measure you on.

The category has rules. Sportsbook and fantasy content comes with age gates, state restrictions and platform policies. You need to already know how these work.

It moves fast. Briefs land with short lead times, priorities change with the sports calendar, and the client expects answers the same day. You need to be comfortable working at that pace without letting quality slip.

We are an AI-native business. Kyra is Claude-first and our campaign workflows run through our own proprietary platform, built with AI at the core. On top of that there is plenty of room to use AI tools to make your own working day more efficient. We are not looking for someone who is open to AI. We are looking for someone who is already getting real value from it: building their own workflows, automating the repetitive parts of the job and using the time saved to think harder about the client. You will be expected to bring that with you.




🏈 WHAT YOU'LL DO: THE GAME PLAN

Grow the client relationship. Grow the client relationship. You own the client relationship and retention on this account, and you’re measured on net revenue retention (NRR). You are the client’s senior contact at Kyra, accountable for strategy, approvals, escalations and commercial conversations. You keep them informed, manage their expectations and identify what we should be doing next with them. 🏆

Agree how the account runs. You own the operating playbook: casting, outreach, contracting, briefing, review, approval, go-live and reporting. You keep it current, and when a process is slowing delivery you change it. 📋

Make the casting calls. You set the casting strategy for every campaign: creator profile, tier, mix and volume. You set the negotiation approach on fees and usage rights and approve deals before contracting. You are responsible for compliance: 21+, state restrictions, platform policy and disclosure. 🎯

Execute delivery every day. You oversee every live campaign from first outreach to the moment content goes live. You know the status of every workstream, surface risk early and protect the quality of what we put out. ⚡

Pace the budget. You track creator spend and delivery against the contracted plan, flag variances early and adjust allocation to protect both performance and margin. 💸

Lead the team. You manage two Campaign Managers. You set priorities, review their work, give direct and constructive feedback and develop their skills. 🤝

Analyse performance. You agree KPIs with the client before launch, monitor performance in flight and adjust creator mix, creative or distribution when the data calls for it. 📊

Next campaign, stronger. Every campaign ends with a debrief. You take what we learned into the next brief so the account keeps improving. 🔁




📈 HOW WE'LL KNOW IT'S WORKING

We measure success by what the brand gets from us. 

The brand hits its moments. Content is live when the game, the fixture or the launch happens. Creators are contracted, posts are delivered and volumes are met on the timelines the client has planned around.

The brand gets the reach it paid for. Blended CPM and CPV come in at or better than the agreed rate on every campaign.

The brand can react quickly. Turnaround from brief to live is short enough that the client can respond to a result, a trade or a trending moment with creator content.

The brand trusts the delivery. The account runs on a documented playbook, feedback windows and dependencies are tracked, and issues leave meetings with an owner and a date. The client does not need to chase us.

The brand brings us the next brief. The client renews because the work is good and the relationship is easy, and comes to Kyra first with new ideas. Revenue growth is shared with Client Solutions. The client's confidence in delivery sits with you.

What good looks like by month six. The account is running to plan without the interim lead, the client has signed off the operating cadence, rates are being met or beaten, and your two Campaign Managers can each run a campaign end to end on their own.




🙋 WHO THIS ROLE IS FOR

 - 5+ years agency-side running creator programmes for sportsbook, DFS or fantasy brands, or US league partnerships (NFL, NBA)

 - Real numbers: CPV targets you've hit, creator and post volumes per month, typical turnaround from outreach to live

 - You've owned a senior client relationship yourself, including the difficult conversations

 - You've managed Campaign Managers while staying close to the work

 - You're fluent in views, CPV and CPM and can turn performance data into clear recommendations

 - You know FTC disclosure and the compliance rules around betting content

 - US-based, working EST hours

 - Not currently working on a competing sportsbook, DFS or betting brand

 - Organised, direct and calm when plans change at short notice

 - Experience in a fast-growing business or account, where the scope, the team and the client's expectations have scaled quickly and you have had to keep delivery steady through it

 - Already using Claude or similar AI tools to do real work, with your own workflows for casting, research, reporting or client comms, and able to show what they have saved you or improved
   


📅 WEEKEND WORK

Campaigns go live around games, fixtures and events, so this role involves some weekend work. Please only apply if you're open to that.

Kyra reserves the right to amend your duties from time to time in line with the needs of the business.

💟 Support

About the Role

• Participating in calls/meetings with internal and external stakeholders where concepts and pitches are discussed and developed.

• Negotiating costs with suppliers, crews and contractors

• Organising allocation of resource and personnel pre, during and post-production

• Working with insurance companies pro-actively reporting and documenting risk

• Tracking production costs and providing reconciliation reports as requested

• Ensure there are on-set log notes to hand post shoot

• Mentor and work closely with junior members of the team

• Experience as a Senior Producer at a production company or publisher - social media experience is a must

• Proficiency in building the entire scope of production docs is essential including; call sheets, schedules, risk assessments and P&L

• Understanding of content from an audience and publisher POV as well as a brand/client POV

• Demonstrable working exposure and knowledge of video pre-production, production and post-production including workflows and processes, equipment and software programs/tool

ROLE SUMMARY:
Help us turn audit findings into lasting improvements! You’ll lead external audit engagement across Group Engineering at LSEG. The role also covers regulatory responses, issues and risk reporting. Bring these services together through safe use of artificial intelligence (AI) across Governance, Risk and Compliance.

Reporting to the Head of Technology & Cyber GRC, you’ll set priorities and lead managers, specialists and analysts. This is a first-line role, working with management to address risk. Independent assurance remains with the audit and assurance teams.

WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING: 
Lead external audit engagement. Manage the relationship with external auditors and bring Finance, control owners and application teams together. Coordinate planning, scope discussions, readiness, evidence requests, walkthroughs and support for testing. Review observations and management responses. Resolve evidence gaps, resolve disagreements and supervise remediation through to closure.

Be responsible for internal audit and regulatory responses. Prioritise Engineering’s response to internal audits, regulatory examinations and enquiries, and relevant client or contractual assessments. Check evidence and responses, agree owners and track commitments. Keep leaders advised of concerns and decisions needed.

Challenge issues and remediation. Review self-identified issues and audit or regulatory findings. Question root causes, proposed actions and closure evidence. Confirm that remediation reduces the underlying risk, rather than just completing an action plan. Identify repeat weaknesses and resolve delays. Coordinate risk acceptances through agreed approval routes.

Make risk information useful. Maintain a consistent Technology and Cyber risk profile and clear risk and control indicators. Use source-system signals to flag emerging risks and breaches of agreed risk limits. Guide risk committees and provide concise Board and executive reporting. Explain what has changed, why it matters and what leaders need to decide.

Improve delivery through AI. Lead the team that builds and maintains AI agents for GRC evidence gathering, analysis and reporting. Choose use cases and work with engineers or delivery partners. Keep agent logic and change knowledge in-house. Assign owners and set limits on agent access and actions. Test output quality and require human approval for material conclusions. Manage logging, changes, incidents and retirement. You do not need to be the lead engineer.

Develop people and services. Recruit and mentor colleagues across audit, risk, data and AI governance. Set clear expectations, invite different views and help people build new skills. Measure service quality, reduce rework and focus effort on the highest risks.

 WHAT YOU'LL BRING:
ESSENTIAL SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:
External audit experience is essential. We’re looking for the following:
• You have led external audit engagements from planning to closure. Your examples show direct responsibility for evidence quality, findings and management responses.
• You understand Technology and Cyber controls and the evidence auditors and regulators expect. You can assess risk appetite and interpret risk and control indicators.
• You have managed audit, regulatory or remediation portfolios in regulated environments. You challenge weak root causes and check that corrective action reduces risk.
• You have built or improved a risk, audit or GRC capability and developed teams with different specialisms.
• You can weigh evidence, provide direction and explain technical or regulatory issues to senior leaders. You build constructive relationships while challenging conclusions when needed.
• You understand AI risks and controls well enough to oversee agent development and maintenance. You can question engineers on data access, testing, reliability and human oversight.

USEFUL EXPERIENCE:
Experience with statutory or financial-statement technology audits is particularly useful. So is work with Information Technology General Controls (ITGCs) or Internal Controls over Financial Reporting (ICOFR). Internal audit experience, financial-services knowledge and early-warning analytics would also help. Relevant accounting, audit, technology-risk or cyber-security qualifications are welcome, alongside equivalent experience.

WHAT YOU'LL GET IN RETURN:
Set the direction for your services and build a team with the skills to deliver them. Work directly with senior Engineering, Cyber Security and Finance leaders, auditors and regulators. Your impact will be visible in better evidence, fewer repeat findings and faster risk decisions. You will also develop experience leading responsible use of AI.

About this role
Suspense thrives on uncertainty, a calculated pause that draws in the observer. In this pause, placeholders emerge as valuable cues. Their very presence suggests that what is yet unseen could hold the answers, a revelation or a solution. When used thoughtfully, a placeholder can tease and compel, engaging the imagination.
Responsibilities
In websites, a loading spinner is no different than the ellipsis of a suspenseful plot twist; it tells the viewer that what is coming is worth waiting for. Key benefits of effective placeholders include:
• Maintaining engagement: By signaling more to come, placeholders prevent user drop-off.
• Setting expectations: Clear, well-placed placeholders hint at what content is coming next, adding structure.
• Building suspense: The anticipation of more content holds attention, just as in storytelling.
Placeholder content, however, must tread a careful line. Too sparse, and it risks undermining its own suspense; too dense, and it overwhelms with unnecessary clutter. The balance lies in leaving just enough room for the mind to wander and fill the gaps.

About Lightfoot

Lightfoot builds connected-vehicle technology - in-cab driver coaching, vehicle safety products and fleet telematics. Our software supports real hardware in real vehicles, with customers including Tesco, Asda, Ocado, Virgin Media and Iceland.

We’re big enough to have established products and engineering teams, but small enough that strong technical decisions can still change the direction of the company.

We’re rebuilding the software Lightfoot runs on - the customer portal, the APIs behind it and the mobile app - in Python, React and React Native on AWS. We’re also changing how we build software: stronger architecture, better automated testing, secure-by-default delivery and agentic development used properly on production systems. We’re looking for the technical leader who will shape that transition and lead the team building it.

Type: Permanent, full-time, Monday to Friday.  

Location: Remote. We’d want you to attend our Office in Exeter, Devon roughly every two or three weeks, usually with an overnight, for the things that are genuinely better done together - architecture sessions, kicking off important work, retrospectives and time with the team. Not for the sake of being seen.

About the role

This is first and foremost a technical leadership role. You’ll lead the Applications engineering function, but we’re not looking for a manager who has stepped away from engineering. We want someone who can set technical direction, make architectural decisions, raise the engineering bar across the team and stay close enough to the detail to know whether those decisions are working.

You’ll be responsible for

- Leading the architecture of our next-generation platform across backend, web and mobile.
- Shaping the migration from our existing PHP/MySQL estate without pretending we can replace everything at once.
- Defining engineering standards and patterns for the new platform.
- Owning the testing strategy — what we test, where we automate and how quality is built into delivery.
- Leading our move to agentic software development, turning a proven individual approach into a repeatable team capability.
- Building security and observability into the platform from the start.
- Developing the technical capability of the team through design reviews, mentoring and hands-on leadership.
- You’ll also line-manage the team and remain accountable for delivery. Those things matter, but the reason we’re hiring you is your technical judgement.

What’s already decided, and what’s yours

The broad technology direction is agreed:

- Python / FastAPI for new backend services.
- React / TypeScript for web.
- React Native for mobile.
- AWS as the platform.
- Managed and serverless services where they make sense.
- Agentic development as a normal part of engineering.

You won’t be asked to spend six months choosing a stack.

The interesting decisions are the ones underneath it: service boundaries, API design, migration sequencing, testing strategy, engineering standards, secure-development practices, observability and how agentic development works across a team.

One important constraint: our database is shared across several engineering teams and is mission-critical beyond Applications. Significant schema change is negotiated, not decided unilaterally. That’s a real architectural constraint, and we’d rather tell you about it now.

Staying hands-on

This isn’t a role where success is measured by how many sprint tickets you close.

It is a role where you’ll be expected to stay technically credible: reviewing designs, challenging assumptions, prototyping important patterns, getting into difficult implementations and helping the team solve hard problems.

You’ll lead engineers primarily through strong technical judgement, not through distance from the code.

What we’re looking for

You do not need to be the strongest engineer in every technology above.

You do need to be a strong technical leader.

We’re looking for someone who

- Has led engineers technically, not just managed them.
- Has designed and evolved substantial production systems.
- Can make architectural decisions and explain the trade-offs behind them.
- Has strong backend engineering depth, ideally in Python.
- Has worked with AWS and Docker in production.
- Has modernised or re-platformed a live system that people depended on.
- Understands automated testing deeply enough to define a strategy, not simply mandate more tests.
- Treats security as an engineering responsibility.
- Can get into an unfamiliar or long-lived codebase and work out what it really does.
- Can communicate technical trade-offs clearly to engineers and non-technical stakeholders.
- Stays calm when systems, customers or priorities get noisy.

- Being able to navigate PHP and older JavaScript is useful because that’s the estate we’re migrating from. You don’t need to love it.
- For the right person, technical strength matters more to us than arriving as the finished engineering manager.

Why this is a good job

- You get to shape the next platform, not just maintain the current one. The technology direction is agreed, and the transformation is already underway.
- The architecture isn’t finished. There are real decisions to make about how the next generation of Lightfoot should be built.
- Agentic engineering is real here. We’re already using it successfully on production engineering work. You’ll help turn that from something one strong engineer can do into a capability the whole team can use well.
- The work is tangible. Our software connects to devices fitted to real vehicles. You’ll see vehicles using systems your team built - delivering groceries, installing broadband and operating some of the UK’s largest fleets.
- Technology you can explain at a barbecue: vehicles, drivers, safety, and data at scale. You will literally see your technology in the windscreen of vehicles driving around town, delivering your groceries or installing your broadband.
