# Why join us?

We are a small, rapidly growing team of 50 people at the moment (18 people in the engineering & product team, 6 people in the sales & marketing team). Our first venture together was [senecalearning.com,](http://senecalearning.com/) which scaled to 12M users and a successful acquisition in 2022.

# Culture

We are well-funded but the hardest period of a start-up is always the first couple of years, when the team is small, and you are heavily relied on personally. You won’t be expected to work evenings & weekends, but you will be expected to work hard when on the job.

# About the role

The core responsibilities of the role will be managing client relationships, working with 100-150 fast-growing start-ups across the UK and US to ensure that we are delivering the best possible service at the same time.

You will have continued client interaction and will be managed by the CEO. At the same time, you will work with 18 software engineers using AI to automate the day-to-day workflows that you & your team encounter. You will then be in charge of rolling these out to your teams & clients.

Novabook is the “Accountant for Startups” founded by Stephen Wilks & Lukas Feddern. Our team previously founded, scaled and sold a technology company for $50M. We started Novabook to solve the problems we faced during this process. Our aim is to make the financial processes of starting, running and selling a business in the UK easier. 

# Why join us?

We are a small, rapidly growing team of 50 people at the moment (18 people in the engineering & product team, 6 people in the sales & marketing team). Our first venture together was [senecalearning.com,](http://senecalearning.com/) which scaled to 12M users and a successful acquisition in 2022.

After launching in May 2024, we already have hundreds of clients, millions in ARR and are growing quickly, this is an opportunity to join the ride at an early stage. We’ve raised over £10M in capital to scale Novabook. 

Novabook was born out of our personal experiences with the shortcomings of traditional accountancy practices while running Seneca. After dealing with inefficient software and unreliable accountancies for 8 years, we believe it's time to tackle these challenges head-on.

# What technological problems are we solving?

Software that accounting firms currently run on is extremely outdated & disjointed. This results in a lot of manual work, which is costly and error-prone. We are building a suite of integrated products to automate 90% of the workflow within accounting firms. We are rapidly scaling our engineering team to facilitate this build-out across workflow, payments, open banking, payroll & automated bookkeeping domains.

Some examples of recent projects:

- Evaling the performance of our AI document ingestion pipeline 

- Minting and embedding real bank accounts into our application to allow clients to pay bills and employees

- Automating the categorisation of bank transactions using AI agents

- Building an orchestration layer to empower accountants to create agents for repetitive tasks

- Building out employee systems of record for payroll

# What is our tech stack?

- TypeScript monorepo

- Lambdas - APIs serving the app and several asynchronous queue orchestrated flows

- Next.js web app deployed on Vercel, here we have a full component library with custom theme built-in

- React native mobile app

- AI workflows across multiple business domains

- We primarily use Jest & Playwright for tests.

- Terraform

# How do we work & what is the culture like?

We work in an agile way & continuously adapt our processes via retrospective. We work in 4-week product cycles followed by a 1-week “cool down” period for addressing technical debt & planning. We have daily stand-ups in each team & use Linear for project management and tracking.

Our culture is collaborative, hard-working & transparent.

# What we’re looking for in you:

- Strong academic background in a STEM-based subject e.g. Comp Sci, Maths, Engineering, Physics, Chemistry etc

- Experience with our technology stack

- Desire to take full end-to-end ownership of problems from solution ideation all the way out into production

- Hardworking & desire to build an amazing company

Product owners and Business Analysts in the Product Directorate; colleagues across the NRLA as users of reporting and insight and owners of source data; consultants and suppliers working on the warehouse, personalisation and AI.

Main Purpose and Scope Of Job:
Turn the NRLA’s data into insight the business acts on, and into the clean, well-modelled data that personalisation and AI depend on. The Data Analyst works with colleagues across the business to understand, translate and scope their requirements, builds reports and analysis from the data warehouse, and works with the rest of the team to extend and enrich it. 
The role supports the NRLA 2.0 ambition to give every member a personalised experience: it prepares and tests the data behind segments, models and recommendations, measures whether personalisation is working, and helps bring AI into the team’s own work and into NRLA products. It raises data literacy across the business and asks what decision each request will inform, so that the team’s work changes what the NRLA does for members.

• Engage with users to scope work, translate business requirements into technical specifications, and agree priorities with the Deputy Director. 

• Complete ad hoc requests for data and analysis from structured and raw sources, and turn repeated requests into reports or self-service tools.

Nscale is taking on the hyperscalers by building a vertically integrated GenAI cloud platform. About the role

The Director, Legal, Infrastructure, EMEA is Nscale’s dedicated UK-based infrastructure counsel for EMEA, reporting to the VP, Legal, Infrastructure.

This is a hands-on execution role covering the full contracting lifecycle for Nscale’s EMEA data centre campuses: construction, design and consultancy, major equipment supply and O&M, real estate, and power from term sheet through delivery and closeout.

As Director, you will lead your own matters end-to-end, negotiate directly with major counterparties, and apply consistent commercial and legal positions across multiple jurisdictions. You will work closely with local external counsel where jurisdiction-specific advice is required.

What you’ll be doing

• Lead the negotiation of owner-contractor, EPC, EPCM and design-and-build agreements for data centre campus construction across EMEA.

• Draft and negotiate design and consultancy agreements with architects, engineers and specialist consultants, including framework/work-order structures, ownership of deliverables and professional liability.

• Negotiate supply, installation and O&M agreements for on-site power generation and critical electrical and mechanical equipment, including performance guarantees, warranties and service levels.

• Support site acquisition, development arrangements and ground leases, as well as power procurement, utility, interconnection and power purchase arrangements, in coordination with regulatory and local counsel.

• Maintain and improve Nscale’s infrastructure contract templates and playbooks, including appropriate use of JCT, NEC, FIDIC and bespoke contracting structures.

• Run counterparty comment rounds and drive consistent house positions across projects, while adapting for local law and market practice.

• Manage contracts through delivery and closeout, including change orders, cost and schedule claims, payment and retention issues, defect correction and dispute avoidance.

• Coordinate insurance and bonding requirements with the insurance team, and partner with Debt Capital Markets Legal on lender requirements for project-financed sites.

• Manage EMEA outside counsel, including scope, budgets and quality of advice.

• Partner closely with construction, procurement, finance, real estate, energy and operations teams to support project delivery at pace.

What you need

• 7+ years PQE in construction and infrastructure legal experience, gained in-house and/or at a top-tier law firm.

• Qualified solicitor or barrister in England and Wales, or another relevant EMEA jurisdiction, in good standing. England and Wales qualification is strongly preferred.

• Strong track record negotiating major construction, EPC/EPCM, design-and-build, professional services and equipment supply agreements for large-scale, mission-critical or industrial projects.

• Experience working across multiple EMEA jurisdictions and managing local counsel effectively.

• Fluency in construction risk allocation, including pricing structures, delay remedies, warranties and defects, indemnities, insurance, liability caps and dispute-resolution provisions.

• A confident first-chair negotiator, able to run multiple high-value contracts in parallel and drive them to signature.

• Ability to explain complex legal and commercial risk clearly to non-lawyers and senior stakeholders.

• Comfort working alongside project finance, power, insurance and regulatory counterparts.

Nice to haves

• Prior experience at a hyperscaler, colocation provider, data centre developer, major contractor or infrastructure investor.

• Energy and power project experience, including equipment supply, O&M, utility/interconnection or power purchase arrangements.

• Experience with JCT, NEC and/or FIDIC forms.

• Construction claims and dispute-resolution experience.

• Additional European language skills.

Join Nscale as we build a world-class AI cloud platform. If you’re ready to lead infrastructure contracting for hyperscale data centre projects across EMEA at one of the most ambitious AI infrastructure companies, we’d love to hear from you.

Network Platform Strategy & Ownership

Act as the technical authority for network programmability across the Global Backbone & Edge Networks organisation.

Develop automation workflows that reduce customer onboarding times and eliminate manual configuration.

The Guardian team builds practical safety and oversight systems for increasingly capable AI agents. Our goal is to make it possible for agents to take on longer-running, higher-autonomy work while preserving meaningful safeguards, respecting user intent, and intervening when actions could cause serious or difficult-to-reverse harm.

Auto-review is an early example of this work. When an agent reaches a permission boundary, a separate model evaluates the proposed action in context and determines whether it should proceed. The team is now extending this foundation into more capable oversight systems that account for richer user context, support a broader range of agent experiences, and integrate across OpenAI products.

Guardian sits at the intersection of engineering, alignment research, product, infrastructure, and security. The team already has a strong engineering foundation in London and will continue to grow there as a concentrated, highly collaborative group.

About us

ORCA Computing (“ORCA”) is at the forefront of a new era in high-performance computing, developing full-stack photonic quantum systems designed to transform how organisations tackle machine learning, generative AI, and complex optimisation challenges in data centre environments.  Headquartered in London, ORCA has delivered eleven on-premises quantum computers worldwide – demonstrating that its technology is not theoretical but already delivering real world results.

At the core of ORCA’s innovation is its hybrid quantum-classical architecture, engineered for seamless integration into existing AI and HPC infrastructure.  ORCA PT Series quantum systems are room temperature and rack-mounted which connect directly to GPU clusters via NVIDIA’s CUDA-Q platform, enabling accelerated AI workloads delivering advantages over traditional silicon-based systems.  Backed by a strong portfolio of patent families spanning photonic integrated circuits, quantum memory, and multiplexing technologies, ORCA is enabling enterprises, research institutions, and HPC operators to unlock new levels of performance, efficiency, and scalability.

With the recent launch its next-generation PT-3 system, ORCA is entering a pivotal phase of growth and technological advancement.  Its solutions are already being embedded into generative AI pipelines, delivering measurable improvements in model performance, while also addressing the rising energy demands of large-scale AI adoption.  With a focus on practical deployment and a clear roadmap to fault-tolerant quantum computing, ORCA is leading the development and deployment of quantum technology, providing a commercially viable path to the future of computing.

What you’ll do:

- Technical support (L2): You will take ownership of customer support tickets — triaging and validating incoming cases (including first-line helpdesk activity where needed), carrying out remote diagnostics, reviewing logs, reproducing issues, and applying fixes, patches, and configuration changes. The role is primarily focused on system software and network configuration, but includes basic hands-on hardware work.

- Root cause analysis & reporting: You will drive issues through to root cause, producing clear troubleshooting records, Root Cause Analyses (RCAs), and Failure Analysis Reports (FARs) with support from our L3 senior engineers, and presenting findings to customers where appropriate.

- Engineering liaison: You will bridge the gap between customers and our L3 engineering specialists with your experience with resourcing/technical project management — preparing complete escalation packages, working alongside senior engineers on complex issues, and feeding lessons learned back into our knowledge base.

- Pre-delivery & site surveys: You will support technical pre-delivery work for new systems, including conducting site surveys and confirming that customer facilities, power, networking, and environmental conditions are ready for installation.

- Installation, commissioning & handover: You will be on-site for system installation and commissioning, handing systems over to customers and delivering system operations training to their teams.

- Servicing & maintenance: You will manage and oversee on-site detector cryogenic servicing carried out by our specialist supply partner — preparing the ORCA system for service, bringing it back online afterwards, and handing it back to the customer. You will also carry out scheduled maintenance and install software and firmware updates.

- Customer engagement: You will build strong working relationships with customers’ technical and operational teams, working closely with our Customer Success Managers to keep customers informed, and bringing commercial awareness to every interaction. Whether on-site or remote, you will often be the only ORCA representative in the room, acting with professionalism, sound judgement, and confidence on the company’s behalf.

- Travel & extended-hours support: You will travel internationally on a regular basis to customer sites, and support customers outside UK business hours as part of our extended support coverage.

- Service development: You will help shape how ORCA’s service and support offering evolves as our install base grows — improving support processes, tooling, documentation, and knowledge base content, and feeding customer insight into how our service plans, maintenance, and training are delivered.

- Technical documentation: You will contribute to ORCA’s customer-facing technical documentation — including user manuals, release notes, site preparation and installation guides, operating and maintenance procedures, troubleshooting guides and FAQs, service bulletins, and training materials — making sure it reflects how customers actually use our systems.

What you’ll bring:

Essential skills and experience:

- Experience in a technical support, field service, or service engineering role, ideally supporting complex technical systems in a customer-facing setting.

- Strong software troubleshooting skills, including working in production Windows and Linux environments, analysing logs, scripting (ideally Python), and diagnosing networking and configuration issues.

- Experience owning support tickets through to resolution, including structured root cause analysis and clear technical reporting and documentation.

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the confidence to engage customers directly, represent ORCA independently, and explain technical issues in plain language.

- Strong workload and information management skills, including prioritization, reporting and accurate record-keeping.

- Commercial awareness, and an understanding of how service quality shapes long-term customer relationships.

- Willingness to travel internationally on a regular basis, and flexibility to support customers outside UK business hours.

Nice to have:

- A degree in engineering, physics, computer science, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent practical experience.
- Experience in a deeptech, scientific instrumentation, HPC, or data centre environment.

- Experience with on-site installation, commissioning, or servicing of complex equipment.

- Experience writing customer-facing technical documentation, such as user manuals, release notes, or procedures.

- Familiarity with optics, photonics, or cryogenic systems.

- Some experience supporting SDKs or software applications, particularly Python-based tools (e.g. PyTorch).

- Experience configuring and debugging on-premise enterprise-grade network routers and switches for L2 and L3 connectivity

- An interest in quantum computing and new technologies more broadly.

Who we’re looking for:

- Customer focus: You enjoy working with customers, build trust quickly, and take pride in leaving them confident in their system and in ORCA.

- Problem solving: You have a can-do attitude and approach problems methodically, working through to the root cause rather than stopping at the symptom.

- Clear communication: You communicate clearly with everyone from customer users to senior engineers, and adapt your style to your audience.

- Team player: You work well as part of a small, close-knit team, share what you learn, and step in to help colleagues when needed.

- Curiosity: You’re eager to learn, interested in new technologies and systems, and keen to deepen your knowledge of ORCA’s photonic quantum computers, with ideas on how we can do things better as we grow.

Why join us

Joining ORCA Computing offers the opportunity to work at the forefront of quantum technology, where innovation is already delivering real-world impact. Across commercial, operational, and product roles, you’ll collaborate with multidisciplinary teams to bring advanced quantum systems to market and help integrate quantum capabilities into modern AI and data centre ecosystems.

ORCA provides a rare chance to contribute to a pivotal moment in the evolution of computing. With a culture built on ownership, collaboration, and ambition, the company empowers individuals to solve complex challenges and shape how next-generation quantum technologies are developed, deployed, and scaled across industries – driving a more efficient and powerful future for AI and compute.

job_description:
We have an exciting opportunity for an experienced Principal Lead, TRE Accreditation & Assurance to lead the review and development of Our Future Health's Trusted Research Environment (TRE) accreditation and assurance framework.

Reporting to the Director of Assurance, you will play a key role in strengthening our approach to secure research access, ensuring our accreditation processes remain robust, proportionate and scalable as the programme grows. You will bring specialist expertise in information governance, accreditation and assurance, working collaboratively with internal and external stakeholders to develop and implement sustainable improvements.

Despite big improvements in healthcare in our lifetimes, today millions of people in the UK still live in poor health as they get older. Diseases like cancer, dementia, diabetes, and heart disease affect the lives of many people in our communities. Our goal is to create a world-leading resource for health research, to improve our understanding and spot the patterns of how and why common diseases start, so treatments can begin sooner and be more effective.

Our Future Health will be the UK's largest ever health research programme, bringing people together to develop new ways to detect, prevent, and treat diseases. We are a charity, supported by the UK Government, in partnership with charities and industry. We work closely with the NHS and with public authorities across all nations and regions of the UK.

What you'll be doing:

In this role, you will lead the development and implementation of improvements to our TRE accreditation process and ongoing assurance arrangements. Working closely with teams across Information Governance, Information Security, Technology, Legal and Access Governance, your key responsibilities will include:

• Lead the review, redesign and implementation of our TRE accreditation framework, including accreditation requirements, assessment methodologies, policies and processes.
• Develop and implement robust ongoing assurance arrangements, including monitoring, periodic reviews, audits, reassessments and management of non-compliance.
• Lead the delivery of the TRE accreditation and assurance improvement programme, managing priorities, milestones, dependencies and risks to ensure successful implementation.
• Provide specialist advice and evidence-based recommendations on complex accreditation, information governance, security and assurance matters.
• Collaborate with internal teams, independent assessors, TRE owners and external stakeholders to develop effective, consistent and proportionate accreditation processes.
• Coordinate engagement with relevant governance bodies, supporting the review and approval of revised accreditation requirements and processes.
• Strengthen the quality and consistency of independent assessments, ensuring accreditation and assurance arrangements meet relevant regulatory requirements and standards.
• Establish sustainable governance arrangements, operational processes and guidance to support the effective implementation and ongoing management of the revised framework.
Requirements
Ideally, you will have substantial experience in accreditation, assurance, information governance or related activities within a regulated environment, such as health research, the NHS, government or industry.

You will bring a strong understanding of secure data environments and the ability to translate complex governance and technical requirements into practical, sustainable solutions.

To succeed in this role, you will also have some of the following skills and experience:

• Strong knowledge of information governance, data protection and information security frameworks, including UK GDPR and ISO 27001.
• Experience designing, implementing or improving accreditation, certification or assurance frameworks, including assessment methodologies, monitoring, audit and compliance processes.
• A good understanding of Trusted Research Environments (TREs), Secure Data Environments (SDEs) or comparable secure data platforms, including their governance, operational and security requirements.
• Proven experience leading complex, cross-functional programmes or improvement initiatives, translating strategic objectives into practical outcomes.
• Experience in risk assessment, assurance planning, governance and regulatory compliance within data-intensive or regulated environments.
• An understanding of the legal, ethical and governance considerations associated with sensitive health data, genomics and large-scale research datasets.
• Strong stakeholder management and influencing skills, with experience engaging senior leaders, governance bodies, independent assessors and external partners.
• Excellent communication and analytical skills, with the ability to navigate complex issues, exercise sound judgement and provide clear, evidence-based recommendations.
• A collaborative and adaptable approach, with the ability to manage competing priorities and drive improvements in an evolving environment.
• A degree in a relevant field, such as information governance, cybersecurity or data science, relevant professional certifications (e.g. CDMP), or equivalent practical experience.

Closing date: 9th November 2026

• 30 Days Holiday + Bank Holidays – Enjoy a generous holiday allowance with the flexibility to take bank holidays when it suits you.

The Director is accountable for the system the way a product owner is accountable for a product: adoption in code, pattern reuse, override rates, and first-pass compliance are the scoreboard. When telemetry shows a pattern failing, the Director retires it.

This role is designed for a highly experienced design leader who brings exceptional executive presence, narrative storytelling ability, and political acumen, while remaining deeply hands-on and invested in growing the people on their team: a player-coach who ships production design work alongside the team and leads complex, high-stakes design initiatives across Pfizer’s AI platforms and enterprise LLM integrations.

The Director works across every modality the platforms speak (screens, conversation, voice, and agent-to-agent interaction) and moves fluidly between shipping production design work, delivering design standards as code, and growing the team. • Experience Metrics: Connect design outcomes to measurable KPIs: adoption, task success, trust, time-to-resolution, and first-pass compliance.

We're hiring an Engineering Manager who wants to spend 80% of their time writing code, not attending management meetings.

About the role
Are you an experienced Software Engineer who loves writing code, solving complex technical problems and helping other engineers become better at what they do?
At Pigment, our Engineering Managers are engineers first.
Unlike traditional Engineering Manager positions, this role is designed for someone who wants to remain deeply involved in building software while taking on meaningful people-management responsibilities.
You'll spend approximately 80% of your time designing, coding and shipping production features, with the remaining 20% dedicated to coaching engineers, running regular 1:1s, providing feedback and supporting their development.
We're particularly interested in Senior Software Engineers who have naturally taken on coaching, mentoring or technical leadership responsibilities and are ready to develop further as people managers.
You don't necessarily need to have held an Engineering Manager title before. What matters most is your technical ability, your experience helping others grow and your motivation to combine engineering with people leadership.
You'll join Pigment's Reporting & Collaboration community, building sophisticated frontend experiences that help customers interact with complex data, configure workflows and make better business decisions.
 


What you'll do
🧑‍💻 Software Engineering (80%)

You'll remain an active contributor to our production codebase, working alongside other engineers on challenging frontend projects.

• 
Write, review, refactor and ship production code regularly using React, TypeScript and JavaScript.

• 
Design and build sophisticated user interfaces for interacting with large datasets, including filtering, visualisation and complex configuration.

• 
Take ownership of engineering tasks and features from technical design through implementation, testing and deployment.

• 
Solve challenging problems involving frontend performance, scalability, state management and user experience.

• 
Participate in technical discussions, code reviews, debugging and architectural decisions.

• 
Collaborate closely with Product Managers, Designers, Tech Leads and Software Engineers to deliver high-quality features.

• 
Contribute to AI-powered product experiences and use modern development tools where appropriate.

• 
Maintain the same technical expectations and engineering standards as our Senior Software Engineers.

You'll continue to write production code, not simply oversee the engineers who do.

📚 Coaching & People Management (20%)

Alongside your engineering responsibilities, you'll help other engineers develop their skills, confidence and careers.

• 
Coach and mentor engineers, sharing technical knowledge and helping them improve their problem-solving abilities.

• 
Hold regular 1:1 meetings with your direct reports to discuss progress, challenges and career development.

• 
Provide constructive feedback, recognise achievements and support individual development plans.

• 
Help engineers establish clear goals and understand the skills required to progress.

• 
Support performance reviews and development discussions, including more challenging conversations when necessary.

• 
Work alongside Tech Leads to understand engineers' technical contributions and development needs.

• 
Help foster a collaborative engineering culture where people continuously learn from one another.

At Pigment, technical leadership and people management are intentionally separated. Tech Leads own the technical direction of teams, while Engineering Managers focus on coaching and developing engineers alongside their own coding responsibilities.

You'll initially focus on contributing as a Senior Engineer before gradually taking on direct reports.

Who we're looking for
You're an engineer first, with a genuine interest in developing people.

• 
You have substantial professional software-engineering experience and are technically operating at a strong Senior Engineer level.

• 
You're currently hands-on with production code and want coding to remain the majority of your working week.

• 
You have strong frontend development experience with React, TypeScript and JavaScript.

• 
You've built complex, scalable applications, ideally within B2B SaaS, enterprise software, analytics or data-intensive environments.

• 
You have experience coaching, mentoring or supporting other engineers through code reviews, pairing, technical discussions or structured feedback.

• 
You enjoy sharing knowledge and helping other engineers improve.

• 
You're interested in taking ownership of 1:1s, career development and people-management responsibilities, or already have experience doing so.

• 
You're comfortable solving complex technical challenges independently while collaborating with others.

• 
You care about product quality, engineering standards and delivering meaningful value to customers.

• 
You're fluent in English. French is not required.

Previous formal people-management experience is a plus, but not a requirement. We're equally interested in strong Senior Engineers who have demonstrated the ability to coach others and are ready to take the next step.

Our interview process
Because Engineering Managers at Pigment spend approximately 80% of their time coding, they go through the same core technical assessments as our Software Engineers.

We want you to understand these expectations from the beginning.

1️⃣ Technical Screen

A technical discussion including a 15-minute code refactoring exercise.

AI assistance is not permitted during the refactoring exercise.

2️⃣ Live Coding

A hands-on algorithmic coding interview focused on problem-solving, code quality and technical reasoning.

AI assistance is not permitted.

3️⃣ System Design

A discussion exploring your approach to designing software systems, evaluating technical trade-offs and solving complex engineering problems.

4️⃣ Final Interview with the EML (Engineering Manager Lead)

A conversation exploring your motivation, engineering mindset, approach to coaching and alignment with Pigment's culture and expectations.

Important: Our Engineering Managers are assessed against the same senior technical engineering standards as our Software Engineers. This is a role for people who genuinely enjoy coding and want to keep doing it.

Is this role right for you?
You'll probably love this role if:

• 
You enjoy writing code more than spending your day in management meetings.

• 
You're a strong Senior Engineer who wants to help others grow.

• 
You want to develop people-management skills without moving away from engineering.

• 
You enjoy the challenge of balancing meaningful individual contributions with coaching responsibilities.

This probably isn't the right role if:

•

• 
You haven't written production code regularly for some time.

At Pigment, you don't have to choose between being an excellent engineer and helping other engineers grow.

Hi 👋 I'm Elvin, Head of Design at Pinpoint.

We're a high growth HR tech company building software that helps in house recruitment teams attract, hire, and onboard the right talent. Today we have a strong foundation in place: a mature product, rapid growth, strong product market fit, and happy customers.

Inside Pinpoint sits a part of the product most ATSs don't have: background checks, right to work, reference checks, one way video interviews and the credits and billing that power them. We call it Marketplace. It's the squad behind the revenue that scales with how much customers use us, and an important strategic bet towards continued growth.

For the past two quarters I've been its designer, its PM and the Head of Design at the same time. The next phase is harder than what we've already shipped, and it needs someone whose whole job it is, which is why we're hiring a Staff Product Designer.

You'll be the only designer on the Marketplace squad, working alongside our Head of Commercial Product (the squad's PM), our Tech Lead, a Senior Product Engineer, and our Head of Roadmap Engineering.

What you should know up front
• 100% remote. You can be based in the UK, Portugal, Spain or Poland, working UK hours, with a few in person team meetups a year. We're headquartered in Jersey with a team of 100 across the UK, EU and US.
• The product is a set of status driven workflows: a check gets ordered, a vendor or a regulator decides what happens next, and the design has to handle every outcome, including the ones that fail. Our third party vendors set what's possible and the compliance rules are fixed, so you'll spend as much time understanding how a vendor actually behaves as you do in Figma.
• AI is how we work, not a tool we're trialling. I ship my own PRs through Claude Code now, and I hadn't shipped one 3 months ago. You don't need to have done that yet, but you do need to be using AI across your work today and to want to learn.
• There's no dedicated researcher. Decisions have been quick and under pressure for a while. We want someone who can make a good call fast and who also pulls the squad toward research backed judgement as the norm.
• Our values actually matter here. We hire people who reflect them in how they work, collaborate, and make decisions.

• Own design for every usage based feature in Pinpoint, end to end: from the first conversation with a vendor or customer, through the spec and the design, to shipped and measured.
• Ship the next phase of Pinpoint Checks: DBS update service with automated routing, rechecks, sending check data to downstream systems, decision and audit flows, and the UK high compliance checks that follow.
• Turn credits from something customers are given into something they understand and use. Credit visibility, self serve costing and in platform credit management are being scoped now and they are yours to design.
• Shape Marketplace product strategy with the PM going into 2027, then execute on it. Discovery here is shared between you and the PM, not handed to you.
• Write the plan into the ticket before anything is built: the decisions made, the edge cases covered, the questions closed, so an engineer (or you) can build it with Claude without a second round of questions.
• Prototype in code where it beats Figma, submit your own PRs for small front end fixes, and QA what ships.
• Be the person Support, Sales and Legal come to when a check is stuck or a customer asks what a vendor does with their data. You'll know the domain better than almost anyone in the company within 90 days.
• Bring Marketplace work to weekly design crit and feed new patterns (status cards, order flows, decision recording) back into Thumbtack, our design system.

• Experience designing complex B2B software products alongside a PM and engineers, with shipped work to show for it. Owning an area as the sole or lead designer is a plus
• Startup or scale up experience and the mentality that comes with it: small teams, few handoffs, and a willingness to do whatever the product needs that week
• Hands on work designing around constraints set by someone else: a regulator, a compliance rule or a third party vendor's API. Background screening, identity, fintech, payments, insurance and legal are the obvious homes for it, and comparable complexity elsewhere counts
• Multi state workflows in the portfolio, such as orders, cases, applications and checks, where the system decides the next step and the design has to handle the moments when it can't
• Familiarity with what changes at enterprise scale: permissions, configuration, multiple personas, and flows that hold up at 10 users and at 10,000
• Daily use of AI across the whole job rather than only to produce screens faster, covering research, testing, investigating bugs, prototyping and documenting, plus the technical depth and appetite to learn to ship small PRs with Claude Code
• Production ready UI craft that clears a high bar, shown in the portfolio
• Ownership of the call when the data isn't there: deciding, explaining the reasoning, owning the outcome, and solving the problem in front of you whether or not it is strictly a design problem. Over time, pulling the squad towards research backed judgement as the norm
• Fluency in commercial outcomes, so margin, adoption and conversion get discussed as naturally as flows and components
• Bonus points for HR tech or ATS experience, and for credits, billing or usage based pricing
You may not enjoy this role if
• You want a research team, a brief and a backlog handed to you. Here you write the brief.
• You're waiting to see how the AI thing plays out before changing how you work.
• You'd rather own the design system or lead a team. This is an IC role on one squad, and Thumbtack governance stays with me.
• Your portfolio is agency work or consumer apps only. Marketplace serves enterprise customers ordering checks at volume, and the panel will test for it.

We want Pinpoint to be the best place you've ever worked, somewhere you feel valued, supported and excited to grow. Here's what you get:
• Comprehensive healthcare: excellent medical, dental and vision coverage for you and your family
• Unlimited holidays: take the time you need to rest and recharge
• Mental health support: unlimited, immediate access to professional counselling via Spill
• Retirement contributions: 401k or pension contributions depending on your location
• Remote first: work where you're most productive, with flexibility and trust as the default
• Equity with real upside: share in the long term value you help create
• Fully paid parental leave: up to 16 weeks of paid leave for new parents
• Learning budget: annual funds for courses, books or anything that supports your growth
A detailed overview of our benefits is here.

What you're wondering
• What does success look like in the first 90 days? By 30 days you can answer a Support question about a stuck check without me. By 60 you own one of the Q4 items end to end with the plan written into Linear. By 90 I'm out of Marketplace standups and you're the named design owner on the Marketplace roadmap.
• How does the design team actually use AI? Designers here ship real PRs, written with Claude against our product and design system repos and reviewed by an engineer like anyone else's. We prototype in code rather than Figma for anything complex, and we've built AI that checks AI: a design code review skill that runs before a PR, plus design system and token compliance checks.
Claude still misses the last mile on padding, states and tokens, so human review is mandatory and nothing ships without it. 
• Is there really no research function? No dedicated researcher, and there won't be one. There is a documented method set, discussion guide templates, and a live list of customers who have agreed to talk to us, with the intro coming warm from their CSM. What's been missing on Marketplace is the time to use it: for two quarters I've been the designer, the PM and the Head of Design at once. You'd have the access. We want someone who can make a good call fast, then pull the squad back toward research backed judgement as the default.
• What tools do you use? Figma, Thumbtack (our design system in Figma and Storybook), Claude and Claude Code, Linear, Fibery, PostHog, Notion and Slack. The product is Rails and React with TypeScript.

ABOUT THE ROLE

This is a senior individual contributor role in our Data Services & Governance team where you'll act as the thought and technical leader owning the semantic layer and analytics standards for Pleo. This means that you won't own a domain but you'll own what good looks like across all of them by developing, improving , maintaining and evangelising our modelling standards and AI-augmented development practices that every Analytics Engineer work with, regardless of which team they sit in. 

The semantic layer you will be designing and maintaining will be the single source of truth that AI agents, BI tools, and analysts query. This is foundational work with company-wide reach which will be ideal for you if you enjoy building things from the ground up. Our semantic layer is still in very early stage. Tooling selection is live, and this role has a strong voice in it. Our BI stack is also in transition so, you would not be inheriting a mature setup and maintaining it. You'd be deciding what it should be, then building it.

For additional context, our tech stack currently include: GCP, BigQuery, dbt Core, Airflow, SQL, Python, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot.




WHO YOU'LL WORK WITH

You'll report to the Data Engineering Manager who oversees the Data Infra & MLOps team as well as the Data Services & Governance team. Your primary relationship will be with Analytics Engineers embedded across the Intelligence function who should come to you for architecture guidance, semantic layer decisions, and standards questions. You will also partner with a Staff Data Engineer on data engineering standards and pipeline practices, and with others on self-serve analytics and BI tooling governance. You'll engage with the Data Serving team on entity definitions and with the GenAI Platform team on what AI-ready data looks like at the platform boundary.




WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

 - Own the semantic layer: define what a metric definition is, how it's structured, where it lives, and how it's enforced. The goal is one canonical definition of Monthly recurring revenue (MRR), churn, transaction, customer - used by analysts, BI tools, and AI tools without divergence. You make that real, not aspirational.

 - Set data modelling standards for the function: what clean, layered, well-tested dbt architecture looks like across all domains, at all levels of complexity. 

 - Build and run the Analytics Engineering community of practice including code reviews, shared patterns, documentation, onboarding etc. The goal is to create a social infrastructure that makes standards stick.

 - Own the AI-native development practice. Use AI coding tools as a native part of how you write, review, and migrate data models (not as a demonstration, but as your actual workflow). Evaluate what works in a governed data engineering context, what introduces risk, and shape how the Analytics Engineering community adopts it.

 - Lead responsible AI-augmented migration work using AI tooling to accelerate data modelling and migrations across the Analytics Warehouse and Operational Data Platform.

 - Design data models and metric definitions in a documented and structured manner enabling reliable consumption by AI services without human intervention.

 - Engage upstream with backend and product engineers to drive data contract discipline and schema ownership upstream, rather than managing inconsistency downstream.

 - Contribute to Data & AI Products for external customer-facing analytics where data modelling patterns and conversational analytics needs and capabilities grow.




WHAT YOU BRING

 - Deep demonstrated expertise in dbt and modelling practices: not just strong modelling, but a formed view of what modelling architecture should look like across a function. You can defend trade-offs, teach them, and enforce them in teams you don't manage.

 - Deep BigQuery and SQL expertise, including performance, cost considerations, and the architectural challenges of complex analytical domains.

 - Real experience owning a semantic layer (LookML, dbt MetricFlow, or equivalent). You have a point of view on what metric consistency should look like at scale, what breaks when it doesn't, and how to design it so AI tooling can consume it without degrading trust.

 - AI-native development practice in a data engineering context. You use AI coding tools (Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, or equivalent) as a genuine part of how you work, and you can be specific about where they add real value and where they introduce risk in a governed analytics codebase.

 - A track record of setting standards across teams you don't directly manage and making them stick by leveraging effective influencing techniques as opposed to relying on authority. 

 - Understanding of what LLMs and agentic tools need from a data layer such as how to model data, write documentation, and define metrics so that AI tools get consistent answers at runtime. 

 - Proven experience engaging credibly with backend engineers on data contracts and with senior stakeholders on what the semantic layer strategy means for the business.




WHY THIS ROLE IS A GOOD FIT FOR YOU



This role is a good fit if:

 - You can hold a standard without needing it applied perfectly, and you know which compromises are fatal and which are just untidy.

 - You genuinely enjoy growing a community of practice through influence rather than authority and you take pride in seeing colleagues adopt and grow standards.

 - You find the "how do we make data legible to an agent, not just to an analyst" problem interesting in its own right, rather than as a trend to keep up with.

This role is not a good fit if

 - You want to own a domain. The Intelligence teams have strong AEs doing that. This role is for someone who wants to own the standards they build to.

 - You advise others to use AI coding tools but don't use them yourself. AI-native development is part of the mandate, not a differentiating nice-to-have.

 - You are more comfortable being consulted than being accountable. The semantic layer and modelling standards you set have downstream consequences across the whole function and in AI features customers use.

 - Mapped the current state of modelling standards and the semantic layer across the function (where definitions are consistent, where they diverge, and what the highest-impact gaps are) to draft a plan the function has bought into.

We're looking for a Head of Data and Analytics to own our data strategy and turn the information flowing through Pod into decisions that grow the business. This is a senior leadership role reporting to our CIO. You'll set the direction for how Pod uses data and the standards for managing it well, and you'll be the person our leadership team turns to for the insight behind our biggest decisions. 

How we work matters as much as the tools. We follow a 'manage the core, free the edge' approach. 

The core is well-governed and observable. Working closely with Architecture on a shared data model so published facts are consistent, joinable and open. Platform Engineering builds and operates the platform. Software teams identify and publish facts they own. 

This role owns the reporting layer: the single, trusted set of business measures and definitions the rest of Pod reports from. Teams across the organisation, from operations to sales to finance, are then free to explore and act on this data for themselves, supported by the analysts this role leads. 

We favour open, engine-agnostic formats over proprietary warehouse lock-in, and we are building AI and agents in as a first-class way to explore and interpret data. 

Here's what our CIO had to say:

"At Pod, data isn't a support function, it's a core part of how we make decisions, serve customers and scale our business. We're looking for someone who can bring together strategy, governance, analytics and AI to create a trusted data foundation that helps every team move faster and make better decisions. This is an opportunity to shape how data is used across the organisation and have a direct impact on our growth, customer experience and operational excellence."

Data Strategy & Leadership -

• As well as Shaping the roadmap for our data capability as a shared, well-governed core, working closely with software engineering and architecture.

• As well as evaluating and introducing new reporting, BI, and analytics tools and platforms that give teams fast, trustworthy access to data, favouring open, engine-agnostic formats over proprietary warehouse lock-in. 
AI, Business Intelligence & Analytics -

• You’ll lead the development of dashboards, reporting and self-serve analytics that give teams fast, trustworthy answers
• As well as partnering with commercial, operations, product and customer experience teams to turn questions into insight and champion a data-driven culture, helping teams move from gut feel to evidence. 
Data Governance & Quality - 
• You’ll establish data governance standards, covering quality, security, privacy and regulatory compliance
• You’ll set and govern data-quality standards such as freshness and granularity, holding teams accountable for the facts they publish
• As well as working closely with IT and security teams to keep our data safe and compliant. 
Team & Stakeholder Leadership -

• You’ll provide dotted-line direction to data analysts embedded in other functions, creating a consistent community of practice across Pod
• As well as being as a mentor and role model, raising data capability across the wider business.

You've built, developed and led high-performing teams, creating an environment where people can do their best work. You also know how to influence and guide colleagues outside of your direct reporting line, building alignment and consistency across multiple teams.

Domain-Oriented Data Thinking

You have experience working within a data mesh or domain-oriented operating model, where business teams own and publish the data products and reporting facts they generate. You understand how to balance local ownership with strong governance, standards and consistency.

AI-Driven Analytics Experience

Whether through natural language interfaces, agent-based experiences or semantic layers, you understand both the opportunities and the governance considerations required to deploy these capabilities responsibly.

- Mentor junior colleagues and contribute to a collaborative, high-standard engineering culture. 
- Maintain high standards of data security and information handling given the sensitive nature of the intelligence and client data our tools support.

**Essential Skills and Experience:**

- A degree in computer science, software engineering or a related technical discipline, or equivalent practical experience. 
- Proven professional experience as a full stack engineer, with solid hands-on experience across backend and frontend development. 
- Strong Python skills, with experience building APIs or backend services. 
- Practical experience with React (or an equivalent modern frontend framework), building production user interfaces. 
- Experience working with cloud platforms (AWS preferred) and cloud-native architecture. 
- Comfortable working with SQL and reasoning about data models. 
- Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to break down ambiguous requirements into a clear technical plan. 
- Good communication skills, able to work directly with Solution Engineers and, where needed, analysts to clarify requirements. 
- A methodical approach to testing, code quality and documentation. 
- High levels of IT literacy, including confidence picking up new tools and frameworks quickly. 

**Desirable Skills and Experience:**

- Experience with Databricks or Spark, or another large-scale data processing platform. 
- Experience with infrastructure-as-code and CI/CD pipelines. 
- Experience working in a small or fast-moving engineering team, ideally building internal tools or platforms. 
- Experience contributing to the consolidation or re-architecture of multiple applications into a single platform. 
- Experience using AI-assisted or agentic development tools (e.g. Claude Code, Cursor) as part of a disciplined engineering workflow – able to critically review, test and take full ownership of any AI-generated code.

What you'll do 🏡💻
Puzzel's leaders need numbers they can rely on, but today our data differs from one department to the next. You will be our data wrangler. You control what goes into our Snowflake data lake, make sure what the business needs is going in, and organise it so every department extracts it the same way, in the same language. You remove ambiguity, such as what counts as a customer, and you own the definitions.
Our AI transformation lead builds on top of this data, so you are laying the foundations. You will report to our CFO and work across the finance team, the customer organisation, AI transformation and anyone who owns data in the business.
You think critically about what has happened and stay curious about it. When you spot an anomaly, you act on it. You rely on evidence, not gut feel, you are confident enough to challenge how we handle data, and you work independently.
AI is part of how we work. You will use it every day to build faster and catch problems earlier, and the data you own is what our AI tools draw on, so it has to be right.
• The data platform. Take ownership of our Snowflake instance: what goes in, how it is structured, and access, cost, performance and security.

• The pipelines. Run and extend our Fivetran and API integrations so data from every function lands reliably, with monitoring and alerts when something breaks.

• The definitions. Agree what each core metric means (customers, ARR, churn, pipeline, headcount, usage) with the people who own the data. Publish one definition, name one owner, and escalate where you cannot agree.

• The data model. Extend our dbt models into a clear, documented schema, from raw data through to a governed reporting layer.

• Reconciliation and quality. Tie reports back to source systems, including financial ledgers. Spot anomalies, trace them to the cause and act on them. A number that does not reconcile does not go out.

• The reporting layer. Build and run the models, dashboards and monthly management pack for the board, executive team and directors, on a fixed calendar.

• The explanation. Each month, explain what moved and why across revenue, ARR, churn, pipeline, margin and usage, and answer the questions the data raises before anyone asks.

• Adoption. Get definitions and reports to the people who need them, in a form they can use, so teams stop building their own versions.

• Experience working within, or closely alongside, a finance team.

• Strong SQL, and experience building a modelled reporting layer in dbt or equivalent.

• Working competence with a cloud data warehouse, ideally Snowflake.

• A track record of analysis that changed a decision, with examples of what you found and what happened next.

• A detailed, evidence-driven approach: experience reconciling data between sources, and a sceptical eye for data that looks plausible but is wrong.

• Experience getting senior people from different functions to agree a definition, then holding the line on it.

• The confidence to challenge how data is handled, and the drive to work independently as a self-starter.

• Daily use of AI tools in your work, with examples of what you built and how you checked it.

• The ability to explain a number, and its caveats, to a board member in a few lines.

• Build synthetics monitoring from the ground up: a distributed probe scheduler and runners (HTTP/gRPC/DNS), availability and latency metrics, and integration with our alerting.

• Harden the ingest path: durability and replay, backpressure and adaptive concurrency, multi-region, and per-tenant fairness and limits.

• Act as tech lead — set technical direction, run design reviews, mentor, and stay hands-on in the code.

• Instrument everything with Logfire (we run on our own product).

• Strong systems engineering skills, comfortable in Rust (our ingest path is Rust) — or able to ramp quickly given strong systems experience in a comparable language.

• Hands-on experience with at least one major cloud's telemetry/logging stack (AWS CloudWatch, GCP Cloud Logging, or Azure Monitor) and its auth model.

• Experience building or operating an observability/telemetry ingestion pipeline at scale.

At Pythian, we are experts in strategic database and analytics services, driving digital transformation and operational excellence. Pythian, a multinational company, was founded in 1997 and started by ensuring the reliability and performance of mission-critical databases. We quickly earned a reputation for solving tough data challenges. We were there when the industry moved from on-premises to cloud environments, and as enterprises sought more from their data, we expanded our competencies to include advanced analytics.

Today, we empower organizations to embrace transformation and leverage advanced technologies, including AI, to stay competitive. We deliver innovative solutions that meet each client’s data goals and have built strong partnerships with Google Cloud, AWS, Microsoft, Oracle, SAP, and Snowflake. The powerful combination of our extensive expertise in data and cloud and our ability to keep on top of the latest bleeding edge technologies make us the perfect partner to help mid and large-sized businesses transform to stay ahead in today’s rapidly changing digital economy.
Why you:
Pythian sits at the intersection of data engineering, AI production, and managed services — helping enterprises turn data complexity into competitive advantage. With three decades of deep managed services heritage and strategic partnerships across the leading cloud and database technology ecosystems, we are at the forefront of helping clients move from AI experimentation to AI in production.
We are looking for a polished, quota-carrying Senior Sales Executive who is energized by the AI moment and knows how to help enterprise clients build the modern, well-managed data foundations that make production AI possible at scale. You are comfortable hunting new logos, converting inbound leads, and growing existing accounts. You bring credibility in conversations about Database Managed Services, Production AI, and cloud and database technologies — and you know how to co-sell effectively with OEM and hyperscaler partners to drive mutual value.
What Makes This Role Unique:
Pythian’s portfolio spans the full stack from data foundations to production AI — Production AI, Database Managed Services, AI Strategy & Automation, Data Migrations, Cloud Consulting, and Agentic AI solutions, supported by partnerships across Google Cloud, Oracle, AWS, Microsoft Azure, SAP, and the broader modern data ecosystem. This means you’re never selling a point solution; you’re building long-term, high-value partnerships with clients who want a trusted advisor to help them scale intelligently.
If you’re energized by the AI transformation happening across enterprise technology right now, know how to sell complex managed services, and want to represent a company with deep technical credibility and a growing AI practice — this role is built for you.

What you will be doing: 
Territory & Pipeline
• Build and execute a territory plan with a disciplined mix of new logo hunting, inbound conversion, and account expansion.
• Maintain a robust, accurately forecasted pipeline in Salesforce; provide weekly pipeline reviews and revenue projections.
• Develop targeted account strategies for key prospects in retail, manufacturing, logistics, financial services, and other enterprise verticals.
• Identify and pursue net-new logos while deepening relationships and expanding wallet share within existing accounts.
AI & Data Services Sales
• Lead discovery and solution conversations around Production AI, AI Strategy, Agentic AI, and AI Automation with enterprise buyers (CAIO, CDO, CTO, CIO).
• Articulate how modern, well-managed data estates — across databases, cloud data platforms, and data migrations — are the critical scaffolding for scalable AI.
• Sell the business case for Database Managed Services and DBA Support, connecting operational reliability to AI readiness and cost efficiency.
• Help clients understand Pythian’s phased “Data Foundations to Production AI” journey and position appropriate entry points based on their maturity.
Partner & OEM Co-sell
• Co-sell with hyperscaler and OEM field teams — including Google Cloud, Oracle — to drive joint pipeline and leverage partner co-sell programs, Marketplace motions, and funded assessment opportunities.
• Navigate partner deal registration, funding programs, and co-sell qualification processes across multiple technology ecosystems to accelerate deal velocity and protect margin.
• Build and maintain strong field relationships with partner account teams, knowing how to activate the right partner resources at the right stage of a deal.
• Serve as the primary relationship owner for your accounts while leveraging Pythian’s delivery, solutions, and field CTO resources as needed.
Deal Execution & Internal Orchestration
• Lead enterprise sales cycles end-to-end: discovery, business case development, proposal, negotiation, and close.
• Act as the internal project manager for your deals — coordinating across Solutions Architecture, Delivery, Legal, and Finance to keep complex cycles moving, ensure scope integrity, and deliver proposals on time.
• Know when and how to engage the right internal resources (Field CTO, practice leads, delivery SMEs) and manage those relationships to build credibility with prospects without over-committing delivery capacity.
• Prepare and present compelling proposals, RFP responses, and executive-level business case materials.
• Document client interactions, capture competitive intelligence, and share win/loss insights to continuously improve Pythian’s go-to-market.
Travel as required to attend client meetings, partner events, industry conferences, and Pythian’s annual sales kickoff.

What we need from you:
• 10+ years of enterprise technology sales experience with a consistent record of meeting or exceeding quota.
• Active experience selling Data & AI services — managed databases, cloud data platforms, AI strategy, or production AI implementations — to enterprise buyers.
• Demonstrated ability to sell managed services: you know who to call, how to build the business case, and how to navigate procurement for recurring-revenue engagements.
• Experience co-selling with hyperscaler or OEM field teams (Google Cloud, Oracle, AWS, Microsoft, or similar), including familiarity with partner programs, deal registration, and funded motions.
• Strong internal project management instincts: proven ability to orchestrate cross-functional resources — solutions architects, delivery leads, legal, finance — across complex, multi-stakeholder sales cycles without losing momentum or scope control.
• A hunter’s instinct for new logos combined with the relationship acumen to grow and retain existing accounts.
• Polished enterprise presence with the ability to engage confidently at VP and C-suite level across business and technical audiences.
• Proficiency in Salesforce for pipeline management, forecasting, and account planning.
Strongly Preferred
• Experience selling within one or more of Pythian’s core technology ecosystems: Google Cloud (BigQuery, Vertex AI, Gemini) and/or Oracle (database, infrastructure), and also AWS, Microsoft Azure, Snowflake, Databricks, or SAP.
• Familiarity with the modern data stack and cloud data platforms across multiple hyperscalers.
• Comfort positioning AI solutions — Agentic AI, GenAI/RAG, MLOps, AI automation — to enterprise decision-makers.
• Experience with Database Managed Services or Infrastructure Managed Services sales cycles and pricing models.
• Background selling into $300M–$1B revenue companies in manufacturing, retail, logistics, finance, or healthcare verticals.
• Relevant cloud, database, or AI certifications are a plus.
Core Competencies
• Strategic territory planning and disciplined pipeline management.
• Consultative selling — ability to diagnose business problems before proposing solutions.
• Influence, persuasion, and consensus-building across complex enterprise buying committees.
• Continuous learning mindset — genuinely curious about AI developments and their enterprise implications.
• Clear, compelling written and verbal communication; strong presentation and proposal skills.
• Relevant Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of experience and education.

What you will receive: 
• Love your career: Competitive total rewards package. Blog during work hours; take a day off and volunteer for your favorite charity.
• Love your work/life balance: Flexibly work remotely from your home, there’s no daily travel requirement to an office! All you need is a stable internet connection. 
• Love your coworkers: Collaborate with some of the best and brightest in the industry!
• Love your development: Hone your skills or learn new ones with our substantial training allowance; participate in professional development days, attend training, become certified, whatever you like! 
• Love your workspace: We give you all the equipment you need to work from home including a laptop with your choice of OS, and an annual budget to personalize your work environment! 
• Love yourself: Pythian cares about the health and well-being of our team. You will have an annual wellness budget to make yourself a priority (use it on gym memberships, massages, fitness and more). Additionally, you will receive a generous amount of paid vacation and sick days, as well as a day off to volunteer for your favorite charity.

 Embedded Security Engineer

 Location:London, UK

 Salary:Competitive

 Contract:Permanent

 Hours:Full-time

About the role 

We are seeking a Security Engineer to join a client team based in London. You will support the delivery and maintenance of access control and CCTV systems across the client’s portfolio, assisting with project implementation, system administration, troubleshooting, and ongoing operational support.

This role is ideal for someone with experience in physical security systems who is looking to further develop their technical skills within a dynamic environment. The successful candidate will work closely with senior engineers and client stakeholders to help deliver projects and support day-to-day operational requirements.

This is an on-site role based in the St Paul’s area of London, requiring attendance five days per week. Occasional travel within the UK and Europe may be required.

What You Will Do

• Support the implementation of access control and CCTV projects, including system programming, testing, commissioning, and project close-out activities.

• Provide remote support for technical issues and break-fix incidents across client sites.

• Assist with planned preventative maintenance (PPM) activities and reactive support requirements.

• Participate in the Request for Change (RFC) process to support maintenance and project activities.

• Maintain commissioning documentation and assist with project handovers.

• Keep project documentation and commissioning records accurate and up to date.

• Travel occasionally within the UK and Europe to support project delivery and technical support requirements.

• Assist with the configuration and administration of C-Cure and Victor systems, including system updates and user requirements.

• Support the monitoring and management of incidents through a 24/7 Command Centre environment.

• Liaise with vendors and technical support teams to assist in fault resolution and system improvements.

• Monitor technical bulletins and communicate relevant information relating to system performance and known issues.

• Support project delivery activities, including requirements gathering, testing, deployment, and documentation.

• Escalate technical or operational issues to senior engineers where appropriate.

• Work collaboratively with colleagues across global teams and functions.

• Assist in the preparation of reports relating to incidents, system performance, and service delivery.

• Participate in team meetings and contribute to continuous improvement initiatives.

• Ensure all activities are carried out in accordance with company procedures and client requirements.

What We Are Looking For

• Experience working with physical security systems, including access control and CCTV platforms.

• Experience with C-Cure 9000, Genetec Security Center/Synergis, or Victor VMS is desirable.

• Understanding of physical security technologies, ICT infrastructure, networking, and server environments.

• Previous experience supporting security system installations, upgrades, or migrations.

• Good working knowledge of Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.

• Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple tasks and priorities.

• Good problem-solving and troubleshooting abilities.

• Strong verbal and written communication skills.

• A willingness to learn and develop technical expertise within enterprise security systems.

NB: The successful candidate will be required to pass our security screening procedures and those required by our client(s) if necessary

 Security Systems Designer 

 Location:London, UK

 Salary:Competitive

 Contract:Permanent

 Hours:Full-time

What we are looking for 

QCIC are seeking experienced individuals to join our Enterprise Design & Build team at Senior Consultant level. The successful candidate will have a background in Enterprise security systems design with the ability to project manage the technical and commercial delivery of projects. This involves managing all aspects of the projects including stakeholder engagement, technical escalation, and financials. The group works simultaneously on several projects for global clients so the ideal person should be comfortable working in a fast-paced environment and running multiple projects consecutively. 

The role will involve in-depth knowledge of a range of security systems including, but not limited to Access Control, CCTV/VMS, Intruder Detection systems and intercom systems. Knowledge of the following systems’ manufacturers would be beneficial but not critical – Genetec, CCURE and Lenel. Working hours may fluctuate as support will be required in multiple regions including APAC, EMEA and US. 

What you will do 

Systems Design 

• Lead on preparing electronic security designs in line with client standards using the QCIC internal design tool for global clients in multiple time zones. The designs are taken through concept and preliminary strategy stages to detailed design 

• Ability to read, understand and apply client specific design standards 

• Design security systems, including hardware specifications, layout plans, and integration requirements taking into consideration current software versions and specifications 

• Develop detailed project documentation, including system schematics, technical specifications, and installation guidelines as well as effective document control management 

• Review and approve equipment specification in line with client standards 

• Present proposed designs to client teams and gain design approval 

• Collaborate with internal applications team and/or systems integrators to allow delivery of systems programming and testing and commissioning of installed systems 

• Stay updated on the latest security technologies and trends, making recommendations for enhancements 

• Ensure compliance with industry standards, regulations, and best practices 

Project Delivery 

• Ensure that projects are completed from design through to deployment within agreed deadlines, within budget and any potential issues escalated in line with internal policy whilst maintaining the clients’ best interests 

• Manage contractor delivery, ensuring quality and risk aspects 

• Act as a point of escalation for the group both technically and operationally 

• Work competently on an independent basis 

• Work collaboratively in a multidiscipline global team 

• Communicate directly with clients and actively participate/lead meetings 

• Continually ensure that practices, policies, strategy, and services represent the client’s and the Company’s best interests, and that Company policy is in keeping with current legislation, International Standards and Codes of Practice etc. 

Commercial 

• Prepare fee proposals and scope of works and update internal systems 

• Manage budgets for the projects within the account 

• Be able to report clearly on the progress and financials of projects and prepare weekly reporting for the account manager/senior management 

• Manage and plan for resources required for the project 

• Report regularly into key stakeholders on project progress identifying achievements and risks and promoting continuous improvement 

NB: The successful candidate will be subject to employment and financial screening

 Salary:Competitive

 Contract:Permanent

 Hours:Full-time

What you will do

• Provide high-quality HR support to facilitate the resolution of everyday people queries and to ensure operational delivery of the full range of HR activities for the business.

• Maintain the HR and benefits systems with any changes to employees, terms, and conditions and produce appropriate letters as needed.

• Work closely with the Senior HR Manager to audit, review, and update all HR policies in line with current legislation and best practice.

 Who are we?
At Qflow, we’re on a mission to transform one of the world’s most impactful industries: construction. Having established Qflow as a trusted solution across many of the UK’s leading Tier 1 contractors, developers and utilities companies, we’re now expanding rapidly across North America and international markets. Today, our platform is deployed across billions of pounds worth of construction projects worldwide, and we’re continuing to grow at pace.
We’re looking for an experienced product leader to help shape the next generation of Qflow’s platform. You’ll work at the heart of the business, translating customer problems into valuable product experiences and partnering closely with Engineering, Design, Data and Commercial teams to deliver products that create measurable impact for our customers.
If you’re naturally curious, love solving customer problems and enjoy turning complexity into simple, scalable products, we’d love to hear from you. This is an opportunity to influence a product that’s transforming one of the world’s largest industries while working alongside a collaborative, ambitious team during an exciting period of growth.
Your team and your role
Our Product team exists to ensure we’re solving the right problems for our customers while delivering products that create measurable business value.
As a Product Lead, you’ll own the product end-to-end, working closely with both the Senior Leadership Team (SLT) and Engineering to translate strategy into delivery. You’ll develop a deep understanding of our users, balancing customer needs, commercial priorities and technical considerations to maximise the impact of every sprint.
You’ll collaborate daily with Engineering, Customer Success, Sales and Data teams to continuously validate problems, prioritise opportunities and deliver features that delight customers.
This role offers the opportunity to shape both what we build and how we build it, contributing to the evolution of our product practices as Qflow continues to scale internationally.

What you’ll be doing

• Own and prioritise Qflow’s product roadmap, ensuring work aligns with company objectives and customer value.

• Manage and mentor a junior product manager, and ensure their work aligns with the wider vision. 
Customer Discovery & Product Thinking 
• Build a deep understanding of customer workflows, pain points and opportunities. 
• Partner with Customer Success and Sales to gather qualitative and quantitative customer insight. 
• Validate assumptions through customer research, product usage data and experimentation. 
• Continuously refine product opportunities based on evidence rather than opinion. 
Cross-functional Collaboration 
• Work closely with Engineering to clarify requirements, remove ambiguity and support efficient delivery. 
• Collaborate with Engineering to create user journeys and intuitive product experiences. 
• Partner with Data teams to define success metrics and measure product outcomes. 
• Work alongside Commercial teams to ensure customer feedback informs roadmap decisions. 
Delivery & Continuous Improvement 
• Support sprint planning, backlog refinement and product demonstrations. 
• Help identify delivery risks and proactively work with Engineering to remove blockers. 
• Monitor feature adoption and customer outcomes after release. 
• Drive continuous improvements to product processes and ways of working. 
Product Communication 
• Clearly communicate priorities, roadmap updates and product decisions across the business. 
• Act as a voice of the customer, and an ambassador for the Product team, ensuring stakeholders understand the “why” behind decisions. 
• Support internal enablement by helping teams understand new features and customer value. 

What we are looking for:

• 5+ years’ experience as a Product Lead, Product Director, Senior Product Manager or similar product role within a SaaS environment. 
• Strong experience working with Agile software development teams. 
• Proven ability to manage and prioritise complex product backlogs.

• Excellent attention to detail and experience in working in data-driven environments; both operationally day-to-day as part of your role, as well as products where data is a core component. In Qflow, data IS our product, so you’ll need to have a high level of data literacy. 
• Experience translating customer problems into actionable product requirements. 
• Strong analytical thinking with confidence using data to support decision-making. 
• Comfortable working with ambiguity in a fast-moving scale-up environment. 
• A collaborative mindset with the ability to build trusted relationships across Product, Engineering and Commercial teams. 
• Passion for building products that solve real customer problems. 
Nice to have
