Scale AI is the data foundation for AI, helping organizations build and deploy reliable production AI applications. We partner with leading enterprises and government organizations to accelerate their AI initiatives through our data annotation platform, generative AI solutions, and enterprise AI capabilities.

Role Overview

As a Forward Deployed AI Engineering Manager on our Enterprise team, you'll be the technical bridge between Scale AI's cutting-edge AI capabilities and our most strategic customers. You'll work with enterprise clients to understand their unique challenges, lead a team that architects specific AI solutions, and ensure successful deployment and adoption of AI systems in production environments.

This is a Management role that combines deep engineering and AI expertise, leading a team, and working on customer-facing problems. You'll work directly with customer engineering teams to integrate AI into their critical workflows.

Key Responsibilities

Customer Integration & Deployment

• Partner directly with enterprise customers to understand their technical infrastructure, data pipelines, and business requirements

• Design and implement custom integrations between Scale AI's platform and customer data environments (cloud platforms, data warehouses, internal APIs)

• Build robust data connectors and ETL pipelines to ingest, process, and prepare customer data for AI workflows

• Deploy and configure AI models and agents within customer security and compliance boundaries

AI Agent Development

• Develop production-grade AI agents tailored to customer use cases across domains like customer support, data analysis, content generation, and workflow automation

• Architect multi-agent systems that orchestrate between different models, tools, and data sources

• Implement evaluation frameworks to measure agent performance and iterate toward business objectives

• Design human-in-the-loop workflows and feedback mechanisms for continuous agent improvement

Prompt Engineering & Optimization

• Create sophisticated prompt engineering strategies optimized for customer-specific domains and data

• Build and maintain prompt libraries, templates, and best practices for customer use cases

• Conduct systematic prompt experimentation and A/B testing to improve model outputs

• Implement RAG (Retrieval Augmented Generation) systems and fine-tuning pipelines where appropriate

Leadership & Collaboration

• Serve as the Engineering Manager and technical point of contact for strategic enterprise accounts

• Lead a team that is collaborating with customer data scientists, ML engineers, and software developers to ensure smooth integration

• Work closely with Scale's product and engineering teams to translate customer needs into product improvements

• Document technical architectures, integration patterns, and best practices

Problem Solving & Innovation

• Debug complex technical issues across the entire stack, from data pipelines to model outputs

• Rapidly prototype solutions to unblock customers and prove out new use cases

• Stay current on the latest AI/ML research and tools, bringing innovative approaches to customer problems

• Identify opportunities for productization based on common customer patterns

Required Qualifications

• 5+ years of software engineering experience with 3+ yrs of Management experience with strong fundamentals in data structures, algorithms, and system design

• Production Python expertise with experience in modern ML/AI frameworks (e.g., LangChain, LlamaIndex, HuggingFace, OpenAI API)

• Experience with cloud platforms (AWS, GCP, or Azure) and modern data infrastructure

• Strong problem-solving skills with the ability to navigate ambiguous requirements and rapidly iterate toward solutions

• Excellent communication skills with the ability to explain complex technical concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences

Preferred Qualifications

Agent Development Wiz

• Deep understanding of LLMs including prompting techniques, embeddings, and RAG architectures

• Experience building and deploying AI agents or autonomous systems in production

• Knowledge of vector databases and semantic search systems

• Contributions to open-source AI/ML projects

Infrastructure Guru

• Experience with containerization (Docker, Kubernetes) and CI/CD pipelines

• Experience using Terraform, Bicep, or other Infrastructure as Code (IaC) tools

• Previous work in a devops, platform, or infra role

• Familiarity with enterprise security, compliance, and governance requirements (SOC 2, GDPR, HIPAA)

Customer Product Whisperer

• Proven ability to work with customers in a technical consulting, solutions engineering, or product engineering role

• Domain expertise in verticals like finance, healthcare, government, or manufacturing

• Experience with technical enablement or teaching programs

Sample Projects

The following are some examples of the types of projects we’ve worked on with customers. All of these projects leverage customer data, integrate directly into customers’ existing systems, and are deployed on their infrastructure.

Deep Research for Due Diligence

For a global professional services firm, we developed a sophisticated deep research agent to assist in due diligence. This agent employs a multi-agent architecture for robust fact-checking, integrates several internal MCP tools, and processes complex, unstructured data sources. This solution reliably saves employees hundreds of hours weekly.

Churn Prediction

Working with a TelCo organization, we built a model utilizing customer data to predict churn likelihood. The system then curates personalized offers based on this prediction. This model was integrated into a "next best action" copilot, enabling call center agents to proactively surface relevant offers to customers, leading to a significant reduction in churn.

Data Extraction Voice Agent

We partnered with a healthcare organization to create a lifelike voice agent and avatar designed to gather unstructured health information from patients. Engineered for low latency, the agent adeptly manages conversational flow, adheres to safety guardrails, and efficiently handles data extraction. This automation saves the organization's nurses hundreds of hours each week.

Sales enablement & GTM onboarding

• Design and run onboarding for new GTM hires - building the curriculum, materials and 30/60/90-day milestones that get sellers productive quickly

• Build and maintain a central library of enablement content (product and use-case overviews, customer stories, competitive positioning, objection handling) and keep it current as our offerings evolve

• Partner with Product, EPD and Marketing to turn new launches and capabilities into clear, field-ready training for the sales team

Sales operations - playbooks, process, tooling & forecasting

• Work alongside the Head of Commercial Strategy & Operations to document and refine our sales playbooks, stage definitions, qualification criteria and deal handoffs, and support their rollout across regions

• Strong commercial instincts and a genuine interest in how deals get won - from first meeting to signed contract

• Excellent written communication - you can turn complex material into clear training content, crisp bid responses and polished executive-level comms

• Strong project management skills, with the ability to run several workstreams and hard deadlines in parallel without dropping the ball

• A strong orientation toward outcomes, and a history of being scrappy when it counts

• Low ego and highly collaborative - you’re excited to work alongside smart, humble teammates and do whatever it takes to help the team succeed

• An easygoing interpersonal style that lets you hold sellers accountable on pipeline discipline while earning their trust, and build credibility with senior external advisors

• Proven ability to build high-trust relationships with a wide range of people across sales, finance, legal and delivery

• Excellent qualitative and quantitative analytical skills

• 2-4 years in sales operations, revenue operations, sales enablement or business operations at a high-growth tech company, or at a top-tier VC firm, consulting firm, investment bank, or similar

job_title: Head of Data Onboarding & Dataset Operations
job_description:
### **About Scalpel**

Scalpel AI is building the foundational AI infrastructure for the surgical supply chain. Our machine vision platform brings intelligence, accuracy, and speed to orthopedic and spine tray operations across OEMs, 3PLs, and Hospital SPDs. Scalpel gives operations leaders a system built for modern surgical logistics, replacing guesswork with data and restoring trust from warehouse to OR.

### **About the Role**

We are looking for aHead of Data Onboarding & Dataset Operations, a cross-functional leader who will design, run, and continuously improve the entire end-to-end process of dataset creation across vendors, hospitals, and product lines.

This person is accountable for the strategy, execution, quality, and timeliness of onboarding thousands of trays into the Scalpel AI platform.

You will be the operational brain behind the dataset — the human equivalent of the AI “Virtual Manager” — ensuring every tray moves predictably from nomination → capture → annotation → model training → deployment → monitoring.

This role combines operational leadership, technical systems thinking, and cross-team orchestration.

### **Your Responsibilities**

##### 1\. Own the Global Dataset Strategy

- Define the roadmap for onboarding vendor datasets (Stryker, Zimmer, J&J, S&N, others).
- Translate customer pipeline into a scalable onboarding plan.
- Prioritise trays and vendors that unlock the most commercial value.
- Drive quarterly coverage targets across specialties (Joint Reconstruction, Spine, Trauma, General Surgery).

##### 2\. Lead the Tray Lifecycle End to End

Be accountable for the entire lifecycle: Nomination → BOM validation → Capture → QC → Annotation → Training → Model QA → Deployment → Monitoring

- Ensure each tray progresses through the lifecycle within defined SLAs.
- Flag delays, anticipate risks, and escalate appropriately.
- Maintain complete operational transparency for internal teams.

##### 3\. Build & Run the Data Capture and Annotation Engine

- Manage capture squads (OEM capture, warehouse capture, hospital capture).
- Scale annotation workflows internally and via external vendors.
- Establish image quality, annotation accuracy, and variant identification standards.
- Ensure predictable throughput for 50–100 trays per month.

##### 4\. Develop Core Operational Infrastructure

- Define and maintain theTrayPassport data model (lifecycle, timestamps, SLAs, owners).
- Partner with Platform Engineering to build dashboards for:
 - Tray status tracking
 - Backlog and risk prediction
 - Accuracy monitoring
 - Vendor coverage
- Define and enforce lineage, auditability, and version control.

##### 5\. Manage BOM Variation, Variant Drift & Modular Trays

- Oversee resolution of discrepancies between OEM BOMs, distributor BOMs, SPD configurations, and surgeon preferences.
- Ensure correct mapping of variants, sizes, and similar-looking instruments.
- Work with Product and CV to build processes to handle missing, extra, migrated, or unknown instruments in real time.

##### 6\. Drive Cross-Functional Alignment

Work closely with:

**Computer Vision**

- Plan training cycles, retraining schedules, and model QA.
- Provide them with high-quality, structured data and active feedback loops.

**Data Engineering**

- Streamline ingestion pipelines, automate QC, and ensure data integrity.

**Ops & Customer Success**

- Plan data capture at OEMs, warehouses, and hospitals.
- Ensure readiness for demos, pilots, and go-lives.

**Product**

- Improve internal tools (Capture app, annotation workflows, dashboards).

##### 7\. Forecasting & Planning

- Create monthly/quarterly forecasts for:
 - Capture capacity
 - Annotation hours
 - Training compute requirements
 - Squad staffing
- Anticipate bottlenecks weeks in advance.

##### 8\. Implement Continuous Improvement Culture

- Continuously optimise capture protocols, SOPs, and workflows.
- Integrate Rapid Capture Protocols (RCP).
- Incorporate synthetic data and CAD-to-Blender pipelines where beneficial.
- Reduce end-to-end tray onboarding timelines from weeks → days.

##### 9\. Metrics & Reporting

- Maintain target KPIs:
 - ≥95% first-pass accuracy on new models
 - ≥99% accuracy after retraining
 - SLA adherence (capture, annotation, training)
 - Weekly throughput per squad
 - Dataset readiness for each vendor
- Publish weekly dataset operations reports to leadership.

##### 10\. Risk Management

- Identify operational risks early:
 - Capture delays
 - Annotation backlogs
 - BOM inconsistencies
 - Accuracy failures
 - Drift
- Implement standard responses, escalation paths, and corrective actions.

##### **What Success Looks Like in 12 Months**

- 1,000+trays onboarded across major vendors.
- End-to-end onboarding time reduced to <7 days per tray.
- Predictable, SLA-driven pipeline with zero surprises.
- High accuracy models deployed for all priority vendors.
- Dataset operations function running like a machine.
- CV team receiving clean, consistent, high-quality training data.

### **Who We're Looking For**

##### **Technical / Operational**

- 7+ years’ experience in:
 - Data operations, ML operations, computer vision ops, or scaled technical workflows.
 - Running large-scale annotation or data pipelines.
 - Managing execution-heavy operations with SLAs.
- Strong familiarity with CV/ML workflows (not deep research, but operational).
- Experience managing vendor teams, offshore teams, or large-scale annotation vendors. 

##### **Leadership**

- Proven cross-functional leadership across engineering, product, and operations.
- Head of Data Onboarding & Dataset Operations 5
- Experience managing teams and external vendors.
- Strong ownership mindset and ability to run mission-critical programs. 

##### **Soft Skills**

- Highly structured thinker.
- Excellent communication skills.
- Strong prioritisation ability.
- Comfortable switching between high-level strategy and tactical execution. 

##### **Nice to Have**

- Experience in surgical workflows, medical devices, healthcare supply chain, or robotics.
- Exposure to synthetic data generation (CAD, Blender).
- Experience building internal tools for dataset management.

### **Why Join Us?**

**Impact That Matters** – Your work directly influences the safety of surgical procedures worldwide

**Work on Cutting-Edge AI** – Be part of a team working with **state-of-the-art computer vision and ML pipelines**

**Competitive Salary & Benefits** – Including a pension scheme and 20 days of holiday + bank holidays

**Start-up Energy** – Join a fast-moving, mission-driven team with big ambitions and strong backing

### **How to Apply**

Send your CV and a brief cover letter to [**_jobs@scalpel.ai_**](mailto:jobs@scalpel.ai)

WE PULL MEDICAL TECHNOLOGY FROM THE FUTURE TO SOLVE HUMAN HEALTH.

 

Scarlet is authorised to assess and certify medical devices. We combine clinical, technical and regulatory expertise with AI agents and software so rigorous certification can keep pace with product development at the world’s most ambitious technology companies, without lowering the safety bar.

Our customers have cut a year or more from their certification timelines for new AI-enabled medical devices and shortened product-update cycles from months to weeks. You’ll join a team building the infrastructure that makes these outcomes repeatable at scale.

 


ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Product Manager at Scarlet, you will own a meaningful product area end to end. You will develop a deep understanding of the people and problems within it, set a clear direction, decide what matters most, and work with product design and engineering to deliver measurable improvements.

You will sit close to regulatory experts, account managers and customers in our London office. Their expertise will give you rich signals, but not a ready-made roadmap. Your job is to turn those signals into a coherent product strategy, make trade-offs openly and ensure what we build improves both the quality and speed of certification.

You will have substantial autonomy. We will trust you to form a point of view, test it against evidence and change course when the evidence changes.

 


RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own the strategy, roadmap and outcomes for a product area, from discovery and definition through launch, adoption and iteration.

 - Partner closely with product design, engineering and regulatory experts to turn complex requirements into clear, trustworthy workflows.

 - Spend time with customers and internal users to understand their work, observe friction and distinguish underlying problems from requested features.

 - Prioritise across customer value, regulatory rigour, operational efficiency, technical constraints and Scarlet’s company goals.

 - Keep the team aligned on the problem, the intended outcome and the trade-offs behind each decision.

 - Communicate product direction, decisions, progress and learning clearly across Scarlet.

 - Help improve how Scarlet practises product management as the team grows.

 


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Evidence of owning and shipping complex products from discovery through delivery and iteration.

 - Strong product judgement, including examples of difficult prioritisation choices made under real constraints.

 - Enough technical fluency to work effectively with engineers on systems, data, APIs and the trade-offs of AI-enabled products.

 - Clear, precise written and verbal communication, including the ability to explain complex decisions to different audiences.

 - Comfort working in ambiguity, taking responsibility and updating your view when new evidence appears.

 - High standards for product quality, reliability and trust.

 


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Experience in health technology, enterprise software, vertical SaaS or another regulated industry.

 - Experience building products for complex, multi-stakeholder or expert-led workflows.

 - Experience with AI-enabled products, including evaluation, failure modes and appropriate guardrails.

 - Experience in an early-stage or fast-growing company where product practices were still being formed.

 


INTERVIEW PROCESS

We typically collapse steps 3 to 5 into one in-person session.

 1. Intro chat with Johnny https://www.linkedin.com/in/johnnytreasure/ - 30 minutes

 2. Engineering and design chats with Niclas https://www.linkedin.com/in/niclaslovenilsson/ and Jono https://www.linkedin.com/in/jono-milnes-13759b79/ - 30 minutes each

 3. Problem solving session with a member of tech ops - 30 minutes

 4. Interview with Johnny https://www.linkedin.com/in/johnnytreasure/ - 30 minutes

 5. Culture interviews with the founders Jamie https://www.linkedin.com/in/jamie-cox-01458b3a/ and James https://www.linkedin.com/in/james-dewar-78758992/ - 30 minutes each

 6. References and offer.

 


APPLICATION NOTE

You do not need to meet every preferred qualification to apply. We are interested in the quality of your judgement, the outcomes you have helped create and the way you learn. If this role excites you and your experience has taken a different route, we would still like to hear from you.

About The Role
We are actively building diverse teams and welcome applications from everyone.

Location: Birmingham (SCC operate hybrid working, which comprises of a mix of office and home working)

Contract Type: Permanent

Salary Package: £26,926 plus large company benefits, a broad flexible benefits scheme, and 2 paid-for volunteering days a year

Hours: Shift Pattern: Four days on, four days off. Alternating between day and night shifts. Each shift is 12 hours in duration.

job_title: Senior Manager, ITOM & AIOps Solution Consulting
job_description:
At ServiceNow, we put AI to work for people. IT operations is where that matters most. When services slow down or fail, everyone feels it. Our IT Operations Management (ITOM) and AIOps portfolio helps organisations see their whole IT estate, predict issues before they reach users, and resolve them automatically. It sits at the heart of our Autonomous IT story.
Our UK & Ireland Specialist Presales Solution Consulting organisation is going through a significant evolution. We’re bringing separate specialist teams together into one organisation with one way of working: one front door for requests, deployment based on deal criteria rather than availability, and a shared set of measures across every domain. We’re doing it because customers buy the platform, not individual products, and our specialists need to show up as one team.
We’re looking for a Senior Manager to lead our ITOM and AIOps presales specialists through this change. This is a quota-carrying sales leadership role and a first-line people leadership role in equal measure. You’ll build a high-performing team, bring them with you through a new operating model, and make sure their expertise reaches the deals and customers where it makes the biggest difference.
How you’ll work with sales
Your team brings specialist depth when an opportunity needs it, and you share accountability for the result. In practice, that means:
• Partnering with the Solution Consulting Directors in each core industry area: Enterprise Industries, Financial Services, Public Sector, Energy Telco & Media, and Ireland. Together you’ll agree which accounts and opportunities to prioritise, how specialists get engaged and how you’ll measure impact.
• Running a criteria-based engagement model. Requests come through a single front door, self-service assets are offered first where they fit, and specialist time goes to the opportunities with the highest stage, value and complexity.
• Building capability across the Core SC community so they can lead standard ITOM conversations and demos with confidence, spot when a specialist is needed, and bring your team in early.
• Creating pipeline with the regions through specialist-led activities such as hands-on workshops, customer connect sessions and value labs, rather than waiting for opportunities to arrive.
You’ll succeed through influence, not reporting lines. Comfort with matrix management is essential.
What you get to do in this role
Lead and grow a high-performing team
• Recruit, coach and develop a team of ITOM and AIOps specialists, growing experienced and emerging talent alike.
• Set clear expectations, run consistent operational and team cadences, and hold the team to a high standard for customer impact and follow-through.
• Build belonging and momentum in a team that’s adapting to a new way of working.
• Develop specialists into T-shaped consultants: deep in ITOM and AIOps, and fluent in how IT operations connects to asset management, security, risk and data across the platform.
Champion the change
• Actively support and help the Specialist Solution Consulting operating model. Translate it for your team, raise concerns early and model the behaviours you expect.
• Establish consistent rules of engagement with Core SC, Account Executives and partners.
• Be data driven using data to support business execution and change
Win deals and drive consumption
• Lead from the front on strategic opportunities, owning the technical win for ITOM and AIOps alongside Core SC and sales.
• Shape cross-domain, platform-level solutions with specialist peers in asset management, Risk & Security, Employee Workflows and Data & AI.
• Make the CMDB a strength in every customer conversation. It’s the foundation of the ServiceNow platform, and your team brings the deepest expertise in the discovery and service mapping that keep it accurate.
• Partner with our Customer Excellence Group to help customers adopt and get value from capabilities they already own.
Enable and influence
• Own the ITOM and AIOps contribution to UK & Ireland SC enablement, from Level 100 for every Core SC to Level 200 champion tracks. Ensure your team is operating at Expert Level 300.
• Track record of building and maintaining reusable assets: demos, use cases, discovery guides and points of view.
• Develop industry points of view on IT operations, and represent ServiceNow at customer, partner and industry events.
• Work closely with EMEA ITOM peers, product management, partners and enterprise architects.
How you’ll be measured
This is a sales role. You’ll carry a quota for ITOM and AIOps across the UK & Ireland, alongside the shared specialist measures that every domain uses.
Quota attainment
Revenue delivered for ITOM and AIOps across the UK & Ireland
Tech-win conversion
How often specialist engagement turns into a technical win
Specialist-sourced pipeline
New pipeline your team creates with the regions
Consumption uplift
Customers getting more value from what they already own
Team capacity
How well specialist time goes to the deals that matter most

To be successful in this role you have:
Experience and leadership (essential)
• 10+ years in IT operations, pre-sales, solution engineering or technical consulting, ideally in enterprise software.
• 5+ years leading pre-sales or technical teams as a people manager.
• A consistent track record of attaining and exceeding quota in a technical sales leadership role, including managing complex sales cycles from start to finish.
• Proven track record of change management execution.
• Experience in a matrix organisation, influencing senior peers and sales leaders without direct authority.
• Strong coaching and talent development skills, including hiring and succession planning.
• Confidence presenting to and advising senior IT leaders such as C-suite, Heads of IT Operations and Heads of Infrastructure.
IT operations expertise (essential)
A deep, practical understanding of modern IT operations, including:
• Observability and monitoring, including event, metric and log correlation.
• AIOps: noise reduction, anomaly detection and predictive operations.
• Discovery, service mapping and configuration management (CMDB).
• Incident, problem and change practices, with ITIL 4 or equivalent.
• Site reliability engineering and service reliability concepts.
• Hybrid and multi-cloud operations, and IT automation.
• The ability to connect operational capability to business outcomes: availability, cost, risk and user experience.
ServiceNow experience (desirable, not essential)
• Hands-on or pre-sales experience with ServiceNow ITOM, such as Discovery, Service Mapping, Event Management, AIOps, Service Reliability Management, CMDB and CSDM, and Digital End-User Experience.
• ServiceNow certifications such as Certified System Administrator, or Certified Implementation Specialist in Discovery, Service Mapping or Event Management.

FAQs
How do I apply for a role?
+−Via the links on our careers pages only – we aren’t able to accept applications via email.

What entry level roles are available?
+−In 2027, we expect to take on around 50 entry-level consultant software engineers. We will not be taking on apprentices or interns in 2027.

What start dates are available?
+−Entry-level developers may join at various points throughout the year, please see our open role pages for details.

Are there any short term or temporary placements available?
+−No. We are not offering any internships or industrial placements at present.

Which permanent role should I apply for?
+−If you are a career switcher or returner, you should apply for the role of Consultant Software Engineer – career switchers and returners.
Otherwise you should apply for the role of Consultant Graduate Software Engineer. Note that you don’t need a degree for this role if you are a proficient programmer.

Can I apply for more than one role?
+−There is no need to apply for more than one role – you can simply indicate your interest in other roles when you apply. In any case, we consider people for all suitable roles so it isn’t critical which role(s) you specify on your application.

Can I work remotely?
+−For your first 1-2 years of training we would expect you to be in the office 4-5 days per week. Beyond that there is greater flexibility, but most of our employees will be in three or more days per week on average.
In practice we are often able to say “yes” to people who wish to work fully remotely for short periods, or have other flexible working needs – e.g. to accommodate caring responsibilities. But there will inevitably be certain projects or activities which require you to attend our offices, so we can’t guarantee that remote working will always be possible.
We are an inclusive employer, so if you have a disability or other personal circumstances that make regular office working a challenge, please do get in touch to discuss further.

Can I work part-time?
+−Unfortunately not. All of our software development roles are full-time roles, at least in the first instance. You may be able to move to part-time working once you have been with us for a while, by mutual agreement.

Do we offer visa sponsorship?
+−For permanent roles, Softwire offers visa sponsorship for non-UK nationals and will cover application costs for a Skilled Worker visa or Indefinite Leave to Remain.

Are there any academic grade requirements?
+−No. None of our roles require any particular academic grades (from school, university or any other institution), and all of our offers are unconditional.

Does Softwire offer careers specialising in particular areas, for example, Machine Learning or Artificial Intelligence?
+−Our engineers typically work across a range of technologies and industries during the first few years of their career, so we don’t generally offer specialised entry level roles, although we value existing experience, and will aim find project assignments that make best use of it.
There are further opportunities to specialise later in your career, for example in Data Engineering or AI engineering. All our roles will feature a strong focus on developing consultancy / client-facing skills, and using AI in an effective, high-quality way.

Can I visit Softwire’s offices to see what they’re like?
+−The final stage group interview for permanent entry level roles is conducted in our offices and will be a chance for those candidates to look around and meet members of our team.
All those that receive an offer of employment from us are welcome to visit our offices before making their decision. Due to the volume of applicants, we are regrettably unable to offer earlier visits – apologies!

What salaries are offered?
+−Full salary details are listed on the job open role pages.

What does the application process look like?
+−There are six stages: submission of the application form; online tests (typically lasting 2 hours); a 30-minute non-technical interview; a 90-minute technical interview; a 45-minute soft skills interview and a final group interview day held in our offices. At each stage we aim to get back to you within two working days, the only exception being after the group interview when we might need more time to make a final decision on your application. All interviews except the final one are conducted remotely, with humans (not bots!) and you are able to choose your own time slots for the interview, using our online booking system.

What is the best preparation for the assessment process?
+−Lots of coding practice! Hobby projects, academic projects, any coding at all. The aim should be to obtain good coding fluency – it’s not about knowing every corner of a language, but about being comfortable working with the basic concepts. We use CodeSignal to deliver our coding test. If you would like to practise using their test environment, feel free to register with them and try some of their exercises. You may also find good exercises on HackerRank and LeetCode. We strongly recommend that you put some practice in before taking the tests, both on the CodeSignal platform and elsewhere, and especially so if you are a beginner.

How much coding experience do I need to apply?
+−We are very much open to beginners applying but to assess you we do require you to have some coding experience, even if it’s only a little. (Without such experience, how would either of us know that coding is something you actually enjoy!) We recommend a minimum of around 25 hours or so before you take our online coding test. And the more experience you do have, the better your chances in our assessment.

How can I get started in coding?
+−You can get started with any mainstream programming language, with the most common examples being: Python, Ruby, JavaScript, Java or C#. (Knowledge of HTML/CSS is useful but they aren’t programming languages.) There are plenty of sites that will teach you the basics, for example, Codecademy. If you’d rather learn more formally, you can try a coding Bootcamp such as Softwire’s Techswitch or the Softwire Coding Bootcamp. Many of these Bootcamps accept candidates with little to no experience.

What training does Softwire provide for software developers?
+−Our entry-level new starters begin with a dedicated, full-time training program over their first couple of weeks, guided by a dedicated mentor. This induction provides a comprehensive introduction to Softwire and the main high-level technologies we use. Following this, they immediately join a team for hands-on training, contributing to a real-world project; either in-house or for a client. This practical work is supported by close mentoring and is combined with part-time, off-project, training sessions for a further three months. Beyond that we offer an optional Level 4 apprenticeship for those that wish to continue with a formal learning programme. Regardless of their path, all new developers receive continuous, on-project reviews from our experienced team, ensuring practical education remains at the core of their development.

What are the working hours?
+−Our employees are contracted for a minimum of 37.5 hours per week. Long working hours are quite rare at Softwire, and few people regularly work much more than 40 hours per week. Employees need to be working during ‘core hours’, to overlap with their team mates. Core hours may vary per team but are typically 10am-4pm.

STARLIMS provides leading Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) solutions that have served customers worldwide for more than 30 years. The STARLIMS suite helps laboratories improve the reliability of sampling processes, manage complex testing workflows and analytical methods, support compliance with global regulatory requirements and industry standards, and deliver comprehensive reporting, monitoring and analysis.
With support centers across the globe, STARLIMS solutions are used in laboratories across a wide range of industries, including pharma and biotech, life sciences, food and beverage, manufacturing, oil and gas, petrochemical, chemical, public health, forensics and environmental, offering global career opportunities.
ABOUT THE ROLE
The Business Consultant is a highly visible position that plays a key role in the sales process and in customer retention. Business Consultants support the Sales team in meeting annual revenue objectives through technical expertise and strategic guidance, and are expected to operate with professionalism, strategic insight and a customer-centric approach.
The role requires in-depth knowledge of the laboratory informatics industry and strong proficiency with STARLIMS products. You will work closely with teams across the organization to develop technical solutions tailored to customer needs, contributing to the overall sales strategy and influencing purchase decisions.
PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES
• Sales Support: Partner with the Sales team to drive the pre-sales process and stay aligned with revenue targets.
• RFI/RFP Support: Contribute the technical sections of RFIs and RFPs, ensuring the content is accurate, comprehensive and competitive.
• Solution Demonstrations: Develop and deliver tailored demonstrations that showcase the strengths and value of STARLIMS and address each customer’s specific needs and challenges.
• Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work closely with Professional Services, Product Management, Sales Operations, Marketing and Support to enable cohesive, efficient pre-sales and post-sales workflows.
• Customer Engagement: Communicate regularly with customers to ensure satisfaction, act as a trusted technical advisor and build lasting partnerships.
• Industry Expertise: Stay current on industry trends, competitive products and emerging technologies to position our solutions effectively.
• Strategic Input: Provide feedback on product enhancements and strategic initiatives, weighing both financial outcomes and customer impact.
• Integrity and Communication: Present complete, accurate information to internal and external stakeholders, keep commitments and uphold company values.
QUALIFICATIONS
• Strong understanding of the laboratory informatics industry.
• Hands-on experience in laboratory environments, or strong familiarity with laboratory operations and informatics requirements.
• Strong understanding of relevant regulatory standards.
• Ability to develop tailored technical solutions and explain complex information clearly.
• Strong problem-solving and analytical skills, with a customer-focused approach.
• Effective verbal and written communication skills for internal and client-facing interactions.
• Collaborative approach to working across departments to achieve business objectives.
Preferred
• Basic experience with SQL-compliant databases, particularly Oracle and Microsoft SQL Server.
BENEFITS
STARLIMS offers market-competitive benefits.
If you are looking for an opportunity to stay ahead of the innovation curve while building on a proven foundation, we want to hear from you.

• Provide feedback to sales and marketing leadership, inducing customer priorities, pain points, and needs 
• Leverage social media to connect with prospects and advance deal cycles.

Who We Are Looking For
The AI and Trading Analytics Researcher (Officer) will be a member of the AI and Trading Analytics team within State Street Associates (SSA), the quantitative research division of State Street Markets. The team conducts quantitative research on financial markets, developing systematic trading models, alpha signals, and analytics that support Markets trading businesses (FX, Securities Lending, etc.). They will also contribute to the development of an agentic AI platform, empowering trading and sales desks to derive insights more efficiently.

The AI and Trading Analytics team operates at the intersection of quantitative research, markets, and technology. Team members work in a hybrid model, spending part of the week embedded on the Markets trading floor at One Congress (OCB) in Boston and part of the week at SSA’s research office in Cambridge. This structure enables close, continuous collaboration with traders while situating the work within a rigorous research environment.

State Street Associates provides the broader research platform in which the team operates. SSA is a long‑standing partnership between State Street Markets and leading academics, focused on proprietary indicators and novel empirical methods. Within this context, the AI & Trading Analytics team collaborates closely with SSA researchers and academic partners, applying statistical and ML techniques to extend core research insights into systematic strategies and predictive signals for internal trading desks.

Working with senior researchers, traders, and technology partners, the AI & Trading Analytics Researcher contributes to end‑to‑end research, from idea generation and model development through validation and implementation. The role emphasizes robust, interpretable, and scalable approaches that bridge academic research, empirical market analysis, and real‑world trading application.

Why this role is important to us
The team you will be joining is a part of State Street Markets. As a leading provider of trading and lending solutions to the world’s institutional investors, we deliver the industry’s most innovative platforms, financing and portfolio solutions. Our capabilities are backed by proprietary, high-value research, insights and indicators that power clients’ investment decisions, accelerate performance and help investors stay ahead of shifting markets. Across our comprehensive set of solutions – data-driven macro market intelligence that give an information advantage; client-first platforms and tools that redefine trading; financing solutions that streamline liquidity access; and portfolio solutions designed to help achieve peak performance – we deliver a breakthrough edge to drive business success.

What You Will Be Responsible For
As an AI & Trading Analytics Researcher, Officer you will:
• Support the development and testing of quantitative models, trading analytics, and alpha signals to address specific Markets business needs.
• Work with SSA research experts and academic collaborators to help translate advanced research ideas into practical internal trading analytics and models.
• Apply established statistical methods and ML to extract insights from large financial datasets and proprietary SSA research indicators.
• Develop and maintain research code, AI-based analytical tools, and model components in Python and SQL, supporting implementation and reuse.
• Collaborate with traders and subject matter experts while embedded on the trading floor to test ideas, gather feedback, and refine analytical approaches.
• Support the translation of research findings into internal tools, systematic indicators, and client‑facing materials.
• Communicate results clearly through written analysis, documentation, and presentations for internal and external audiences.

What We Value
We are looking for highly motivated, quantitatively minded candidates with a strong interest in financial markets and a desire to learn, develop, and apply new research ideas in a practical setting. Successful candidates will have a strong desire to learn and take initiative in solving problems, including a willingness to investigate unfamiliar topics, ask thoughtful questions, seek input from others, and develop their technical and market knowledge over time.

Education & Preferred Qualifications
• Advanced degree and/or relevant experience in a quantitative field such as finance, economics, mathematics, computer science, or a related discipline.
• 1-4 years’ work experience in investment management, investment research, quantitative research, data science, or a similar field involving quantitative analysis.
• Strong quantitative and analytical foundations, with familiarity with statistical analysis, time series methods, data analytics, and machine learning / AI.
• Demonstrated interest in financial markets, with familiarity with concepts in investment management, asset allocation, risk management, or investment strategies.
• Strong coding skills (Python preferred), with a willingness to develop technical proficiency.
• Proactive, motivated, and detail-oriented, with a willingness to take initiative, work through problems, incorporate feedback, and produce accurate analysis.
• Highly effective written and verbal communication skills and the ability to collaborate successfully with researchers, traders, and other stakeholders.

$125,000 - $143,750 Annual
The range quoted above applies to the role in the primary location specified. If the candidate would ultimately work outside of the primary location above, the applicable range could differ.

London, United Kingdom

Apply Now
At Hudl, we build great teams. We hire the best of the best to ensure you’re working with people you can constantly learn from. We think of ourselves as the team behind the team, supporting the lifelong impact sports can have: the lessons in teamwork and dedication; the influence of inspiring coaches; and the opportunities to reach new heights. That’s why we help teams from all over the world see their game differently. Our products make it easier for coaches and athletes at any level to capture video, analyze data, share highlights and more.

Ready to join us?

Your Role

We're hiring a Senior Software Engineer to join our Core Data team in London.

This team builds the systems that power how Hudl understands sport at scale. From identifying players and teams across thousands of leagues to processing the moments that become highlights, stats and analysis, our services sit at the center of Hudl's platform.

As a Senior Engineer, you'll help shape the technical direction of the Global Sports Library (GSL), the backbone that connects identities, metadata and game context across Hudl products. You'll design and evolve APIs, distributed systems and large-scale data pipelines that ensure Hudl products operate from a consistent understanding of the game.

This role is deeply backend-focused and comes with significant ownership. You'll tackle complex engineering challenges around scalability, entity resolution, data consistency and platform architecture, while helping raise the technical bar across the team through design leadership, mentoring and pragmatic decision-making.

The systems you build won't support just one product or one sport. They'll become shared capabilities used across Hudl's ecosystem, powering experiences for teams, athletes and fans around the world.

• Be a key technical leader. You'll support the team by breaking down complex engineering problems, advocating for best practices and guiding others in addition to your focus on delivery.

• Maintain efficiency. You'll ensure your team delivers high-impact work efficiently by focusing on outcomes over outputs. Your leadership will empower the team to make data-driven decisions and iterate quickly on feedback.

• Collaborate across disciplines. You'll work closely with leaders from various disciplines to plan and deliver enhancements across our product suite. Your ability to integrate diverse perspectives will be key to driving innovation.

• Foster Agile practices. You'll participate actively in Scrum ceremonies and play a significant role in maintaining a strong team culture.

Location

Time spent collaborating with your teammates in-office will be a regular part of how you work. We're currently considering applicants within commuting distance of London. You'll be expected to work more days in-office than remote, but will have the freedom to coordinate your specific in-office schedule with your team.

Must-Haves

• Strong technical proficiency. You have extensive experience in full-stack engineering and have spent time with cloud-based systems and services. You're also an advocate of TDD and CI/CD.

• Technical coaching experience. You're comfortable translating requirements, creating architectural proposals and guiding other engineers through implementation.

• A collaborative, team-first mindset. You know building excellent software is a team effort and you're willing to pitch in whenever a teammate needs a hand.

• Mentor mentality. You believe in the multiplier mindset and enjoy helping fellow engineers hone their skills through code reviews and pair programming.

Nice-to-Haves

• Tech stack knowledge. Professional background in C#, GraphQL, Elastic, MongoDB and AWS is ideal.

• Experience with media at scale. You've worked with video encoding and on-demand rendering in a professional setting.

• Passion for sports. You have an interest in the sports world and an understanding of sports analytics is a definite plus.

• Familiarity with hybrid teams. You've worked with hybrid or remote teams before and can adapt quickly to our working environment.

Our Role

• Champion work-life harmony. We'll give you the flexibility you need in your work life (e.g., flexible vacation time above any required statutory leave, company-wide holidays, remote work options and more) so you can enjoy your personal life too. Plus, every five years, we give you a paid sabbatical to unplug and recharge.

• Guarantee autonomy. We have an open, honest culture and we trust our people from day one. Your team will support you, but you'll own your work and have the agency to try new ideas.

• Encourage career growth. We're lifelong learners who encourage professional development. We'll give you tons of resources and opportunities to keep growing.

• Provide an environment to help you succeed. We've invested in our offices, designing incredible spaces with our employees in mind. But whether you're at the office or working remotely, we'll provide you the tech you need to do your best work.

• Support your wellbeing. Depending on location, we offer medical and retirement benefits for employees—but no matter where you're located, we have resources like our Employee Assistance Program and employee resource groups to support your mental health.

Compensation

The base salary range for this role is displayed below—starting salaries will typically fall near the middle of this range.

We make compensation decisions based on an individual's experience, skills and education in line with our internal pay equity practices.

BONUS POINTS:

ABOUT THE ROLE

For years, avatars have been something you watch. You write a script, we render a video, someone presses play. That model has taken AI video a long way but it has a ceiling. A video can't answer a question. It can't read the room. It can't role-play a tough conversation and adapt when you push back.

We're changing that. Interactive Avatars listen, talk, and respond in real time; inside your product, your website, or your internal tools. You bring the logic and the language model; we power the avatar layer: the speech, the expression, the listening, the sense that there's someone actually there.

It's early. Interactive Avatars is in closed beta today, and the teams building on it are pushing it into places we didn't expect - AI sales reps, always-on support agents, interactive trainers, onboarding guides. We're hiring a Product Manager to own it and take it from beta to a platform that thousands of developers build on.

This is a role with real scope. You'll help define what a real-time avatar API should be, the surface developers integrate against, the experience end users feel, and the commercial model that makes it a business. You'll work directly with the engineering and research teams building the real-time avatar stack, and with the design partners already live in the beta.

 


THE PROBLEM YOU'RE SOLVING

Today, a developer who wants a lifelike, real-time avatar in their product has to stitch together a streaming pipeline, a rendering layer, an agent, and a set of hard real-time problems - latency, interruption handling, listening behavior, expressiveness, consistency across sessions, most of which have nothing to do with the product they're actually trying to build.

We have the avatar technology and a working beta. What we need is a PM who can turn that into an API a developer can integrate in an afternoon, trust in production, and build a real business on top of, all while holding a quality bar high enough that the experience feels human, not uncanny.

 


WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

 - Owning the end-to-end Interactive Avatar API. This is the developer-facing surface (SDK, integration patterns, docs), the real-time experience quality, and the path from closed beta to general availability, and defining what the roadmap looks like over the coming cycles

 - Getting close to the developers and teams building on the beta: understanding how they integrate, where the API fights them, which real-time behaviors make or break the experience, and what "production-ready" means to them

 - Translating that understanding into a clear product direction. What to build, in what order, and why, and keeping the team aligned as the strategy evolves

 - Working closely with the engineering and research teams building the real-time avatar stack; contributing clear specs, sound judgment on trade-offs (quality vs. latency vs. cost), and the context that helps them build the right thing the first time

 - Partnering with go-to-market and commercial teams to define how the API is packaged, priced, and sold - a real-time API has a fundamentally different business model from batch video, and shaping that is part of the job

 - Defining and tracking the metrics that tell us whether the product is working across adoption, integration success, real-time quality, reliability, and the commercial signals that prove it's a business


WHO YOU ARE

You've owned a developer-facing product before like an API, an SDK, or a platform and you know that the product is the developer experience. You understand that adoption is won or lost in the first hour of integration, and that trust is won or lost the first time something breaks in production. You build accordingly.

You're comfortable in a space where the roadmap isn't fully formed. You don't need a clean brief to get started. You can talk to developers, watch them integrate, synthesize what you see, and come back with a point of view. You're also honest about what you don't know and willing to update when the evidence changes.

You care about the detail, and you can hold a quality bar for something subjective and hard: a real-time avatar either feels present and responsive or it feels off, and the difference lives in latency, interruption handling, expressiveness, and consistency. You know how to make that bar concrete and defend it.

You think commercially. A new API isn't just a technical surface. It's a business, and you have instincts (or scar tissue) around how developer products get adopted, packaged, and monetized.

 - Comfortable operating in an early-stage, 0→1 environment where discovery and delivery happen in parallel and the roadmap is still being shaped

### The role

You will own and ship core platform systems that power how health data flows through Terra — from upstream data suppliers (wearables, health apps, sensors) into our unified schema, and out to downstream developers and AI consumers via our REST API, Streaming API, and webhooks.

This is not a maintenance role. You will build new data connectors, scale real-time streaming pipelines, harden our authentication layer, and design the systems that handle millions of API calls per day. You will work across the entire stack — from low-level data ingestion to developer-facing API surfaces.

You will ship fast, iterate through feedback loops, and think in first principles. We don't have layers of process. We have ownership and velocity.

### What You Will Build

Unified API & Data Normalisation: Design and extend the systems that ingest raw health data from 100+ upstream providers (Garmin, Fitbit, Oura, Apple Health, Google Fit, Withings, etc.) and normalise it into Terra's standardised schema — consistent today, consistent next year.

Upstream Data Supplier Connector: Architect and build Terra's new upstream connector capability, allowing data suppliers to push data directly into the platform. Define ingestion contracts, enforce data quality SLAs, and ensure schema compliance.

Streaming API: Scale our real-time streaming infrastructure for live sensor data (heart rate, steps, distance) from Apple Watch and BLE/ANT+ devices via websocket listeners. Sub-second latency matters here.

Authentication & Developer Experience: Own the authentication layer for both upstream suppliers and downstream developers. Build the OAuth flows, API key management, and RBAC + least privilege access controls that keep 1,000+ developers secure.

Webhooks & Event Delivery: Design and harden the webhook delivery system that pushes health data events to downstream consumers. Guaranteed delivery. Retry logic. At-scale.

Teams API: Contribute to our Teams API — enabling coaches, researchers, and organisations to aggregate and analyse group data across athletes, patients, and study participants.

Health Scores & Derived Data: Build the backend systems that transform raw health metrics into validated scores (recovery, strain, stress, immunity) backed by research.

Infrastructure & Reliability: Maintain 99.5%+ uptime on a platform that processes billions of events. Design for fault tolerance, observability, and horizontal scale

### What We Are Looking For

5+ years of production backend engineering. You have shipped systems that handle real traffic at scale. Not toy projects — real, battle-tested infrastructure.

Deep API design experience. You've built REST APIs consumed by external developers. You understand versioning, rate limiting, pagination, error handling, and what it takes to make a developer love your API.

Strong with distributed systems. Message queues, event-driven architectures, stream processing, data pipelines — you've built and operated them.

Proficiency in Python and/or Go. Our stack is opinionated. You should be deeply fluent in at least one.

Database expertise. PostgreSQL, Redis, time-series stores. You know when to use what and how to make it fast.

Cloud-native mindset. AWS/GCP. Containers. CI/CD. Infrastructure as code. You don't wait for DevOps — you are DevOps.

Security-first thinking. Encryption in transit and at rest (TLS 1.2+, AES-256). Data minimisation. GDPR, HIPAA, SOC 2 are not afterthoughts — they're built in from the start.

Autonomous and fast. You don't need to be told what to do. You see the problem, you own it, you ship the fix. High velocity, high standards.

### Big Plus

You are an athlete. You train, you compete, you push limits — or at the very least, you are obsessed with quantifying your own data. The discipline, ambition, and courage it takes to show up every day and get better is the same energy we run on. If you understand the data because you live it, you'll build a better product.

### How we work

We are a high-velocity team. We think in first principles, build via feedback loops, and default to "yes." When someone says something is hard, we focus on how to build it, not whether to.

Skin in the Game. Everyone has equity. Everyone has stake. Your work directly moves the platform.

Deep Work. We protect focus time. No meeting culture. We ship, not talk.

## About Tetrate

Tetrate will become the standard for delivering AI at scale for enterprises. Engineers building AI agents expect their tools to be fast and dependable, but instead, they often get scattered API keys, no cost visibility, no policy enforcement, no fallback when a provider degrades, and a six-month infrastructure project between them and production. Nobody can meter, govern, or optimize what nobody can see, and as AI becomes the standard way business gets done, every enterprise ends up with a version of this problem.

Our answer is a global AI traffic orchestration layer, built on Envoy. The market knows it today in an early form as the AI gateway, but as agents multiply and begin calling models, tools, and each other, this layer is where cost, policy, identity, and reliability get decided for humans and agents on the same terms. Policy is set once and enforced wherever the workload has to sit—on-prem, in-region, or at the edge. This makes return on investment and data sovereignty stop competing with each other.

Envoy already carries traffic at this scale, meaning the data plane is proven before we ship it. With eight years of running tier 0 infrastructure for regulated industries, we arrive knowing what a security review, an audit, and a production incident actually demand. Enterprises get this as a product rather than a transformation program, and publicly, we frame it as transforming application and agentic networking for the multi-cloud era.

The role

The Retention & Recovery Lead owns one pipeline that follows every merchant from the first sign they might leave, through retention, a well-run exit and collections, to write-off or debt sale.

Today we treat churn and collections as separate problems, and neither has a clear owner. In practice they are usually the same merchant at different points in time: a merchant who goes quiet in March becomes, by June, an unpaid fee, a terminal still in the field and a balance nobody is chasing. Collections activity also sits in pockets across the business, from unpaid subscriptions and fees, negative balances and chargebacks to terminal recovery, dissolved companies and fraud losses. As our credit products grow, so will the need.

You’ll bring all of this together under one strategy, one queue and one set of metrics. We want someone who knows collections and its pain points, and who approaches the whole lifecycle with a product and design mindset: redesigning journeys end to end, and deciding where AI and automation belong and where people add the most value. You’ll start hands-on and build a small credit control team as the capability grows.

What you’ll do

 - Own the retention-to-recovery pipeline end to end, from the first churn signal to write-off or debt sale, running from one prioritised queue with one set of definitions.

 - Work with our data team to build and run an AI retention engine that identifies merchants heading towards churn, recommends the next best action for each and puts them in a queue to be worked. Prove what works with holdout groups, and do more of it.

 - Agree with Commercial how save conversations are delivered, and make sure our own risk actions, such as held settlements, are weighed before they push a good merchant out.

 - Design a proper exit for every merchant who leaves: a recorded reason, fees stopped, terminal returned, final balance netted and a final statement, so merchants do not need to contact Customer Relations to close their account.

 - Build automated collections that start the day a balance turns negative: settlement netting, direct debit, card on file, payment links and payment plans. Journeys run through the Teya app and portal first, with phone as the exception.

 - Run managed and external recovery for larger balances: credit control, payment plans, an agency panel, write-off thresholds and, as a last resort, debt sale.

 - Own the recovery strategy for fraud-related balances with Fraud Operations and Legal. They keep investigation and legal action; you make sure every balance has a recovery route and a priority.

 - Run the existing book as a separate remediation project with its own end date, so it does not pull focus from the new flow.

 - Connect the work of Billing, Payments, Logistics (terminal recovery), Credit, Customer Relations and the termination and withheld funds process into one joined-up flow.

 - Define and own the pipeline’s metrics, report them monthly, and feed what you learn back into onboarding, pricing and risk policy.

 - Prepare the capability to scale with Teya’s growing credit book, and hire and lead the credit control team.

What success looks like

In your first six months

 - Definitions agreed and reported for flow recovery rate, stock recovery rate and true churn.

 - A single queue live, worked by hand from simple rules while the model is built.

 - An exit process in place for every leaving merchant, and an automated collections first version running in at least one market.

 - The credit control team hired or in hiring, and the legacy book project under way with a clear plan.

By the end of your first year

 - The first retention model live, beating the rules-based baseline and tested against holdout groups.

 - Flow recovery rate by day 90 tracking towards our 70% target, with time to recovery and cost to collect reported monthly.

 - The first debt sale completed, where the legal and data preconditions are met.

 - Measurably fewer Customer Relations contacts from merchants who are leaving or owe us money.

 - Hands-on collections or recovery experience at some point in your career, ideally with small businesses, covering payment plans, agencies and write-offs, so you know where the pain points sit.

 - Experience with retention, churn or customer lifecycle work, or a clear view of how retention and collections connect.

 - A strong product mindset: you think in journeys, systems and outcomes, not only operational volume.

 - A track record of designing, rolling out and running new processes, shipping a working first version quickly and improving it.

 - A practical, curious approach to AI and automation, with the judgement to know where they help and where they don’t.

 - Comfortable with data: defining metrics, working with data scientists on models and reading the results of tests and holdouts.

 - Experience in a smaller, fast-moving company such as a start-up, scale-up or fintech. Experience at larger organisations is welcome alongside this.

 - Strong stakeholder management across Risk, Commercial, Finance, Billing and Legal, and the ability to get teams behind one approach.

 - A clear, confident communicator in writing and in person, highly motivated and able to work independently.

Nice to have

Introducing The Insights Family

The Insights Family exists to know what kids and families do next. Since 2017 we have listened to kids, young adults and parents at a scale no one else can match: close to a million people a year across 22 markets, more than 5.5 billion data points and counting. We are not a panel you dust off once a year. We are an always-on instrument, and the world's leading media, entertainment, toy, licensing, advertising and consumer brands use us to replace guesswork with independent, real-time evidence. 

Kids sway 78% of family spending, yet most decisions about the trillion-dollar family economy are still made on assumption and instinct. The kid sets the agenda; the parent makes it real, and our job is to put their real voice into the rooms where the biggest decisions get made. Our next chapter is about scale: deepening our footprint across EMEA and accelerating growth in the US from our locations in Manchester, London and New York. If you want to help define a category rather than follow one, this is the place to do it. 

**Our Culture and Values** 
As a growing business, ensuring we are all committed to our core values is vital to creating the culture we all want to work within and establishes the foundations for high performance and growth. 
The core values we crafted as a team: 
• Accountable: Embracing ownership across all aspects of our business, including actions, decisions, and outcomes, and willingly taking responsibility for the results we achieve. 
• Inquisitive: Having a strong desire to learn, explore, and ask questions, and being curious about finding new solutions and opportunities. 
• Collaborative: Working together as a team, fostering a cooperative environment, and leveraging collective expertise to achieve shared goals. 
• Data-Driven: Relying on evidence, analytics, and insights to guide decision-making and drive our strategies. 
• Supportive: Providing assistance, encouragement, and resources to team members, customers, and partners, fostering a supportive and nurturing environment. 
• Empowered: Encouraging individuals to take ownership of their work, providing them with the autonomy and resources needed to make impactful decisions and drive innovation. 
• Customer-First: Putting customers' needs and satisfaction at the forefront of business decisions and strategies, prioritising their success and providing exceptional experiences and value. 

About the role

A lot of companies treat customer success as a help desk. Answer the question, run the quarterly review, hope the renewal comes in. We see it differently. Our customers pay us for answers about kids and families, so every question they ask tells us something about what they are trying to do next, and nobody at TIF hears more of those questions than this role. 

You will look after your own portfolio of customers, and you will own all of it: the relationship, the renewal and the growth. The day-to-day support matters and we want it done brilliantly, but the job does not stop when the query is answered. If a customer asks about one market, show them what the data says about the next one. If half their 
team never logs in, find out why. When you spot a way we could be more useful to a customer, that is your opening, and often our next piece of revenue. 

To be clear, this is a growth role. You will carry a number for the accounts you look after, and we will measure you on retention and expansion, not on how many tickets you close. It suits someone who genuinely likes customers and likes selling, and who would rather bring a customer an idea than wait for renewal season. The role covers 
five areas: 

**Portfolio Ownership & Growth Planning 
**• Own the end-to-end relationship for a portfolio of named accounts, from onboarding through adoption, renewal and growth, with responsibility for the portfolio's growth revenue: upsell, cross-sell, seat growth and tier upgrades. 
• Build account growth plans tied to each customer's business outcomes, and forecast your expansion pipeline with sales-level rigour. 
• Work with the VP Customer Success, Sales and CEO on account priorities, mapping stakeholders and building multi-threaded relationships with economic buyers, not just day-to-day users. 

**Insight-Led Support & Findings** 
• Own day-to-day customer queries and treat every one as an intent signal: resolve it quickly and well, then bring back what else the data shows. 
• Work with Research Solutions to turn TIF data into proactive, account-relevant findings that open the next value conversation. 
• Make support visible and repeatable: log every touch, spot patterns in what customers ask, and feed them into product and commercial conversations. 

**Adoption, Health & Whitespace** 
• Live in our portal usage data and customer health signals to spot whitespace, adoption gaps and risk early, and help shape how we measure customer health across all accounts. 
• Partner with Sales on handoffs and kick-offs, then lead onboarding of new accounts with clear first-90-day value milestones that shorten time-to-value. 
• Drive adoption of new TIF products as they launch, including Trackers, Custom Audiences, the API and our customer AI Agent, meeting customers where they are. 

**Commercial Conversations & Renewals** 
• Lead renewal conversations early and commercially, negotiating value and impact, not just avoiding churn. 
• Deliver Quarterly and Executive Business Reviews that make the quantified case for expanded investment. 
• Convert findings into qualified expansion opportunities and carry them through to close, contributing to team-wide Net Revenue Retention (NRR) by flagging risk early and supporting peers. 

**Proof, Advocacy & Referral**

• By 6 months: A steady rhythm of insight-led business reviews, renewals engaged early with no surprises, and a growing expansion pipeline with your first growth revenue closed.

• Your curiosity default is tuned to 'what else', 'what now', 'how can I go faster'.

Overview
Thorn SDS is a UK specialist Managed Service Provider. We empower technology professionals and organisations across the Space, Defence, and Security sectors — and now, we’re growing our team with a Data and Migration Engineer who’s ready to make an impact.
Join an existing team designing and building the shared tooling needed to migrate services and data onto a new enterprise platform. Help turn the Migration Approach into reusable automation that supports migration preparation, rehearsal and execution.
This hands-on role suits an adaptable engineer who enjoys collaborative, agile delivery across unfamiliar technologies. Manual investigation will sometimes be needed, but the emphasis is on automating repeatable high-risk work.
Security Clearance
Successful applicants will be required to obtain a high level of security clearance prior to appointment. (See: Gov.UK – United Kingdom Security Vetting)
What you’ll be doing
You’ll work as part of a medium-sized delivery team, taking ownership of technical tasks and helping to ensure solutions are delivered to the required quality, budget and timescales. Responsibilities include:
Discovery and assessment
· Live inventory: Automate discovery and inventory refreshes, highlighting changes, dependencies and information gaps while retaining source traceability.
· Migration Discovery: Support discovery of high level data migration requirements for each application set and their dependencies populating a Migration Passport.
Migration tooling design and delivery
· Reusable automation: Help design, build and integrate scripts, frameworks, pipeline templates and runbooks for the shared migration fabric.
· Reliable execution: Enable non-production rehearsals and safely rerunnable workflows, with recovery controls and controlled promotion of tested tooling.
Target-platform integration
· Infrastructure and storage: Automate integration with VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF), NSX, Dell PowerScale and Dell PowerFlex through agreed interfaces, accounting for storage mapping, permissions, metadata, capacity and performance.
· Containers and delivery: Develop containerised tooling and repeatable Kubernetes deployments where appropriate. Integrate CI/CD, infrastructure as code (including Terraform), image registries and binary repositories.
· Engineering controls: Automate builds, tests, dependency versioning, security checks and artefact promotion, maintaining traceability and respecting access, secrets and connectivity constraints.
Monitoring and validation
· Migration visibility: Integrate platform monitoring and logging, potentially Elastic Stack, to automate progress reporting, diagnostics and evidence capture.
· Data integrity: Allow for automation of source-to-target reconciliation using counts, volumes and checksums as appropriate, with item-level checks where needed. Account for authorised transformations and live-source changes; link results and exceptions to migration records.
Working approach and scope
· Design contribution: Contribute engineering input to the Migration Tooling and Pipeline Design as required, covering tooling options, movement paths, interfaces, orchestration, validation and recovery. Support prototypes, design documentation and reviews without assuming overall design ownership.
· Collaborative delivery: Work iteratively with the existing team, platform service owners and migrating parties. Produce maintainable code, automated tests, clear documentation and practical handover material.
· Platform boundaries: Consume agreed platform capabilities rather than creating parallel services. Support migrations without assuming ownership of every migration or the underlying platform.
· Future extension points: Allow for data cataloguing, tagging, archiving and records keeping; delivery of these capabilities is not currently agreed in scope.
What you’ll bring
• Experience in designing and developing automation using Ansible, Python, Bash/PowerShell or similar languages, including APIs and error handling

• Applying software delivery practices, including version control, code reviews, automated testing, CI/CD and infrastructure as code

• Delivering migration and synchronisation tasks, validating data completeness and integrity throughout

• Working with virtualisation, enterprise storage, permissions and infrastructure dependencies

• Supporting containerised tooling, monitoring, logging and technologies such as Kubernetes and persistent storage

• Troubleshooting complex integration issues across platforms, adapting to unfamiliar technologies and communicating findings clearly

• Working with technologies such as VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF), Dell PowerScale, Dell PowerFlex, Terraform and Elastic Stack

• Managing container builds, image registries, software repositories and controlled artefact promotion

• Supporting Windows/Linux, databases, file and object storage, directory services and dependency mapping

• Planning migration rehearsals, synchronisation, cutover and recovery activities to minimise disruption

• Working in secure or restricted-connectivity environments, supporting metadata, cataloguing, archiving and records management

• Producing technical documentation to support implementation, governance and ongoing support

• Maintaining engineering and security standards while keeping up with industry developments and building effective working relationships

What You’ll Get
• Competitive salary

• 25 days Annual Leave that length with years of service (plus Bank Holidays)

• Employer Pension Contributions

• Group Life Insurance

• Dental & Health Cashback Plans

• Wellbeing Services (includes GP, Physio and Savings Benefits)

• Thorn Wellbeing Support Contribution

• Octopus EV Salary Sacrifice Scheme

• Supported Training & Personal Development Opportunities

Ready to Take the Lead?
If you’re looking to push your career forward in a secure, technically demanding environment, we’d love to hear from you. Join Thorn SDS and play a key role in delivering, integrating and supporting resilient enterprise server infrastructure where it matters most.
Important Information
All applicants must already hold the Right to Work in the UK.
Successful applicants will be required to obtain the appropriate UK Government Security Clearance prior to appointment and must meet the required eligibility criteria.
Due to the nature of our work, factors including nationality, previous nationalities and country of birth may affect the projects or roles for which an individual is eligible. Further information on national security vetting and clearance eligibility is available on GOV.UK.
A full UK driving licence would be advantageous, as occasional UK travel may be required.
