About Thorn SDS
Thorn SDS is a specialist Managed Service Provider supporting organisations and professionals across the Space, Defence and Security sectors.
Thorn SDS is seeking a proactive, organised and people-focused Internal Recruiter to manage the end-to-end recruitment process across the business. The successful candidate will work closely with hiring managers and department heads to understand recruitment requirements, attract high-quality candidates and ensure vacancies are filled efficiently with the right people.
The Role
Your responsibilities will include:
• Manage the recruitment lifecycle, from vacancy approval and job advertising through to offer and pre-employment checks.

• Work closely with hiring managers to understand role requirements, skills, experience and cultural fit.

• Write engaging and accurate job descriptions and advertisements.

• Source candidates through job boards, LinkedIn, social media, referrals and other recruitment channels.

• Screen CVs, conduct initial telephone and video interviews, and shortlist suitable candidates.

• Coordinate interviews, gather feedback and maintain communication with candidates throughout the process.

About You
You’ll be an experienced recruiter who enjoys working in a fast-paced environment and can confidently manage multiple vacancies across both our UK sites and in Germany.
You’ll have:
Essential
• Previous experience in an internal recruitment, talent acquisition or agency recruitment role

• Experience managing multiple vacancies and prioritising competing demands

• Strong candidate sourcing, CV screening and interviewing skills

• Excellent communication, relationship-building and stakeholder management abilities

• Strong organisational skills and attention to detail

• Ability to work independently, use initiative and meet recruitment deadlines

• Good working knowledge of Microsoft Office and recruitment systems

Desirable
• Experience recruiting technical and operational roles

• Experience recruiting within the security, defence, engineering, technology or other regulated sectors

• Experience using an applicant tracking system (ATS), LinkedIn Recruiter and online job boards

• Knowledge of UK employment legislation and right-to-work requirements

• Experience developing talent pipelines and advising hiring managers on recruitment strategy

Benefits
· 25 days annual leave increasing with length of service plus Bank Holidays
· Hybrid working
· Employer pension contributions
· Group Life Insurance
· Health & Dental Cashback Plans
· Wellbeing support, including GP and physiotherapy services
· Thorn Wellbeing Support Contribution
· Octopus EV Salary Sacrifice Scheme
· Employee Referral Scheme
· On-site parking
· Training and professional development opportunities
Applicants must have the Right to Work in the UK and either hold, or be eligible to obtain, UK National Security Clearance.

Take the Next Step in Your Defence Engineering Career
Thorn SDS is a niche Managed Service Provider, who are committed to enabling technology organisations and professionals to thrive within the Space, Defence and Security sectors.
Join Thorn SDS as a Senior IT Engineer, taking greater ownership of technical delivery across Defence and Security environments. You’ll remain hands-on while solving more complex problems, delivering project work and supporting less experienced engineers.
What You’ll Do
· Install, configure and support IT hardware, software, servers and infrastructure.
• Diagnose and resolve complex hardware, software, operating system and network issues.

• Deliver network and infrastructure work including switching, routing, VLANs, cabling and connectivity.

• Plan and deliver upgrades, deployments, migrations and decommissioning activities.

• Own defined work packages or smaller technical projects, including testing and documentation.

• Produce and maintain accurate technical, configuration and asset documentation.

• Work with customers, project teams and technical stakeholders to resolve delivery issues.

• Provide technical guidance, coaching and knowledge sharing to IT Engineers and colleagues.

What We’re Looking For
You’ll have established hands-on IT engineering experience and be comfortable working independently. Experience in several of the following would be valuable:
• Windows desktop and server environments, Microsoft 365 and Active Directory.

• TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, switching, routing and VLANs.

• IT infrastructure, structured cabling and hardware deployment.

• Linux or other operating systems.

• Technical troubleshooting, documentation and project delivery.

• Mentoring or supporting less experienced technical colleagues.

• Relevant certifications such as CompTIA Network+ or Security+, Microsoft certifications or Cisco CCNA are welcome, but practical capability, communication and continued technical development are most important.

What You’ll Get
• 25 days Annual Leave, plus Bank Holidays and length-of-service increases.

• Company pension, Life Insurance, Health & Dental Cashback Plans and EV Salary Sacrifice Scheme.

• Wellbeing services, including access to a GP and physiotherapy.

• Support towards professional certifications and ongoing technical development.

• A clear route into Specialist / Lead roles across Infrastructure, Networking, Cloud or Cyber Security.

• Employer Pension Contributions

Develop Your Career:
If you have the expertise to support this requirement and are eager to make an impact in a critical role, please apply today!

Important information
All applicants must already hold the Right to Work in the UK.
Successful applicants will be required to obtain the appropriate UK Government Security Clearance prior to appointment and must meet the required eligibility criteria.
Due to the nature of our work, factors including nationality, previous nationalities and country of birth may affect the projects or roles for which an individual is eligible. Further information on national security vetting and clearance eligibility is available on GOV.UK.
A full UK driving licence would be advantageous, as occasional UK travel may be required.

Overview

Thorn SDS is a specialist Managed Service Provider based in Alton, Hampshire. We empower technology professionals and organisations across the Space, Defence, and Security sectors — and now, we’re growing our team with a Senior Network Engineer who’s ready to make an impact.

This is a full-time role (5 days per week) based in North Hampshire area but will initially involve occasional travel nationwide for site installation. You’ll be working independently but as part of an integrated delivery team. In terms of seniority you would be operating at a senior engineer level (SFIA Level 5), shaping and supporting mission-critical network infrastructure in highly specialised environments.

Security Clearance
Due to the nature of the work, you must hold – or be eligible to obtain – a high level of National Security Clearance. (See: Gov.UK – United Kingdom Security Vetting)

Some UK travel with overnight stays may be required.

What You’ll Be Doing

You’ll own and optimise complex network environments, getting hands-on across a wide range of technologies and responsibilities. You will be responsible for network architecture, firewall design and configuration, integration with the existing network infrastructure, connectivity testing, security policy implementation, and production of the associated design and as-built documentation.

The role will span multiple customer projects but will initially be dealing with the replacement of a site-to-site analogue link with a digital IP based solution. This involves developing a low-level network design, associated build and configuration documentation and performing the implementation of these.

Specifically, you will take ownership of the networking aspects of the project, including:

• Design Phase:

• Delivery of high-level and low-level network design.

• Contribute to network security approach including firewall considerations and any security zoning inline with site / MoD policy.

• Define network monitoring requirements and solution.

• Build Phase:

• Configure network addressing

• Configure management access controls

• Support security accreditation

• Contribute to test planning and support the test execution.

• Physical installation at site (Firewall, Servers, LAN)

• Contribute to MoD Engineering Change Request documentation.

What You’ll Bring

• Proven experience as a Senior Network Engineer

• Strong capability across most of:

• Routing & Switching

• Network Security including Firewalls

• Network device installation

• Monitoring & Management

• Network Virtualisation

• Network Automation

• Excellent troubleshooting skills and the ability to untangle complex issues

• Certifications such as CCNA / CCNP (or equivalent) are a bonus

• Strong communicator and collaborator

• Analytical mindset with attention to detail

• Ideally, knowledge and experience of MoD Engineering Change Request artefacts

What’s In It For You

• Competitive salary

• 25 days Annual Leave (plus Bank Holidays) lengthens with years of service.

• Employer Pension Contributions

• Group Life Insurance

• Dental Cashback Plan

• Health Cashback Plan

• Wellbeing Services (includes GP, Physio and Savings Benefits)

• Thorn Wellbeing Support Contribution

• Cycle to Work Scheme

• Supported Training & Personal Development Opportunities

• Octopus EV Salary Sacrifice 

Ready to Take the Lead?

If you’re looking to push your career forward in a high-stakes, fast-moving environment, we’d love to hear from you. Join Thorn SDS and become a key player in delivering secure, reliable network solutions where they matter most.

All applicants must have the Right to Work in the UK.

Apply now and shape the future of secure networking.

The Reality
We're a 30-person company with more than 3.4 billion downloads of our open-source cloud-native API gateway. Our technology powers critical infrastructure across financial services, healthcare, retail, transportation, and public-sector organizations globally. We're building strategic partnerships with NVIDIA, Oracle, Nutanix, HPE, SUSE, Microsoft, and others. We're at an inflection point where AI security and cloud-native adoption are creating unprecedented demand for what we've built.
We have a strong technical team, but customer demand is outpacing our capacity. We need another exceptional solutions architect who can meet the bar our existing team has set. That means deep technical expertise, excellent customer presence, and the ability to solve complex problems under pressure.
What We're Building
Traefik Labs provides the connectivity layer for modern infrastructure. We started with the most popular cloud-native API gateway (Traefik Proxy), then added enterprise API Gateway capabilities with security and governance, and now offer full API Management with developer portals, versioning, and lifecycle controls (Traefik Hub).
Recently, we've added AI Gateway for securing LLM deployments and MCP Gateway for AI agent governance. These aren't theoretical features. Enterprises are deploying AI in production right now and need someone who can design the architecture, prove it works, and get it into production with security, scalability, and observability.
The Role
You'll join our solutions architecture team in EMEA, reporting directly to me (the CEO). The bar is high because our existing solutions architects are exceptional. You'll need to be technical enough to architect complex deployments, solve real problems in customer environments, and write code when required. But you also must be comfortable in front of technical leaders, CTOs, present at industry events, and win technical trust in high-stakes evaluations.
You'll work on landing new logos and expanding existing customers. That means everything from initial technical discovery calls to POCs to post-sale technical expansion discussions. You're part forward-deployed engineer, part trusted advisor, part problem solver.
What You'll Actually Do
• Run technical discovery and solution design. Understand customer architecture, identify requirements, and design how Traefik fits their infrastructure. Sometimes this means whiteboarding. Sometimes this means reading their Kubernetes manifests.
• Lead proof-of-concept engagements. Build the demo environment. Configure the deployment. Debug issues. Write scripts and automation. Get it working in their environment, not just yours.
• Present to technical audiences. Explain API gateway architecture to platform engineers. Present security models to CISOs. Lead technical workshops for DevOps teams. Stay in the technical domain.
• Solve real customer problems. Air-gapped deployments. Multi-cluster Kubernetes. Complex authentication flows. NVIDIA NIM integration. You figure it out, document it, make it repeatable.
• Work with product and engineering. You'll see use cases we haven't considered, edge cases that break assumptions, and features customers actually need. Feed that back. Influence the roadmap.
• Contribute to reference architectures and technical content. Expand our deployment patterns, create integration guides, and document best practices. Build on what the team has started.
• Support the sales team. Help qualify opportunities. Run technical workshops. Defend the architecture in competitive situations. Make sure we're bidding on deals we can actually win.
• Expand existing customers. Work with current customers on new use cases, additional clusters, and API Management upgrades. Figure out what else they need and how we can help.
Who Won't Succeed Here
Let's be direct about what doesn't work:
• Pure presenters who can't build. If you're great at slides but can't actually deploy Kubernetes, troubleshoot networking, or read YAML, this isn't for you.
• Engineers who can't talk to humans. If you're brilliant technically but can't explain concepts to non-technical audiences or read the room in customer meetings, you'll struggle.
• People who need perfect documentation. There's no complete playbook. Customer scenarios vary wildly. You need to figure things out, not wait for instructions.
• Solutions architects who won't get their hands dirty. Sometimes you need to SSH into a customer's server, debug a configuration, or write a quick script. That's part of the job.
• Anyone allergic to ambiguity. Customer requirements are often unclear. Use cases evolve. You need to navigate uncertainty and still deliver results.
• People who can't context-switch. One day, you're deep in Kubernetes networking. The next day, you're discussing AI security models. Then you're presenting architecture to a CISO. That's the reality.

Traefik Labs builds the connectivity layer for modern infrastructure. It started with Traefik Proxy, the OSS gateway most teams meet first. If you want to see how we think rather than how we market, read our blog.
The Role
You'll join the product team as a peer to other product managers and split the surface area.
A product manager here is closer to an individual contributor than a coordinator. You'll write the spec and then test the thing you specified. You'll sit in a customer call in the morning, tear down a competitor's gateway in the afternoon, and sketch a mockup that evening because engineering needs to see it before the next standup. The job pulls in several directions at once, on purpose. If that sounds exhausting rather than energizing, this isn't the seat for you.

The platform building blocks are in place or underway — Microsoft 365, Copilot, Entra ID, SharePoint, and Anthropic's Claude models via AWS Bedrock. What we don't yet have is a dedicated person who can both build and operate the secure, production-grade AI platform that lets AI work safely against our data and embed with our lines of business to turn that capability into measurable value.
This role does both. You'll be the technical engine and the on-the-ground partner who makes AI a productive, trusted tool across the enterprise — and who multiplies that impact by enabling others to build, not just building yourself.

What you'll do
Your time will span two connected halves.

Build and operate the AI platform
Model platform and private hosting. Own our Claude deployment on AWS Bedrock end to end — model access and versioning, region and data-residency decisions, provisioned throughput vs. on-demand, and the private, VPC-isolated hosting posture that keeps our data inside our boundary and out of third-party training. Evaluate and manage additional models where they fit, and maintain a routing layer so applications aren't hard-wired to a single model or provider.
Harness and orchestration management. Build and maintain the application harness that sits between our users and the models: prompt and context management, tool and function calling, agent orchestration, retrieval pipelines, guardrails and content filtering, caching, and fallback behavior. Own the evaluation harness too — regression suites, quality benchmarks, and the release process that lets us upgrade models without breaking what's in production.
Data connectivity. Design and build secure, governed connections between AI systems and TNS data — Microsoft 365 and Graph, SharePoint, databases, data warehouses, APIs, and line-of-business systems. Own the retrieval architecture, indexing and freshness strategy, and the permission-trimming that ensures every user sees only what they're entitled to see, with no leakage across boundaries.
Security and access control. Architect least-privilege access across identity, network, and data layers — IAM and Entra ID, private networking, encryption and key management, secrets handling, and tenant isolation. Defend against AI-specific threats: prompt injection, data exfiltration through model outputs, insecure tool use, and over-permissioned agents. Partner with security and governance so every deployment is auditable and compliant by design, with a full audit trail of prompts, outputs, and data access.
Monitoring and observability. Instrument the platform for production operations — latency, error rates, throughput and quota headroom, output quality and drift, guardrail trips, and anomalous usage. Build the dashboards and alerting that let us find problems before users do, and the usage telemetry that tells us which solutions are actually delivering value.
Cost management. Own AI spend as a first-class engineering concern: token-level cost attribution by application and line of business, budgets and alerting, model right-sizing (using the cheapest model that meets the quality bar), prompt caching and context optimization, batch processing where latency allows, and provisioned-throughput decisions. Produce the chargeback and unit-economics reporting leadership needs to fund the portfolio with confidence.
Reusable foundations. Turn all of the above into patterns, templates, and guardrails so each new use case is faster, cheaper, and safer to build than the last.

What you'll accomplish in your first year

• Enable at least one capable AI champion in each line of business.

What you bring (required)
• Strong software / solutions engineering background with hands-on experience building and deploying production AI/LLM applications — RAG, agents, tool use, orchestration, and evaluation.

• Direct experience with a managed model platform in production; AWS Bedrock strongly preferred, along with the surrounding AWS estate (IAM, VPC, KMS, CloudWatch, PrivateLink).

• Demonstrated ability to build and operate data connectivity to enterprise systems with permission-aware retrieval.

• Working command of enterprise security and data governance: identity and access, data protection, encryption and key management, and AI-specific threat models.

Nice to have

• Prior forward-deployed or customer-facing engineering experience.

Qualifications

Who you are
The rare blend of builder and partner. You carry the technical depth of a staff engineer and the people instincts of an internal consultant. You're energized by variety — a private-networking and key-management problem in the morning, a finance-team workflow in the afternoon. You measure yourself by value delivered and adopted, not lines of code. You teach and multiply rather than hoard knowledge. And you operate with ownership: when a deployment is struggling or a cost-line spikes, you own the fix.

How your success is measured
In short: reduced cost to serve on named processes, use cases shipped and sustained in production, adoption across lines of business, champions enabled, platform reliability and cost-per-unit-of-value, and a clean security and governance record.

**Job Purpose**:

The AI-EPOCMON team at the Intelligent Systems Research Centre (ISRC) is seeking a motivated Research Assistant with strong software engineering skills and experience in AI. The post will support the completion of the software delivery work package of a US-Ireland Centre-to-Centre project developing an AI-driven, low-cost, multianalyte point-of-care platform for detecting systemic therapeutic concentrations in biofluids.

#### What we are looking for ...

A product designer that has a strong leaning towards UX, with a background in user research, testing and behaviours. Creating elegant user flows, wireframes and prototypes that solve problems with intuitive solutions.

A passion for typography, layout and digital design. A strong aesthetic and experience working with fashion, luxury and lifestyle brands. Someone able to take their wireframes through to fully fleshed out UI frameworks and designs.

- A beautiful portfolio that showcases your processes, talents and your attention to detail

- Must be digitally focused, able to design websites from scratch to work with developers and product managers

- You have experience of working with fashion / luxury and lifestyle brands

- A highly conceptual thinker who enjoys developing initial ideas through to completion

- Confident self starter, great team player, with the ability to explain ideas to others

- You are passionate about typography / layout and possess an excellent attention to detail

- Alongside a strong aesthetic sense, you will also have a clear understanding of UX and UI standards.

- You will always be interested in pushing the boundaries of what digital has to offer

- Good work ethic and attitude, self-governing and able to manage your own time and deliver projects from concept to development

- Be an excellent communicator both written and verbally

- You may have a passion for art direction and photography and see this as fundamentally important as part of the UI design process

- Great organisational skills and the ability to work across a diverse and various projects, within tight deadlines

Figma, Sketch, Photoshop, Illustrator, InDesign, Invision, Keynote

Make Unity run everywhere, and make it matter to the people building the next generation of vehicles. You'll work directly with automotive OEMs, Tier-1 suppliers and silicon partners to define what we build, why, and in what order. • Product strategy: A clear, evidence-backed strategy for Unity's embedded and automotive runtime: where we play, where we don't, and why.
• Roadmap and prioritization: What gets built and in what order, balancing customer commitments, partner programs, hardware changes and long-term platform health. You'll make hard trade-offs and explain them.
• Executive communication: Writing and presenting product strategy, business cases and roadmap decisions to internal and external stakeholders. Representing Unity's product direction in executive conversations with automakers and partners.
• Opportunity validation: Running discovery, proofs of concept and business cases that lead to clear go/no-go decisions on new customers, partners and features.
• Product definition: Turning what you learn from customers, partners and the market into crisp requirements and success metrics that Engineering can act on.
• Commercial input: Working with pricing, partnerships and go-to-market teams on packaging, licensing and deployment models.

What we're looking for
• Senior product management experience: A track record of setting strategy and shipping platform, SDK, runtime or embedded software products, including making and defending hard prioritization calls.
• Executive and strategic communication: You can turn a complex technical and commercial picture into a clear recommendation. You've influenced senior leaders, inside your company and at customers or partners, through clear writing and presentations.
• Strategic thinking: You can size an opportunity, understand the competitive and partner landscape, and connect product decisions to business outcomes.
• Automotive or strategic partner experience: You've built and maintained relationships with automakers, Tier-1 suppliers or major technology partners, and you understand how they buy and make decisions.
• Technical credibility: Working knowledge of embedded operating systems (such as Android Automotive, QNX or Embedded Linux), real-time graphics and performance on constrained hardware. Enough to make sound trade-offs with Engineering and hold your own with customer technical teams.

• Experience in automotive HMI: cluster, infotainment, ADAS visualization, map navigation.
• Experience shipping games or interactive real-time 3D experiences, or working with real-time 3D engines.
• Prior engineering experience in embedded, graphics or platform software.
• Experience with software licensing or usage-based commercial models.
• Experience working with automotive-grade hardware and the long-term constraints of in-vehicle software.

• Run fast, thoughtful, and innovative recruiting processes that give candidates a great experience and reflect the ambition and pace of Via's engineering culture

• Develop a sharp point of view on the technical talent market - spotting patterns, sharing insights with hiring teams, and constantly looking for ways to raise the bar on how we hire

• Exceptionally smart, gritty, and resourceful as your previous experience matters less to us than your ability to think on your feet and get things done

• Naturally curious and always learning; you want to understand the why behind decisions and enjoy contributing ideas, not just executing on a problem

• Steady, optimistic, and solution-oriented in every situation; we are Via’s culture carriers

• Energised by ambiguous, complex challenges that require good judgment and thoughtful problem-solving

• Partnership with YellowNest, a salary exchange benefit that helps reduce childcare fees for working parents

THE SHORT VERSION

An engineer who owns the numbers. You find where people drop off between signup and their first real win with Viktor, design the experiment that fixes it, build it end to end and ship it the same week.

 


THE HARD PART

Viktor lives where work already happens, in Slack and Teams, with web, desktop, and mobile apps on the way. People talk to him like a colleague, and the whole product is a conversation with an AI employee who writes code, runs it, and ships real work back.

We want people to hand Viktor the work they'd give a great hire, and earning that is as hard as making the thing work at all. Viktor acts on his own and sometimes gets it wrong, and your job is to make people trust him with their real work anyway.

Most growth playbooks assume a product people click through. Viktor is a conversation with an AI employee, so activation means a first task that goes well. The levers are onboarding conversations, defaults and nudges as much as screens.

 


WHAT YOU'LL ACTUALLY DO

 - Find where users stall, from install to first win to team-wide use, and fix it yourself.

 - Run experiments: a clear hypothesis, shipped behind a flag, a result you act on. You design measurement with our Growth Data Scientist.

 - Own activation for Viktor in Slack and Viktor projects: first run, first task, time-to-value.

 - Make features discoverable and move retention through in-product prompts, lifecycle nudges and better defaults.

 - Own land-and-expand loops: invites, sharing, referrals.

 - Instrument everything you ship so every change has a number behind it.

 - Whatever needs building. Small team, large surface.

 


WHO YOU ARE

 - Customer-first, and you get excited about what data and user feedback reveal about how to grow usage. Then you have the product intuition to ship the fix.

 - You think in metrics. You can define an activated user from the data, take a metric apart, and say which funnel stage is leaking and why.

 - You've moved activation, retention or conversion, and you can show the before-and-after.

 - You run experiments: A/B tests with a clear hypothesis and a result you act on.

 - You've shipped a real product that real people use, and you owned it end to end. A product with real users is the point, not a side project that never left localhost.

 - Real engineering strength. You ship your own PRs, including ones that touch the database and user data, without anyone else gating them. Depth in your own area matters more than full-stack breadth.

 - Detail oriented. Empty states, microcopy, edge cases: you notice, and you won't ship until it's right.

 - You talk to users and own outcomes, not tickets. You shape the problem, cut scope when you should, and ship the thing that moves the metric.

 - Speed, with the bar up. You ship today, not Thursday, and it's still good.

 - Agentic coding is your daily workflow. You build with AI by default and you're faster because of it.

 - Genuine drive. You build things because you can't not.

 


WHY THIS ROLE IS DIFFERENT

 - No layers. You work directly with both founders, design, and growth, and decisions get made in the room, not in a Linear ticket.

 - You own the surface customers actually see. Every win shows up in activation and retention the next week.

 - We use Viktor to build Viktor. You ship the product using the product, every day.

 - Real ownership: a surface of the company that customers depend on. When it wins, everyone knows whose work it was.

 


EVEN BETTER IF

 - You've founded something or been an early-stage builder.

 - You've shipped something with real traction: users, revenue, downloads, a product people know.

 - You've built growth loops (referrals, invites, lifecycle) in a PLG or B2B product.

 - You've built with the AI tooling we live in and have opinions about it.

 


TECH

The product lives in Slack and Teams today, with web, desktop, and mobile apps on the way. TypeScript/React for the web, Python on the backend and agents, Modal for infrastructure. This role leans instrumentation and experimentation. You move across the stack, database included, when an experiment needs it.

 


HOW WE WORK

Small team, high trust, low process. Decisions are made by owners, not committees. You will ship your first week. You will talk to users your first day.

We don't do alignment meetings or stakeholder syncs. We build things, see if they work, and iterate.

 


WHY VIKTOR

We're one of the fastest-growing companies in the world. The product works. The market is pulling.

This is a rare window: everyone here owns a surface of the company that customers depend on. That doesn't last forever. Right now, it's still true.

 


COMPENSATION

Top-of-the-market salary and the kind of ownership that only exists at this stage.

The best work happens when you're in the room. This role is Munich or Warsaw, or remote in Europe, and we bring the whole team together in person a few times a year.

## Description

### **About Vinterior**

Vinterior is the UK’s leading marketplace for premium pre-owned furniture and homeware. We connect buyers with professional sellers offering vintage, antique and contemporary pieces, making it easier to find furniture with character and give beautiful things a longer life.

Founded in 2016 and backed by investors including Seedcamp, Venrex, Active Partners and Channel 4 Ventures, we’re building a sustainable alternative to buying new, with ambitions to grow across Europe.

We’re a small, remote team with a practical, entrepreneurial approach. People here take ownership, work closely across functions and get involved in the detail. You’ll have the opportunity to make a visible difference to the business while helping more people choose pre-owned.

### **Role overview**

As Financial Controller, you’ll own the day-to-day running of Vinterior’s finance function, reporting directly to our Founder & CEO, Sandrine, and managing our Finance Manager.

This is a broad, hands-on role in a small team. You’ll keep our accounts accurate, our cash well managed and our reporting timely, while taking ownership of financial controls, compliance and improvements to how we operate. You’ll also get involved in the practical contractual and people administration questions that come with running a small business.

You enjoy understanding how things work, investigating discrepancies and seeing problems through to resolution. You’re comfortable moving between detailed financial work and conversations about budgets, profitability and business priorities.

There is scope to grow into Head of Finance and, over time, Finance Director as you demonstrate the commercial judgement, leadership and impact required, and as the business develops.

### **What you’ll do**

- **Own financial control and reporting.** Deliver accurate month-end accounts, balance-sheet reconciliations and clear financial reporting for the leadership team and Board. Maintain reliable revenue recognition and investigate discrepancies.
- **Keep marketplace payments running smoothly.** Ensure transactions reconcile across our platform, payment providers and accounting system, including seller payouts, refunds, fees and foreign exchange. Identify and resolve revenue leakage.
- **Manage cash and financial planning.** Maintain cash-flow forecasts, budgets and a rolling financial outlook. Explain variances, challenge assumptions and flag risks early, with practical recommendations.
- **Take ownership of compliance.** Keep financial, tax and relevant marketplace obligations organised and up to date, including statutory accounts, VAT and international requirements. Identify gaps, coordinate specialist advice where needed and ensure actions are completed.
- **Oversee payroll and support people administration.** Ensure payroll is accurate and timely. Work with the colleague responsible for people administration to keep employment documentation and contractual changes accurate, current and appropriately reviewed.
- **Improve commercial performance.** Help colleagues understand the financial impact of their decisions. Identify opportunities to improve margins, payment costs and operating expenditure, and help turn recommendations into results.
- **Make processes and systems better.** Own our finance systems, including Xero and payment-provider reporting. Use automation and AI where useful to reduce manual work and strengthen accuracy and controls.
- **Deliver improvements across teams.** Work with Product, Engineering, CX and other colleagues on projects such as payment changes and international expansion.
- **Develop the finance function.** Manage and coach our Finance Manager, delegate effectively and document key processes so the function runs reliably. Manage external accounting relationships and other specialist support.

### **Why join us?**

- **Own a finance function.** Take meaningful responsibility for how finance runs, with direct access to the Founder & CEO and visibility across the business.
- **See the impact of your work.** Your improvements to reporting, payments, costs and controls will make a tangible difference.
- **Build your leadership experience.** Develop a colleague, work across functions and broaden your commercial judgement, with scope to progress as your contribution grows.
- **Work towards a mission that matters.** Help make pre-owned furniture a compelling alternative to buying new.
- **Enjoy remote working and close collaboration.** Work independently while staying connected to a small, practical and entrepreneurial team.

## Requirements

- You have a professional accounting qualification such as ACA, ACCA or CIMA, or substantial equivalent experience running financial control and reporting.
- You have personally owned month-end accounts, reconciliations, cash forecasting and budgeting. You’re comfortable doing the detailed work yourself as well as reviewing someone else’s.
- You enjoy working in a small business where responsibilities are broad and you can make improvements without waiting for a detailed brief.
- You take pride in getting things right. When something doesn’t reconcile or an obligation is unclear, you investigate, establish what needs to happen and follow through.
- You bring sound judgement and commercial curiosity. You can explain what the numbers mean, challenge assumptions constructively and recommend practical action.
- You communicate clearly with colleagues outside finance, involve the right people early and raise problems before they become surprises.
- You can support and develop a colleague, delegate effectively and manage external accounting relationships.
- You’re confident with accounting systems, spreadsheets and financial modelling, and interested in using new tools to improve how you work.
- You can work independently in a remote team while staying connected, responsive and organised.

Experience in a marketplace, e-commerce business or founder-led company would be useful, as would exposure to Xero, payment platforms, international VAT or broader business compliance. You don’t need to have encountered every issue before, but you do need the curiosity and judgement to work out how to address it.

- Annual Leave: 25 days of paid leave in addition to 8 bank holidays
- Private Medical Insurance: Comprehensive private medical insurance coverage to ensure your well-being
- Health and Well-being Allowance: A monthly allowance of £50 for health and well-being expenses
- Charity Days: You will receive paid leave to support your chosen charity and make a positive impact on the community.
- Tenure Gift: You will receive additional paid leave for 1+ years of service to the company.
- Employee Vinterior Discount: Enjoy a special discount on Vinterior products as an employee of Vinterior.

Please note that all benefits are subject to the terms and conditions outlined in our employee handbook.

Our interview process looks for people who share [our company values](https://www.notion.so/Our-Company-values-c1e9685b54734b06985f1749f233c0dc?pvs=21).

If these principles resonate with you and describe the kinds of people you would like to work with, then you are likely to enjoy and thrive in the working culture at Vinterior

At Vinterior, we believe that diversity is our strength. We encourage applications from individuals of all backgrounds and are committed to providing a fair and inclusive hiring process. The HR Graduate will develop broad, practical experience across the employee lifecycle through a structured programme of rotations covering recruitment, HR administration and operations, learning and development, employee relations, reward, payroll support and employee engagement. The role combines hands-on delivery with supervised learning, building the knowledge, judgement and skills needed for a career in HR.

Reporting to the Head of Operational HR, the graduate will work alongside HR specialists and operational teams during placements at office and project locations, including Essex, London and Acton. Each rotation will have agreed learning objectives, practical tasks and regular feedback from the relevant placement supervisor. Responsibilities will develop progressively in line with competence, with appropriate supervision and escalation of sensitive or complex matters. Rotation timing and locations will be agreed according to development objectives and business requirements.

Requirements: 

- **Rotational development:** Complete agreed placements across HR functions and office and project locations, maintain a learning log, seek feedback and review progress against development objectives. Prepare clear handovers between placements.
- **Recruitment and resourcing:** Support vacancy administration, job adverts, applicant tracking system updates, interview scheduling and candidate communications. Assist with shortlisting and assessment activities against agreed criteria under the recruitment team’s guidance.
- **Onboarding and induction:** Coordinate references, pre-employment documentation and checks in line with company procedures. Track outstanding actions, prepare induction schedules and liaise with managers and IT/ITRM on access and equipment requirements.
- **HR administration:** Draft contracts, employee letters and changes to terms using approved templates for review. Support probation tracking, employee transfers, leaver administration and arrangements for the return of company equipment.
- **HR systems and records:** Maintain accurate starter, employment change and leaver information in Cascade and employee files on SharePoint. Check supporting approvals, maintain audit trails and handle personal information securely and confidentially.
- **HR helpdesk:** Log and triage enquiries, respond to routine queries within agreed guidance, allocate tickets to the appropriate HR colleague and track actions through to closure. Escalate matters outside the graduate’s knowledge or authority.
- **Training coordination:** Assist with identifying training needs, arranging courses and bookings, issuing joining instructions and monitoring attendance and e-learning completion. Gather feedback and maintain training records in Cascade.

- **Early careers and talent:** Help coordinate apprentice and graduate recruitment, programme administration, development activities and review meetings. Support appraisal and objective-setting communications and completion tracking.

- **Office and project placements:** Attend allocated locations and build an understanding of different operating environments. Support local inductions and employee queries, complete required site inductions and comply with site safety, access and PPE requirements.
- **Reward, benefits and payroll support:** Help administer benefits queries and approved pay or employment changes, collate and check payroll inputs and refer discrepancies for review. Learn the links between HR records, reward and payroll without independently approving changes.
- **HR reporting and improvement:** Prepare routine reports and check data accuracy across recruitment, headcount, absence and training. Contribute to policy reviews, process mapping and small improvement projects, presenting findings and suggestions for review.

- Good written and verbal communication skills.

- Working knowledge of Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook, and willingness to learn HR systems.
- Responsible handling of confidential information and awareness of when to seek guidance.

You’ll own the channels end-to-end: when a campaign is briefed, you’re the one who activates it across LinkedIn, Google and paid social, optimises it, and reports back on what it delivered.

This is a hands-on, build-it-yourself role. It’s an exciting time in Walr’s growth, our digital marketing is at an early stage, and you’ll be the person who puts the systems in place — including the AI-assisted and agentic workflows that let a small team operate like a much larger one. You’ll work as a peer alongside our Senior Marketing Executive.

If you’ve built digital from scratch in a startup or scale-up and want to do it again on a global scale with the backing of a 180-person business, this is the role.
Key Responsibilities

• Own all digital activation for Walr’s marketing campaigns, working to campaign concepts agreed with the wider marketing team.

• Plan, launch and optimise multi-channel demand generation across LinkedIn, Google, paid social and retargeting — owning each channel, its budget and its performance against pipeline and lead targets.

• Support SEO and AEO (answer engine optimisation) so Walr is found in search and in AI-generated answers.

• Own email marketing and marketing automation: run our current platform, lead the assessment of our automation stack and any migration, and keep it tightly integrated with Salesforce.

• Own the lead flow end-to-end — web forms, routing and CRM integration — working with our IT and ops team so every enquiry reaches Sales quickly and nothing falls through the gaps.

• Build nurture and lifecycle email programmes, from post-enquiry sequences to quarterly content.

• Build and maintain marketing reporting and dashboards: channel performance, cost per lead and pipeline influenced.

• Build, document and scale AI-assisted and agentic marketing workflows for content production, campaign operations and reporting.

• Manage paid media budgets and agency or freelance resource where used.

• Contribute to marketing strategy and annual planning alongside the Senior Marketing Executive and Marketing Leader.

Required experience and skills

• 2+ years of hands-on digital marketing in B2B SaaS or technology — ideally marketing a platform or product, not only services.

• You’ve built digital from scratch: set up paid campaigns, SEO, tracking and automation in a startup or scale-up marketing team of one or two, or in a dedicated digital team at a larger SaaS business and now want more ownership.

• Proven, quantified results you can talk through: campaigns run, cost per lead achieved, pipeline influenced, tools owned.

• Hands-on with the core stack: LinkedIn Campaign Manager, Google Ads, GA4 and Search Console, a marketing automation platform (HubSpot, ActiveCampaign, Marketo, Klaviyo or similar), a CMS (Salesforce), no-code tooling such as Make.com, Zapier, or n8n, and AI tools such as Claude and ChatGPT used directly in your work.

• Comfortable with pace and change. You’d rather ship, measure and improve than wait for perfect.

🛠️ About our Simulation Teams

Simulation is advancing end-to-end autonomous driving research. The team’s mission is to accelerate AV2.0 by incubating capabilities that become company-level advantages — generative world models and the synthetic data they produce are one of those. The goal of this role is to build, scale, and optimise next-generation world model architectures (GAIA and successors) and bridge them into high-throughput generation and training infrastructure, so synthetic data can dramatically accelerate autonomy development. You will post-train world models for new embodiments and behaviours (rig transfer, pose transfer, dashcam restaging), generate multimodal synthetic experience at scale, and land that data in the same training stack we use for real driving. You sit between ML research and engineering: collaborating with scientists on architecture and conditioning, and with platform engineers on generation jobs, training artefacts, and how synthetic data is mixed into training. Your work will decide how fast we can train, evaluate, and deploy driving models on vehicles we have barely collected from.

 

🧠 Your day-to-day

 - Model development: Post-train, distill, and evaluate GAIA-family large video diffusion models to improve generation quality, controllability, and generalisation. Run ablation studies and investigate failures in visual quality, temporal consistency, motion, and action conditioning.

 - Generation at scale: Build and run synthetic video generation pipelines across tens of thousands of driving segments. Optimise inference efficiency, manage GPU resources, and ensure data quality throughout the pipeline.

 - From generation to training: Integrate synthetic data across different stages of driving-model training, develop sampling strategies, and measure its impact through evaluation suites and on-road performance.

 - Cross-team collaboration: Work with driving-model teams to determine effective data mixtures and with simulation and evaluation teams to turn generated scenarios into useful closed-loop tests.

 - Applied research: Translate advances in world modelling, video generation, flow matching, distillation, and data-centric training into measurable improvements in the models and data we deploy.

 

🧩 What you’ll be working on

 - Post-train and iterate GAIA-class world models for synthetic-data capabilities: embodiment transfer (new camera/vehicle embodiments), pose transfer (rewritten ego trajectories), and related conditioning (geometry, calibration, actions).

 - Own the generation loop: config → large-scale GPU inference → training-ready artefacts, with clear lineage from the model and settings that produced them.

 - Land synthetic data in driving-model training (behaviour cloning, reward models, RL): binarisation, mix ratios, quality filters, and experiments that measure suite and on-road impact — including when synthetic should replace scarce real rig data.Diagnose and fix geometry, artefacts, calibration, and controllability failures that determine whether generated video is training-grade.

 - Improve throughput and yield: inference optimisations (distillation, KV cache), valid-generation rate, and self-serve workflows so model developers can request synthetic sets without a specialist.

 - Expand coverage to new vehicle platforms and safety-critical scenarios (OEM bring-up; Emergency Lane Keeping / Automatic Emergency Braking).

 - Partner with world-model researchers, infra, and driving-model owners so generation, evaluation, and training stay one system.

 - Strong Python and PyTorch (or equivalent); comfort with GPU training, debugging, and reading model code.

 - Hands-on experience with video, generative, or world models (diffusion / flow-matching / autoregressive video, novel-view synthesis, neural rendering, or similar).

 - Working knowledge of cameras and 3D geometry (multi-camera rigs, intrinsics/extrinsics, warps/reprojection) and why they break generation or downstream training.

Do you want to help us improve human health and understand life on Earth? Make your mark by shaping the future to enable or deliver life-changing science to solve some of humanity’s greatest challenges.

Help strengthen the services behind world-leading genomics research at the Wellcome Sanger Institute. As Head of Financial Business Partnering for Scientific Platform Services, you will guide decisions about investment, resources and service delivery that support our scientific mission. Reporting to the Chief Financial Officer within Finance, you will lead a small business partnering team and collaborate with senior scientific and operational leaders. You will have scope to shape costing and pricing, improve performance and support external commercial opportunities.

About the Role
As Head of Financial Business Partnering, you will lead financial business partnering across Genomic Platforms, Cellular Platforms and Technical Development & Scale-Up, covering around 200 colleagues and an annual budget of approximately £15 million. Your work will help leaders balance cost, capacity and scientific needs, making the best use of resources to support research.

Responsibilities include: 
• Guiding senior leaders on financial planning and analysis, scenario modelling, resource allocation and capital investment business cases.
• Developing and implementing costing and pricing models for internal scientific services and external commercial opportunities.
• Translating financial and operational data into performance measures, management information and clear recommendations.
• Shaping commercial proposals and supporting negotiations alongside scientific colleagues, Finance and the Innovation and Impact team.
• Leading, coaching and developing finance business partners, supporting effective delegation, performance and collaboration.
• Improving processes, reporting and systems while maintaining robust financial controls and supporting effective governance.

About You
You will bring experience as a senior finance business partner or in a comparable finance leadership role, combining analytical expertise with sound commercial judgement. Your experience could come from research, manufacturing, engineering or another similarly complex operational environment.

Essential capabilities:
• Apply advanced knowledge of budgeting, forecasting, scenario modelling, business case development, valuations and activity-based costing.
• Demonstrate experience developing and implementing pricing and standard costing models in a complex environment.
• Influence senior operational leaders, build trusted relationships and explain complex information clearly.
• Lead and develop teams through coaching, delegation and constructive performance management.
• Analyse complex issues, assess risk and develop evidence-based recommendations using financial modelling, Excel, dashboards and financial planning tools.
• Improve operational performance through process redesign, strategic problem-solving and practical solutions.

Desirable experience: Financial management of research grants and business systems implementation would be helpful but are not essential.

We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, including those underrepresented in finance leadership and research organisations. You do not need a research-sector background if you can demonstrate the essential capabilities above.

Next Steps
If you’re excited by the opportunity to shape financial strategy and operational performance in support of world-leading genomics research, we’d love to hear from you.

Please include a cover letter along with your CV. In your cover letter, include details on how your knowledge, skills and experience match the requirements of the role described.

• Experience using AI coding assistants for data analysis and other technical tasks.

• Fluency in SQL and working with large scale data (we use tools like Hive, Presto, Druid, and Spark).

• Experience collaborating with product development teams in a fast-paced environment to test, analyze, and evaluate user-facing features for an online platform.

• Ability to explain data and insights clearly to non-specialist audiences and gain their understanding and confidence.

• Curiosity and critical thinking skills; a lifelong learner who sees situations through multiple lenses.

• Empathy towards and commitment to work with the Wikimedia volunteer communities. Discretion and competence in handling sensitive or confidential data.

• Commitment to the mission of the organization and our values and guiding principles.

• Prior experience working in areas related to trust & safety, information security and privacy, or fraud and anti-abuse.

• Contributed to Wikimedia projects or have experience working in other open source projects.

The Wikimedia Foundation is looking for a Senior Software Engineer, Android to support the App Experience and App Growth teams within the Core Experiences engineering group. 

Our teams have a clear and ambitious goal: make our apps the destination for knowledge lovers and grow our active readership. 

Availability

It’s important to state that we are a fully remote team at a global organisation. To ensure there are enough opportunities to communicate, this role needs at least four hours of your workday to occur between 15:00 UTC and 21:00 UTC.

You are responsible for:

• Delivery and enablement - Delivery of medium complexity initiatives from technical discovery through delivery. Breaks down initiatives into features, drive estimation and manage scope. Identifies risks early, and helps the team make pragmatic tradeoffs across quality, velocity, maintainability, and user impact.

• Implementation - Improving the mobile Wikipedia product experiences that serve a global, multilingual audience on Android. Leads system design for medium-sized projects and can design and build accessible, adaptable, scalable components. 

• Quality, testing and observability - Consistently builds software that is easy to test, observe and debug. Instruments features that enable deeper analysis by Product Analysts. 

• Cross-functional collaboration - Partners with product managers, designers, analysts, and native app engineers to shape pragmatic solutions that balance user needs, technical constraints, platform expectations, and delivery timelines.

• Prioritisation - Proactively identifies high-impact technical opportunities and risks across the engagement timeframe, works with the team to clarify priorities and sequencing. Actively keeps the team aligned on outcomes, capacity, and shared goals.

• Culture and standards - Complies with team standards in code review, technical design, testing, documentation, accessibility, observability, and decision-making - fostering transparency, empathy, and collaboration.

• Operational Awareness - Plans work with awareness of downstream or upstream effects.

Qualities that are important to us:

• Clear communicator - You can explain your ideas simply and adapt your communication to different audiences across engineering, product, and non-technical audiences in both synchronous and asynchronous channels.

• Autonomy - Operates with high autonomy in a team setting and cross-team settings. You own your work end-to-end and practice a culture of responsibility and follow-through.

• Feedback - You give and receive feedback with curiosity and empathy. Helps others resolve misunderstandings productively.

• Builds strong relationships - Proactively brings the right people into discussions, identifies process improvements. 

• Comfortable with ambiguity - You are comfortable with ambiguity and can collaborate to solve complex problems with pragmatic solutions. Connects ideas and can regularly balance trade-offs across related domains to create well-rounded solutions.

• Knowledge sharing - Strong knowledge-sharing practices, documents work for handover and consistently helps others understand and apply shared knowledge. You enjoy working with others to solve problems and are open to feedback. You inspire trust and progress through support, example, and thoughtful contributions.

• Outcome-oriented - You prioritise work that delivers value to users and aligns with organizational goals.You balance ideal solutions with the constraints of legacy, user expectations and delivery needs

Requirements:

• Bachelor's and 5-10+ years related professional experience with significant experience building Android applications

• Strong professional experience and proficiency with Kotlin, XML, Jetpack Compose, and familiarity with architectural patterns in Android

• Experience of Android performance optimisation techniques to ensure smooth, responsive, and high-performing applications under a variety of conditions.

• Experience working in a self-driven, lean environment

• Commitment to the Foundation's Mission and Values

Additionally, we would love it if you have:

• Experience adding webview-wrapped experiences to existing native mobile apps (iOS or Android)

• Experience in maintaining cross-platform mobile applications.

• Experience building mobile games or other interactive mobile experiences. 

• Experience with data science, machine learning, and/or AI (e.g., familiarity with prompt engineering, Jupyter notebooks experience, etc.)

• Familiarity with Wikipedia / wikitext / markdown editing or content management systems (e.g., MediaWiki, Drupal, WordPress)

• Experience with leveraging agentic coding to scale the work of small engineering teams.

• Bachelor's, master's, or doctorate degree in computer science, management information systems, or STEM field (or equivalent certification)

• Prior experience with MediaWiki or Wikimedia projects.

• A history of open source contributions

About the Wikimedia Foundation

The Wikimedia Foundation is the nonprofit organization that operates Wikipedia and the other Wikimedia free knowledge projects. Our vision is a world in which every single human can freely share in the sum of all knowledge. We believe that everyone has the potential to contribute something to our shared knowledge, and that everyone should be able to access that knowledge freely. We host Wikipedia and the Wikimedia projects, build software experiences for reading, contributing, and sharing Wikimedia content, support the volunteer communities and partners who make Wikimedia possible, and advocate for policies that enable Wikimedia and free knowledge to thrive. 

The Wikimedia Foundation is a charitable, not-for-profit organization that relies on donations. We receive donations from millions of individuals around the world, with an average donation of about $15. We also receive donations through institutional grants and gifts. The Wikimedia Foundation is a United States 501(c)(3) tax-exempt organization with offices in San Francisco, California, USA.

As an equal opportunity employer, the Wikimedia Foundation values having a diverse workforce and continuously strives to maintain an inclusive and equitable workplace. The Wikimedia Foundation is a remote-first organization with staff members including contractors based 40+ countries*. The Editing team is part of the Contributors group. They work on tools for editing across MediaWiki, principally VisualEditor, DiscussionTools, and Edit check. Data Platform Engineering
The Mission of the Data Platform Engineering team is to empower Wiki Communities and the Wikimedia Foundation to gain insights, conduct research, and build compelling user experiences, through access to privacy-aware data and data platform services. The Data Platform is a collection of systems and services providing end-to-end capabilities for our data producers and consumers to collect, discover, and use data.

Release Engineering
The Release Engineering team enables developers to confidently build, test, and deploy code changes across Wikimedia projects, including Wikipedia, by creating the tools, infrastructure, and automation that keep software delivery fast and reliable.

Connection team

The Connection team is part of the Contributors group. They aim to improve how contributors connect and understand their impact. The team was formed in 2021 to focus on the needs of campaign and event organizers and participants and hopefully improve the experience of Wikimedia campaigns.

Tools Infrastructure (with Observability)

The mission of the Tools Infrastructure team is to provide a free, reliable, secure and scalable Cloud hosting platform to support Wikimedia contributors and developers to run tools, bots, data pipelines, and services that support Wikipedia and its sister projects. 

The Observability team’s mission is to provide insight into the health, performance and behaviour of production code and systems for teams within the Wikimedia Foundation and for volunteers at large.

job_description:
About us
Food waste costs the world over $1 trillion a year. At Winnow, we're on a mission to change that — bringing AI-powered technology into hospitality kitchens to help eliminate waste at scale, with an ambition to save our clients $1 billion annually.
We started in London in 2013 with a simple belief: technology could make kitchens smarter and food systems more sustainable. Today that belief has grown into a global team spanning the UK, Romania, Dubai, Shanghai, Singapore, Malaysia, North America, and Mexico, working across 90+ countries and 3,500+ sites.
We're proud of the results we help our clients achieve. Names like IKEA, Hilton, Accor, Marriott, IHG, Compass Group, Iberostar, and Mandarin Oriental trust us to cut their food waste by over 50% on average — and when our technology is fully adopted, it reduces pre-consumer waste by 50–70% and delivers food cost savings of 2–8%.
We're building something that matters, and the people who thrive here feel that every day. We're proud to have been named one of The Sunday Times Best Places to Work and ranked #4 in the FoodTech 500 (2025) — recognition of both our innovation and our commitment to building a purpose-led company where people can make a real difference.
Our values
Our values sit at the centre of all that we do. If they resonate with you, we'd love to hear from you and for you to help us on our mission.
• People of action - done is better than perfect. We move fast, learn faster
• Equal parts head and heart - we balance passion with pragmatism
• Hungry and humble - we're ambitious about our mission, not our egos
• Bravely honest - we say what we think, respectfully, with colleagues and customers alike
• Bound by food - it's what unites us, and it's what we're fighting for
• People and planet positive - we're leaving both better than we found them
Requirements
About the role
The Machine Learning and Data Science team builds and maintains the computer vision models at the heart of Winnow's product: systems that watch a kitchen bin and turn what they see into accurate, trustworthy waste data. We're looking for a Head of Machine Learning and Data Science to take full ownership of one of the most technically challenging areas in the company. You’ll lead the team, set the technical direction, and make sure our models keep getting better as Winnow scales into new sites, new cameras, and new food environments.
Your first priority is clear: take food recognition to the accuracy our customers need, which means bringing rigour to data quality, labelling, evaluation and ML operations. From there, your remit extends to production forecasting, and over time to shaping how we use AI more broadly across the product, including LLM-based features.
This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who wants deep technical ownership and direct impact, rather than a large organisation. Reporting to the Head of Technology, you’ll be a key part of the technical leadership of Winnow. You’ll make the case for where we invest in ML, and be the bridge between ML and the rest of the business - translating model performance into terms that product, engineering and customer-facing teams can act on.
As the function matures, we expect this role's remit to grow beyond the initial scope focused on food recognition. That includes:
• Strategic ownership - develop and execute a long-term vision of creating a state-of-the-art AI/ML ecosystem. Influence how AI and ML are used in Winnow’s products and how we develop best-in-class models and techniques.
• ML operations - designing and building highly automated ML pipelines, reproducible processes, and an infrastructure designed for continuous improvement.
• Performance measurement - defining the metrics used to objectively measure the performance of the ML systems, diagnosing and troubleshooting issues.
• Annotation and labelling processes - owning the tooling and processes behind how training data gets labelled to ensure that we have what we need to drive high-quality AI systems.
• Edge/device and camera hardware input - technical input into camera and edge-compute decisions as new hardware generations come online, not just building models to fit existing constraints.
• Privacy and responsible AI - broader ownership of how personal data is handled in the recognition pipeline (face-blurring is an early example), especially given customer security/compliance expectations.
• Vendor and third-party model evaluation - managing relationships with external model providers and annotation partners as reliance on them grows.

Key responsibilities
Technical direction
• Set and maintain the technical strategy for Winnow's core computer vision pipeline, including food-tracking, waste-stage classification, weight estimation, and food-identity recognition models and beyond.
• Take broader ownership of all ML/AI activities in the company (e.g. production forecasting) once the food recognition accuracy targets are met.
• Act as an advisor on LLM-based product features with a view to owning this area over time.
• Guide model improvement work to maximise performance of the overall system, including fully utilising all hardware capabilities (multiple cameras), and edge and cloud computing capabilities.
• Oversee the creation and upkeep of high-quality datasets and annotation guidelines that the team's models are trained and validated against.
• Drive improvements to ground-truth and label quality, including label aggregation approaches for cases with multiple or conflicting annotations.
• Sponsor and conduct exploratory research into new techniques - for example, using vision-language models as a verification layer on top of existing classifiers - and make informed calls on when to invest further versus park an experiment.
• Set out a clear future-state vision, and a step-by-step plan to deliver it, for stakeholders across the business.
• Own the team's technical workspace, including data repositories, pipelines, toolsets, dashboards, and a combination of cloud and on-prem infrastructure.
Cross-functional partnership
• Work closely with Engineering to build systems that combine software and AI to deliver high accuracy reliably, and ship models into production, including on edge hardware.
• Partner with Product to translate customer and operational needs into a model roadmap, and to explain model performance and limitations in plain terms.
• Represent ML and Data Science in technical reviews and sign-offs for new model releases, RFCs and major pipeline changes.
• Build the business cases for ML investment and work with the Head of Technology on budget allocation.
Team leadership
• Lead, coach, and grow a team of four research and data scientists, setting individual and team goals and supporting their technical and career development.
• Shape the team's hiring plan and lead recruitment for new roles, holding a high bar for every hire.
• Spot and address underperformance early, using clear improvement plans and working with the People team where needed.
• Own the team's quarterly OKRs end to end - shaping objectives, tracking key results, and reporting progress to engineering and product leadership.
• Build a strong team culture around rigorous experimentation, clear documentation, and shared ownership of model quality.
• Manage prioritisation across a busy roadmap of model improvement work, data quality initiatives, and exploratory research.

About you 
Experience
• Proven experience leading a machine learning or data science team, including direct people management, ideally within computer vision or a related applied ML domain.
• Strong hands-on background in computer vision - object detection/tracking, classification, or segmentation - and comfort going deep on model architecture and evaluation when needed.
• Experience running ML work through a clear operating rhythm (e.g. OKRs, RFCs, sign-off processes) in a fast-moving product environment.
• Track record of shipping models into real-world production systems, ideally including edge or resource-constrained deployment.
• Experience with data quality and annotation workflows, including label aggregation or multi-annotator agreement techniques.
You might also have
• A PhD or MSc in a relevant field.
• Exposure to using large vision-language or foundation models as auxiliary tools within a production ML pipeline (e.g. verification, labelling assistance).
• Experience working with camera/IoT hardware constraints, or in a company whose product runs on physical devices in the field.
• A background in a data-scarce or noisy-label domain where rigorous experimentation and ground-truth quality make an outsized difference.
• Experience in software engineering practices: automated testing, version control and breaking down larger software systems.
• Experience with graph databases and distributed computing systems (e.g. Spark)
How you work
• You get a lot done and can motivate and lead a team to do the same.
• You lead by example technically, while knowing when to step back and let your team own a problem.
• You're comfortable making prioritisation calls with incomplete information, and can explain the reasoning to both engineers and non-technical stakeholders.
• You care as much about the rigour behind a result (data quality, evaluation methodology) as the result itself.
Our technology stack
You’ll be working with:
• ML frameworks: TensorFlow, PyTorch, Pandas, NumPy
• Python/Linux environment
• MLOps tooling such as MLflow
• Jupyter Notebooks
• Relational and non-relational databases: AWS Redshift, PostgreSQL, vector databases
• Apache Airflow for workflow orchestration
• AWS cloud infrastructure as well as on-premise dedicated hardware
• Git
Benefits

• Competitive salary 
• Pension contribution - up to 6.5% of employer contribution 
• Company part-funded private health insurance and eyecare allowance
• Life insurance (3 times base salary)
• Company stock options package
• 2 Wellness hours per month plus a £48 gross monthly wellness allowance
• Employee Assistance Programme – 24/7 helpline for your wellbeing
• 25 days of paid vacation time in addition to national holidays, plus extra vacation time based on length of tenure with Winnow
• Option to purchase up to 5 additional days of annual leave per year
• Learning and development allowance of £300 annually
• Early Finish Fridays – log off at 3pm on a Friday if you've completed your tasks by then
• You will love what you do – waking up every day solving one of the biggest social problems of our generation: food waste

Wolf & Badger is on a mission to make retail fair. Supporting our community of independent designers from more than 70 countries, we connect customers with fashion, design, home and beauty from brands vetted against our sustainability guarantees, through our online marketplace and flagship stores in London, New York City and Los Angeles. We are a scale-up business based in the UK and US and a Certified B Corporation, with social and environmental purpose at the core of everything we do. We were the first UK online marketplace to become a certified B Corp, have been recognised by the Financial Times as one of Europe's Long-Term Growth Champions, and were one of the first marketplaces globally to take orders placed by AI shopping agents.

## The Role

London is where Wolf & Badger started, and we want to be the first name UK press, stylists and creators think of for independent fashion and design. We are looking for an organised and creative Senior PR & Partnerships Manager to make that happen.

Reporting to our Head of PR & Partnerships, who is based in New York and sets our PR strategy across the UK and US, you will lead PR delivery in the UK. Your focus is UK press, UK creators and influencers, and events, from London Fashion Week moments to activations in our Soho store and beyond. You will run our London press office day to day and be the person UK journalists, stylists and creators deal with.

You will work closely with our London content and social teams, our growth marketing team, our Brand Partnerships team and our Soho store team. We use AI to take the repetitive work off your plate, so your time goes on relationships, stories and good judgement.

At Wolf & Badger we champion a low-ego environment where cross-functional debate is encouraged in order to reach the best outcomes. We strive to be mission-orientated and fair at all times, and you will join us in growing an engaged, forward-thinking and high-functioning team.

This is a full-time role based in our Central London office and Soho store 3+ days per week, with occasional evening and weekend work for events.

## Key Responsibilities & Accountabilities

** 
UK Press**

- Deliver our UK PR plan, agreed with our Head of PR & Partnerships, and land regular coverage for Wolf & Badger and the independent designers we champion
- Build close relationships with UK fashion, lifestyle and sustainability media, stylists and tastemakers
- Find and pitch the stories UK media will want: our independent designers, our B Corp standards, our Soho store and how we use AI in shopping
- Run the London press office: press enquiries, press materials, sample, image and credit requests, celebrity and event dressing, and press appointments in our Soho store, keeping track of every sample loan with our designer brands and store team, and passing anything sensitive to our Head of PR & Partnerships
- Keep the UK side of our shared PR and events calendar, including awards entries
- Success looks like: a high volume, steady run of quality UK coverage for Wolf & Badger and our designers, activating key moments and actively cementing the positioning of the Wolf & Badger platform for UK industry, community, customers and brands; a growing list of journalists and stylists who call us first and an efficient press office service, in conjunction with our community team, where no request or sample loan slips
